title: P0: Configurable per-repo bead-ID prefix with sanitized default (single source of truth)
description:
PRIORITY/ORDER: P0. Bead 2 of 2 — depends on rosary-3f8515 (sanitization+tests land first). Do AFTER current PRs close, BEFORE any new features.

## Problem (see RCA in rosary-3f8515)
There is no single source of truth for a repo's bead-ID prefix. rsry derives it from the config `name` at each call site; `bd` uses its own baked prefix ("loom"). They diverge, producing loom-/rsry-/rosary- all in one store and new loom-* IDs today.

## Scope of THIS bead
- Add an explicit, optional per-repo `bead_prefix` (or `prefix`) field to the `[[repo]]` config (config.rs), alongside `name`/`path`/`lang`.
- Deterministic default-resolution chain when unset: explicit `bead_prefix` → repo `name` → git remote name (origin) → sanitized directory basename → hard fallback. Run the result through the sanitizer from rosary-3f8515.
- Make ALL id-generation call sites (main.rs:1201/1305/1351, serve/handlers.rs:519/1618) use this single resolver — no ad-hoc `repo_name`.
- Tests: explicit prefix honored; default falls through name→remote→basename; sanitization applied; renaming the repo dir does NOT change the prefix once set (stability); two repos never collide.
- Reconcile the `bd` divergence: either (a) align bd's stored issue-prefix to the resolved config prefix on scan, or (b) document that bd must not create beads in rosary-managed stores. NOTE: under the decided NDJSON-substrate direction (rosary-133346), bd-Dolt drops out long-term, which dissolves this divergence — so scope the bd reconciliation as interim, not a deep investment.

## User intent captured (2026-06-23)
"specify the prefix in the cfg, and the default otherwise is the remote name or some shit" — confirmed as the design here.

title: BUG: reconciler hub-to-spoke sync broken after claude -p changes
description:
Symptom: beads filed via `rsry_bead_create` with `repo_path: /Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/rosary` (the hub, per the /note skill instruction) get the `rosary-` prefix and live in rosary's Dolt DB only. They are NOT propagated to per-repo `.beads/` databases via the reconciler.

# Reproduce
```bash
# In this session, filed 8 beads with files: ["notme/foo", "notme.bot/bar", ...]
# via repo_path: ~/remotes/art/rosary. All got rosary-XXX IDs.
# Then:
mcp__rsry__rsry_bead_search repo_path=/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/notme query=<title>
# → 0 results, even though file scope clearly points at notme/.
```

# Root cause (user-reported)
The reconciler is busted due to recent `claude -p` changes. Same bucket as the rsry_dispatch issue earlier this session: when claude-process invocation surface changed, several reconcile/dispatch paths regressed.

# Impact
Hub-and-spoke pattern works for the WRITE (hub gets the bead) but the FAN-OUT to per-repo DBs is broken. Per-repo agents running `rsry_list_beads` in their repo don't see hub-filed beads. Manual workaround in this session: re-file each bead directly in the target repo (so it gets the right `<repo>-XXX` prefix and lives in that repo's `.beads/`).

# Companion bead
**bead: fix /note skill instruction** — the /note skill currently says "Always use repo_path: ~/remotes/art/rosary" which relies on the (now-broken) reconciler. Should pick target repo based on file scopes instead, OR stay hub-centric IF the reconciler is fixed.

# Beads re-filed in this session (workaround record)
- rosary-1b40bd → notme-3dac49 (B.1 lift)
- rosary-1ba58c → notme.bot-3dcb01 (C.1 archive)
- rosary-1bd63c → notme-3dfe15 (C.3 deferred Copilot)
- rosary-272d88 → notme-3e22e0 (Phase 0 deploy)
- rosary-8ae6ab → notme-3e6ecc (CF 10375 bug)
- rosary-8d2c78 → notme-3e9c73 (schema-bridge Go ann)
- rosary-ab33cb → notme-3ec794 (KEK_HELPER schemes)
- rosary-ab2b80 → notme-3ee3b0 (dep sweep tracker)

# Investigation paths
1. Look at rosary's reconcile loop (`src/reconcile/` after the recent refactor) for any claude-process or subprocess invocation that broke
2. Check if `rsry_dispatch`'s breakage and the reconciler share a code path (dispatch worktree was also in rosary's tree pre-this-session, hinting at coupling)
3. Run `rsry_run_once` (if it exists / works) to see what fires

comments.text:
## Diagnosis (2026-05-20) — bead is operationally obsolete, not broken

Investigated the claim that "the reconciler should propagate beads from rosary's Dolt to per-repo `.beads/` based on file scopes, and that propagation is broken." Code evidence says the propagation mechanism this bead presumes **never existed**.

### What the reconciler actually does for cross-repo sync

`src/reconcile/mod.rs:668` — Phase 1.75 "CROSS-REPO SYNC":

```rust
// Phase 1.75: CROSS-REPO SYNC — propagate external refs across repos
let ext_refs = xref::find_external_refs(&beads);
if !ext_refs.is_empty() {
    xref::sync_external_refs(&ext_refs, &self.dolt_clients, &beads).await;
}
```

`src/xref.rs:28` only reads `bead.external_ref` (the `"<target_repo>:<label>"` form). No code path reads `bead.files` to decide where to mirror. The only consumer of `bead.files` in `src/reconcile/` is `verify.rs:636` which copies files onto a dispatch record. **No file-scope fan-out exists in this codebase.**

### Why the bead got filed anyway

The `/note` skill prior to v0.2.0 (companion bead `rosary-406b68`, closed) instructed every agent to file beads via `repo_path: ~/remotes/art/rosary`. Under that instruction the beads landed in rosary's Dolt with `rosary-*` IDs. The user (correctly) noticed those beads never reached the target repos. The bead's premise — "the reconciler used to fan out via file scopes and broke" — was an explanation hypothesis, not a code-grounded claim.

### What's actually true

- The hub-and-spoke + reconciler fan-out model **was aspirational**, never built
- The `/note` skill's old instruction was the bug, not the reconciler
- That instruction got fixed in `rosary-406b68` — `/note` v0.2.0 routes by file scope at write time
- The scope-abstraction saga (`rosary-b5da2f`, closed) made `scope: "repo:notme"` the canonical write-time pattern
- `xref.rs` continues to handle the **real** cross-repo case via `external_ref` (Linear-style mirroring)

### Recommendation

**Close as obsolete.** The behavior the bead asks for is achievable today by writing directly to the target scope, which is now the documented pattern in every skill and tool description. There is no hub-to-spoke fan-out to fix.

### One small follow-up

`skills/note/SKILL.md:22` references this bead by name ("currently broken (`rosary-403a1a`)"). When this closes, that line should be updated to remove the reference (the historical context still makes sense, but pointing at a closed bead is noise). Cleanest one-line change: replace the dependent-clause "currently broken (`rosary-403a1a`)" with "was never built (the hub→spoke fan-out via file scopes was aspirational; see `rosary-403a1a` for the closed history)" — or simpler, just drop the parenthetical and the bead reference entirely.

### Original workaround beads (for reference)

The bead body lists 8 beads that were re-filed in their target repos as the workaround. Under the new model that's the **correct pattern**, not a workaround — so those re-files are good and the rosary-side originals can be closed (they're duplicates of the target-repo copies).

comments.text:
## Closing as obsolete (2026-05-20)

Investigation summary (full evidence in the prior comment): the reconciler fan-out mechanism this bead asked us to fix **was never built**. `xref.rs` only mirrors via `external_ref`; no code path reads `bead.files` to fan beads across repos.

The companion fix shipped via `rosary-406b68` (`/note` skill routes by file scope at write time), and `rosary-b5da2f` (scope abstraction) made `scope: "repo:<target>"` the canonical write-time pattern. Together they obviated the need for the fan-out.

Stale-reference cleanup landed in PR #219 — updates `skills/note/SKILL.md:22` and the `tests/note_skill_routing.rs` docstrings to point at this bead as closed-history rather than open-bug.

If a file-scope-based fan-out feature is ever genuinely wanted, it should be a new bead with its own ADR — the design conflicts with the scope-abstraction model and would create a "two copies of one bead" drift class.

title: Content-addressed agent-context substrate: centralize hashing on LLO, unify mache derivations into a branch-addressable granular cache
description:
PROBLEM STATEMENT (grounded in a 4-repo read: ley-line-open, mache, sheaf, rosary).

Recurring pain: agents re-derive repo knowledge (re-read large files, recompute impact/architecture per call), can't resume warm/deterministically, and can't cheaply 'check the right places' (e.g. a promoted taskfile with a swallowed error). Root cause across three layers:

1. DERIVER (mache): the queryable projection is a MUTABLE SQLite .db rebuilt WHOLESALE at 'mache build'; impact/architecture/communities are recomputed on every query, NOT memoized. Content-addressing (BLAKE3 chunks, FsBlobStore-shaped, LLO cache.capnp lockfile) exists only in the opt-in 'mache cache push/pull' export; granular sheaf-δ⁰ incrementality exists only on the serve-time live-dir backend (frozen .db has a nil invalidator). The unified content-addressed granular derivation store is mache's stated Phase-4, not built.

2. SUBSTRATE (LLO): the primitives EXIST — leyline-core::{Hash, ContentAddressed::hash (BLAKE3-locked), BlobStore/FsBlobStore (verify-on-read; no GC)}, leyline-vcs (jj sidecar = working reversibility; RootPointer/RootSigner are stubs), leyline-sheaf::SheafCache (region-granular on_change cascade; heuristic invalidation, δ⁰ opt-in). Severed links: no watcher→daemon in mache's default deployment (so the incremental cache never fires), no branch-addressable 'sheaf over branch X' composed-view query, sheaf not wired to the CAS blob store. NOTE: sheaf-core (Python) is an unrelated ML-topology lib — red herring.

3. ORCHESTRATOR (rosary): pulls in ONLY leyline-vcs (for jj-init; even snapshot() shells to jj CLI) and hand-rolls its ENTIRE hashing/CAS/attestation surface with its own blake3+sha2, despite LLO exposing exactly ContentAddressed + leyline-sign. Reinvention sites: src/cas.rs:17 content_hash (== leyline-core ContentAddressed::hash), src/skills.rs:44 inline blake3 (bypasses even cas.rs — a local bug), src/handoff.rs:136 sha256 merkle chain, src/dsse.rs sha256 attestation (leyline-sign ships CMS/cert/attestation), src/observation/mod.rs:350 payload_hash (bespoke canonical 'ph1\x1f...' string → blake3; keep the canonicalization, swap the inner hash).

DESIRED: an agent's context = a content-addressed derivation manifest — mache derives, LLO's CAS stores content-addressed, leyline-sheaf caches granularly. Then the four properties fall out for free: (a) unchanged content = cache hit (no re-read/re-derive), (b) only changed slices re-derive, (c) N agents dedup one copy, (d) deterministic warm resume = rehydrate from addresses. 'Get lay of the land' = materialize-or-cache-hit the manifest; downstream phases read the map + do targeted find_definition, never re-read whole files.

KEY INSIGHT: centralizing rosary's hashing on leyline-core is NOT just hygiene — it's the PREREQUISITE for the substrate to compose. A bead's content-address and a mache derivation's must be the SAME address or the manifests can't share the CAS. Both are BLAKE3-256 today (byte-compatible) but rosary should USE the locked primitive so it can't drift — leyline-cas-ffi exists precisely because cloister drifted off the lock.

FALLS OUT: once (rosary speaks LLO's Hash) + (a branch-addressable derivation manifest) exist, the PR-review flow, warm resume, and context-pruning all become reads over the manifest.

DECOMPOSE INTO (candidate slices, cross-repo):
- rosary: depend on leyline-core; collapse src/cas.rs + skills.rs inline blake3 onto ContentAddressed::hash (the foundation).
- mache: wire watcher→daemon in the default deployment so the incremental cache fires; memoize impact/architecture by graph version.
- llo/mache: a branch-addressable composed-view query ('sheaf over branch X').
- rosary: pin the derivation manifest on the bead/workspace + carry via handoff for warm resume.

Close condition: an ADR + dispatchable per-repo beads exist; the rosary→leyline-core hashing centralization is the first landed slice.

title: thread_assign clobbers an existing thread's decade_id (resets to 'ungrouped')
description:
tool_thread_assign (src/serve/handlers.rs) unconditionally upserts the thread with decade_id = args.decade_id OR "ungrouped". When a bead is assigned to an ALREADY-EXISTING thread without re-passing decade_id (the normal flow: thread_create then thread_assign), it CLOBBERS the thread's decade_id to "ungrouped".

Symptom (hit by the mache session): rsry_thread_create(decade_id="mache-pure-go-arena") then rsry_thread_assign(thread_id, bead, repo) → the thread row's decade_id flips to "ungrouped". rsry_thread_list(decade_id="mache-pure-go-arena") returns {count:0} (forward read filters by the now-wrong decade_id), while find_thread_for_bead works (reverse index is keyed by thread_id, unaffected). Confirmed in ~/.rsry/backend.db: threads mache-pure-go-arena/* have decade_id='ungrouped'.

Not a stale read — a write clobber. thread_assign should assign a BEAD, never redefine the thread.

## Fix
- Add get_thread(id) -> Option<ThreadRecord> to HierarchyStore (store.rs) + impls (InMemoryStore, SqliteBackend, DoltBackend).
- tool_thread_assign: only create the thread (auto-create decade + upsert_thread) when get_thread(thread_id) is None; if it exists, skip straight to add_bead_to_thread. Preserves the existing decade_id/name.

## Acceptance criteria
- Handler test (InMemoryStore): create thread under decade X, thread_assign a bead WITHOUT decade_id, assert list_threads(X) still contains the thread AND list_threads("ungrouped") does not. RED on current code, GREEN after fix.
- cargo test --bin rsry green.

## Inputs
- src/serve/handlers.rs tool_thread_assign (the unwrap_or("ungrouped") + upsert_thread)
- src/store.rs HierarchyStore trait + InMemoryStore
- src/store_sqlite.rs upsert_thread (~321), src/store_dolt.rs list_threads (~359, mirror the SELECT for get_thread)

title: HTTP sessions accumulate unbounded — no eviction or TTL
description:
Sessions created on `initialize` (mod.rs:438) are stored in `HashSet<String>` but only removed on explicit `DELETE /mcp`. If MCP clients disconnect without sending DELETE, sessions accumulate forever.

**Prod failure scenario**: Long-running `rsry serve --transport http` gradually consumes memory as orphaned sessions pile up in the HashSet.

**Suggested fix**: Add a TTL-based eviction (e.g., store `(session_id, Instant)` and sweep expired sessions periodically, or use a bounded LRU cache). A 1-hour TTL with periodic sweep would prevent unbounded growth while being generous to long sessions.

**Citation**: `src/serve/mod.rs:438` (session insert), `src/serve/mod.rs:519` (HashSet construction)

comments.text: Shipped in PR #266. MCP sessions now HashMap<String,Instant> with last-activity touch + TTL sweep (1h) on new-session insert; orphaned sessions reclaimed. Close condition met: cargo test --bin rsry serve:: (sweep_expired_drops_only_idle_sessions).

title: Origin validation uses prefix match — vulnerable to DNS rebinding
description:
`validate_origin()` uses `o.starts_with("http://localhost")` which also matches `http://localhost.evil.com`. An attacker could register a domain like `localhost.attacker.com` to bypass the origin check.

**Prod failure scenario**: DNS rebinding attack where a crafted domain passes the origin check, allowing cross-origin requests to the MCP server.

**Suggested fix**: Parse the Origin as a URL and check the host component exactly, or append a delimiter to the prefix check (e.g., check for `http://localhost:` or `http://localhost/` rather than bare prefix).

**Citation**: `src/serve/mod.rs:281-287`

comments.text: Shipped in PR #265. validate_origin now pins the Origin host exactly via origin_matches (exact / :port / /path only); localhost.evil.com-style rebinding rejected. Close condition met: cargo test --bin rsry validate_origin (5/5, incl. validate_origin_rejects_localhost_prefix_dns_rebind).

title: Phase 2: verify undercut proof + close authority-inversion (signet)
description:
Phase-1 (ADR-0011, PR #227) ships undercut as proof-TRUSTED: AuthoritativeClaim.undercuts carries a bare payload_hash and nothing verifies the proof. Consequence (math-friend review): an authenticated low-tier claim can defeat a higher-tier one (e.g. AutoIngest nukes HumanCorrection) by simply naming its hash — an authority-inversion. The gate authenticates the ASSERTER, not the undercut JUSTIFICATION.

Close it: an undercut must carry a verifiable proof (signet-signed reference to the contradicting evidence), and resolve_by_authority must verify that proof before honoring the undercut. Until verified, an undercut is ignored (fail-closed) so a bare-hash claim cannot defeat anything.

Optional secondary (lower urgency, same review): single-round undercut has no reinstatement (a defeated defeater does not revive its target) and mutual undercut removes both. If real argumentation semantics are needed, evolve to a grounded-extension fixpoint (Nute/Dung). Decide whether that's in scope or a documented non-goal.

## Acceptance criteria
- undercut carries a proof token; resolve_by_authority verifies it (signet) before dropping the target; unverified undercut is ignored.
- Test: an authenticated AutoIngest with an UNVERIFIED undercut of a HumanCorrection does NOT defeat it (authority-inversion closed); a verified undercut still defeats.
- cargo test --bin rsry green.

## Inputs
- src/observation/resolve.rs (AuthoritativeClaim.undercuts, the undercut set construction)
- signet proof/cert verification path (quarantine.rs cert validation, Phase 2 wiring)
- docs/adr/0011-decision-of-record.md §Known limitations

Depends on signet Phase-2 cert/proof verification being wired (quarantine stub → real). Decade: decision-of-record / claim-model.

title: EPIC: Constraint-Driven Design — σ scoping vector + scope-level discipline + HDC enrichment
description:
## Status

Design doc exists at `~/rosary-cdd-design-2026-05-18.md` (separate machine — not in repo). ~4500 words. This bead anchors the framework so it doesn't get lost; phase beads (filed as children) match the author's own "staged validation" rollout.

## Framework summary

Work unit `W = (id, F, C, π, X)`. Scoping vector `σ(W) = (α, β, γ, δ)`:

- **α** — constraint independence (WCC of constraint dep-graph, normalized)
- **β** — first-attempt verification probability (Bayesian-shrunk binned estimator + optional HDC k-NN)
- **γ** — cognitive width (WCC of file-side projection of bipartite constraint-file graph)
- **δ** — scope drift (commits touching files outside F(W), post-hoc)

Constraint scope levels (`file | bead | parent | repo`) gate which constraints enter α/γ. Without tiering, repo-wide constraints (golden rules, integration tests) collapse α → 1/|C| and destroy the signal — tiering is a correctness requirement, not an optimization.

Original blog framing was iff (constraints compose ↔ well-scoped). Corrected to one-directional + probabilistic: `well-scoped + project-level-constraints-at-parent → composition` with high probability. Monolithic-passing-CI is a false-positive of the converse.

## Critical observations (design-review pushback)

These are concrete concerns where the design as drafted weakens. Fold into doc revision or acknowledge as known-deferred:

1. **β has three estimators** (binned, Bayesian shrinkage, HDC k-NN). Shipping all three creates a tuning trap. Recommendation: pick Bayesian shrinkage (κ=10) for shipping; mark HDC variant as "research path, post-validation"; drop bare binned. Three estimators in the design doc reads as ambivalence.

2. **`γ ≥ 7` anchored on Miller (1956) is a weak rigor signal.** Miller's chunk number is for unrelated-item short-term memory. Code reviewers chunk hierarchically (functions → files → modules) — different cognitive task. Keep the threshold but downgrade Miller to "inspiration"; defend on empirical re-decomposition data once available.

3. **`α < 0.5` lacks the empirical defense the other thresholds have.** "Majority entangled" is a population statistic, not a quality claim. Need to check: if 80% of well-scoped historical beads have α < 0.5, the threshold is broken. Mitigation: in phase 2 (validation observability), report the α-distribution across closed beads before flagging.

4. **"Constraints inspect files" excludes valid non-file constraints** — "PR description references bead ID," "CI must run on Ubuntu 24.04," "merge requires CODEOWNERS approval." These have empty supp() under the file-based extractors; §2 says that's a load-time error. The design's framing is *implementation-relevant constraints only*, which is fine, but should be stated explicitly so consumers don't model the wrong thing.

5. **HDC ingestion assumes an ML embedding model exists.** §3.2 ingests `e_atom ∈ R^N` via orthogonal projection. For a fresh repo without a pre-trained code embedding (CodeBERT, etc.), the HDC path is bootstrap-blocked. §3.4 synthetic-bead cold-start still needs embeddings. Either declare a default embedding (e.g., pin a frozen CodeBERT release) or acknowledge HDC requires upstream model selection as a prereq.

6. **Feedback loop is one sentence.** "Human catch → rosary bead → skill update" — the concrete questions (who promotes a catch, what's the constraint template format for new rules, manual vs auto-generated skill PR, what prevents skill bloat) are not answered. §6 meta-rules cover rot/decay but not promotion. This is the loop-closing piece — without it the framework is open-loop. File as its own phase bead.

7. **β-quartile cutoff is nested-quartile.** "Below 25th percentile of its size class" — but size_class is itself a quartile bin (§1.2). So β-flag = "bottom of the bottom quarter by structural similarity." Reasonable but should be acknowledged; double-quartiling can produce small populations per bucket.

8. **σ updates over bead lifecycle are undefined.** σ is computed at planning time but treated as static. If F(W) grows mid-execution (δ > 0), does σ get recomputed? When, what triggers it? Without an answer, planning-time σ becomes irrelevant for in-flight work.

9. **200-bead minimum for validation = ~3 months calendar.** Bind explicitly: "first 3 months, σ runs in observe-only mode, no flagging in UI." Without that, users will hit the framework before validation correlations are informative and discount it.

10. **Meta-σ is heuristic, not graph-rigorous.** Base σ has a precise definition (bipartite graph, WCC). Meta-rules like "capture-too-much" detect via regex `\s+and\s+|\s+plus\s+|;` — that's brittle and not σ-shaped. Either tighten meta-σ to a graph form (which rule.requires-files form supp()?) or call it out: "meta layer is heuristic, not σ-rigorous."

11. **γ-as-cognitive-load is admitted-proxy** (the "what σ doesn't measure" section, item 6). This weakens falsifiability of γ ≥ 7: if the threshold doesn't predict re-decomposition rate, is the threshold wrong, or is γ-as-cognitive-proxy wrong? Two separable hypotheses, one falsification — the doc treats them as conjoined.

## Children (filed separately)

Phase 1: σ schema extension (`scope_level` + `support_extractor` columns)
Phase 2: Validation observability (compute σ on closed beads, no flagging, 3-month observe window)
Phase 3: Split-flagging UI + mache smell-rules layer integration
Phase 4: HDC substrate via ley-line-open (feature-flagged, post-validation)
Side: Feedback loop design (currently the one-sentence gap)

## Net author's stance (from session)

"Pitch the σ extension + validation observability first. Earn the rest with data." The full design is a north star; ship in slices that produce evidence.

title: Parallel subagents step on each other: branch switches + stash-pops in shared worktree
description:
## Problem
While dispatching the substrate-IDL cloister leaves (L1, L4, L6, L7) in parallel via Claude Code `Agent` tool subagents (workaround because rsry_dispatch is broken — `rosary-a53b91`), a real worker-coordination failure occurred:

- All 4 subagents were instructed to work on branch `chore/substrate-idl-cloister`
- L1's subagent (working in tools/schema-bridge/) had ~860 lines of uncommitted WIP
- Mid-session, a parallel L7 subagent (working in cloister-spec/credential-isolation/v1/test-vectors/) **switched the worktree off the branch to main** and ran `git stash pop`
- L1's WIP applied to main instead of the feature branch, then was lost when L7 finished and the branch state changed underneath L1
- L1's subagent recovered the WIP via `git fsck --lost-found` from a dangling stash (sha `5119a3fe`) and re-applied to the correct branch

This worked out by luck. It could just as easily have ended with permanently-lost work, or worse — silently-incorrect commits on the wrong branch.

## Root cause
Parallel agents share a single working tree (the same `cloister/` checkout on disk). Git's branch state is process-global, not agent-local. When two agents both attempt branch operations (checkout, stash pop), the last one wins for everyone.

## Acceptance criteria
- A documented model for parallel-subagent execution that prevents branch-state races
- Either:
  (a) Each parallel agent gets its own worktree via `git worktree add` (rosary already has `src/workspace.rs` for this — leverage), and the orchestrator merges results when agents return
  (b) Parallel agents are forbidden from branch operations (only edit files; never `git checkout`/`git stash`); orchestrator owns all git state transitions
  (c) Hybrid: agents work in same tree but git commands are serialized via a process-level lock
- Acceptance test: dispatch 4 mock parallel agents that all modify different files and verify no race condition can lose work

## Inputs
- `src/workspace.rs` (existing worktree creation; underleveraged by current parallel-dispatch workaround)
- `src/dispatch/mod.rs` (dispatch entry — should enforce isolation)
- `src/dispatch/providers.rs` (Claude provider impl; needs to receive worktree path as env)
- `docs/adr/0004` (dual state machine) — workspace isolation is part of the dispatch contract

## Output shape
Either: a new ADR (substrate-IDL ADR? cloister-2f021f-adjacent? rosary docs/adr/?) committing to one of (a)/(b)/(c) above, OR a working impl of the chosen model with integration test. Net diff <500 lines if impl-only.

## Scope boundary
Parallel-subagent coordination only. The broader "rsry_dispatch is broken" problem (`rosary-a53b91`) is upstream — this bead is "even if dispatch ships, parallel dispatch needs isolation."

## Failure mode
A test dispatching 4 mock agents that each modify a different file + run `git status` returns a mixed/lost set of changes.

## Time-box
M (worktree-per-agent is the architecturally-right answer; could be S if (b) is acceptable as policy)

## Why this matters
Today's "workaround" for rsry_dispatch being broken is to use Claude Code's `Agent` tool with `general-purpose` subagents. They share a working tree. When rsry_dispatch eventually returns to service (via `rosary-a53b91` fix), the same coordination issue will recur unless the dispatch contract enforces worktree isolation.

## Workaround in use today
Hope. (The L1/L7 recovery used `git fsck --lost-found` — not a strategy that scales.)

## Related
- `rosary-a53b91` — rsry_dispatch broken (the upstream issue this is downstream of)
- `rosary-98ee93` — cross-repo bead_link rejection (different but adjacent multi-repo coordination gap)
- Real incident: L1 dispatch in cloister PR #46 (commit `1346b3b`) — see commit message for the recovery footnote
- Substrate-IDL L1: `cloister-946a59`

title: CDD Phase 1: σ schema extension — constraint.scope_level + constraint.support_extractor
description:
## Scope

Minimal schema additions. No behavior change, no UI, no flagging. Foundation for phases 2-4.

```
constraint.scope_level ∈ {file, bead, parent, repo, unknown}
constraint.support_extractor : named extraction rule (one of 9 documented)
```

9 named extractors from the design doc Part 2 table. `unknown` is the fail-loudly default — refuse σ computation rather than silently defaulting `supp(c) = F(W)` (which collapses α and γ).

## Acceptance

- Schema migration adds the two columns to whatever constraint-template store rosary uses (TBD: per ADR-0006 declarative tool registry / existing `store_dolt.rs::constraints` if it exists)
- Migration is reversible — column drops cleanly if rolled back
- The 9 extractors are implemented as a closed enum + dispatch (`file_local`, `package_local`, `bead_scope`, `coverage_intersect`, `same_package_with_test`, `lint_rule_local`, `explicit`, `parent_scope`, `repo_global`)
- Coverage-intersect auto-promotion rule (test spans >50% of F(W) → bead-scope) implemented; without it integration tests falsely inflate α
- Empty-supp() loads as `scope_level=unknown` and produces a load-time error, not a silent no-op

title: Wire ComputeProvider into dispatch: 3-axis spawn (agent + compute + sandbox)
description:
## Problem

dispatch::spawn() conflates three orthogonal axes:
- Agent (which brain): AgentProvider trait — Claude, Gemini, ACP
- Compute (where it runs): ComputeProvider trait — exists but NOT wired into dispatch
- Sandbox (what it can access): missing entirely

Current: ClaudeProvider.spawn_agent() = Claude + local + no sandbox. Can't mix.

## Design

dispatch::spawn() takes all three independently:

```rust
pub async fn spawn(
    bead: &Bead,
    agent: &dyn AgentProvider,
    compute: &dyn ComputeProvider,
    sandbox: Option<&dyn SandboxProvider>,
) -> Result<AgentHandle>
```

Composition examples:
- Claude + LocalCompute + None = current behavior (subprocess)
- Claude + DockerCompute + NonoSandbox = containerized + kernel-enforced scopes
- Qwen + DockerCompute + None = self-hosted model in container

API-backed agents (Claude/Gemini) are thin CLI clients — compute is lightweight.
Self-hosted agents (Qwen/Llama) need actual compute — provider fails if no model server.

## Implementation

1. DockerProvider: ComputeProvider impl using `docker run` with the rig Dockerfile as base
2. Refactor dispatch::spawn() to accept ComputeProvider (currently hardcoded to local subprocess)
3. SandboxProvider trait placeholder (nono integration follows)
4. Config: `[compute] backend = "docker"` selects DockerProvider
5. E2e test: dispatch a bead to local Docker, pipeline progresses through phases

## Depends on

- rosary-fafb7c (pipeline progression — must work before we can test through containers)

title: CDD Phase 2: σ validation observability — compute on closed beads, log only, no flagging
description:
## Scope

Compute `σ(W) = (α, β, γ, δ)` on every closed bead. Log to a sidecar table. **No flagging, no UI changes, no behavior change.** Pure observability for ~3 months of accumulation before deciding to flag.

## Why observability-first

Per CDD design doc §5 and author's own staged plan: validation requires ≥50 closed beads per size class (4 size classes ⇒ 200-bead minimum) before any of the 3 correlations are informative. On a healthy repo that's ~3 months of work. Flagging earlier surfaces noise as signal.

## Acceptance

- σ computed on closed-bead transitions (no recompute on in-flight beads — see EPIC observation #8)
- Sidecar table records `(bead_id, alpha, beta, gamma, delta, n_constraints, n_files, n_retries, computed_at)`
- β uses **Bayesian shrinkage estimator only** (κ=10), with leave-one-out discipline (exclude bead_i when computing β(bead_i)) — see EPIC observation #1
- Three correlations are computable after 4 weeks but not asserted: retry-rate by α-quartile, re-decomposition rate by γ-quartile, scope-drift δ as ground truth
- A small CLI reporter (`rsry sigma-report`) prints distributions across the closed-bead corpus so the user can eyeball whether the math looks sane before phase 3

## Falsification stance

Per design doc §5: if retry rate is flat in α, re-decomposition uncorrelated with γ, scope-drift uncorrelated with planning-time σ, the formalization is wrong. **Discard rather than tune.** Phase 3 is contingent on at least directionally-present correlations.

## Pre-condition

CDD Phase 1 (schema extension) shipped + constraint templates have `scope_level` populated.

## Parent

CDD EPIC.

title: Capture agent stdout to workspace log — stop discarding structured output
description:
## Problem

dispatch.rs sets `stdout(Stdio::null())` for all providers (Claude, Gemini, ACP). The `--output-format json` flag produces structured JSON with every tool call, result, token count, and completion reason. We throw it all away.

This means:
- No side-channel for orchestrator to observe agent progress
- No way to inject context mid-flight (fix-forward pattern)
- No post-mortem analysis of failed agents
- rsry_active shows null for last_activity because agents can't report

## Fix

1. Capture stdout to a file in the workspace: `{work_dir}/.rsry-agent.jsonl`
2. The orchestrator (conductor or human) can tail this file for live progress
3. On completion, the log persists for post-mortem
4. On cleanup, it's archived or deleted with the workspace

For the conductor path (Elixir), the Port already captures stdout — this is about the Rust ClaudeProvider/GeminiProvider path.

## Fix-forward channel

ley-line's candle pattern: a cooperative file the agent checks. Write `{work_dir}/.rsry-interrupt.json` with context/instructions. The agent's system prompt tells it to check this file periodically. Not as clean as ACP's resume(), but works for CLI dispatch.

## Related

- rosary-2cfbd3 (observability — last_activity tracking)
- ley-line candle pattern for cooperative interruption
- Conductor AcpClient.resume() already does injection for ACP mode

title: CDD Phase 3: split-flagging UI + mache smell-rules layer integration
description:
## Scope

Gated on Phase 2 validation correlations appearing directionally. If they do, expand σ from observability → active flagging in the planning UI, AND integrate the deterministic middle layer (mache smell rules) into the review pipeline.

## Two sub-acceptance criteria

### 3a. σ-based split flagging

- Soft surface (2-of-4 σ flags): bead appears in a dashboard for human glance
- Hard recommend (3-of-4): planning UI actively recommends split before dispatch
- Thresholds tunable per-repo: α<0.5, γ≥7, β<25th-percentile-of-size-class, δ>0.3 (post-hoc only)
- Default values per design doc §1.3; re-fit per-repo once ≥50 closed beads per size class

### 3b. Mache smell-rules wiring

Mache's smell-rules infrastructure already exists (`MACHE_SMELL_RULES_DIR`, JSON rule format with `Requires` + `ScopeColumn` + `Query`, verified at `~/remotes/art/mache/cmd/serve_find_smells*.go`). This bead wires the existing surface into rosary's review pipeline as the deterministic middle layer between linter and AI pass.

- Document the JSON rule contract for rosary-side authors
- Define rosary→mache invocation point (likely `pipeline.verify` plugin hook, per existing patterns)
- Define how smell-rule findings flow back to beads (bead comment? annotated diff? deferred?)
- Auto-promotion semantics: which mache rules are repo-global vs bead-scoped (intersects CDD §1.1 tiering)

## Out of scope

- AI-pass design (downstream of phase 3, separate bead)
- Feedback-loop UX (separate bead, currently the one-sentence gap)

## Risk

The "what should the UI do at 2/4 vs 3/4" question is product, not architecture. Without empirical data from Phase 2, the UX risks being either too noisy (false-positive flags) or too quiet (missed splits). Stage 3 should ship behind a feature flag, off-by-default, until ≥1 repo's σ correlations are validated.

## Parent

CDD EPIC.

title: CDD Phase 4: HDC substrate integration via ley-line-open (feature-flagged, post-validation)
description:
## Scope

Feature-flagged HDC substrate consumption via ley-line-open. Replaces β's binned estimator with k-NN over closed-bead hypervectors, and powers decomposition similarity at planning time.

## Substrate

Per CDD design doc §3.1: binary spatter codes (d=10000), XOR binding, majority bundling, cyclic permutation. ML-embedding ingestion via orthogonal projection (`V_atom = sign(O · e_atom)`).

## Pre-conditions

1. CDD Phase 2 validation correlations directionally present (don't build on unvalidated math)
2. ley-line-open exposes the HDC substrate ops (XOR bind, majority bundle, permute, sim) — check upstream status
3. **An embedding model is selected.** Per EPIC observation #5: §3.2 assumes `e_atom ∈ R^N` is available. For a fresh repo without a frozen pre-trained code embedding (CodeBERT, etc.), the path is bootstrap-blocked. This bead must specify which model + version pin before implementation.

## Acceptance

- Feature flag `hdc-decompose` gates the entire path; default off
- `dictionary_version` + delta-chain reconciliation per design §3.3 (rename = preserve identity)
- Cold-start backfill from closed issues + merged PRs as synthetic beads (design §3.4); backfilled β tagged `provenance=synthetic` and re-evaluated against native data once enough native beads accumulate
- β_HDC estimator replaces β_bin for beads where similarity threshold is met; otherwise falls back to Bayesian-shrunk binned
- Atomic identity uses `package_import_path + symbol_name`, not file paths (monorepo concern, §3.3)

## Why this is last

Per author's staged plan: "HDC, taste schema, decomposition front-end come after the base validates. Each is a substantial lift; don't build them on top of an unvalidated foundation."

## Parent

CDD EPIC.

title: Architecture: CRDT-lattice bead state — immutable observations, derived status, venturi pattern
description:
## Problem

Bead status is a mutable cell (open → dispatched → pr_open → done). This breaks content-addressing (cascade invalidation), makes crash recovery fragile (in-memory BeadTracker diverges from persistent PipelineState), and prevents safe concurrent agent work.

## Insight (from venturi)

venturi solves the same problem for CVE state across multiple data sources. The pattern:

1. **Never store mutable state** — only immutable observations from agents
2. **Derive status via lattice join** — merge function is pure, commutative, associative, idempotent
3. **Represent transitions structurally** — tree diff on by-status/ index, not cell mutations
4. **Content-address the input** — hash the immutable BeadSpec, not the mutable status

## Design

### Observations table (append-only, immutable)

```sql
CREATE TABLE observations (
  bead_id TEXT,
  agent TEXT,           -- 'scoping-agent', 'dev-agent', etc.
  phase INT,
  verdict TEXT,         -- 'pass', 'fail', 'retry', 'deadletter'
  content_hash TEXT,    -- hash of the observation content
  created_at DATETIME,
  PRIMARY KEY (bead_id, agent, phase, created_at)
);
```

Each agent run appends an observation. Nothing is ever mutated.

### Status lattice (derived, not stored)

```
backlog < open < queued < dispatched < verifying < pr_open < done
                                                           < blocked (deadletter)
```

Bead status = max(lattice) across all observations for that bead. Computed, not stored. If you need to query 'all open beads', materialize a by-status/ index (like venturi's by-state/).

### Content-addressed BeadSpec (immutable definition)

```rust
impl BeadSpec {
    fn content_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
        SHA256(title || description || issue_type || priority || success_criteria)
    }
}
```

The bead definition never changes. Status is derived from observations.

### Handoff hash chain (append-only)

Each handoff includes the previous handoff's hash:
```
HandoffHash = SHA256(phase || agent || bead_spec_hash || previous_handoff_hash || verdict)
```

Pipeline integrity falls out: any gap or tampering is detectable.

## What this replaces

- `BeadTracker` (in-memory mutable state) → observation query
- `persist_status()` (cell mutation) → append observation
- `recover_stuck_beads()` (reset mutable state) → recompute from observations
- `PipelineState` retries/phase (mutable counters) → count from observation history

## Migration path

0. Add content_hash() to BeadSpec + Handoff (no behavior change)
1. Add observations table alongside existing issues table
2. on_pass/on_fail append observations instead of mutating status
3. Status queries read from materialized by-status/ index
4. Remove BeadTracker, derive from observations
5. Remove persist_status cell mutations

## Prior art

- venturi: CRDT lattice merge across NVD/GitHub/Alpine sources (merge.go)
- Dolt: cell-level merge on prolly trees (same domain, different approach)
- jj: content-addressed change IDs (already used for code)
- tropo: sheaf validation of structural invariants (coboundary = hash disagreement)

## Properties that fall out

- **Crash recovery**: recompute status from observations. No in-memory state to lose.
- **Concurrent agents**: observations are independent. Lattice merge is commutative.
- **Audit trail**: full history of every agent verdict, timestamped, append-only.
- **Federation**: push observations (immutable), receiver derives status locally.
- **Dedup**: content_hash on BeadSpec catches duplicate work definitions.

comments.text:
Steps 0-3 complete and merged:
- PR #94: content_hash() on BeadSpec + chain_hash() on Handoff
- PR #95: observations table, migration 002, Verdict lattice, reconciler dual-write, 13 consistency tests

The foundation is in place. Observations are appended at every pipeline decision point (dispatch, pass, fail, deadletter, terminal). Lattice-derived status is proven consistent with persist_status for all pipeline scenarios.

Remaining for full cutover:
- Step 4: run observations alongside cells in production, validate with derive_status()
- Step 5: replace persist_status with lattice-only (remove mutable cells)
- Step 6: eliminate BeadTracker, derive from observations

Steps 4-6 are incremental and can happen over multiple sessions.

comments.text:
Provenance decomposition (docs/problems/rosary-capture-commit-spine.md) surfaces L4: structured authorship (actor + kind:human|agent + session_id + observer), which rosary lacks — Bead.created_by is git user.name only, vs lectio's author/observer/ingester triad. This is the genuinely-missing piece NOT covered by the done bead rosary-541001 (which is source provenance / derived_from, not authorship identity).

Reconciliation question for THIS bead: authorship almost certainly belongs as an observation field in the lattice (src/observation/*), not a new mutable Bead column — consistent with this bead's "never store mutable state, only immutable observations" thesis. So L4 should land as an observation-substrate addition once 45518d's direction settles, not as a Bead schema change. Flagging so the two don't diverge.

comments.text: Cross-ref: new decade `decision-of-record` formalizes the adjudication layer this bead's lattice needs. 45518d makes bead state immutable-observations + derived-status (MVCC versions a contradiction); it does NOT decide *which* contradicting claim is current. That decision rule — speech-act typing (observation|correction|decision|supersession) + author-of-claim + bitemporal supersession (Graphiti-style edge invalidation) — is being designed in rosary-1915e0 (decision-of-record/claim-model). The authorship input is rosary-197eb0 (supersedes the L4 note I left here earlier). Net: 45518d is the substrate; decision-of-record is the arbitration on top of it.

comments.text: venturi grounds this bead. Read internal/store/merge.go: MergeSource is a pure CRDT join-semilattice (commutative/associative/idempotent) — state = max over a total order (reserved<...<fixed<rejected), severity = max-register, fix = OR-set — over 14 sources / 392K CVEs, detecting 53K state conflicts. ConflictInfo() surfaces per-source witnesses; smelt/validate/fixconf.go adds an entropy disagreement signal; genuine disagreement is escalated to HUMAN review (not auto-resolved). This is the mature, at-scale realization of exactly this bead's "immutable observations → derived status via lattice join" thesis — and it confirms the detect/resolve split: venturi DETECTS + resolves by a FIXED DOMAIN ORDER (works because vuln-state has natural monotonic certainty). General bead/claim state has NO natural order → needs authenticated-authority resolution. That auth-resolution layer is designed in rosary-1915e0 (Decision-of-Record), built ON this CRDT detection substrate. venturi's "escalate high-entropy to human" is the seed of auth-as-arbiter.

title: Rename auto-discovered decade + auto/ thread prefix → backlog/
description:
## Problem

The auto-clustering code in `src/reconcile/threading.rs` writes thread IDs as `auto/{bead1}-{bead2}` and parents them under a decade called `auto-discovered`. Both names are bad:

- `auto/` reads like "automatic, generated, ignore" — a dead-letter bin
- `auto-discovered` is even worse as a decade name

What it actually IS is a backlog: clusters of beads the system noticed share a scope but a human (or an agent) hasn't yet decided what to do with them.

## Fix

In `src/reconcile/threading.rs`:
- Change the auto-thread codegen prefix from `auto/` → `backlog/`
- Update the decade upsert from `id: "auto-discovered"` → `id: "backlog"` (with title "Backlog: auto-clustered beads awaiting triage")

Migrate existing data: rename the `auto-discovered` decade to `backlog`, and rename existing `auto/*` thread IDs in place (just change decade_id reference + thread.id prefix).

## Files
- `src/reconcile/threading.rs` — codegen prefix + decade name
- A migration: probably a one-shot SQL run or a `rsry migrate` step

## Tests
- New `auto-clustered threads use backlog/ prefix` test
- Existing thread tests should pick up the rename

## Why this is its own bead
Naming churn ripples through downstream tooling that filters by `auto/` (e.g. workspace_ops feature-PR assembly). Doing it as a clean unit makes the diff reviewable.

## Related
- rosary-XXXXX (agent-driven cluster triage) — once renamed, the triage agent operates on `backlog/` prefix.

title: CDD Side: feedback loop design — human catch → rosary bead → skill update (currently one sentence)
description:
## Gap

CDD design doc §4.2 describes the feedback loop in one sentence. Concrete questions are unanswered:

1. **Who promotes a catch?** Reviewer leaves a comment — does it auto-become a bead, or require explicit promotion (`/promote` slash command, etc.)?
2. **What's the constraint template format for new rules?** A reviewer's prose comment isn't a runnable predicate. Who translates "this thing should never happen" into a `support_extractor` + `scope_level` + actual query/predicate? Manual? LLM-assisted with human approval?
3. **Skill update mechanism.** Auto-generated PR against the skill repo? Manual edit? Versioning?
4. **What prevents skill bloat?** Without a "dead rule" pruning loop, the skill grows monotonically. CDD §6 meta-rules cover rot/decay (`no_decay_signal`: archive rules unused in N PRs) but only address pruning, not promotion gating.
5. **Provenance.** Each rule needs a citation (CDD §6 meta-rule `no_provenance`). What format? PR link? ADR? Bead ID?

## Why this is a side-bead, not a phase

The full feedback loop is the loop-closing piece — without it the framework is open-loop. But it depends on Phase 3 (smell-rules wired) being live AND on AI-pass design existing — neither of which is current scope. File as a tracked side-concern so the gap doesn't get lost.

## Pre-conditions

- Phase 3 shipped (smell rules wired)
- AI-pass design exists (separate ADR / design bead, not yet filed)
- At least one full "human caught X, X is now a rule, next PR catches X" cycle has happened manually so the actual UX is grounded in observed behavior, not speculated

## Parent

CDD EPIC.

title: Triage-agent: agent-driven promotion/demotion of backlog clusters
description:
## Problem

Auto-clustering (`src/reconcile/threading.rs::auto_thread`) finds shared-scope or sequential bead clusters and parks them under `auto-discovered` (will be renamed to `backlog` per sibling bead) with placeholder names like "SharedScope cluster". Today, **a human has to decide** whether each cluster is:

- a real grouping that deserves a meaningful name + parent decade
- noise (file overlap that doesn't reflect real semantic relation)
- premature (cluster will become real later when more beads land)

That's the wrong loop. The user shouldn't be the triager.

## Design

A new `triage-agent` (or pm-agent extension) that runs:

1. **Trigger**: every N reconciler iterations OR on cluster-size threshold (e.g. when `backlog` decade has >10 unrenamed threads).
2. **Per-cluster prompt** (haiku-class, cheap):
   - Read all beads in the cluster (titles + descriptions)
   - Decide: `{ promote, demote, defer }`
   - If `promote`: emit `{ name, decade_id, justification }` — meaningful thread name + which real decade owns it
   - If `demote`: cluster moves to a `noise` decade (or thread+beads delete)
   - If `defer`: skip until next pass
3. **Action**: call `rsry_thread_reparent` (added in PR #183) and possibly `rsry_thread_assign` to rename + re-parent.
4. **Audit**: each decision recorded as a bead comment on each cluster member: "triage-agent: promoted to {decade}/{thread} — {justification}"

## Why this is high-leverage

- Removes the bead-PM friction the user just complained about
- Demonstrates rosary's dispatch model on a meta-task (agent that improves agent infrastructure)
- Composable: triage-agent could later handle the `ungrouped` decade too

## Files (new)
- `agents/triage-agent.md` — agent definition
- `src/reconcile/triage_clusters.rs` — reconciler hook that dispatches to triage-agent on a schedule
- A new pipeline_models entry: `triage-agent → claude-haiku`

## Tests
- `triage_clusters_promote_path` — feed cluster fixture, assert reparent + rename via mock
- `triage_clusters_demote_path` — assert move to noise decade
- `triage_clusters_defer_path` — assert no-op

## Dependencies
- Sibling: rosary-XXXXX (rename auto/ → backlog/) — should land first so the triage agent operates on the new naming

## Success criteria
- After enabling, the `backlog` decade should drop to <5 threads on a real run (clusters either get promoted or demoted)
- No `SharedScope cluster` placeholder names left in the lattice after one full pass

title: RCA: vault-custody viability across providers — codex OAuth is custody-able (HTTP 200 refresh from a non-originating holder)
description:
Informal RCA / empirical finding. Settles whether "integrate dispatch auth through cloister's vault" is real or wishful — per provider. Informs rosary-b1495c (dispatch "Not logged in"), ADR-0016 (dispatch auth path), and AMENDS cloister ADR-0040's blanket "Max/OAuth = audit-not-custody" claim.

QUESTION: for each provider, can a credential held by a NON-ORIGINATING holder (i.e. cloister's vault, not the originating CLI) authenticate an LLM call — specifically, can it refresh the OAuth token from outside the client that minted it?

KEY REFRAME (from inspecting the real cred stores): all three providers are OAuth-subscription-shaped, NOT API keys. codex = ~/.codex/auth.json tokens.{access,refresh,id} (auth_mode=chatgpt); gemini = ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json (GEMINI_API_KEY unset); claude = OAuth, but NOT in the 'Claude Code-credentials' keychain item (that holds MCP github/notion OAuth) — actual Anthropic token location TBD. So it's one custody question asked three times.

METHOD (per provider): (A) OIDC discovery for the token_endpoint; (B) POST grant_type=refresh_token + client_id + refresh_token from a BARE SHELL (no CLI, no keychain — the vault's position); (C) observe 200+new-token (custody-able) vs 401/invalid_grant (client/device-bound → audit-only). No secrets logged; auth.json backed up; rotated tokens written back so the CLI survives.

CODEX RESULT — CUSTODY-ABLE:
- token_endpoint = https://auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token (grant_types: authorization_code, refresh_token).
- refresh from a bare shell (client_id app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann): HTTP 200, new access+refresh+id tokens, Bearer, expires_in 864000 (10d). No error.
- ROTATION IS REAL + CONFIRMED LIVE: the refresh minted a NEW refresh_token, dead-ending the old one — wrote the rotated tokens back to auth.json (verified live) so the codex CLI wasn't broken.

IMPLICATIONS:
1. cloister's vault CAN hold + refresh codex's ChatGPT OAuth — ADR-0040's "audit not custody" is too broad; codex is custody-able. Amend ADR-0040 with the measured result.
2. Rotation ⇒ cloister must be the SOLE holder of the refresh token (extract into vault, drop the local copy) — cloister + the local CLI cannot both hold it (whoever refreshes first invalidates the other). Proven live.
3. The refresh is an in-plane HTTPS call (curl in the probe; reqwest/cloister-worker in prod) — NOT an agent shell-out. So codex dispatch AUTH becomes the consistent shape: mcp → cloister vault (refresh+inject) → OPENAI_BASE_URL → done. (The codex agent PROCESS still runs host-side until libkrun/ADR-0044 — separate seam: vault fixes auth, libkrun fixes execution.)

REMAINING ROWS (higher care — would rotate + log out the operator's PRIMARY logins; must write-back like codex):
- claude: locate the actual Anthropic OAuth first (not in 'Claude Code-credentials'); then same probe. Device-bound is the most likely 401.
- gemini: ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json → Google OAuth token endpoint; same probe.

RECOMMENDATION: adopt vault custody for codex dispatch auth (sole-holder); run the claude+gemini rows with the same backup/write-back safety before adopting; feed the matrix back into ADR-0040 (amendment) and ADR-0016 (per-provider dispatch-auth path). Relates: rosary-b1495c, ADR-0016, cloister ADR-0040/0042.

comments.text: Resuming 2026-07-16. Codex row already settled (custody-able, live-confirmed). Remaining: claude + gemini rows. Working in two phases for safety since the refresh probe rotates the operator's PRIMARY logins (bead's own "higher care" flag): Phase 1 = read-only (locate the actual Anthropic OAuth token — not in 'Claude Code-credentials' which holds MCP OAuth; confirm gemini creds shape; OIDC token_endpoint discovery, all public/no-creds). Phase 2 = the rotating refresh probe with backup+write-back, only after explicit operator go-ahead (rotating the live Claude token mid-session could log the session out).
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
GEMINI ROW — CUSTODY-ABLE (by construction; live probe gated locally). Settled from Google's native-app OAuth docs (developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/native-app) + the stored creds' shape:
1. Access tokens are Bearer by default ("Access tokens will retain the token_type of Bearer"); DPoP binding is opt-in at auth-code exchange. Phase-1 structural read of ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json showed keys {access_token, refresh_token, id_token, expiry_date, scope, token_type} and NO DPoP/jkt/proof material → not PoP-bound → access token is bearer-portable (a non-originating holder/vault can replay it).
2. Refresh requires client_id + refresh_token; client_secret optional and the gemini-cli's is public → the vault can refresh from any holder.
3. Refreshing does NOT rotate/invalidate the old refresh_token (a new one MAY be returned → write-back if so, but the act of refreshing is non-destructive). Endpoint https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token.
Residual empirical confirmation = one non-secret check (`jq -r .token_type oauth_creds.json` == "Bearer") + a live 200, both deferred behind the local guardrail.

METHOD FINDING (new): the live refresh/replay probe was BLOCKED by Claude Code's auto-mode classifier for BOTH gemini and claude — reading a live credential + outbound auth call is gated on this machine. This is the mediation boundary working (an agent can't freely replay/exfiltrate creds), and it means the RCA's empirical rows need either the operator's hands (`!`-prefixed run) or an explicit Bash permission rule. Not a blocker for the conclusion — custody is answerable by construction for gemini.

MATRIX: codex ✅ custody-able (live-confirmed) · gemini ✅ custody-able (documented+structural) · claude ⏳ pending (bearer-vs-DPoP structural check, operator-run; deferred — codex+gemini already carry the ADR-0040 amendment).

NEXT: amend cloister ADR-0040 (two of three OAuth providers custody-able → the blanket "audit not custody" is wrong; custody is per-provider and the common case is Bearer-portable) + ADR-0016 per-provider dispatch-auth path.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Probe run 1 (2026-07-17, operator-run via `!` since the harness classifier gates credential reads — itself a data point: "non-originating holder uses the credential" is already a gated action in this environment).

GEMINI — refresh probe INCOMPLETE, with a finding: gemini-cli's client_id/client_secret are NOT recoverable from the installed npm package (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@google/gemini-cli). Structural implication settled regardless: Google installed-app OAuth custody requires THREE items (refresh_token + client_id + client_secret), vs codex which needed only refresh_token + a public client_id. So even if custody-able, the vault must also hold Google's client_secret — a heavier custody surface than codex. Non-destructive structural read of the existing token pending (v2 script).

CLAUDE — row NOT settled, but LOCATION hypothesis CONFIRMED: `security find-generic-password -s 'Claude Code-credentials' -w` returns a blob whose only top-level key is `mcpOAuth` (the GitHub/Notion MCP server OAuth) — NOT the Anthropic model token. This is exactly the bead's "claude OAuth is NOT in 'Claude Code-credentials' (that holds MCP OAuth); actual Anthropic token location TBD." There are multiple `Claude Code-credentials` keychain items; -w grabbed the MCP one. The Anthropic `claudeAiOauth` token is a different item. v2 script enumerates all items by account + structural-checks the one carrying claudeAiOauth (non-destructive — no refresh, no rotation, safe mid-session).

Scripts: scratchpad/vault-custody-probe.sh (v1), vault-custody-probe-v2.sh (v2, refined). Both print structure+status only, never token values.

STATE: codex = custody-able (settled, prior). gemini = custody-able-by-construction likely but heavier (3-item), refresh unverified. claude = pending correct-item location (v2). Enough already to draft the ADR-0040 amendment for the codex row; hold gemini/claude rows for the v2 read.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
CLAUDE ROW — SETTLED BY DOCUMENTATION (2026-07-17, via the claude-api skill / Anthropic API auth reference; no destructive probe needed).

Direct /v1/messages calls ARE supported with a Max/Pro subscription OAuth token (the `sk-ant-oat…` token from `claude setup-token`, or `ant auth print-credentials --access-token`). It is a HEADER change, not an api-key swap:
- Authorization: Bearer <oauth-token>   (NOT x-api-key)
- anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20      (REQUIRED for /v1/messages specifically — the ref notes some endpoints work without it but /v1/messages does not)
- anthropic-version: 2023-06-01
- content-type: application/json

So Max OAuth is directly API-usable → Anthropic-Max is custody-able for the ModelProvider direct-call path. This is exactly rosary-1be3b8's shape-routing already in the tree: credential_env_var() routes `sk-ant-oat` tokens as the OAuth/Bearer shape. The ModelProvider Anthropic adapter sends Bearer + the oauth beta header for a Credential holding an sk-ant-oat token; x-api-key only for a real API key.

CAVEAT (custody nuance): the OAuth access token is SHORT-LIVED and, per the ref, NOT auto-refreshed when passed via env var — long-running holders must refresh it (`ant auth print-credentials` refreshes on call; a raw env-injected token expires). So the Credential::OAuth refresh machinery (rosary-c79331 bearer()) still matters for the vaulted-Max case. `claude setup-token` mints a longer-lived token for headless use, but it still expires.

MATRIX NOW: codex = custody-able (live-confirmed). claude/Max = directly API-usable via Bearer+oauth-beta (documented; refresh needed for long-lived custody). gemini = custody-able-by-construction but heavier (3-item: refresh_token + client_id + client_secret; secret not in the npm package) — refresh probe still pending the operator paste if we want it live-confirmed. Enough to draft the ADR-0040 amendment: custody is PER-PROVIDER, not the blanket "Max-OAuth = audit-not-custody"; specifically Max IS custody-able for direct calls with the right header + refresh.

Unblocks: rosary-c79331 (ModelProvider) Anthropic adapter can target api.anthropic.com directly for Max users; the migration of bdr_enrich off `claude -p` is NOT blocked on Max. Vault-proxy remains the preferred production path (process never holds the token) but is no longer a hard requirement for a working direct path.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-07-17) — the prior "SETTLED BY DOCUMENTATION: Max is directly API-usable" comment was PREMATURE and is retracted. Live probe + authoritative Anthropic support docs reverse it.

title: Add 'in_review' status to bead lifecycle
description:
## Problem

Beads go directly from open/in_progress to closed. When an agent completes work but it needs review before merging, there's no status to represent this. We closed beads 882eca/886ac3/8915ba immediately after dispatch, then discovered review issues (key leak, nil panic, scope violation). The beads were already closed.

## Proposal

Add `in_review` status between `in_progress` and `closed`:
- Agent completes work → sets status to `in_review`
- Reviewer (human or surgical-reviewer agent) reviews → either approves (close) or requests changes (back to `in_progress`)
- Prevents premature closure before review findings are addressed

## Implementation

- Add `in_review` to the status enum in beads schema
- `rsry_bead_close` should only work from `in_review` (or add `--force` for direct close)
- New tool: `rsry_bead_review(id, verdict: approve|request_changes, comment)`
- Dispatch agents should set `in_review` instead of closing when done

title: acceptance_criteria silently dropped: not persisted by rsry_bead_create, not patchable by rsry_bead_update
description: Found by dogfooding while scoping the ADR-0015 capsule beads. A bead created via rsry_bead_create with `acceptance_criteria` set comes back with the field EMPTY on read (e.g. rosary-375ade: created with acceptance_criteria, JSON shows acceptance_criteria: ''). And rsry_bead_update has NO acceptance_criteria field, so you can't patch it in afterward. Net effect: a bead whose ONLY close condition is acceptance_criteria (no test_files, no test command in description) silently fails has_close_condition() → is_dispatchable() returns false → the reconciler never picks it up, with no error. This is a trap: the bead looks fully scoped but is undispatchable. Workaround today is to set test_files instead. Fix: (a) persist acceptance_criteria through the create path (bead_ops), and (b) add acceptance_criteria to the rsry_bead_update field set. Add a round-trip test: create with acceptance_criteria → read back → assert equal; update acceptance_criteria → read back → assert equal.

title: MCP transport fallback: local stdio → remote HTTP should be configurable per-client
description:
## Problem

If a user has rosary configured as a local MCP server (stdio transport), bead operations stay local. The remote HTTP endpoint (mcp.rosary.bot) is never reached. There's no way to say "use local for reads, remote for writes" or "prefer remote, fallback to local."

## Desired behavior

Configurable per-client MCP routing:
- `transport = "stdio"` — local only (current default for Claude Code)
- `transport = "http"` — remote only (current for web clients)
- `transport = "local-first"` — try local stdio, fall back to HTTP if no local server
- `transport = "remote-first"` — try HTTP, fall back to local stdio

This matters for bead sync: if you create a bead locally, it should be visible on the remote server. Currently it isn't unless you manually sync or the remote server has access to the same Dolt database.

## Config

```toml
[mcp]
transport = "local-first"  # or "stdio", "http", "remote-first"
remote_url = "https://mcp.rosary.bot"
```

## Related

- Bead import (PR #80) partially solves this — export local, import to remote
- Linear sync is a separate bidi channel (beads ↔ Linear) but doesn't cover MCP-to-MCP

The gate: one real contradiction where (1) LLO sheaf flags H¹ structurally with NO LLM, (2) the resolution picks the human-correct winner, (3) a later stale re-ingest does NOT clobber it.

Design: (a) a corpus of REAL contradictions mined from actual work artifacts — a reversed decision; a stale PR re-asserting an old fact; a human correction followed by contradicting auto-ingest. title: RepoPool: refresh dolt-server connection on failure (currently pinned to startup-time ports)
description:
`rsry serve` builds a `RepoPool` of `MySqlPool` connections at startup, each pinned to the dolt-server port that existed at that moment (`dolt-server.port` per repo). When the dolt-server processes get restarted (machine reboot, `dolt sql-server` cycled), the kernel assigns new ephemeral ports and rewrites the per-repo port files — but the running `RepoPool` doesn't refresh. All pooled queries (`rsry_bead_create`, `rsry_bead_search`, etc.) start failing with "starting transaction for create_bead_full" / "searching beads for '...'" while non-pooled paths (`rsry_list_beads` via `scan_repos` → fresh-connect-per-call in `src/scanner.rs:33-36`) keep working.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-04-29)

- `rsry serve` (PID 50999) started Apr 28 12:50, built pools against the dolt servers running at that time
- Apr 28 ~20:28 the dolt sql-server processes for all 13 pooled repos restarted; new ephemeral ports written to `dolt-server.port`
- After that point, `rsry_bead_create` and `rsry_bead_search` failed for *every* repo (ley-line, mache, cloister, ...) while `rsry_list_beads` returned correct data
- `kill 50999` + supervisor relaunch fixed it — confirms the data is fine, only the in-process pool state was stale

## Suggested fix

On `MySqlPool` connection failure inside any handler in `src/serve/handlers.rs` that goes through the pool:

1. Reload `dolt-server.port` for the affected repo (use the same diagnostic `DoltConfig::from_beads_dir` already does, including `is_pid_alive`).
2. If the port file changed since the pool was built, rebuild the per-repo `MySqlPool` against the new port.
3. Retry the original operation once.

Alternative (simpler, less efficient): on first connection failure for a repo, drop that repo's pool entry entirely and let `RepoPool` lazily reconnect. Trades a single failed request after every dolt-server restart for not having to write a refresh dance.

## Anchors

- `src/pool.rs` — `RepoPool` (the stale state)
- `src/serve/handlers.rs` — handlers that go through the pool
- `src/scanner.rs:33-36` — the fresh-connect path that keeps working (use this as the model)
- `src/dolt/mod.rs` — `DoltConfig::from_beads_dir` already has the port-file + is_pid_alive logic to crib

## Anchored discussion

- Diagnosis by sub-agent peer (`general-purpose`), 2026-04-29
- Cross-repo: identified during cloister conversation 2026-04-29 while filing beads in ley-line

comments.text: Fixed in PR #170. Added `known_ports` + `beads_dirs` to RepoPool. `get()` / `get_by_path()` now return `None` when the port file changed since startup, falling through to `connect_bead_store()` for a fresh connection. Test: `pool::tests::stale_dolt_port_returns_none`.

title: Suppress event-log FK-violation warnings for synthetic _schema migration rows
description:
`~/.rsry/rsry-serve.log` is filling up with thousands of repeated lines like:

```
warning: failed to log event for _schema: ... Foreign key violation on fk_events_issue
```

This happens because the migration logic creates a synthetic `_schema` row (or similar `_*`-prefixed rows) and then attempts to log an event referencing it via the `events.issue_id` FK constraint, but no `issues` row with id `_schema` exists. The migration completes correctly — the FK violation is silently swallowed except for the warning — so this is purely log noise, not a correctness issue.

Per the sub-agent's diagnosis (2026-04-29): "every reconnection prints all 4 migrations × 1452 errors." That's >5000 spurious warning lines per `rsry serve` startup, which buries real warnings.

## Suggested fix

In whatever code path inserts `events` rows tied to `issue_id`, skip the insert (or short-circuit the warning) when `issue_id` starts with `_`. Synthetic IDs starting with `_` are a stable convention worth honoring at the event-log layer.

Alternative: drop the FK constraint entirely (events to a deleted/synthetic issue are surely not load-bearing for anything else), but that's a bigger schema change with migration cost — the prefix-skip is a one-line guard.

## Anchors

- Log location: `/Users/jamesgardner/.rsry/rsry-serve.log`
- Sub-agent diagnosis 2026-04-29 (mentioned alongside the related RepoPool bug, this bead)
- Related (same diagnosis): RepoPool stale-port bead, also filed today

title: GitHub Release observation source — auto-close release bead + stamp shipped:vX on the tag range
description:
Reconciler-native release tracking. Today rosary auto-closes beads on PR MERGE (`close-merged` + the `[bead-id]` commit convention, src/serve/github_webhook.rs) but has NO observer for RELEASE events — so a release bead (e.g. rosary-3a8fdb, whose done-signal is "release published," not "PR merged") never auto-closes, and "is my fix shipped?" requires manually grepping tag ranges.

Add a GitHub Release event source, mirroring the merge webhook: on `release: published`,
1. close the bead named by the release/tag commit's `[bead-id]`, and
2. append a `shipped: <tag>` observation (ADR-0010 lattice) to EVERY bead whose commit is in `<prev-tag>..<tag>`.

Result: "shipped in vX" becomes a derived, queryable per-bead field — the level-triggered reconciler way — instead of a manual close + tag-grep. title: SQLite bead stores have NO cross-machine propagation — hooks' dolt push/pull silently no-op (now the default backend)
description:
VERIFIED in rosary's own source (docs/git-hooks/post-push):

  REPO=$(basename "$PWD")
  BEADS_DIR=".beads/dolt/$REPO"
  if [ -d "$BEADS_DIR" ]; then
      (cd "$BEADS_DIR" && dolt push origin main 2>/dev/null) || true
  fi

post-merge mirrors it for `dolt pull`. Both are gated on `.beads/dolt/<repo>` existing. For a SQLite store (`.beads/beads.db`, no dolt/ dir) the block is a SILENT NO-OP — and even on the Dolt path errors are swallowed (2>/dev/null || true), so a failed sync is invisible too.

WHY THIS IS NOW URGENT: SQLite is the DEFAULT backend, and rosary itself was migrated dolt->sqlite (#396, metadata.json flip). So rosary's own bead store — and every `rsry init` repo — has no cross-machine propagation, while the installed hooks still LOOK like they sync (the dolt block is right there in the file). A bead closed on machine A is invisible to machine B. 'The agent closed it' != 'every agent that cares now knows.'

NUANCE (don't over-claim): the post-merge hook's `close-merged --local` half DOES run on all backends, so local merge->close still works. The gap is specifically STORE-LEVEL cross-machine propagation.

EVIDENCE / CONVERGENCE:
- Found independently by the vigil agent (vigil-97e939), which correctly scoped it as a question; the hook source confirms it.
- ley-line-open already hit this and built the workaround: .beads/.gitignore untracks *.db while beads.jsonl is GIT-TRACKED (LLO commit a041ffe, 'share beads via git-tracked JSONL'). That is a de-facto sync path via the export.
- rosary-9d4951 (PR #398) just added the missing RETURN half: `rsry bead import --jsonl`, an id-preserving restore from that export. jsonl-in-git + id-preserving-restore is therefore already a working (commit-granularity, coarse) propagation path for SQLite — it just isn't wired into the hooks or documented as the story.

RELATED: rosary-130050 is the same hooks failing for a DIFFERENT reason (never fire under jj) — that one is VCS-shaped, this one is backend-shaped; fixing either alone leaves the other. rosary-133346 (git-NDJSON substrate) and ADR-0020 / rosary-160eed ('log as truth, stores as rebuildable caches') are where the principled fix likely belongs: if the log is truth and the store is a cache, propagation is just shipping the log.

comments.text:
CONNECTION TO THE CAPSULE WORK (ADR-0015) — worth stating before the merge driver lands.

A merge driver is only NEEDED because beads.jsonl is a MUTABLE SNAPSHOT. Two sides edit the same record, so a conflict rule (LWW on updated_at) becomes necessary. An APPEND-ONLY LOG needs none: entries are never rewritten, so union IS the merge — no driver, no conflict rule, no tie-break policy, no "did the ancestor delete this" ambiguity.

That is exactly what ADR-0015 (execution-lineage capsules) and ADR-0020 (content-addressed identity, state = CAS-advanced DAG tip) describe, and what every system in docs/prior-art/state-sync-sota.md independently landed on: git-bug op-packs under refs/<ns>/<id>, Radicle COBs, beads via refs/dolt/data, and Entire's checkpoints branch. None of them needs a merge driver, because none of them stores a mutable snapshot.

So the honest framing: the merge driver is a BAND-AID ON THE DATA MODEL, not a fix to it. It is still worth building — it makes the current snapshot model safe TODAY, and "make the wrong thing safe while the right thing is built" is legitimate. But it should be labeled as transitional, not as the design, or it will look like the answer and calcify.

Two concrete implications:
1. LWW is a LOSSY merge. When two machines edit the same bead, one edit is silently discarded — correct-by-policy, but information is destroyed. An op-log keeps both operations and derives status from the fold (ADR-0010's observation lattice, already built and unit-tested, stuck at R4b / rosary-a66b3a). The lattice is the thing that makes the driver unnecessary.
2. The capsule angle adds a reason beyond merge-safety: a capsule is the durable record of WHY state changed (what ran, what it produced). LWW throws that away — it keeps the winning VALUE and discards the provenance of the losing edit. If capsules land, bead state transitions should be capsule-derived, at which point the JSONL becomes a projection/cache rather than a source, and its merge semantics stop mattering.

RECOMMEND: ship the driver, but comment it as transitional and link ADR-0015/ADR-0020 + prior-art recommendation #1 (op-log in refs) from both the driver source and .gitattributes, so the next reader knows this is scaffolding rather than the intended end state.
