title: Durable dispatch off exec: finish codex app-server runtime + ACP-native claude path (fable analysis)
description:
Fable (claude-fable-5) analysis of moving dispatch off `codex exec`/`claude -p` (exec anti-pattern) onto programmatic interfaces. Informs ADR-0016 + rosary-9be65d (exec smell rule) + rosary-2500f3 (validate native codex).

KEY FINDINGS (grounded in code):
1. acp.rs ALREADY solves the claude language boundary — it's a complete Rust-native ACP client: RosaryClient::request_permission is the per-tool-call allow/deny callback; should_approve/is_safe_bash deny Bash(rm -rf /) while allowing Bash(cargo) under Implement (acp.rs:446-477) — the scoped-Bash reign the CLI can't bind; held child handle + SIGTERM→SIGKILL reaping (acp.rs:90-124); completion via protocol StopReason not exit code. claude-agent-acp (Zed's TS Agent-SDK wrapper) is the language-neutral JSON-RPC bridge. So "drive claude programmatically from Rust without exec" is BUILT, just not default.
2. codex_native.rs is ~30% — a wire contract, NOT a runtime. It starts threads but NEVER observes completion: wait() returns false for a running turn by construction (codex_native.rs:425-431); every RPC re-connects and discards the event stream (:225-247, :340-341); on-request approvals can't be answered (no server→client handler); 30s timeout wrong for minute-long turns. Does not work end-to-end today (definitive).
3. codex exec's reign is already materially BETTER than claude exec's — codex exec --sandbox is a real OS sandbox (Seatbelt/Landlock); claude -p --allowedTools is advisory.

PER-PROVIDER DECISION:
- codex → finish the app-server JSON-RPC runtime; rosary OWNS the server child (stdio JSON-RPC, like the Python/TS SDKs) rather than dialing an ambient socket (ambient daemon = the launchd-context bug class). Native sandbox + answerable approvals + resumable thread_id handle + kill=turn/interrupt. Keep CodexExecProvider as fallback until a live soak passes.
- claude → ACP (claude-agent-acp, acp.rs) as the orchestrator-path default (behind a config flag); hardened `claude -p` + `--permission-prompt-tool mcp__rsry__<approve>` (reuse should_approve) as the MCP-detached fallback until the detached path is replaced by a held-handle design. Do NOT force ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (Max cost regression).
- gemini → leave on exec.

FIRST INCREMENT (one file, one seam, one demo): finish codex_native.rs event loop — persistent connection per dispatch; read frames → (i) events append to STREAM_LOG_FILENAME, (ii) approval requests answered from PermissionProfile, (iii) turn-completed writes Some(ok) into the existing Arc<Mutex<Option<bool>>> (codex_native.rs:394,425-431); kill()=turn/interrupt. AgentProvider/pipeline untouched (CodexProvider::spawn_run already returns Box<dyn AgentSession>). Demo: RSRY_EXPERIMENTAL_CODEX=1, dispatch a trivial Implement bead → assert wait()==true after real completion + AgentSessionRef(codex,thread_id) persisted + stream log has items + mid-turn kill interrupts cleanly + bead retries. Verify: cargo test -p rosary codex_native.

VALIDATE (cheap, parallel): does claude-agent-acp authenticate under Max OAuth HEADLESS? Historically stdin-mode flips OAuth behavior (mod.rs:877-880). Empirical, one dispatch. If it fails, claude path degrades to (c)+approval-tool.

OPEN TENSIONS: turn/start response semantics unverified vs a live server (2500f3) — decides the event-loop shape; who owns the codex server process (ambient vs rosary-spawned child; keep Rust-side dumb, OTP supervises per ADR-0016 D6); ACP adapter trust surface (3rd-party, version-skew, keys off display title acp.rs:361 not schema id, MaxTurnRequests counts as success acp.rs:328-331 → misclassifies truncated runs); reign ceiling unchanged — tool-call-layer approval; OS containment stays cloister libkrun/ADR-0044 (codex is the exception, OS sandbox already). Consistent with ADR-0016 mcp→hits-api→done; vault-proxy env injects into server/sidecar child same as CLI (D4, Max audit-not-custody ceiling holds).

comments.text:
VALIDATION RESULT (ACP Max-OAuth probe, claude-agent-acp@0.21.0):

1. NOT ent-gated / Max works: ACP initialize returns authMethods:[] (agent self-authenticates via local Claude Code creds, no protocol-level API-key/enterprise handshake). session/new got PAST login (failed on a config error, NOT an auth error) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset → it uses the operator's Max login. Answers b1495c-adjacent Q: ACP is not enterprise-only.

2. VERSION-SKEW CONFIRMED LIVE (fable's flagged risk, now empirical): session/new returned -32603 "Invalid permissions.defaultMode: auto." — but `auto` IS a valid, NEW current Claude Code permission mode (per code.claude.com/docs; Shift+Tab cycle, --permission-mode auto, disableAutoMode setting). The operator uses `auto` in their live session. So the ACP adapter (0.21.0) is BEHIND current Claude Code and rejects a mode Claude Code supports. The adapter lags Anthropic's release cadence.

DESIGN IMPLICATION — tempers the fable recommendation: fable put ACP as the claude DEFAULT + `-p`+--permission-prompt-tool as fallback. This measurement argues for the reverse leaning: `claude -p` + `--permission-prompt-tool mcp__rsry__<approve>` drives CURRENT Claude Code directly (no third-party adapter to version-skew), reusing acp.rs's should_approve as the binding permission callback — robust against new modes/features — at the cost of held-child lifecycle vs protocol session. ACP stays an option but its adapter-lag is a real durability cost, not a footnote (broke on the first probe). If ACP is used, rosary must pass a mode the adapter accepts (override the operator's `auto`) — itself fragile.

NOTE: codex path (finish app-server runtime) is unaffected — it speaks codex's own protocol, no third-party adapter. Codex-first sequencing stands.

title: Dispatched agent reign not enforced: Bash runs outside --allowedTools + unbounded (worker ran `find /`)
description:
Found by dogfooding: dispatched rosary-375ade (scoping-agent, claude provider, headless `claude -p`). The worker shelled out `find / -path "*/registry/src/*capnpc-0.21*/src/lib.rs"` — an unbounded filesystem crawl from root that hammered the whole disk and (on macOS) trips TCC prompts for Documents/Desktop/etc.

TWO gaps:
1. **Allowlist not binding.** The dispatch passed `--allowedTools Read,Glob,Grep,mcp__mache__*,mcp__rsry__*` — Bash is NOT in that list — yet the agent executed a Bash command (the `find /`). In a headless `-p` dispatch there is no human to approve an out-of-allowlist tool, so either permissions are being bypassed or the allowlist is advisory. Either way the agent's *reign* (tool access) is not actually enforced.
2. **No filesystem sandbox.** Even for intended Bash (the scoping-agent prompt advertises `Bash(git log)`), execution is unbounded — an agent can `find /`, read outside its worktree (~/.rsry/worktrees/rosary/<bead>), touch other repos, home dotfiles, etc. Dispatched work should be confined to the worktree (+ read-only ~/.cargo where needed), not the whole machine.

Fix direction: make `--allowedTools` actually gate execution in headless dispatch (no silent bypass); scope Bash to the worktree (deny absolute paths outside the workspace / cap `find` roots); align the scoping-agent's advertised `Bash(git log)` with what's actually granted. Relates to the trusted-kernel epic (rosary-b503be) — reign enforcement is a precondition for broader agent fanout.

Repro: dispatch any bead whose scoping/impl touches an external crate API; watch .rsry-stream.jsonl / ps for `find /`.

comments.text: PR #356 fixes the READ-ONLY half (the reported incident). Root cause verified empirically: in headless claude -p, --allowedTools is only auto-approve, NOT binding — unlisted tools run (ReadOnly ran find /; even Implement's scoped Bash(cargo *) doesn't bind). Fix: PermissionProfile::claude_disallowed_tools() → --disallowedTools in both claude arg-builders; ReadOnly+Plan now deny Bash,Edit,Write,NotebookEdit (verified via file-marker harness end-to-end). RESIDUAL (keep open / trusted-kernel b503be): Implement's SCOPED Bash still unbound — 'allow cargo, deny find /' can't be a denylist (broad Bash deny kills cargo). Needs a permission-prompt-tool (MCP handler denying anything not in the profile) OR an OS sandbox confining the worker to its worktree. That's the real fix for full reign enforcement.

title: P0 runaway: targeted run re-dispatches a deadlettered bead forever (deadlettered_ids not recorded on verify path)
description:
REPRODUCED live in a dogfood run (rosary-3eef9c): 158 observations in ~4min, 77 Dispatched / 71 Deadletter cycling. Same pathology as the rosary-11214e 4353-event runaway.

ROOT CAUSE: the targeted-run exit condition (reconcile/mod.rs:523) checks cumulative.deadlettered_ids.contains(target). But deadlettered_ids is populated in ONLY one place — the liveness sweep for SIBLING beads (mod.rs:705). The TARGET bead's own deadletter comes through the verification path: verify_completed -> VerifyResult.deadlettered (a usize COUNT), aggregated at mod.rs:954 (summary.deadlettered += vr.deadlettered) — the id is never recorded. So the exit check never fires -> infinite re-triage + re-dispatch.

REGRESSION: the split of counter-vs-ids (tests_state.rs:820) correctly stopped SIBLING deadletters from false-EXITING a targeted run, but left the target's OWN deadletter not recording its id -> swung to never-exiting.

FIX: add deadlettered_ids: Vec<String> to VerifyResult (reconcile/verify.rs:20); push the bead_id where the ActionOutcome::Deadlettered is counted; extend summary.deadlettered_ids from vr at mod.rs:954. Regression test: targeted run exits when the TARGET deadletters via the verification path (not only the liveness sweep).

SEVERITY: unattended rsry run on any bead that can't pass verify loops forever — burns agents/tokens + pollutes the observation corpus (this is where 11214e's 4353 events came from).

## Decision

rmcp's standard `ServerHandler` returns a global tool list. Per-session filtering is not built in. Two paths for rosary:

title: CLI bead ops outside a repo silently create + operate on a phantom .beads store in cwd (search returns empty/exit 0; create black-holes work items)
description:
Reported 2026-07-16: `rsry bead search cloister-cf9fc4` from `/` prints "No beads matching" (exit 0); same command inside the repo finds it. Systematic-debugging root cause (all steps verified against code + live repro):

## Root cause chain (src/main.rs)
1. `Command::Bead` `--repo` defaults to "." (main.rs:1552 arm; clap default at the Bead variant).
2. `scanner::resolve_repo_path(".")` → cwd → `config::discover_repo_root(cwd)` walks up; **on failure falls back to raw cwd** (`unwrap_or(expanded)`, scanner.rs:72-81) — the "am I even in a repo?" signal is swallowed.
3. `resolve_beads_dir(cwd)` (main.rs:869): no `.beads`, `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` fails (not a git repo) → returns `cwd/.beads` anyway.
4. `connect_bead_store(cwd/.beads)` **creates an empty beads.db on connect** (the Backup/Restore arm at main.rs:1560 explicitly works around this: "connect_bead_store would create an empty beads.db").

## Consequences (verified by repro)
- `bead search`/`list` from any non-repo cwd: silent empty result, exit 0 — looks like "no such bead".
- **Littering**: repro from /private/tmp created /private/tmp/.beads/beads.db (61KB schema, 0 rows). Any writable cwd gets a phantom store.
- **Worst case**: `bead create` from a non-repo cwd writes real work items into a phantom store no scan ever reads — silent data black hole.

## Symlink/dual-checkout angle (user suspicion, resolved)
Not symlinks: ~/github/art/cloister and ~/remotes/art/cloister are two real checkouts. Search "worked" from the github checkout only because cloister runs Dolt SERVER mode (.beads/dolt/ + dolt-server.port in both) — both checkouts converge on the same server data. A SQLite-mode repo (e.g. agents) would NOT converge: a second checkout gets a separate empty store via the same create-on-connect path. Same root cause, different symptom.

## Fix direction
a) CLI layer: when `--repo` was defaulted (not explicit) AND discover_repo_root failed, fail loud: "not inside a registered repo; cd into one, pass --repo <path>, or use --all". Distinguish "resolved a real repo" from "fell back to cwd" (change scanner::resolve_repo_path to return an enum/Option instead of unwrap_or).
b) Read ops (search/list/status parity): add cross-repo fallback — search all registered repos from ~/.rsry/config.toml when outside a repo (user expectation: `rsry status` is already global). Print per-repo attribution.
c) Store creation should be explicit (init/enable), not a side effect of connect for read paths — gate connect_bead_store with create=false for read ops, or check beads_dir.exists() first at the CLI layer.

Repro commands:
  cd /private/tmp && rsry bead search cloister-cf9fc4   # silent empty + creates /private/tmp/.beads
  cd ~/github/art/cloister && rsry bead search cloister-cf9fc4   # found (Dolt server convergence)

title: Dispatched agents can't reach the rsry MCP server in their spawned context
description:
Observed during rosary-b1495c smoke testing (2026-06-23). A dispatched claude agent is granted `mcp__rsry__*` and `mcp__mache__*` in --allowedTools, but its spawned process has no MCP server configured, so those tools aren't actually connected — the agent reported "the mcp__rsry__* tools aren't connected in this session" and could not comment on its own bead.

The spawn must provide the MCP server config to the child claude (e.g. `--mcp-config`/settings pointing at `rsry serve --transport stdio` and the mache server) so the allowed MCP tools are real. Without this, agents can't comment progress, search beads, or use mache during dispatch. Pre-existing, unrelated to the auth fix, but blocks the agent feedback loop.

comments.text:
FIX PATH (investigated 2026-06-24): `claude` supports `--mcp-config <configs...>` (load MCP servers from JSON) + `--strict-mcp-config`. So the fix is: at spawn (providers.rs spawn_agent base_args + build_command, and spawn_detached), write a workspace mcp-config JSON declaring the servers the agent's --allowedTools already reference (rsry + mache) and pass `--mcp-config <path>`. rsry server cmd is unambiguous: `rsry serve --transport stdio`.

OPEN QUESTIONS before implementing (why I didn't just do it): (1) the nested `rsry serve` needs the right config/repo context (RSRY_CONFIG / cwd) so the agent's bead tools hit the correct repo — must pass that through; (2) mache's exact stdio MCP launch command (binary/args) needs confirming; (3) whether to use --strict-mcp-config (isolate to just these) vs inherit. Bounded once those 3 are pinned. Not a blocker for core dispatch (which works); it restores the agent feedback loop (comment/search/mache during dispatch).

title: main's .beads/beads.jsonl was wiped to empty by PR #403 (silent, text-merged)
description:
Observed 2026-07-23 while rebasing rosary-f9516f onto main: commit baa4537 ([rosary-efd300] #403) contains '.beads/beads.jsonl | 1115 ----' — the entire git-tracked bead export was replaced with an EMPTY file, and git's default text merge accepted it silently.

Root cause is almost certainly the pre-commit hook exporting from a worktree/clone whose .beads/beads.db is empty or missing: `rsry bead export --jsonl --status all -o .beads/beads.jsonl` on an empty store writes an empty file, which the hook then `git add`s. Nothing in the path notices that 1115 records vanished.

Detected by the new merge driver (rosary-f9516f): rebasing across it reported '1115 resurrected' — its one-sided-deletion policy restored every bead. PR #406 therefore also repairs main's export. But the wipe should not have been committable in the first place.

Fix candidates: (a) pre-commit refuses to stage an export that loses more than a small fraction of the previously committed record count (fail-loud, matches the merge driver's posture); (b) the hook skips entirely when the store reports 0 beads.

comments.text:
CONFIRMED IN GIT HISTORY — this already happened on main, and the mechanism is mine (#399/#402).

  aef995c (#402)  +1113   export first tracked
  f8f6fbd (#404)  +6/-2
  26bd6b8 (#405)  6 +++---
  baa4537 (#403)  -1115   <-- ENTIRE EXPORT DELETED
  a3d3aee (#406)  +1118   <-- restored (incidentally, by the merge-driver PR's rebase)

main is healthy right now (1117 records) ONLY because #406 happened to land after #403 and restored it. That was luck, not design. Between baa4537 and a3d3aee, main's shared bead record was empty.

MECHANISM: docs/git-hooks/pre-commit runs `rsry bead export --jsonl --status all -o .beads/beads.jsonl` and `git add`s it, gated on the export being already-tracked. But `.beads/beads.db` is GITIGNORED — so an AGENT WORKTREE (or any fresh clone, or any checkout where the store hasn't been restored) HAS NO STORE. The export therefore succeeds and returns ZERO beads, the hook stages that empty file, and the commit deletes every record from the shared export.

This recurs on EVERY commit made from a worktree without a store. Agent worktrees are the normal case for dispatch, so this is not an edge case — #403 is simply the first time it was observed.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: git's line-level text merge accepts a wholesale deletion silently — there is nothing to conflict with. It only became visible because #406 landed a RECORD-LEVEL driver that counts resurrections; its "1115 resurrected" was the destruction being reported. I initially dismissed that counter as benign ("the branch predates the export being tracked"). It was not benign.

REQUIRED FIX (the hook must refuse, not just warn):
1. If `.beads/beads.db` (or the configured store) is ABSENT -> do nothing. Never export, never stage. A missing store is not an empty store.
2. If the export would DROP a large fraction of the committed records -> refuse and fail the commit loudly. A legitimate change adds or edits a few lines; it never removes ~all of them. Compare against `git show HEAD:.beads/beads.jsonl` and hard-fail beyond a threshold.
3. Consider refusing when the export is empty but the committed file is not — the specific shape observed here.

RELATED, AND THE REAL LESSON: this is the commit-coupling cost of putting derived state in the WORKING TREE, which docs/prior-art/state-sync-sota.md already argued against — git-bug, Radicle, beads and Entire all keep work state OUTSIDE the working tree (refs/branches), where a checkout without a store cannot overwrite it. rosary-610ad8 (dual state) and rosary-a66b3a (op-log in refs) are the structural answers; this bead is the guard needed until then.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
MECHANISM CORRECTED — my proposed fix ("skip when the store is absent") WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT #403. Verified.

The linked worktree at .git/worktrees/... HAS a `.beads/beads.db`. It cannot have come from git — the file is gitignored, so a worktree never receives it. It was CREATED ON DEMAND: `SqliteBeadStore::connect` creates the db + schema if absent, so ANY rsry command run inside an agent worktree materializes an EMPTY store. The export then legitimately reads 0 beads, the hook stages that, and the commit deletes every record.

So the store is not missing. It is present and empty. An absence check is the wrong guard.

USER'S DIAGNOSIS (correct, and better than mine): this is GIT SEMANTICS FIRING IN A JJ/COLOCATED WORLD. Verified: this repo has BOTH .jj and .git, and `detect_vcs` (src/workspace/mod.rs:50-58) classifies "(_, true) => Git" — colocated repos take the git path. So the git pre-commit hook fires from jj-driven operations AND from every agent worktree — precisely the contexts it was never designed for. The hook currently checks only two things: is `.beads/dolt/<repo>` absent, and is beads.jsonl tracked. It checks NEITHER the store's contents NOR its execution context.

CORRECT GUARDS (need both — either alone is insufficient):

1. CONTEXT — refuse to export outside the canonical checkout. Git-native and verified to discriminate here:
       GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --git-dir)          # canonical: ".git"
       GIT_COMMON=$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir) # canonical: ".git"
       [ "$GIT_DIR" != "$GIT_COMMON" ] && exit 0    # linked worktree -> never export
   Measured: canonical checkout gives git-dir == common-dir; a linked worktree gives
   ".git/worktrees/<name>" vs ".git". Agent workspaces are exactly linked worktrees, so this
   is a precise test, not a heuristic. (rosary also creates jj workspaces — confirm the same
   discriminator holds there, or add the equivalent jj check.)

2. MAGNITUDE — refuse when the export would drop most of the committed records:
       committed=$(git show HEAD:.beads/beads.jsonl | wc -l)
       fresh=$(wc -l < .beads/beads.jsonl)
       # hard-fail the commit if fresh is drastically smaller than committed
   A legitimate change adds or edits a few lines; it never removes ~all of them. This is the
   backstop for any context the first guard misses, and it is what would have caught #403
   (1115 -> 0).

Guard 1 alone misses a wipe from the canonical checkout with a broken store. Guard 2 alone
lets an agent worktree keep rewriting the shared record with near-empty exports. Ship both.

ADJACENT ISSUE WORTH ITS OWN LOOK: that `SqliteBeadStore::connect` silently CREATES an empty
store wherever it is called is the deeper hazard here — it converts "this directory has no
bead store" into "this directory has an empty bead store", which is indistinguishable from
"all beads were deleted" to every downstream consumer. That is the same silent-success shape
as the parse_datetime now() fallback (rosary-af2c64). Consider requiring an explicit
create/init flag for store materialization, so only `rsry init` may bring a store into being.

title: author/created_by are stringly-typed (git username / magic markers / inconsistent Option) — type them as cert-backed identity (ADR-0020)
description:
Attribution fields conflate three different things behind bare strings, and disagree on nullability:
- Comment.author: String (required) — populated with a git username OR magic markers like "rsry-move" (src/bead_move.rs:72), no type telling human/agent/system apart.
- Bead.created_by: Option<String> and Bead.owner: Option<String> — created_by is just git_config_user_name() (src/main.rs:1415/1581/1678).

This is the ADR-0020 anti-pattern: identity by ad-hoc mutable string, not a stable typed identity. ADR-0020's genesis blob specifies a creator-signet-cert; P4 (rosary-16154e) covers role + agent attribution. Introduce a typed Author/principal (human git-name | agent dispatch-id | system marker), cert-backed where ADR-0020 P1 lands, and reconcile the Comment.author vs created_by nullability. Depends on the identity layer (genesis blob, rosary-160bb2) so author becomes part of the content-addressed identity rather than a mutable side field.
acceptance_criteria: A typed Author/principal replaces bare String for comment author + bead created_by/owner; magic markers (rsry-move) become a typed variant; Comment.author vs created_by nullability reconciled; cargo test passes

title: EPIC: Linear-escalation-triage workflow — Linear as primary UI, rosary as the notebook
description:
## Why

User's company uses Linear extensively. Escalation triage today is **~10 manual steps per ticket** (Linear body fetch, comments fetch, GH issue fetch, Zendesk lookup, status transition, comment post, bead creation, sometimes worktree open). Goal: collapse to **3 steps** via rosary MCP, with `linear-escalation-triage` skill as the discipline.

**Critical clarification (user, 2026-05-19):** This is **NOT a bidirectional sync** play. The user manages escalations IN LINEAR. Rosary's job is to make WORKING those escalations easier from Claude Code — fetch context, post replies, transition status, drop a bead for follow-up. Linear stays the source of truth.

## Smallest-first-step discipline (user-stated, same shape as CDD `rosary-44740d`)

Per the user's directive: **build `rsry_ticket_load` first. Run it on 5 tickets. If the loop tightens noticeably, build the rest. If not, half a day spent learning the loop wasn't the bottleneck.** Match this incrementality with phased children — each phase is its own bead with concrete acceptance.

## Phase decomposition

| Phase | Bead | What | Cost | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (smallest) | rsry_ticket_load | Single MCP call returns Linear body + comments + linked GH issue + Zendesk URL + existing bead | ~½ day | Run on 5 real tickets; loop tightens? |
| 1 | rsry_ticket_wrap | Atomic comment + status transition + bead create/update | ~1 day | Replaces 3 separate tool calls today |
| 2 | rsry_sweep | Prioritized ticket queue (P1+ in Triage > 7d, etc.) | ~1 day | Start-of-week oncall sweep usable in <30s |
| 3 | rsry_ticket_focus | Session-level "I'm on X" context | ~½ day | LLM stops re-asking which ticket |
| 4 | /triage slash command + skill | Skill discipline + auto-sweep | ~1 day | One command opens the day's queue |
| 5 (optional) | MCP Apps interactive UI | Rich UI per SEP-1865 (Jan 2026) | speculative | "Feels like an app" verified |

Phase 5 unlocks because **MCP Apps shipped Jan 2026** (SEP-1865, co-developed Anthropic + OpenAI + MCP-UI). Lets MCP servers return interactive React-based UIs directly inside Claude's chat window. The triage queue could render as an actual interactive table with row-level actions. Filed as exploratory — DON'T build until Phases 0-4 prove the loop is the bottleneck.

## Constraints (user-stated)

- Don't reinvent chainctl. Linear's own MCP does Linear stuff; we wrap/compose.
- Don't store credentials. Use the user's existing `CHAINCTL_CONFIG`.
- Skill = source of truth on workflow discipline. MCP = plumbing.

## Out of scope (file separately if needed)

- Bidirectional sync (explicitly NOT the goal — Linear is the source of truth)
- Replacing Linear's UI entirely
- Multi-user / multi-tenant triage state
- Replacing chainctl

## Cross-link

- Same staged-validation discipline as `rosary-44740d` (CDD σ work). Both follow "ship smallest experiment → validate → expand iff value."
- Linear sync infrastructure already exists (`src/linear.rs`, `src/linear_tracker.rs`). These beads compose ON TOP, not as replacement.
- Existing `/note` skill (`rosary-406b68`-fixed) shows the pattern for skill + MCP composition.

## Time-box

Phase 0 only: ½ day. Full Phase 0-4: ~4 days. Phase 5 deferred (need real MCP Apps client adoption + Phase 0-4 validation).

## Success criteria

After Phase 0-4: a real escalation triage that previously took 10+ MCP calls + manual context-switching can be done in 3 steps inside Claude Code:
1. `/triage` (see queue)
2. `/triage CUS-495` (load context + open worktree if needed)
3. `/triage wrap` (post + transition + bead in one shot)

title: publish the UDS (`mcp`) transport in server.json transports block — cloister can't derive what isn't published
description:
rosary HAS a UDS MCP mode — `rsry mcp` ("Start MCP server over a Unix Domain Socket (capnp ToolCall/Result)", confirmed from `rsry --help`). But server.json's `io.github.agentic-research.rosary/transports` block publishes only:
  - stdio:           rsry serve --transport stdio
  - streamable-http: rsry serve --transport http --port 8383

The UDS transport is MISSING from the published contract.

CONSEQUENCE (cloister side): because nothing is published, cloister hardcodes the invocation in its cluster.toml bundle:
    args = [ "mcp", "--ipc-socket", "/run/cloister-uds/rosary.sock" ]
That duplicates a command rosary should own (ADR-0041: each backend repo publishes its own image; ADR-0038: derive bundle config from server.json). cloister's apko-published image defaults to `cmd: serve`, so cloister MUST override the command to get UDS mode — it has no published transport to derive from.

ASK: add a `uds` (or `mcp`) entry to the transports block declaring the command shape, e.g.:
    "uds": { "command": "rsry", "args": ["mcp", "--ipc-socket", "<socketPath>"],
             "note": "capnp ToolCall/Result over a Unix Domain Socket; the socket PATH is supplied by the deployer (cloister convention: /run/cloister-uds/<name>.sock)" }

The socket PATH stays deployer-supplied (it's cloister's deployment convention, not rosary's to choose) — publish the command + flag shape, not the path.

UNBLOCKS: cloister removing the hardcoded `args` from its rosary bundle, and (per cloister ADR-0051) declaring rosary as a same-host UDS *input* rather than a hand-wired bundle.

Close condition: server.json's transports block contains a UDS entry with command+args, and `rsry --help`-documented `mcp` mode matches what's published.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance_criteria">server.json's io.github.agentic-research.rosary/transports block includes a UDS/mcp entry whose command+args match the actual `rsry mcp --ipc-socket <path>` invocation; JSON parses and any server.json schema check passes.

title: [triage P0] rsry_ticket_load — single MCP call for Linear+GH+Zendesk+bead context
description:
## Scope

The smallest first step in `rosary-5d7141` (Linear-escalation-triage EPIC). Single MCP tool: `rsry_ticket_load(ticket_id)` returns the consolidated context the user fetches manually today across 4-5 separate tool calls.

## Acceptance

Given a Linear ticket ID (e.g. `CUS-495`):

```jsonc
rsry_ticket_load({ "ticket_id": "CUS-495" })
→ {
    "linear": { "title": "...", "body": "...", "status": "Triage", "assignee": "..." },
    "comments": [ ... ],            // Linear comments, oldest-first
    "linked_github": {              // null if no GH link
      "url": "https://github.com/org/repo/issues/123",
      "body": "...",
      "state": "open"
    },
    "linked_zendesk": "https://...", // url only; rosary doesn't fetch (auth)
    "existing_bead": {              // null if no triage-bead filed
      "id": "rosary-abc123",
      "status": "open"
    }
```

title: MCP Apps (SEP-1865) as rosary's UI substrate — statusline replacement + triage queue + seam viewer
description:
## Scope

Speculative Phase 5 of `rosary-5d7141`. Use **MCP Apps (SEP-1865, official Jan 2026)** to return interactive React-based UI components from the triage tools so the queue + ticket details render as a real app inside Claude's chat window.

## What MCP Apps actually is (per research 2026-05-19)

- Co-developed Anthropic + OpenAI + MCP-UI
- Official MCP extension formalized as SEP-1865 (Jan 2026)
- Lets MCP servers return interactive UI components (forms, dashboards, tables, multi-step workflows)
- Supported clients: Claude (Desktop + Code + Web), ChatGPT, Goose, VS Code
- 9 launch partners shipped day-1 (Amplitude, Asana, Box, Canva, Clay, Figma, Hex, monday.com, Slack)
- Salesforce coming

## What it could unlock for triage

| Today | With MCP Apps |
|---|---|
| `rsry_sweep` returns JSON, LLM renders as text | Returns a sortable interactive table; row-click loads ticket detail in-place |
| `rsry_ticket_load` dumps body+comments+links as text | Returns a structured detail view with tabs (body / comments / linked-GH / linked-Zendesk) |
| `rsry_ticket_wrap` is N JSON args | Interactive form with status dropdown, comment textarea, "include bead?" checkbox |
| `/triage` is a chat command | "Opens an app" inside the chat with the full queue + selection state |

## Why this is exploratory + last

- **Phases 0-4 must validate first.** If `rsry_ticket_load` alone tightens the loop, MCP Apps adds nothing on top. The smallest-experiment discipline is load-bearing.
- **Client adoption gap.** MCP Apps shipped Jan 2026; Claude Code support is the bottleneck. Verify Claude Code renders MCP Apps responses before investing.
- **Auth model unclear.** MCP Apps' interactive forms post back into the LLM context — credentials for chainctl/Linear in form fields would need a careful auth boundary review.
- **Build cost is non-trivial.** React component bundles per tool; MCP server now embeds UI code; testing in chat client is fiddly. Earn the right to build by proving the loop is the bottleneck first.

## Acceptance (only if Phases 0-4 validated)

- Pick one tool to convert (recommended: `rsry_sweep` — visual queue is the highest-value UI)
- Returns an MCP Apps response (per SEP-1865 spec; check current Anthropic docs)
- Renders in Claude Code with interactive row-selection
- Selecting a row triggers `rsry_ticket_load`'s app variant, which renders the ticket detail
- Auth flows for chainctl/Linear stay outside the rendered UI (no credentials in form state)

## Out of scope

- Building MCP Apps for non-triage tools
- Reimplementing Linear's UI
- Replacing Phase 4 (slash commands) — apps coexist; the slash command remains the entry point

## Risks

- MCP Apps spec is months old; details may change. Pin the spec version at implementation time.
- May depend on rosary running as a remote MCP server (vs stdio), since UI assets need to be served. Check current SEP-1865 transport requirements.

## Time-box

L — speculative; depends on MCP Apps client maturity. NOT ESTIMATABLE until Phases 0-4 validated.

## Parent

`rosary-5d7141`

comments.text:
## Research update (2026-05-19, via subagent)

**Bottom line: MCP Apps is real and stable, but Claude Code does NOT render it today.** This bead should stay deferred indefinitely until that changes.

### Key findings (sources cited)

1. **Spec status**: SEP-1865 is `Final` / Extensions Track, version `2026-01-26`. Hosted at `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`. Several capabilities deferred (modal mode, widget state, file ops) per `ext-apps#201`.

2. **Claude Code support**: **NOT on the client matrix.** Claude Code is terminal-first and has no DOM to host an iframe. Third-party reporting characterizes Claude Code as "the terminal counterpart" using "structured output and bulk operations rather than inline widgets." No public roadmap commits Claude Code to MCP Apps; the 2026 MCP roadmap focuses on extension stabilization, not new host rendering targets.

3. **Transport**: Server↔host can be stdio OR Streamable HTTP — the spec doesn't prescribe. UI is layered on top via predeclared `ui://` resources fetched via standard `resources/read`. App↔host transport is postMessage over a sandboxed iframe. **Implication for rosary**: stdio is fine; the blocker is iframe hosting in Claude Code.

4. **UI authoring**: **HTML-only MVP** with profile `text/html;profile=mcp-app`. JSX/React supported only as build-time inputs that compile to HTML+JS bundles. **No Rust or Python server SDK example exists** — all published examples are JS/TS. A Rust MCP server would need to (a) serve bundled HTML as a resource and (b) speak the MCP `ui/*` JSON-RPC dialect bespoke.

5. **Auth boundary**: Form state flows **directly to the server via JSON-RPC over postMessage**, not through LLM context. Credentials in form state stay out of the conversation transcript by default. Reasonable boundary for the chainctl/Linear case, but relies on host hygiene (prior art of postMessage leaks exists).

6. **Reference impls worth studying** when (if) we revisit:
   - `ext-apps/examples/budget-allocator-server` — closest analogue to a triage queue (rows + per-row controls + server-side validation)
   - `ext-apps/examples/scenario-modeler-server` — multi-step forms, useful for promote-bead-to-thread flows
   - `ext-apps/examples/basic-server-react` — minimum-viable scaffold

7. **Limitations the launch announcement glossed over**:
   - No modal dialog mode (deferred)
   - No file upload primitive
   - No state persistence across messages (`setWidgetState` deferred)
   - No view-to-view communication
   - No standard theming hook
   - Renderer fragility — handshake fails under some configs (`anthropics/claude-ai-mcp#165`); 3P deployments don't mount iframes at all (`#236`)

8. **Effort estimate**: **~1 month** for Claude Code specifically (since it's not a supported host — would need first-party support OR a TUI-equivalent rendering path). ~1 week if we retarget Claude Desktop or claude.ai web instead.

### Revised recommendation

- **Keep this bead OPEN but DEFERRED**. Don't dispatch.
- **Re-evaluate ONLY when** Claude Code adds MCP Apps host support (no signal yet) OR the rosary use case shifts to Claude Desktop / claude.ai web.
- **For now**: Phases 0-4 of `rosary-5d7141` (the triage EPIC) stay text-only via standard MCP tools. That's the right loop to validate first regardless.

### Confidence

High on Q1-Q4, Q7. Medium-high on Q5 (spec is clear; real-world hygiene depends on host). Medium on Q6 (closed-source partners) + Q8 (effort inferred from absent Rust SDK + absent host support).

description: Backlog orchestration work item. Goal: turn the current large Rosary bead backlog into a dispatchable structure where Codex workers can fan out safely while one orchestrating Codex thread coordinates prioritization, dependencies, and collision avoidance. title: Harden release.yml: decouple image job from build + apt-get retry resilience
description:
v0.5.0's release had Build(linux-arm64) fail on a transient apt mirror error (packages.microsoft.com azure-cli repo: 'Clearsigned file isnt valid, got NOSPLIT'), which SKIPPED the image job (needs: build) → image didnt publish. Two fixes:

1. The image job runs its OWN cargo-zigbuild — it does NOT need the build jobs glibc/darwin artifacts. Remove 'needs: build' so a flaky/unrelated binary build cant block image publish. Image is tag-triggered and self-contained.

2. Add apt-get retry resilience to the 'Install system dependencies' steps (build + image jobs) so a transient GH-runner apt mirror hiccup retries instead of hard-failing the whole release. e.g. a 3x retry loop around apt-get update && install, or Acquire::Retries.

Discovered while cutting v0.5.0 (rosary-0d3384). The rc (v0.5.0-rc1) passed because it hit a healthy mirror; the real tag hit a broken one — pure infra flake, not our code. Close: a release where one build leg flakes still publishes the image; apt steps survive a transient mirror failure.

title: MCP write contention across concurrent chats — async write path + WAL + Linear-push backgrounding
description:
## Symptom

With 5-6 concurrent Claude Code chats hitting rosary MCP (each its own stdio MCP server, all sharing the same Dolt instances + `~/.rsry/backend.db` SQLite + same Linear webhook target), bead-mutate calls (`bead_create`, `bead_comment`, `bead_close`) periodically hang. Observed across multiple sessions on 2026-06-17 while running the rosary-cd5d2a review-substrate work alongside parallel mache work.

User framing: *"I am almost tempted to say that we need a queue in front of rosary so we aren't blocking on deps? but unsure if that is overkill or not. I just feel like I am waiting on an MCP call to write to dolt / sqlite sometimes, and due to the writing constraint and me having 5-6 chats it overlaps and hangs."*

## Why the queue-in-front framing is incomplete

A separate queue service in front of rosary would:
- Decouple chat latency from write latency (good)
- Force eventual consistency on `bead_create → bead_comment → bead_close` flows that today are strictly ordered within a single session (bad)
- Add a new component to operate, monitor, and authorize (bad)

The right shape is making **rosary's own write path async**, with eventual consistency at the cross-session boundary and strict consistency within a single session via read-through. That converges with three already-filed beads:

- `rosary-1284f3` — Agent mailbox over Dolt bead substrate
- `rosary-1db9c9` — Incoming triage queue / mailbox
- `rosary-13af35` — Reactive persistent store ADR-0005 ("local firebase" for agent IPC) — **P0 design**

This bead is the **operational forcing function** behind those three: the user is hitting it now.

## Triage — cheap wins to investigate first (in priority order)

Before committing to the substrate-level fix, gather data + capture the easy wins. Each is a discrete sub-bead candidate; this bead is the umbrella.

### 1. SQLite WAL mode on `~/.rsry/backend.db`

Default journal mode is `DELETE` which serializes all readers + writers. `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` typically buys 5-10× concurrency and is a one-line config change. **Investigate first** — if backend.db is the bottleneck, this is the biggest leverage per minute.

Acceptance: confirm current journal mode via `sqlite3 ~/.rsry/backend.db 'PRAGMA journal_mode'`. If `delete`, switch to `wal` in `src/store_dolt.rs` connection setup + add a one-time migration. Measure latency before/after on a stress test (5 concurrent bead_create).

### 2. Async Linear push (`persist_status`)

`bead_create` / `bead_update` / `bead_close` currently call `persist_status()` synchronously inside the handler. If Linear is slow or returns 503, the MCP handler blocks for the user-facing call. Move to fire-and-forget background task with retry + dead-letter on persistent failure.

Acceptance: handler returns within 100ms regardless of Linear API latency. Linear sync still eventually consistent; failures surfaced via a status field on the bead (`linear_sync_status`) or via the dispatch dead-letter mechanism (`rosary-c3034b`).

### 3. Pool warming + connect-time amortization

`RepoPool::get` checks Dolt port staleness on every call. Verify this isn't serializing handlers. Also: first MCP call to a registered repo currently pays the Dolt connect cost (~hundreds of ms). Pre-connect on MCP server startup so the first user-facing call is warm.

Acceptance: cold-start MCP server first bead-mutate completes in <100ms.

## The substrate-level fix (post-triage)

Once the cheap wins land and we have data on what's actually slow, the substrate work converges with `rosary-13af35` (ADR-0005 reactive store):

- **Async write path** — bead-mutate operations write to in-memory state + enqueue durable write; ack to caller immediately
- **Read-through cache** — `get_bead`, `list_comments`, etc. serve from in-memory state first, fall back to Dolt for cache misses
- **Per-session FIFO guarantee** — operations within one session land in order (preserves the `create → comment → close` flow agents depend on)
- **Cross-session eventual consistency** — chat A's `create_bead` is visible to chat B within seconds, not synchronously

This is what `rosary-1284f3` + `rosary-1db9c9` + `rosary-13af35` collectively describe.

## Acceptance for this bead

This umbrella bead is done when:

1. The 3 triage sub-beads above are filed as children with explicit `depends_on` edges
2. Measurement is done — what's actually slow under 5-concurrent-chat load (SQLite contention? Linear push? Dolt connect?)
3. The triage sub-beads land or are explicitly deferred with rationale
4. If contention persists after triage, the substrate work (rosary-13af35 child) gets prioritized over other P2 work

## Cross-links

- `rosary-1284f3` (mailbox) — convergent substrate
- `rosary-1db9c9` (triage queue) — convergent substrate
- `rosary-13af35` (reactive store ADR, **P0**) — the substrate this work needs
- `rosary-c3034b` (dispatch dead-letter) — sibling pattern for async-with-failure-surfacing
- `rosary-b29e00` (mechanical closure enforcement) — related "tools deterministic, agents not" theme

## Provenance

Filed 2026-06-17 from a session debugging the rosary-cd5d2a review-substrate PR (#220) while user reported concurrent chat contention. PR #220 merged at 20:38; this bead captures the architectural concern surfaced during the work.

comments.text:
## Substrate option that wasn't on the table at filing time: DoltLite

DoltHub shipped **DoltLite** (announced [2026-03-25](https://www.dolthub.com/blog/2026-03-25-doltlite/), [github.com/dolthub/doltlite](https://github.com/dolthub/doltlite)) — a SQLite fork where the B-tree backend is replaced with a Dolt-style Prolly Tree. **Embedded library, not a server.** C / Python / Go bindings exist; no Rust binding yet.

### Why it's load-bearing for this bead

Today's contention pain is largely a consequence of Dolt-being-a-server:

| Today's mechanism | DoltLite equivalent |
|---|---|
| Per-repo Dolt MySQL subprocess + ephemeral port allocation | File handle to `.beads/dolt.db` |
| 10-second connect timeout when server hangs ([[rosary-11214e]]'s 154-comment nightmare) | No server to connect to; the failure mode evaporates |
| `RepoPool::get` stale-port checks serialize handlers | One file open per process; OS-level locking only |
| Write contention via MySQL-protocol round-trips per call | OS-level file locking, WAL-style writes |
| Git-style version control preserved | Preserved — that's the whole point of DoltLite |

### Migration shape — much cheaper than I initially feared

Rosary already has the trait abstraction we need: `BeadStore` is implemented by both `SqliteBeadStore` (`src/bead_sqlite.rs`) and the Dolt-backed `store_dolt.rs`. A `DoltLiteBeadStore` is a **third impl alongside the existing two**, swappable by config. No big-bang migration; per-repo backend choice. The triage sub-beads in this bead (WAL mode, async Linear push, pool warming) still ship — they're orthogonal cheap wins — but the substrate-level fix changes shape from "harden Dolt server connect logic" to "ship DoltLite adapter."

### Caveats

- **Alpha status** (per DoltHub's own framing — "there will be bugs"). Production-y rosary on alpha software is real risk.
- **"Vibe-coded using Gas Town"** — DoltHub's AI tool. Code-review story is whatever it is. Worth reading the source before committing.
- **No Rust binding** — would need C FFI (modest, well-trodden territory) or wait for community to ship one.
- **On-disk format differs** — migration from existing per-repo Dolt servers to DoltLite files is a one-shot dump+restore, not in-place.

### Recommended next step

File a child research bead: "Spike DoltLite via C FFI as a third `BeadStore` impl, behind a feature flag, single repo at a time." Acceptance: one repo successfully reads + writes via DoltLite, parity tests pass against the Dolt-server impl. Don't commit to migration until parity is proven.

Cross-link: this superseded the "harden the connect logic" framing in [[rosary-11214e]]; the contention bead and the resilience bead converge on DoltLite as the structural answer.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
## Spike step 1 result: keep going on DoltLite

[[rosary-74db16]] Step 1 (FFI smoke test) ran clean — Rust drives `libdoltlite` via standard `extern "C"`, no bindgen needed, `dolt_commit`/`dolt_log` round-trip works. The "Rust binding doesn't exist yet" risk that worried us is dead — we don't need a binding, we need linkage.

The contention question for this bead now reduces to: when DoltLite swaps in, do the 5-concurrent-chat hangs evaporate? Hypothesis: yes (no server, no port, no MySQL protocol round-trip). Tests remain in the spike's Step 2-3 plan: copy `bead_sqlite.rs` → `bead_doltlite.rs`, parity-test, then a concurrent-write stress test against both backends.

Triage sub-beads (WAL mode, async Linear push, pool warming) are still worth filing as cheap wins regardless — DoltLite adoption is a quarter or more out.

title: Reconciler: persist DispatchRecord to backend store at dispatch + completion
description:
The reconciler spawns agents and builds PipelineState but never calls record_dispatch/upsert_dispatch on the backend store. DispatchRecords (including chain_hash) are only logged to dolt events — not persisted to SQLite.

Fix:
1. Add `record_dispatch` + `upsert_dispatch` delegation methods to PipelineEngine (mirrors upsert_state pattern)
2. In reconcile/mod.rs after spawn succeeds: build DispatchRecord from AgentHandle fields and call pipeline.record_dispatch()
3. In completion/verify path: call pipeline.upsert_dispatch() with completed_at + outcome when agent finishes

This closes the loop: chain_hash + workspace_path + session_id are all stored in the backend SQLite, queryable via rsry_dispatch_history MCP tool.

title: dual bead state (feature-local vs global) instead of a merge conflict rule
description:
Surfaced while building the .beads/beads.jsonl git merge driver (rosary-f9516f).

The merge driver's first draft resolved same-id divergence with last-writer-wins on updated_at. That is LOSSY: when two branches genuinely both modified the same bead, one real edit is destroyed with no record it ever existed — silent data loss in a work-tracking store. The driver now refuses to guess (loud conflict) instead, but a conflict rule is only a bandage.

The real defect is representational: the export (and the store behind it) is a single flattened projection, so a branch/feature-local bead transition is indistinguishable from a global one. Two branches writing the same row is treated as a race when it is actually two DIFFERENT facts.

The fix is DUAL STATE: a representation of 'a feature thing happening' (branch/feature-local bead state) kept distinct from 'the global store' (canonical shared state), so neither clobbers the other. Related existing work:
- ADR-0004 (dual state machine: bead lifecycle + pipeline phases)
- ADR-0010 / src/observation/ — already models per-source observations retained + truth DERIVED by fold; stuck at R4b (rosary-a66b3a, persist_status is still the source of truth)
- ADR-0015 execution-lineage capsules

With dual state + op-log semantics, merging becomes a fold over retained observations and the JSONL merge driver becomes unnecessary entirely — the driver is explicitly TRANSITIONAL scaffolding and should be deleted when this lands.
acceptance_criteria: an ADR (or ADR-0010 amendment) that specifies feature-local vs global bead state + op-log/observation semantics, with the merge driver (rosary-f9516f) marked for removal once it lands

title: Pool repo-path lookup misses symlink-aliased repos — get_by_path uses exact path equality, no canonicalize
description:
RepoPool::get_by_path (src/pool.rs:165) matches a caller-supplied repo_path against registered repos with EXACT PathBuf equality (`*path == root`, line 171) and performs NO symlink resolution anywhere in the chain — the doc comment (line 163) even states "no symlink resolution." Chain: repo_path → config::discover_repo_root (walks up for .git, no symlink resolution) → scanner::expand_path (src/scanner.rs:63 = `shellexpand::tilde` ONLY, no canonicalize) → exact-equality loop.

Consequence: when the same physical repo is addressed via a different symlink alias than the one registered, the lookup MISSES → get_by_path returns None → the store reads as "not found" (silent empty search / black-holed op). This is the session-opening symptom ("rsry bead search returns silently empty … symlinked paths suspected") and is actively triggerable in this environment: ~/github/art → ~/remotes/art is a symlink, and BOTH aliases are listed as working dirs. A repo registered under ~/remotes/art/X but looked up via ~/github/art/X (or vice versa) → root=/…/github/art/X ≠ stored /…/remotes/art/X → miss.

NOT data divergence: the physical .beads/beads.db is one file via either alias (symlink transparent at FS layer), so operations that DO reach the store hit one DB. This is a LOOKUP/routing bug. Distinct from (but same family as) rosary-560953 (phantom store when OUTSIDE a repo) — this is symlink-alias INSIDE a repo.

Fix: canonicalize BOTH sides for the comparison only — `root.canonicalize().unwrap_or(root)` vs `path.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| path.clone())` (canonicalize errors on nonexistent paths, so fall back like main.rs:2479 already does). Scope strictly to pool lookup — do NOT disturb the deliberate "expand tilde but do NOT canonicalize" in src/workspace/lifecycle.rs:19 (worktree-redirect semantics). Consider canonicalizing the stored `paths` at registration (from_config/register) so the loop compares canonical-vs-canonical.
acceptance_criteria: A repo registered under a real path is found via a symlink alias and vice versa: unit test creates a tempdir repo + a symlink alias dir, registers the real path, and asserts get_by_path(alias) returns the store (and the reverse). Comparison is canonical-vs-canonical; workspace/lifecycle.rs symlink-preserving behavior unchanged; existing pool tests still pass. cargo fmt/clippy/test clean.

title: Add _meta.art.cloister/v1.groups to root server.json so cloister can derive a valid backend

title: Add `rsry mcp --ipc-socket` mode: capnp ToolCall/ToolResult over UDS
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 from cloister-be0607's architectural decision. cloister's cluster-in-a-pod design wires sibling bundles via capnp-over-UDS instead of HTTP-over-loopback. rosary today exposes `rsry mcp` (stdio) and `rsry mcp --http :8383`; we need a sibling `rsry mcp --ipc-socket /path/to/sock` that speaks the same MCP protocol but over a UDS using capnp ToolCall/ToolResult encoding.

## Context

cloister has two backend kinds for sibling bundles:
- `httpForward` — JSON-RPC over HTTP (today's ROSARY_MCP_URL path)
- `udsForward` — capnp ToolCall over UDS (the new path for cluster-in-a-pod)
- `leylineNet` — signed capnp + AEAD for cross-cluster (not in-pod)

The capnp encoding is already implemented on cloister's side in `src/wire/codec.ts`. Per ADR-0005 amendment, intra-cluster wire skips AEAD — plain capnp framing on a UDS gated by filesystem ACLs.

## Scope

1. New flag `--ipc-socket <path>` on the `rsry mcp` subcommand (analogous to `--http <addr>`):
   - Binds to a Unix Domain Socket at `<path>` (e.g. `/run/cloister-uds/rosary.sock`)
   - Accepts incoming framed capnp messages: `ToolCall` requests, replies with `ToolResult`
   - Same tool dispatch logic as the HTTP path — only the transport + serialization differ
2. The MCP semantics stay identical (same tools — `rsry_bead_*`, `rsry_dispatch`, etc., same arguments, same result content); only the wire format + transport change.
3. Existing `--http` + stdio modes keep working. The three are independent.
4. The capnp framing matches cloister's `src/wire/codec.ts` exactly (length-prefixed messages, ToolCall/ToolResult schemas in `wire/cloister.capnp`).

## Implementation hint

rosary's MCP server is in Rust. capnp has a mature Rust binding (`capnp` + `capnp-rpc` crates). Re-use cloister's schema by importing `cloister/wire/cloister.capnp` into rosary's build, generating Rust types. The dispatch handler is the existing rsry MCP one; only the I/O loop changes.

## Acceptance

- `rsry mcp --ipc-socket /tmp/rosary.sock` starts; a capnp ToolCall written to the socket gets a capnp ToolResult back
- Round-trip test against cloister's `src/wire/codec.ts` decoder — same bytes rosary emits parse cleanly on cloister's side
- The `--http`, `--ipc-socket`, and stdio modes can coexist (start any combination)
- Cross-check fixtures from cloister's `wire/cross-check-fixtures.capnp` validate the byte format

## Refs

- cloister-be0607 — the cluster-in-a-pod deployment that consumes this
- cloister ADR-0005 — internal wire as leyline-net + amendment for intra-cluster plain capnp
- cloister `udsForward` backend kind (already in manifest)
- rosary-08a48e — the umbrella deploy bead this is a sub-task of

title: Expand bead dep model: typed edges + parent-close containment gate + PR-chain surfacing
description:
Three linked gaps found while building rsry init (aaffb0):

1. Per-repo bead 'dependencies' table is (issue_id, depends_on_id) only — no dep_type. The canonical AGENTS.md template advertises blocks/related/parent-child/discovered-from but only 'blocks' exists. Add dep_type column (default 'blocks'), typed add_dependency, get_children query. Makes the template honest.

2. close-merged --local closes ANY non-terminal bead whose id appears in a merge commit — no containment check. A parent/epic with open children auto-closes on one child's PR (this is how rosary-aaffb0 got wrongly closed). Gate: skip close when the bead has open parent-child/discovered-from children (or is a planning type); still record the PR association.

3. The local close path records PR only as free-text comment; the gh path emits a structured pr_url event that a chain view can walk. Local path should emit the same pr_url event so a parent + its children's PRs surface as a chain.

Close condition: task check green; new tests for typed deps + containment gate; template no longer claims nonexistent edge types.

title: Decouple rosary from bd: speak the bead JSON contract, own the store (supersede ADR-0012-layering)
description:
DECISION (from operator): rosary must NOT couple to the `bd` tool or its Dolt storage. Beads are a useful PRIMITIVE; rosary should *speak* the bead format without *being* bd.

Current reality (verified 2026-06-24): rosary already has its own Bead model (src/bead.rs) + SqliteBeadStore + DoltBeadStore (src/bead_sqlite.rs `connect_bead_store`), and invokes the `bd` binary ZERO times at runtime (only spawns `dolt` + `claude`). So rosary already does NOT depend on bd. The problem is the merged ADR `docs/adr/0012-bead-substrate-layering.md`, which DECIDED the opposite ("adopt bd/Dolt as shared store; rosary stops reading .beads/ directly; drive bd --json"). That ADR must be SUPERSEDED.

Why decouple (evidence): bd 1.0.0 removed the SQLite backend and has changed storage layout ~3x in 6 months; coupling rosary's storage to bd inherits that churn (it already stranded ley-line-open's 227 beads from the bd CLI's POV — though rosary reads them fine via beads.db). The upstream Go lib (`github.com/steveyegge/beads`) is Dolt/CGO-bound; there is no Rust binding; DoltLite has no Rust binding. Beads is MIT, so reimplementing the format is fine.

DESIGN: (1) rosary's own store (SQLite beads.db / Dolt server) stays the source of truth. (2) Interop = emit/ingest the DOCUMENTED bead JSON contract (upstream docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md, versioned via schema_version, parse leniently/additively). (3) Live round-trip with a bd-managed repo, IF ever needed, goes behind a thin OPTIONAL adapter shelling `bd ... --json` — never a hard dep. (4) Dolt-server mode remains an option only where concurrent writers (fan-out dispatch) or cloister/multi-machine genuinely need it; single-user local = plain SQLite.

TASKS: supersede 0012-bead-substrate-layering.md (mark Superseded, point to this decision); confirm rosary's Bead model maps to the documented JSON schema for interop; document the "speak beads, don't depend on bd" stance. Relates to cloister (separate bead) + the ADR-0012 number collision.

Test: `task all` green; ADR file shows Status: Superseded with rationale.

comments.text: ADR written + decision recorded in PR #240: new ADR-0014 "Decouple rosary from bd — speak the bead format, own the store" (Accepted); the "adopt bd/Dolt" ADR renumbered 0012→0013 and marked Superseded by 0014 (also resolves the 0012 collision with #238). Doc-accuracy fixes folded in (see rosary-65861c). REMAINING (keep open): confirm rosary's Bead model (src/bead.rs) maps cleanly to the documented bead JSON contract (upstream docs/JSON_SCHEMA.md, schema_version) for import/export interop, and add the thin (de)serialization layer if gaps exist. That's the implementation half of D2.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: Doc accuracy: rosary reads beads via own SQLite/Dolt stores, not bd; fix Dolt-only framing + ADR-0012 number collision
description:
Audit (2026-06-24) found docs present Dolt-over-MySQL as the ONLY bead-storage mechanism and omit the SQLite `beads.db` path that `connect_bead_store` (src/bead_sqlite.rs) actually uses when a repo has no `.beads/dolt/`. Also: rosary does NOT depend on the `bd` binary at runtime (verified: zero invocations) — any doc implying it does is wrong.

Fixes:
- README.md (~:42), docs/GETTING_STARTED.md (~:29-31, :310), CLAUDE.md (:7, :112), docs/CONFIGURATION.md (~:209), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (~:271): state both paths — Dolt server when `.beads/dolt/` exists, else SQLite `beads.db` directly; clarify no `bd` CLI is invoked either way.
- CLAUDE.md Key Source Files table: ADD src/bead_sqlite.rs (`connect_bead_store` entry point + SqliteBeadStore) and src/bead_dolt.rs (DoltBeadStore over Dolt MySQL) — currently omitted though they are the single dispatch point for ALL bead I/O.
- ADR-0012 NUMBER COLLISION: main has 0012-bead-substrate-layering.md; PR #238 adds 0012-personal-bead-substrate.md. Two ADR-0012 files. Renumber one (e.g. layering -> 0013) when superseding it (see the decouple bead).

Test: docs match code; `rg "directly over MySQL"` etc. no longer claim it's the only mechanism.

title: Soften embeddeddolt warning: don't claim "0 beads / cannot read" when beads.db was read fine
description:
src/bead_sqlite.rs (rosary-21e2d4 / #233) warns "[bead] WARNING: ...has a bd embedded-Dolt store (.beads/embeddeddolt) that rsry cannot read ... Reporting 0 beads for this repo is almost certainly WRONG" whenever `.beads/embeddeddolt/` exists. But rosary's SQLite path reads `.beads/beads.db` successfully even when embeddeddolt co-exists (observed live on ley-line-open: warning printed directly above 227 readable beads). The "cannot read / 0 beads" claim is misleading in that case.

Fix: only emit the warning when a read actually returned 0 / failed AND no usable beads.db is present — i.e. gate it on the embeddeddolt being the ONLY store and the read genuinely yielding nothing. When beads.db exists and is readable, either suppress or downgrade to an FYI ("embeddeddolt present but unused; reading beads.db").

Test: a `.beads/` with both embeddeddolt/ and a non-empty beads.db does NOT print the scary "0 beads almost certainly WRONG" warning; a `.beads/` with ONLY embeddeddolt still warns.

comments.text: Scope note: while fixing the warning, also update src/bead_sqlite.rs:135 — its message says "Run `bd init --server` (ADR-0012)", which is now (a) a stale ADR ref (that content is ADR-0013, Superseded) and (b) contrary to the decouple decision (ADR-0014): rsry reads beads.db fine without bd/server mode. New advice should NOT tell users to adopt bd server mode; at most note embeddeddolt is present-but-unused. Also fix the `ADR-0012 D8` comment ref in src/observation/log_sqlite.rs:74 → ADR-0013 (D8 invariants moved with the renumber).

title: refactor(mcp): collapse rsry_decade_list/rsry_thread_list into rsry_list_beads with resource_type+filters
description:
Currently each resource type (beads, threads, decades) is its own MCP tool. This bloats the tool count and is not idiomatic MCP design. A single rsry_list_beads(resource_type, filters...) pattern is cleaner — callers pass resource_type="decade"|"thread"|"bead" and filter params (status, repo, decade_id, etc).

Specifically: rsry_decade_list and rsry_thread_list should become filter params on a unified list endpoint, not separate tools. This also makes it easier to add new resource types without adding new tools.

Related: the current tool count (24+) is already high — each new resource type adding a tool compounds the problem.

title: Scope installation tokens: pass repositories + permissions to fetch_installation_token
description:
fetch_installation_token in src/github.rs currently requests a broad installation token. GitHub's API accepts `repositories` and `permissions` params on POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens to scope the token.

Change: add optional `repositories: Vec<String>` and `permissions: HashMap<String, String>` params to fetch_installation_token. Rosary dispatch passes bead.repo for repositories and a default permission set (contents:write, pull_requests:write) initially. Later, sigpol mapping will drive permissions dynamically.

Prior art: rosary-57c4fb (closed) set up the GitHub App. This extends it with scoped tokens.

title: Configure signet-git in agent worktrees for commit signing
description:
When rosary dispatches an agent to a worktree, configure git for signet commit signing:

```
git config gpg.x509.program signet-git
git config gpg.format x509
git config commit.gpgsign true
```

Also pass the bridge cert path via SIGNET_CERT_PATH env var so signet-git knows which cert to use.

Depends on: per-dispatch bridge cert minting (rosary-d5c61f) to provide the cert.

title: rsry_dispatch leaves bead status stuck at in_progress when worktree is removed pre-spawn
description:
## Reproduction

1. Call `rsry_dispatch <bead>` MCP tool — this prepares a worktree at `~/.rsry/worktrees/<repo>/<bead>/`, advances the bead status to `in_progress`, and returns a `claude -p ...` command for the caller to spawn.
2. The caller decides not to spawn (e.g. switching strategies) and removes the worktree via `git worktree remove --force`.
3. The bead is now stuck in `in_progress` forever — `rsry status` still counts it as active even though no agent is or ever was running on it.

## Surfaced

Hit this directly today: dispatched 5 obs-* beads in parallel to test the dispatch path, decided to implement Layer 1 in a single PR instead, removed the worktrees. Five beads then sat at `in_progress` until I reopened them manually via the new `rsry bead reopen` CLI (which only exists because of an unrelated PR — without it I'd have needed direct dolt SQL).

## Why it matters

The `in_progress` status is a queue-management signal — triage skips in_progress beads, statusline shows them as active work, dispatcher won't redispatch them. A stale `in_progress` is invisible-but-harmful state.

## Possible fixes

1. **Symmetric cleanup**: when a worktree is removed and its dispatch record was never marked started/completed, revert the bead's status to whatever it was pre-dispatch. Hook into `git worktree remove` somehow (filesystem watcher, or sweep on next reconciler tick).
2. **Time-based recovery**: a sweeper that scans dispatched-but-no-process beads after N minutes and reverts them. The reconciler already has `recover_stuck_beads` patterns — extend that.
3. **Two-phase dispatch**: `rsry_dispatch` only prepares the worktree (no status write); a second `rsry_dispatch_start` confirms the agent has spawned. The MCP caller is responsible for the second call. Cleaner contract but breaks current behavior.

(2) is probably the lightest-touch fix. The reconciler's existing recovery path already handles dead PIDs; extending it to cover never-spawned dispatches is a small addition.

## Test command

cargo test --bin rsry recover_stuck_beads

title: close-merged: full-history git-log backfill (catch beads from periods when reconciler was off)
description:
## Why

`rsry close-merged` (PR #185) walks open beads and checks their recorded PR URL. Live run on the user's config showed `checked=426 no_pr_url=426` — none of the 426 open beads have a PR URL recorded. Means historical merges (32 stalled needs_merge beads from Q1 2026) can't be reconciled by the existing primitives.

`scan_vcs` only looks at the last 50 commits. `poll_pr_status` only checks `pr_open` beads. `close-merged` only works if a PR URL was recorded at some point.

For periods when the reconciler was off, none of these fire. Need a one-shot full-history sweep.

## Proposed

A new `rsry close-merged --backfill` flag (or sibling `rsry sync-merges`). For each registered repo:

1. `git log --merges --all` (or jj equivalent) for ALL history, not just last 50
2. Extract `[bead-id]` references from merge commit messages (and PR-merge squash messages — `(#NNN)` style)
3. For each bead-id found in a merge commit:
   - If bead is open, look up `gh pr view` state to confirm MERGED (avoid false positives from non-merge commits referencing the id)
   - Close the bead with merge SHA + comment

Could also handle the case where the bead has no recorded PR URL: fall back to `gh search prs --query '[bead-id] in:title'` to find the PR.

## Files

- `src/main.rs` — extend `Command::CloseMerged` with `--backfill` flag OR new command
- `src/vcs.rs` — new `scan_vcs_full_history(repo)` function
- Reuses `gh pr view` from existing close-merged path

## Tests

- `backfill_finds_old_merge_commit` — git fixture with a merge from 6 months ago, assert close
- `backfill_falls_back_to_gh_search` — bead with no recorded PR URL, but matching PR exists upstream
- `backfill_skips_non_merge_commits_referencing_bead` — merge SHA must come from a merge commit

## Caveats

- `gh search` is rate-limited
- For large repos, `git log --all --merges` may be slow — gate by `--since` flag
- A bead-id mentioned in a non-merge commit (e.g., a fix-up commit) shouldn't trigger close — only count merge commits

## Related

- PR #185 (close-merged primitive)
- rosary-c6386e (3-loop split; this likely lands in the observer loop's catch-up phase)
- The 32 stalled needs_merge beads diagnosed 2026-05-09

title: bead CLI/MCP discoverability: no 'bead show', --title rejected, comment needs 'add' — agents work AROUND beads not through them
description:
Reported by a dispatched agent working in ley-line-open, and INDEPENDENTLY hit by a second session the same day — so this is reproducible friction, not preference.

WHAT WORKED (keep it): picking up a bead mid-session and getting correct orientation from the description alone — the precise function/line to change, why the naive approach was wrong, an explicit "slow down and design first". The reasoning survived the handoff, not just the diff. Same on close: a real summary (what broke, how found, how verified) means the next session starts from a narrative rather than a squashed commit message. The commit-msg hook requiring a bead ref was described as "a real guardrail, not a suggestion" — it blocked a commit until a bead was filed, which is the right failure mode.

FRICTION (the actionable part):

1. `bead create --title "..."` FAILS — title is positional. Both agents tried --title first and had to iterate against --help. (Confirmed first-hand this session.)
2. `bead comment <id> <body>` does not work — requires the `add` subcommand. Discovered the same way.
3. NO `bead show <id>`. Getting one bead's full description requires `bead list --json` + client-side filtering. `bead review` exists but returns workspace/evidence sections, NOT the description text — so the command whose name implies "show me this bead" returns something else.

Quote: "it was the one moment beads felt like infrastructure I was working around instead of through."

WHY #3 IS THE REAL ONE: the whole value above comes from a bead's DESCRIPTION carrying the reasoning. There is no first-class way to read exactly that for a single bead. The most valuable field has the least direct accessor.

SUSPECTED CONTRIBUTING CAUSE (unverified — needs checking, do not assume): the MCP tool descriptions may mis-signal shape, so an agent guesses `--title`/flat-comment/`review` by analogy instead of reading help. Worth diffing what the MCP tools ADVERTISE against what the CLI actually accepts — if they disagree, that is the same class as rosary-882154 (dep_type advertised nowhere) and the ADR-0021 drift problem: N surfaces describing one operation differently.

SUGGESTED:
- Add `rsry bead show <id>` printing the full description (+ `--json`). Point rsry_ticket_load / rsry_review docs at it.
- Accept `--title` as an alias for the positional (or emit a targeted error naming the positional form).
- Accept `bead comment <id> <body>` as shorthand for `comment add`.
- Audit MCP tool descriptions vs actual CLI/handler signatures for the same drift class.

comments.text:
REFRAME (user): "it's prob a smell w/ how we disclose our tooling". That is a better diagnosis than the missing-command framing above, and the help output corroborates it.

VERIFIED — what a fresh agent actually sees from `rsry bead --help`:

  list     "List beads with optional filters (rosary-e1c759). Defaults to the active (open) set;
            pass `--status all` ... the active-only default is why closed/done beads were invisible here"
  review   "Compose the agent-native review panel for a bead ... Phase 0 of rosary-ccd5a2
            (`rsry review` substrate)"

These are CHANGELOG ENTRIES AND RATIONALE, not affordances. They cite bead ids and past incidents, addressing a reader who already knows the system. An agent scanning for "how do I read one bead's description" sees archaeology and guesses by analogy — which is exactly how you get `--title`, flat `comment`, and picking `review` for the wrong job.

So the defect class is DISCLOSURE, not just a missing subcommand:
- Help text optimized for the maintainer's memory (why it changed) instead of the caller's decision (what it does / when to pick it).
- The same drift as rosary-882154 (dep_type advertised nowhere) and ADR-0021 (N surfaces each re-describing one operation): here the surface is the HELP/TOOL DESCRIPTION, and it has drifted from being a usable interface into being a commit log.

This widens the fix: adding `bead show` alone would not stop the next agent guessing, because the guessing is caused by descriptions that do not disclose. Worth auditing every `rsry bead` subcommand + MCP tool description against the question "could a caller who has never seen this repo pick the right command from this line alone?" — and moving the rosary-id rationale into doc comments rather than the user-facing one-liner.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: rsry bead show <id> exists and prints the full description (+--json); bead create accepts --title as an alias or errors with the correct positional form; bead comment <id> <body> works without the add subcommand; a check compares MCP tool descriptions against actual CLI/handler arg shapes and fails on drift

title: Bug: git worktree branches from stale local main, not origin/main
description:
create_git_worktree (workspace/sweep.rs:86) does `git worktree add -b fix/id` without fetching first. If local main is behind origin/main, the worktree starts from stale code. Agents then include changes already merged to remote main in their diff.

This caused 4 duplicate PRs (#26-28, #39) in the overnight dispatch session — agents independently re-did work that was already merged because they branched from old main.

Fix: `git fetch origin main` before `git worktree add`, and branch from `origin/main` explicitly:
```
git worktree add <path> -b fix/id origin/main
```

This is a P0 for dispatch reliability — every dispatch from a stale repo produces garbage diffs.

title: Establish coverage baseline (line + branch) as a committed ratchet — prerequisite to safe decomposition
description: Before breaking apart mega-files (handoff.rs 854 LOC, and others once the smell gate tightens), stand up a coverage ratchet mirroring the mache smell-baseline pattern: cargo-llvm-cov with BRANCH coverage on, a committed docs/coverage-baseline.json, and a 'task coverage' gate that fails when coverage drops below baseline. This is the falsifiable safety net that lets a decomposition PR prove it preserved behavior (no dropped branch) rather than hope it did. Branch coverage specifically matters for refactors — moving code around must keep every branch exercised. Blocks the handoff.rs split.

comments.text: LANDMINE / prior art: rosary-5732ee flags that a previous agent FABRICATED coverage numbers (claimed 110/6/0 lines on a 'PR #397' that does not exist). Confirmed: NO coverage tooling is in the repo today (zero llvm-cov/tarpaulin in Taskfile.yml or workflows). So this is the FIRST real coverage attempt, not a redo. Design implication — anti-fabrication by construction: the baseline must be GENERATED by the tool (cargo llvm-cov --json), committed as data, and the gate must RE-RUN the tool and compare — never a human/agent-typed number. A committed lcov that CI regenerates cannot be faked (unlike 5732ee). Supersedes/absorbs the concern in rosary-5732ee.

title: Conductor timeout bug: Port.close doesn't deliver exit_status, worker hangs forever
description:
In agent_worker.ex:167, handle_info(:timeout) calls provider().stop_process(state.port) which calls Port.close. But Port.close invalidates the port handle — it does NOT deliver {port, {:exit_status, code}}. The worker stays in :noreply state indefinitely, never advancing to retry or deadletter. The slot stays occupied forever.

The comment on line 170 says "Port/process close will trigger exit_status message" — this is incorrect.

Fix: after Port.close, explicitly send self() a synthetic exit message, or use Port.info to get the OS PID and kill(pid, SIGTERM) then let the real exit_status flow.

Found by theoretical-foundations-analyst during PTY spawn analysis.

title: Mache-powered verify tiers: blast radius + duplication via MCP stdio
description:
Extend the Verifier tier pipeline with mache-powered structural checks that run locally before CI.

## Context

Current verify pipeline: CommitCheck → BeadRefCheck → compile → test → lint → DiffSanityCheck → ReviewCheck (LLM judge on diff). No structural intelligence — can't see blast radius, detect duplication, or give the LLM judge architectural context.

Mache is available as CLI (mache build, mache serve --stdio) AND as MCP server. Both are valid integration points — the verifier can spawn mache serve --stdio as a subprocess MCP client, same pattern as how rosary exposes its own tools.

## New tiers

### MacheBlastRadiusCheck { max_caller_modules: usize }
- mache build --out /tmp/rsry-{bead_id}.db {work_dir}
- mache serve --stdio /tmp/...db → minimal MCP stdio client
- Extract changed public symbols from git diff
- Call get_impact(symbol, depth=2) for each
- Combined impact > max_caller_modules → Partial(advisory)
- Fail-open if mache unavailable

### MacheDuplicationCheck { similarity_threshold: f32 }
- Reuse mache snapshot from blast radius check
- Extract added code chunks from diff
- search(pattern) for representative identifiers
- Near-match in unrelated file → Partial(near-dup: {path})

### LlmStructuralReview (extends ReviewCheck)
- Same claude -p call but with mache context prepended:
  blast radius + get_architecture() output
- LLM judge has structural visibility, not just the diff
- Feature-tier discriminator: 'does this assembled feature fit the architecture?'

## Integration

- Dev tier: MacheBlastRadiusCheck + MacheDuplicationCheck
- Feature tier (assemble_feature_prs): LlmStructuralReview with mache context
- MCP stdio transport: initialize + tools/call + parse JSON — no port conflicts, lifecycle tied to check

## Implementation

1. Minimal MCP stdio client in Rust (or thin CLI wrapper if mache adds query subcommand)
2. build_mache_snapshot(work_dir) -> Result<TempPath> helper
3. Three tier impls
4. Wire into Verifier::for_language + assemble_feature_prs feature-tier verifier

Note: VerifyResult::Partial for advisory findings (blast radius, duplication) — not hard Fail

comments.text:
Implementation note correction: mache already has a full SSE/Streamable HTTP transport running at localhost:7532. No need to build an MCP stdio client or spawn mache serve --stdio subprocesses.

Revised integration approach:
- Check if mache HTTP server is available (GET localhost:7532, fail-open if not)
- POST tools/call to localhost:7532/mcp with appropriate repo context
- Read SSE stream for response, parse JSON result
- This is just HTTP + SSE — much simpler than a full stdio MCP client

The 'minimal MCP client' work in the original description reduces to: a small HTTP client that knows how to POST a tools/call and read an SSE response. Could be ~50 lines of reqwest + eventsource parsing.

build_mache_snapshot() is also not needed — the running HTTP server already has the repo indexed. Just call get_impact / search directly against the live graph.
