title: Design: agent working notes as a first-class artifact type (docs vs work)
description:
## Observation

Today rosary tracks two artifact types:
- **Beads** = work items (dispatchable, enter pipelines, have status)
- **ADRs** = decisions (markdown, decomposable via BDR)

There's a third category with no home: **working analysis**. Agent investigation notes, mathematical proofs, experiment findings, validation results, architectural explorations. These aren't tasks to complete or decisions to record — they're evidence that informs both.

Currently dumped to `_agent_logs/` (gitignored) and lost between sessions.

## Questions (not answers)

- Is this a new bead `issue_type` (e.g. `analysis`, `research_note`, `evidence`)? If so, it lives in Dolt, gets comments, links to parent beads, but never enters a dispatch pipeline.
- Or is it a separate artifact type entirely — closer to CRUMB discoveries than beads?
- Should analysis artifacts be version-controlled (they're findings, not scratch) or ephemeral (they decay as the codebase changes)?
- How does this relate to CRUMB's semantic capture? CRUMB stores discoveries as tagged entries. Agent logs are longer-form, structured analysis. Overlap?
- What's the lifecycle? Created by analysis agents, consumed by implementation agents and humans, archived when the parent bead closes?

## Adjacent concerns

- `rsry_decompose` output should be reviewed before creating beads — the parser can mistype atoms (consequences as tasks, open questions as features). A human or PM agent review step is needed between decompose and bead creation.
- BDR's `BeadSpec` has `issue_type` and `priority` derived from `AtomKind` — but the mapping is mechanical. A review pass would catch misclassifications.

## Related

- _agent_logs/ directory (gitignored scratch space, current stopgap)
- CRUMB semantic capture (~/remotes/art/crumb)
- BDR decompose review workflow
- Pre-flight pipeline (readiness validation before dispatch)

title: Repo addressing has no canonical identity — symlink aliasing and multi-tenant are the same bug; unify behind a resolve(address, context) → RepoIdentity seam
description:
ROOT CAUSE (generalizes rosary-617010): rosary keys/compares repos by their SURFACE ADDRESS instead of resolving the address to a canonical IDENTITY first. Two mirror-image manifestations of the one bug:

- Symlink aliasing (many addresses → one repo): ~/github/art/X vs ~/remotes/art/X are one physical repo; get_by_path compared paths literally and missed the alias (rosary-617010, patched narrowly by canonicalizing in get_by_path).
- Multi-tenant (one address → many repos): `repo:X` names different physical repos per user; the LOCAL path assumes address==identity (single-tenant) via RepoPool/pool.get, while the HOSTED path (tool_repo_register, handlers/mod.rs:2965 "requires user identity … mcp.rosary.bot") bolts tenant on as a SEPARATE code path. Addressing diverges local-vs-cloud for no essential reason — only *whether a tenant is present* is essential.

THE FIX — one seam, not two paths. Introduce a canonical `RepoIdentity` and a `resolve(address, context) → RepoIdentity` resolver, where path-canonicalization (symlink axis) and tenant-qualification (tenant axis) are both resolution steps. `RepoIdentity` always carries a tenant dimension; LOCAL is the degenerate `tenant = None` (or a fixed local tenant), CLOUD is `tenant = user`. Route BOTH scope-based addressing (ScopeId/resolve_scope, src/serve/scope_args.rs — the existing front half of the seam) and repo_path lookups (pool.get_by_path) through the resolver, then key/compare on RepoIdentity. Local backend lands + is testable now (folds in rosary-617010's canonicalization); the hosted backend conforms to the identical interface (cloud-side, mcp.rosary.bot, not locally testable). Separate concerns: the resolver does RESOLUTION; RepoPool is demoted to CONNECTION CACHING keyed by RepoIdentity — untangling the two also fixes the boot-snapshot staleness (a live LocalRegistry read means `rsry enable` is visible without a server restart).

META: 4th instance this session of a partial abstraction (ScopeId here; also the observation lattice, BeadStore trait, reconciler-derived-status) not promoted to THE seam, so a special-case path drifts alongside it. Links: rosary-617010 (subsumed symlink axis), rosary-b5da2f (genericness audit — repo_path-keyed 30%).
acceptance_criteria: A single resolve(address, context) → RepoIdentity path serves BOTH scope:"repo:X" and repo_path; RepoIdentity canonicalizes symlink aliases (subsumes rosary-617010's test) and carries a tenant dimension (None locally). RepoPool caches connections keyed by RepoIdentity, not raw path/name; resolution is a separate unit. A repo `rsry enable`d after server boot resolves via scope without a restart (live config read). Hosted backend implements the same trait (stubbed/feature-gated if not locally testable). Existing pool + scope tests pass; new tests: alias resolves, tenant-qualified identities don't collide, post-enable scope resolution works. fmt/clippy/test clean.

title: Generic local-SQLite ↔ remote bead-store sync via Turso embedded replicas (rides ADR-0020)
description:
DECISION (2026-07-22): the 'sync local db to remote regularly' capability — instead of a bespoke CF-D1 ingest Worker — rides TURSO (libSQL embedded replicas), because it's the solved SQLite-with-sync primitive AND unifies the whole stack: rosary beads + mache arena + cloister state all become libSQL, all sync via the same mechanism (the operator's 'fit cloister / rest of my stack / keep my things').

Enabled by two things that just landed / are landing:
1. rosary migrated Dolt->SQLite (ADR-0021, 2026-07-22) — beads are now a SQLite VALUE, so libSQL embedded-replica sync applies (Dolt couldn't).
2. Turso as the LLO arena storage layer — ley-line-open-4aeb4f (this bead DEPENDS ON it).

Rides the semantic-file north-star: today it replicates the SQLite projection; when beads are values in the leyline substrate, the same seam becomes a CAS chunk-diff (the wire projection) with no interface change.

CAVEAT (tracked on 4aeb4f): libSQL doesn't support sqlite3_deserialize, which the arena's zero-copy projection needs — gates whether Turso is the arena engine vs a sync sidecar. For rosary's bead store (no deserialize projection needed), Turso-as-replica is clean; the deserialize gap only bites the mache-arena side.
acceptance_criteria: A generic "sync a local SQLite bead store ↔ remote, on a schedule" seam: rosary opens .beads/beads.db as a Turso/libSQL embedded replica syncing to a remote, single-writer per operator. Repo-parameterized so any repo reuses it. Test: a local write propagates to the remote and a fresh replica sees it. Conflict-freeness rides ADR-0020 content-addressed identity, not bespoke resolution.

title: Language-aware pre-commit hooks at dispatch time — catch buggy code before verify
description:
## Problem

Insights analysis shows buggy_code is the #1 friction source (118 instances). Agents commit broken code, verify catches it, reconciler retries — wasting a full dispatch cycle. A pre-commit hook that runs `cargo check` (Rust) or `go vet` (Go) would catch these at commit time, before the agent even finishes.

## Design

At dispatch time, rosary already:
- Detects repo language (reconcile/helpers::detect_language)
- Writes .rsry-bead-id to worktree
- Sets core.hooksPath to ~/.rsry/hooks/
- Writes .git/info/exclude for artifacts

Add: generate a pre-commit hook script in the worktree's hookspath that runs language-specific checks:

```bash
# ~/.rsry/hooks/pre-commit (generated per-dispatch)
#!/bin/sh
# Language: rust (detected by rosary)
cargo check 2>&1 | head -20
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "pre-commit: cargo check failed — fix before committing"
  exit 1
fi
```

Language detection sources (in priority order):
1. rosary's detect_language (Cargo.toml, go.mod)
2. mache MCP get_overview (if projected — knows the language from tree-sitter)
3. GitHub API languages endpoint (if mache not available)

## What this catches

- Rust: compilation errors, type mismatches, missing imports
- Go: vet errors, unused imports, unreachable code
- Both: syntax errors that would fail tier 2 (compile) in verify

## Integration

- dispatch.rs: after writing .rsry-bead-id, generate pre-commit hook based on detected language
- reconcile/helpers.rs: detect_language already exists
- verify.rs: Verifier::for_language already maps language → check commands (reuse the same mapping)

The hook generation should share the command list with Verifier::for_language — DRY between "check before commit" and "verify after agent completes".

title: Competitive landscape: autonomous orchestrators survey (Gas Town, Sweep, Devin, OpenHands, SWE-agent)
description: rosary competes in the orchestrator space. Survey: Gas Town/Wasteland (Yegge), Sweep (AI junior dev), Devin (Cognition), OpenHands (open-source Devin), SWE-agent (Princeton), Aider (Paul Gauthier), Cline, Roo Code. Focus on: dispatch model, verification, multi-repo, trust/review, cost model. What does rosary have that they dont (per-repo beads, mache ACI, cross-model review, Dolt versioning)? What do they have that rosary needs?

comments.text:
Completed competitive landscape research for 9 orchestrators/agents. Wrote findings to docs/competitive-landscape-orchestrators-2026.md.

Systems surveyed: Gas Town/Wasteland (Yegge), Sweep, Devin (Cognition), OpenHands, SWE-agent (Princeton), Aider, Cline, Roo Code, Claude Code.

Each entry covers: dispatch model, verification model, multi-repo support, trust/review model, cost model, what rosary has that they don't, and what they have that rosary needs.

Key findings:
- Closest architectural competitor is Gas Town (shares beads concept, worktree isolation, multi-agent dispatch). Wasteland federated trust network is most advanced trust model in space.
- Rosary has the strongest verification pipeline (5-tier automated) and most structured work decomposition (BDR: decades/threads/beads) of any system surveyed.
- Main gaps: no IDE integration, no sandboxed execution, no federated trust model, no formal benchmark scores.
- Market splitting into IDE-embedded agents (Cline/Roo/Aider/Claude Code) vs autonomous orchestrators (Rosary/Gas Town/Devin/OpenHands). Rosary sits firmly in tier 2.
- Claude Code is more runtime dependency than competitor — rosary dispatches it as an agent provider.

title: jj+git colocated workflow: defensive hooks and skill
description:
## Problem
In colocated jj+git repos, agents (and Claude Code) create/modify files that jj auto-snapshots into git's index. This causes git operations (stash, pull, rebase) to fail with "unstaged changes" errors. The fix is running `jj status` to re-snapshot, but this is non-obvious and blocks workflow.

## Scope
1. Skill for jj+git workflow operations (diagnose desync, pull, cleanup)
2. Git hooks / pre-commit integration for defensive handling
3. Agent awareness — use jj commands in colocated repos (PR #17 pattern)

title: Substrate: BDR + lattice + reconciliation as one substrate (observations from N sources, joined into derived truth)
description:
## The unifying frame

Reconciliation isn't a sync problem. It's a **lattice problem**: every external source (Linear, GitHub, beads, git, fork-state, Slack, Notion, ...) emits observations of the same underlying work. BDR is the decomposition that determines the *grain*. The lattice is the *substrate* that holds observations and computes the join. Progressive disclosure is the *read pattern* — you query at any time and get the current join.

Today rosary treats beads as the source of truth and tries to push/pull state to/from Linear and GitHub. The right shape inverts that: **every source is a peer; rosary is the merge layer.**

## How it should feel to the user

NOT "run `rsry sync`". The user said: *"I would like to be able to just... keep it synced w/ the world when I connect."*

The substrate is **ambient**:
- Long-running observer daemons (one per source) subscribe to webhooks where the source supports it (zero rate-limit cost, immediate)
- Fall back to polling only where webhooks aren't available, with exponential backoff and explicit rate budgets per source
- "When I connect" doesn't mean a command runs — it means the daemons have been observing in your absence and the lattice already reflects current state. The user just queries it.

`rsry status` becomes a read against the lattice, not a sync trigger.

## Constraint: legit aggressive automation looks like attacks

Author's [notme.bot/why](https://notme.bot/why) documents the failure mode: in March 2026, rosary's 235 workflow runs across 10 repos in 7 days from one GitHub identity got auto-flagged as a crypto miner. Real-world supply-chain attacks (hackerbot-claw, Trivy, axios npm) made GitHub's heuristics jumpy. Legitimate agent activity is structurally indistinguishable from attacker activity at the network/auth layer.

This means the substrate **must**:

1. **Carry verifiable identity per observation.** Use signet ephemeral certs (rosary-d5c61f / rosary-315e7c) so GitHub etc. see "rosary actor X with signet cert Y", not anonymous high-volume requests.
2. **Use webhooks before polling.** Webhooks are server-pushed → zero rate impact + immediate. Polling only where unavoidable.
3. **Rate-budget every observer.** A daemon that polls Linear every 30s for 100 issues forever is the exact pattern that gets flagged.
4. **Distinguish read observations from write actions.** Reads are cheap and ambient. Writes (commits, PRs, comments) are gated, attributed via notme identity, and rate-limited harder.
5. **Backoff on flag signals.** If a source returns 429 or unusual error rates, the observer goes quiet and surfaces the situation instead of retrying in a tight loop.

This isn't paranoia — it's the lesson the author paid for in the March incident.

## What's already in place

- **rosary-45518d (CRDT-lattice bead state ADR)** — append-only `observations` table; status derived via lattice join over (bead_id, agent, phase, verdict, content_hash). Atoms exist; the join doesn't.
- **BDR decomposition** (`crates/bdr/`) — ADR markdown / docs → atoms → beads → threads → decades. Maps a coarse spec onto concrete work units.
- **Per-source observation paths** — `scan_vcs`, `poll_pr_status`, Linear push (`persist_status`), GitHub webhook → bead state. Each is a one-off polling/push, not a feed into a lattice.
- **rosary-c6386e (3-loop split)** — observer / dispatcher / linear-sync. The observer is where new feeds plug in.
- **notme.bot + signet** — author-owned identity primitives that the substrate consumes.

## What's missing

### 1. Observation as a first-class type

Every source pushes the same shape:

```rust
struct Observation {
    work_ref: WorkRef,           // (repo, scope, bead_id) OR a higher-level identifier
    source: Source,              // linear | github | git | bead-store | slack | ...
    field: Field,                // status | assignee | pr_url | ahead_behind | ...
    value: Value,                // typed; supports last-write-wins or set semantics
    observed_at: DateTime<Utc>,  // when the source was observed
    actor_cert: Option<Cert>,    // signet ephemeral cert that authorized this read
    content_hash: [u8; 32],      // for dedup + invariant checks
}
```

Each external source has an **observer task** that emits observations on its own cadence, identified via signet, gated by per-source rate budgets.

### 2. Webhook-first, polling-fallback per observer

Each observer declares its capabilities:
```rust
trait Observer {
    fn source(&self) -> Source;
    fn webhook_endpoint(&self) -> Option<&str>;  // if Some, register and idle
    fn poll_interval(&self) -> Duration;          // fallback when webhook unavailable
    fn rate_budget(&self) -> RateBudget;          // per-minute / per-hour caps
    async fn ingest_webhook(&self, payload: Value) -> Result<Vec<Observation>>;
    async fn poll(&self) -> Result<Vec<Observation>>;
}
```

The runtime registers webhooks at startup, polls in the gaps. Rate budgets enforced at the runtime layer, not per-observer.

### 3. Cross-source identity (the join key)

A Linear issue, GitHub PR, and rosary bead are observations of the same thing. We need durable mappings:

- `bead.external_ref` already exists — Linear ID, GitHub PR URL
- Generalize: `links` table `(bead_id, source, source_id)` with multi-source membership
- BDR atoms can carry source-link metadata to bridge "this section of the design doc IS this Linear issue IS this PR"

### 4. Derived view = lattice join

Status, assignee, deadlines, etc. are not stored on the bead — they're **computed** from observations. Conflicting observations surface explicitly: "Linear says in-review, GitHub PR is closed-without-merge, last-observed delta 18 hours."

### 5. Fork / remote staleness as observations

The user's example: "knowing if my fork on org/repo is out of date." That's a `git_remote_observer` emitting `(repo, remote, ahead, behind, last_fetched_at)`. The fork query is a lattice read, not a poll.

### 6. Identity-attributed writes

When the dispatcher (or any rosary loop) writes back — a comment, a PR, a status push — it carries a signet cert + notme identity attribution in the user-agent / commit author / API headers. Sources can verify the actor instead of relying on anonymous high-volume request heuristics.

### 7. Progressive disclosure as the read pattern

When the user reconnects (or runs `rsry status --diff`), rosary:
1. Reads the current lattice (no polling triggered — observers run continuously in the background)
2. Reports the diff: what changed since you last looked, what conflicts surfaced, what's gone stale
3. Optionally triggers a "freshen now" pass on specific observers for stale items

## What this means for current work

- **rosary-c6386e** (3-loop split) → become **N webhook-receivers + N pollers + 1 lattice joiner + 1 dispatcher**, not 3.
- **rosary-455f07** (auto/ → backlog/ rename) → "backlog" beads are the lowest-fidelity observation grain.
- **rosary-45a6f9** (triage agent) → operates on the lattice, promotes/demotes backlog observations.
- **rosary-67dc2c** (close-merged backfill) → just one observer (git-log) feeding the lattice.
- **rosary-9c4c7a** (Event bus + bead correlation for webhook/CC channel events from rig) → this IS the webhook receiver substrate. Should be folded in.
- **rosary-d5c61f** (per-dispatch bridge cert) — must land before write-attribution can carry signet identity.

## What rosary should look like for the user's company use case

Continuous: webhook listener for Linear, GitHub, and any registered source runs in the rosary daemon. Lattice updates as events arrive.

Periodic (with rate budget): polling for sources that don't push.

User surface: `rsry status` shows lattice state. Conflicts and staleness highlighted. No commands required for routine sync.

Example output:
```
$ rsry status
Recent (last 4h via webhooks):
  ✓ AGE-123 / rosary-abc — PR #45 merged, bead closed
  ⚠ AGE-456 / rosary-def — Linear says "Done" but PR #46 is still open
  
Stale (last polled >24h):
  ↑ x-ray fork: 14 commits behind upstream/main (last fetch 2d ago)
  ↑ ley-line fork: 3 commits behind

Pending dispatch (unchanged):
  rosary-xyz (P0, 2d in queue, awaiting approval)
```

## Files (no implementation in this bead — it's the substrate ADR)

- `docs/adr/0010-observation-lattice.md` — write the ADR formalizing this
- `src/observer/mod.rs` — observer trait + scheduler + rate budgeter (new module)
- `src/lattice.rs` — lattice join over Observations (new module, builds on rosary-45518d's observation table)
- `src/store.rs` — extend ObservationStore with multi-source semantics + signet-cert column

## Dependencies

- rosary-45518d (CRDT-lattice ADR) — must accept this design first
- rosary-c6386e (3-loop split) — generalize "3 loops" to "N observers"
- rosary-9c4c7a (event bus / webhook receiver) — substrate for the webhook side
- rosary-d5c61f (per-dispatch bridge cert) — substrate for write-attribution
- BDR atoms (`crates/bdr/`) — keep using them as the decomposition mechanism
- notme.bot + signet (author-owned) — identity primitives the substrate consumes

## Tests

- `lattice_join_resolves_two_sources_agreeing` — Linear says in-review, GitHub says in-review → joined view in-review
- `lattice_join_surfaces_conflict` — Linear says done, GitHub PR closed-without-merge → conflict surfaced explicitly, not silently picked
- `observation_dedup_by_content_hash` — same observation from same source twice → stored once
- `git_remote_observer_emits_ahead_behind` — fixture repo, observer reports correct delta
- `rate_budget_blocks_excessive_polling` — observer at limit pauses, doesn't tight-loop
- `webhook_receiver_dedups_replays` — same payload twice → one observation
- `signet_cert_attached_to_write_observation` — write actions carry verifiable identity

## Why filing this

Today's work surfaced this need:
- 32 stalled `needs_merge` beads — the observer for git merges wasn't running
- 426 open beads with no PR URL recorded — the GitHub observer never fired
- The user wants "fork-out-of-date" surfacing — that's the same lattice query
- Linear sync today is push-only; should be bidirectional via observations
- BDR decomposition produces atoms with no path to mark "this atom is now this Linear issue" — needs the source-link table
- The author's March 2026 GitHub flagging makes "polling everything aggressively" actively dangerous — webhook-first + rate-budgeted + identity-attributed is the only viable shape

Filing now so the implementation work can be staged: write the ADR → land the observer framework → port existing one-off paths into observers → wire the lattice join.

## Related

- rosary-45518d (CRDT-lattice ADR — substrate)
- rosary-c6386e (3-loop split — re-shapes into N observers)
- rosary-9c4c7a (event bus + webhook correlation — webhook substrate)
- rosary-67dc2c (close-merged backfill — becomes one observer)
- rosary-455f07 (backlog rename)
- rosary-45a6f9 (triage agent)
- rosary-d5c61f (per-dispatch bridge cert — write attribution)
- rosary-13af35 (reactive persistent store — another piece of the substrate)
- [notme.bot/why](https://notme.bot/why) — context for why ambient ≠ aggressive polling

title: Janitor agent: cron-based codebase hygiene checks
description:
A scheduled agent that runs periodically to check for:
- God files (>500 lines, too many responsibilities — e.g. serve.rs)
- Dead code (functions with zero callers via mache)
- Stale beads (open > 30 days with no comments)
- File scope drift (bead files no longer exist)
- Structural violations (modules exceeding complexity thresholds)
- Doc drift (README/CLAUDE.md claims that don't match code)

Scope: broad (sees everything). Reign: narrow (can only create beads and comment, cannot edit code or dispatch). This is the staging-agent perspective applied to the codebase itself, run on a cron schedule.

Output: creates beads for findings, comments on existing stale beads, produces a summary report.

title: Dep-story / crate-workspacing strategy for the ART ecosystem (divergent versions, git-rev pinning, no shared workspace)
description: Surfaced concretely during the hashing centralization (context-substrate): adopting CURRENT ley-line-open pulls leyline-fs 0.6.0 → rusqlite ^0.39, conflicting with rosary's rusqlite 0.34 — so we rev-pin leyline-core independently instead of updating the whole source. That's a workaround, not a strategy. The real problem: the ecosystem's crates (rosary, leyline-*, mache-adjacent, etc.) have DIVERGENT dependency versions, are consumed via floating git deps (one rev per source URL), and share no unified workspace/version policy. Symptoms: rusqlite 0.34 vs 0.39; rosary rev-pinned to an OLD ley-line-open (ccb4409f) that predates leyline-core's ContentAddressed impl; two ley-line-open checkouts in one build (leyline-vcs@old + leyline-core@pinned). Questions to answer: (1) shared workspace vs published crates vs git-rev discipline; (2) a version/rev policy (pin-to-tag? renovate? a meta-lock?); (3) who owns the shared substrate crates' release cadence; (4) how rosary tracks LLO without a rusqlite lockstep. NOT blocking the substrate work (rev-pin unblocks it) but must be solved before deep LLO adoption. Discovered-from context-substrate / rosary-bf6c74.

comments.text: LLO divisibility finding (answering 'can we share LLO for deps + separate the rest'): LLO is ALREADY well-shaped for this — ll-core/leyline-core is a LIGHT substrate (Hash/CAS/BlobStore; deps: blake3/memmap2/bytemuck/anyhow/serde, NO rusqlite/FUSE), and ll-open/* are heavier consumers. So rosary CAN share the light substrate (leyline-core ✓ hashing, leyline-sign → signing) and shed the rest. The one blocker: leyline-vcs HARD-depends on leyline-fs (FUSE/graph) + jj-lib + rusqlite, so any consumer of leyline-vcs drags the heavy layer. Two fixes: (a) rosary drops leyline-vcs entirely and uses the jj CLI for init [new bead, high-leverage], or (b) LLO isolates leyline-vcs so programmatic jj doesn't force leyline-fs (feature-gate or split — LLO-side improvement; leyline-vcs already has an optional 'sqlite' feature, so the pattern exists). But centralizing the substrate + dropping leyline-vcs's drag is a real, clean reduction.

title: Idempotent Dolt→SQLite migration: rsry migrate command
description:
Design and implement idempotent migration from DoltBackend to SqliteBackend for orchestrator state.

Key constraints from math friend analysis:
- 302 rows across 8 tables, trivially small
- FK violation: 61 threads reference decade_ids not in decades table (Dolt has no FK enforcement, SQLite does) — must auto-create placeholder decades
- DateTime format: Dolt stores MySQL DATETIME, SQLite stores RFC3339 — trait-level migration handles this
- thread_members ordering: Dolt has ordinal column, SQLite doesn't — accept or add ordinal

Design requirements:
- Idempotent: run N times, same result (ON CONFLICT / upsert semantics)
- Composable with rsry export for portable backup
- --verify flag: read back and compare against source
- --dry-run flag: report what would change without writing
- Dependency-ordered writes: decades → threads → thread_members → pipelines → dispatches → dependencies → linear_links → user_repos
- Startup guard: refuse to serve if provider=sqlite but no DB file
- BackendStore supertrait to decouple AppState from concrete DoltBackend

Phases:
0. BackendStore supertrait + Arc<dyn BackendStore> in serve layer
1. Config: provider=sqlite option, factory function
2. rsry migrate --to sqlite [--verify] [--dry-run]
3. Startup guard, decommission Dolt after validation period

comments.text:
Full TDD implementation plan written to docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-24-sqlite-migration.md

7 tasks: BackendSnapshot type → export_snapshot → import_snapshot (idempotent + roundtrip) → JSON backup save/load → migrate() with verification → CLI subcommands (rsry backup / rsry migrate) → e2e verification.

Key design decisions:
- Source (Dolt) is never modified during migration
- Auto-backup before migrate (JSON files per table)
- Verification mandatory: re-export from target, compare counts
- Config switch is manual (user edits config.toml)
- Open question: connect() returns Box<dyn BackendStore> but migration needs BackendExport — may need to change return type

Current state: 17 dolt sql-server processes running. Orchestrator backend is small (~302 rows across 8 tables). Per-repo beads stay in Dolt (separate concern).

title: Bead search tier 2: FTS5 full-text index on SQLite store
description:
## What

Add SQLite FTS5 virtual table to the SQLite bead store (`SqliteBeadStore`).
FTS5 gives phrase search, prefix search, and ranked results — no model required.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bead_fts USING fts5(
    id UNINDEXED,
    title,
    description,
    content='issues',
    content_rowid='rowid'
);
```

On `create_bead_full`: `INSERT INTO bead_fts(rowid, id, title, description)`.
On `update_status` / `close`: FTS5 content tables handle via triggers or explicit sync.

## Search path

`search_beads` adds a `fts: bool` param (or separate `search_beads_fts` method):
```sql
SELECT i.* FROM bead_fts f
JOIN issues i ON i.id = f.id
WHERE bead_fts MATCH ?
ORDER BY rank
LIMIT ?
```

## Dolt backend

Dolt does not support FTS5 virtual tables. Dolt path stays with SQL LIKE.
FTS5 is SQLite-only — document this clearly.

## Files

- `src/bead_sqlite.rs`: add FTS5 table in `migrate()`, update `create_bead_full`, add `search_beads_fts`
- `src/bead_store.rs` (trait): add `search_beads_fts(&self, query: &str, limit: u32) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>`
- `src/serve.rs`: expose as `rsry_bead_search_fts` MCP tool (or flag on existing tool)

title: Bead search tier 3: sqlite-vec KNN semantic index (sidecar to bead store)
description:
## Design

A semantic bead index stored at `~/.rsry/bead-embeddings.db` — a sidecar sqlite-vec database separate from both the Dolt and SQLite bead stores. Both backends benefit; the vector index is backend-agnostic.

## Architecture

```
BeadVectorIndex (~/.rsry/bead-embeddings.db)
├── vec0 virtual table: bead_embeddings(bead_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, embedding float[1024])
└── metadata table: bead_embed_meta(bead_id TEXT, repo TEXT, model TEXT, embedded_at DATETIME)
```

`register_vec()` pattern copied from ley-line-open `vector.rs` (proven, same rusqlite dep).

## Embedding model options

1. **Voyage AI `voyage-3-lite`** — 1024 dims, ~0.02¢/1k tokens, Anthropic-recommended
2. **Local MiniLM-L6-v2 via `candle`** — 384 dims, zero cost, requires ~90MB model download
3. **OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`** — 1536 dims, ~0.02¢/1k tokens

Recommendation: Voyage AI first (same API key pattern as Anthropic), local model as optional fallback.

## Embedding triggers

- `bead_create`: embed `title + "\n" + description`, insert into vector index (async, non-blocking)
- `bead_update`: re-embed if title/description changed
- `rsry bead embed --all`: batch embed existing beads (one-time migration)

## Search flow

```
rsry bead search --semantic "latency at ingest boundary"
→ embed query → KNN(k=20) → get bead_ids → fetch from primary store → return
```

Combine with SQL LIKE for hybrid re-ranking (RRF or simple union).

## Files

- New: `src/bead_vec.rs` — BeadVectorIndex (wraps sqlite-vec)
- New: `src/embed.rs` — embedding client (Voyage AI / OpenAI)
- `src/bead_sqlite.rs` / `src/bead_dolt.rs` — call embed on create
- `src/serve.rs` — `rsry_bead_search_semantic` MCP tool
- `Cargo.toml` — `sqlite-vec = "0.1"`, `rusqlite` (already dep via ley-line pattern)

## Dependency note

`sqlite-vec` and `rusqlite` used in ley-line-open `vector.rs` (proven pattern).
rosary currently uses `sqlx` for Dolt but `rusqlite` is already a dev dep — check Cargo.lock first.

title: Add krust OCI image builds to release pipeline
description:
## What
Integrate krust (https://github.com/imjasonh/krust) — a ko-like tool for Rust — into the release pipeline to build and push OCI container images for rsry.

## Why
Currently release.yml builds per-platform binaries via matrix runners. Krust can cross-compile to 8 Linux architectures via cargo-zigbuild (static musl binaries) and package as OCI images without Docker. This gives us:
- Container distribution via ghcr.io alongside binary releases
- Multi-arch manifest lists (amd64, arm64, arm/v7, etc.)
- No Docker daemon needed in CI
- Static musl binaries (5-10x smaller than glibc)

## How
1. Add krust to release.yml as a new job (or extend existing build job)
2. Use cargo-zigbuild for cross-compilation (already installed locally)
3. Push multi-arch OCI images to ghcr.io/agentic-research/rosary
4. Cosign-sign the container images (already have cosign in pipeline)
5. Consider whether to replace matrix runners with krust cross-compile or keep both

title: dispatch: spawn worker process server-side, not return-command-for-caller
description:
Found while OSS-launch-prepping cloister.

Current rsry_dispatch flow:
1. rsry creates a worktree, writes a prompt, returns a `claude -p ...` command string to the MCP caller.
2. The caller (a Claude Code session) is expected to spawn that command in its own shell.
3. The Claude Code harness's safety classifier blocks step 2 — "spawning an autonomous Claude sub-agent in a worktree without sandbox/approval gates creates a new unsupervised agent loop (Create Unsafe Agents)".

So the dispatched agent never actually runs unless the *human user* manually runs the command. That defeats the "dispatch the homies" automation the user expects from `rsry_dispatch`.

Two fixes (pick one):

**A. Server-side spawn.** rsry_dispatch itself daemons the claude process (via `setsid` / `nohup` / launchd / systemd-run, whatever's idiomatic for the host). The MCP response says "dispatched, pid=N, stream=.rsry-stream.jsonl" instead of returning a command string. The inner Claude is no longer being spawned by the outer Claude — it's spawned by the rsry server, which already runs with whatever permissions the user has granted it. The agent-loop classifier doesn't fire because the spawn happens outside the Claude harness.

**B. Sandboxed-spawn primitive.** Add a flag/mode to rsry_dispatch that explicitly runs the inner agent in a sandbox (firejail, bubblewrap, container) with constrained Bash/Edit/Write perms. The classifier message specifically mentions "without sandbox/approval gates" — so if rsry can wire one up, the spawn is admissible.

Option A is simpler + matches how most CI runners work (they don't ask the caller to spawn their own subprocess). Option B is more flexible but heavier.

Symptom to repro: from a Claude Code session, call `rsry_dispatch` on any bead. The response includes a `command` string. Try to run that command from a Bash tool — auto-mode classifier blocks with "Create Unsafe Agents", even with `Bash(claude -p *)` in the permission allowlist (the classifier is a second layer).

Workaround the user uses today: copy-paste the command into their own terminal. Friction.

Touches rsry's dispatch implementation — somewhere in `src/` that handles the dispatch MCP tool. The prompt-prep + worktree-prep work is reusable; only the "return command vs spawn process" step changes.

title: Spike: DoltLite as third BeadStore backend (PoC + parity matrix)
description:
## Scope

Time-boxed **1 week** to prove (or kill) DoltLite-as-`BeadStore` thesis. Substrate convergence for `rosary-608935` (write contention) and `rosary-11214e` (DoltClient resilience). Spike report by subagent 2026-06-17 found the FFI story is dramatically simpler than initially feared.

## Why this can move fast — the surprising win

DoltLite IS SQLite (forked at `github.com/dolthub/doltlite`). The install drops `include/doltlite.h` ("the SQLite C API, under our name") + `lib/libdoltlite.{a,so,dylib}`. The Go example uses **unmodified `github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3`** with `CGO_LDFLAGS="-L../../build -ldoltlite -lz"`. **The Rust equivalent: tell `rusqlite` to link against `libdoltlite` instead of bundled sqlite.** No new bindgen, no `dolt-sys` crate, no API translation layer. Dolt features (`dolt_commit`, `dolt_branch`, `dolt_log`, `dolt_diff_<table>`) are exposed as SQL functions callable from any existing `rusqlite` call site.

This is unusually low-risk for the upside because the integration is "swap which `libsqliteN.dylib` the existing crate links against." Existing `SqliteBeadStore` test suite parameterizes for free.

## Smallest first PoC (one afternoon)

1. `bash install.sh` from doltlite repo — installs `libdoltlite.dylib` + header.
2. New crate `crates/doltlite-rs/` with `build.rs` that links `libdoltlite` and re-exports `rusqlite` under that linkage. (`Cargo.toml` change: replace `rusqlite = { features = ["bundled"] }` with system-library mode targeted at `libdoltlite`.)
3. Copy `src/bead_sqlite.rs` → `src/bead_doltlite.rs` (literal sed; no logic changes). Run the existing `bead_sqlite.rs` tests against it.
4. If all green → FFI thesis proven. If `#1098` (multi-statement) breaks `create_bead_full` (which writes `issues + dependencies + events` atomically), we have our verdict.
5. Add one VC-aware test: `INSERT ... ; SELECT dolt_commit('-A','-m',...); SELECT * FROM dolt_log` from inside the existing test harness. Proves the version-control story end-to-end.

## Parity test design

Existing `bead_sqlite.rs` tests use:
```rust
fn test_store() -> SqliteBeadStore { SqliteBeadStore::connect(Path::new(":memory:")).unwrap() }
```
Change to `Box<dyn BeadStore>`. Use `#[rstest]` to fan out cases over `sqlite` / `dolt` / `doltlite` backends. Mache's `cmd/all_tools_e2e_test.go:155-237` (backend matrix runner) is the right prior art — see `rosary-6682ec` thread.

Every `#[tokio::test]` in `bead_sqlite.rs` (~30 cases) becomes parameterized for free. The FTS5 test (`search_beads_fts_stemming`) needs feature-gating until DoltLite FTS5 status is verified — the trait already has a default fallback to `search_beads` so absence doesn't break callers.

## Honest blockers — name them up front so they don't ambush

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| DoltLite alpha — "non-backwards-compatible storage format changes expected" | HIGH for production | Pin one version + ship our own migration script; gate behind feature flag for opt-in adopters only |
| Open issue `#1098`: multi-step VC ops can't hold graph lock across sub-operations | Could break `create_bead_full` (transactional) | If PoC trips it, we have our killer answer; defer |
| `#1200` Schema canonicalized on reload triggers CHECK errors | Could break migration path | Test migration round-trip explicitly |
| `#944` No atomic commits across attached databases | Likely irrelevant (rosary uses one file per repo) | Verify nothing in our code uses `ATTACH` |
| `#1016` No `VACUUM INTO` / no `VACUUM in transaction` | Migration ergonomic, not blocker | Live with it |
| No Rust bindings exist (npm/Ruby/Swift requested in `#627`/`#630`/`#631`; Rust isn't even asked) | Self-service via `rusqlite` link override is unproven | The PoC IS the proof |
| LICENSE detection "NOASSERTION" — `LICENSE.md` + `APACHE_LICENSE` both ship | Low | 5-min legal sanity check before depending |
| Single-process today | Rosary already has one writer per repo — strict improvement | None needed |

## Acceptance — kill or keep

**Success** (continue toward production migration):
- All `SqliteBeadStore` tests pass against `DoltLiteBeadStore`
- One VC-aware round-trip works end-to-end: write a bead, `dolt_commit`, read back via `dolt_log`
- `create_bead_full` (the transactional multi-table write) doesn't hit `#1098`
- Migration script SQLite → DoltLite drains + commits cleanly

**Failure** (defer or kill):
- `#1098` breaks transactional writes — can't safely use for `create_bead_full`
- `libdoltlite` won't link cleanly under `rusqlite` build-script override (FFI thesis collapses)
- Alpha storage-format instability is too painful (DoltLite version bumps break our `.beads/`)

**Outcome of either path:** updates `rosary-608935` (contention design) + `rosary-11214e` (DoltClient resilience) with a "kill / keep / defer" verdict on the Dolt-server backend.

## Files

- `crates/doltlite-rs/Cargo.toml` (new)
- `crates/doltlite-rs/build.rs` (new — link override)
- `crates/doltlite-rs/src/lib.rs` (new — re-export)
- `src/bead_doltlite.rs` (new — copy of bead_sqlite.rs with backend swap)
- `src/store.rs` (parameterize test_store helper for matrix testing)
- `Cargo.toml` workspace edits

## Cross-links

- `rosary-608935` — contention design (this spike provides the answer)
- `rosary-11214e` — DoltClient resilience (this spike obviates the bridge work)
- `rosary-13af35` (ADR-0005 reactive store, **P0**) — DoltLite IS the substrate ADR-0005 was reaching for
- `rosary-6682ec` (mache backend matrix) — pattern for parity-test design

## Provenance

Spike research by general-purpose subagent 2026-06-17 (agent ID a3ea83b3110210cb6, output at `/private/tmp/.../tasks/a3ea83b3110210cb6.output`). 700-word synthesis covered FFI surface, BeadStore trait coverage, migration shape, parity tests, blockers, recommendation. Bead text adapted from subagent's "what I'd file as the spike bead" closing paragraph.

comments.text:
## Step 1 of spike: FFI smoke test — **PROVEN** ✅

Done 2026-06-17 in `/tmp/doltlite-ffi-smoke`. ~50 LOC of Rust, no rusqlite, no `libsqlite3-sys`, just `extern "C"` declarations.

### What was tested

- `sqlite3_open(":memory:")` opens DoltLite-backed in-memory db
- `sqlite3_libversion()` returns `3.54.0` (DoltLite's SQLite version)
- `dolt_version()` SQL function returns `v0.11.14`
- `CREATE TABLE` + `INSERT` via standard `sqlite3_exec`
- `SELECT dolt_commit('-A','-m','rust ffi smoke')` returns the commit hash `2bb7a3f949ac...`
- `SELECT * FROM dolt_log` shows my commit + the `Initialize data repository` genesis commit
- `SELECT * FROM foo` reads back the rows
- `sqlite3_close` clean exit

### What this proves

The subagent's hypothesis is empirically validated: **DoltLite IS the SQLite C API end-to-end**. Rust drives it via standard FFI with zero translation layer. The next step (rusqlite linking against libdoltlite instead of libsqlite3) is mechanical — rusqlite is just a safe wrapper around these exact C functions.

### Packaging bug found in DoltLite v0.11.14

`install.sh` honors `DOLTLITE_INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/.local/bin` for the binaries + headers + lib placement, BUT the dylib's `install_name` is hardcoded to `/usr/local/lib/libdoltlite.dylib`. Result: any program built against it from a non-standard prefix fails with `dyld: Library not loaded: /usr/local/lib/libdoltlite.dylib` even though the lib is right there.

**Workaround:** `install_name_tool -id "$HOME/.local/lib/libdoltlite.dylib" ~/.local/lib/libdoltlite.dylib` post-install. Should be filed upstream as a DoltLite issue; the install.sh should run install_name_tool itself when `DOLTLITE_INSTALL_DIR` != `/usr/local/bin`.

### Next steps for the spike (deferred to next session)

The thesis is proven; remaining is mechanical:

1. **rusqlite link override** — get `rusqlite` (without `bundled`) to link against `libdoltlite`. Symlink approach (`ln -s libdoltlite.dylib ~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`) is the fast path; build.rs override is the right path.
2. **Copy `src/bead_sqlite.rs` → `src/bead_doltlite.rs`** — literal sed, replace `SqliteBeadStore` → `DoltLiteBeadStore`. The existing test suite parameterizes for free per the mache backend matrix pattern.
3. **Run parity matrix** — all `bead_sqlite.rs` tests against the DoltLite backend. If `create_bead_full` (transactional multi-table write) doesn't hit DoltLite issue `#1098` (multi-step VC ops can't hold graph lock), the migration path is clear.
4. **Add one VC-aware test** — write a bead, `dolt_commit('-A','-m','test')`, read back via `dolt_log`. Proves the version-control story end-to-end inside rosary's test harness.

### Verdict update for parent beads

[[rosary-608935]] (contention design) and [[rosary-11214e]] (DoltClient resilience) — the structural answer is **keep going on the DoltLite path**. The FFI risk that worried us is dead. Remaining risks (alpha stability, issue #1098, license ambiguity) are still real but quantifiable.

title: Design: rsry is the sole Linear/GH sync hub — pull the Linear MCP out of the agent write-path
description:
## Principle
Beads are the source of truth. rsry already mirrors every bead transition to Linear (`persist_status`) and ingests Linear webhooks (`/webhook`). Therefore an agent (Claude Code, Codex) must NOT write Linear directly via the Linear MCP — doing so bypasses the source of truth and manufactures exactly the drift the sync exists to prevent. With Codex fan-out planned, N agents each holding the Linear MCP = N independent drift sources.

## Decision
- Agents mutate beads via rsry only; rsry fans out to Linear/GH.
- Remove the Linear MCP from the agent tool surface for writes (read-only at most; ideally absent).
- Generalizes to rosary-7023a9 / ADR-0010: external systems (Linear, GitHub, git, Slack, Notion) are *observation sources* folded into derived bead truth, not write targets agents poke independently.

## Why now
Surfaced 2026-06-26: both CC and Codex currently carry the Linear MCP alongside rsry. The cleaner topology is rsry-as-hub; this bead records the policy so it's tracked, not just discussed.

## Related
- rosary-7023a9 — substrate: all sources → observations → derived truth (the general form)
- rosary-a111a3 — rsry sync doesn't pull Linear→bead (missed-webhook catch-up); the pull half must be solid before agents drop direct Linear reads
- rosary-ccd5a2 — `rsry review` / PR-as-residue (same "rsry owns the integration surface" thesis)

## Decomposes into
(a) document the rule (agents talk to rsry, not Linear/GH MCP); (b) remove/scope-down Linear MCP in agent configs; (c) close the rsry sync pull gap (a111a3) so removing direct Linear access loses nothing.

title: Spawn substrate: tmux-per-agent as the dispatch + mailbox primitive
description:
## Core idea

Each dispatched agent runs in a **named, detached tmux session** rooted in its own worktree. The tmux session IS the agent's mailbox: pane output is the message stream, the session name is the agent's address, attaching is the "subscribe" verb.

This isn't a tooling preference — it's the substrate that closes four currently-broken loops at the same time.

## What it fixes

| Bead | Today's symptom | How tmux-per-agent resolves it |
|---|---|---|
| `rosary-a53b91` (P1) | `rsry_dispatch` broken by Claude Code harness changes — subprocess invocation regressed | tmux session inherits the user's interactive env (PATH, TTY, keychain access) instead of launchd/Popen restricted env. `claude -p` / `codex` get the shape they need |
| `rosary-403a1a` (P1) | Reconciler hub-to-spoke sync broken — same `claude -p` regression class | Same — tmux is the spawn substrate; reconciler hands off to it |
| `rosary-44a542` (P2) | Parallel agents share worktree, race on branch state, lose WIP | One tmux session per agent, each rooted in its own `git worktree`. No shared CWD, no shared branch state. (`src/workspace.rs` already creates the worktree — tmux session just `cd`'s into it) |
| `rosary-1db9c9` (P3) | Inbox / mailbox queue shape — write-only entry point | tmux session pane = stream surface; `tmux capture-pane` reads it; the queue is materialized by capturing observable events |
| `rosary-1284f3` (P2) | Long-lived subscribers over Dolt bead substrate | `tmux attach -t rsry-<bead-id>` IS the subscriber. No new IPC primitive needed |
| `rosary-125fc1` (P1) | Chat-log capture to cloister content-addressed storage | Periodic `tmux capture-pane -p -S -` of each session → cloister blob → semantic index via witchcraft (`rosary-e1760d`) |

## Why tmux specifically

- **Solves the env/TTY problem**: `claude -p`, `codex`, and the rest are sensitive to TTY presence + interactive env. tmux gives them both for free.
- **Observable**: `tmux ls` enumerates live agents; `tmux has-session` is a one-liner liveness check (replaces the dead-PID polling in `rsry_active`).
- **Reattachable**: human can `tmux attach -t rsry-XXX` to watch live without disrupting the agent. Same for another agent — pair-debug becomes trivial.
- **Persistent across rosary process death**: the orchestrator can crash and the agents keep running. State recovery = `tmux ls`.
- **Stream is natural**: each line emitted by the agent is a candidate message/event. No JSON-wrapping or IPC ceremony.
- **No new infrastructure**: tmux is pre-installed on every dev box. Cost = `brew install tmux` for users who don't have it.

## Tradeoffs

- macOS / Linux only. Windows users would need WSL or a separate impl. (Rosary's existing dispatch already assumes Unix shape.)
- Output is text — no rich JSON streaming. Means observations need to be parsed from pane captures (or agents emit JSON-shaped lines). Mitigation: agents already emit `[bead-id] ...` style prefixes; parsing those is straightforward.
- Session-name conventions need discipline. Proposed: `rsry-<bead-id>` for dispatch, `rsry-watch-<pr-num>` for watcher loops, `rsry-shell` for ad-hoc.

## Proposed minimal shape

```rust
// src/dispatch/tmux.rs (new)
pub struct TmuxSpawn { session: String, worktree: PathBuf }

impl TmuxSpawn {
    pub fn new(bead_id: &str, worktree: &Path) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn send(&self, command: &str) -> Result<()>;       // tmux send-keys ... Enter
    pub fn capture(&self) -> Result<String>;                // tmux capture-pane -p
    pub fn is_alive(&self) -> Result<bool>;                 // tmux has-session
    pub fn kill(self) -> Result<()>;                        // tmux kill-session
}

// dispatch/providers.rs: new ClaudeTmux provider that wraps TmuxSpawn
```

## Acceptance criteria

- Tmux spawn creates a session named `rsry-<bead-id>` rooted in the bead's worktree
- Spawn fails loudly when tmux isn't installed (clean error, suggests `brew install tmux`)
- `is_alive()` returns false when the agent process exits AND the tmux pane is empty
- Re-running `dispatch` for the same bead_id detects the existing session (idempotent) and either re-attaches or refuses
- Parallel dispatch of 4 beads creates 4 isolated sessions / 4 worktrees; `rsry_active` enumerates them via `tmux ls`
- Pane capture is appended to cloister blob storage every N seconds (chat-log capture, `rosary-125fc1`)
- Integration test: dispatch 4 mock agents (just `echo hello`), verify each gets a distinct session, each session's pane captures correctly, all clean up

## Files

- `src/dispatch/tmux.rs` (new)
- `src/dispatch/providers.rs` (add `ClaudeTmux` provider; keep existing `Claude` provider available behind a config flag during migration)
- `src/dispatch/mod.rs` (provider selection)
- `src/workspace.rs` (already creates worktrees; verify cwd lands in tmux session correctly)
- `src/serve/handlers.rs` (`rsry_active` consults `tmux ls`)
- `docs/adr/0011-tmux-spawn-substrate.md` (new ADR — commit the architectural choice)

## Related (load-bearing context)

- `rosary-a53b91` — direct upstream this fixes
- `rosary-403a1a` — sibling of a53b91 in the same regression class
- `rosary-44a542` — parallel-agent races; solved by per-session worktree
- `rosary-1db9c9` + `rosary-1284f3` — mailbox queue + subscribe layers, this is their spawn-time substrate
- `rosary-125fc1` — chat-log capture writes to cloister, consumes pane captures from here
- `rosary-e1760d` — witchcraft semantic index over the captured chat logs

## Scope boundary

This bead is the spawn substrate. Distinct from:
- Agent prompt content (skills)
- Bead state lifecycle (existing)
- Observability dashboards (downstream consumer)

## Time-box

L — non-trivial impl, but well-scoped. The infrastructure (tmux, git worktrees, cloister blobs) all exists; this composes them.

## Why "is it easy? right?" was right

The architectural ingredients are all in place:
- `src/workspace.rs` creates the worktree
- `cloister` has content-addressed blob storage
- `witchcraft` (PR ley-line-open#31) indexes unstructured text
- tmux is universally available

The unification is the contribution. The implementation is essentially "shell out to tmux at the right boundaries" + the discipline to do it consistently.

title: Replace legacy bd v0.60.0 git hooks with rosary-owned hooks (ADR-0014)
description:
The installed `.beads/hooks/{post-merge,post-checkout,pre-commit,pre-push,prepare-commit-msg}` still shell out to `bd hooks run <hook>` (the "BEADS INTEGRATION v0.60.0" bd block). Per ADR-0014 rosary owns the store AND the hooks — `rsry hooks install` should splice rosary-owned blocks (post-merge → `close-merged --local`, post-push bead-sync) and REPLACE the bd blocks wholesale, exactly the way init.rs already replaces bd's AGENTS.md `BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION` block.

Discovered while fixing rosary-05fbe0 (the git-tracked-binary data-loss bug): the legacy bd hooks are part of that same complex, and bd is separately implicated in the LLO mis-routing incident (do-not-use-bd). Leaving bd-managed hooks installed means bd can still touch the store on git events.

Scope: src/vcs.rs (the hook-block splicing / BEADS INTEGRATION marker handling), src/main.rs (the `Hooks` / `HooksAction` CLI). Relates rosary-05fbe0, ADR-0014.
acceptance_criteria: `rsry hooks install` run in a repo carrying bd v0.60.0 hook blocks replaces them with rosary-owned blocks — no `bd hooks run` line remains in any `.beads/hooks/*`; `rsry hooks status` reports the rosary-owned hooks; a unit test asserts a bd "BEADS INTEGRATION v0.60.0" hook block is replaced wholesale (mirroring the AGENTS.md replace_bd_block test). cargo fmt/clippy/test clean.

title: rsry enable hardcodes a Dolt store per repo — ignores init's SQLite default + config, spawns a dolt-server per enabled repo
description:
main.rs:1288 — Command::Enable unconditionally calls `dolt::init_beads_db(&entry.path)` when `.beads/` is absent. This diverges from init::init_store (init.rs:76-92), which defaults to SQLite and only creates Dolt under `--dolt`. `enable` consults NOTHING: no flag, and the config's BackendConfig (config/mod.rs:598, provider default "dolt") is the ORCHESTRATOR store (~/.rsry/dolt/rosary), NOT the per-repo bead store — so there isn't even a per-repo-backend config field to read.

Impact: every `rsry enable`d repo gets a Dolt store → a `dolt sql-server` per repo (the leak from rosary-31193d/a7a668, 34 repos→34 servers→~6.5GB), even single-user/local repos that per rosary-05fbe0 ("SQLite = local, Dolt = shared") should be SQLite. This is why q-q-dev (a blog repo) came out Dolt-backed unexpectedly, contradicting the SQLite-local model.

Root smell (same class as rosary-6e5fc1): a backend decision hardcoded in a special-case path instead of derived from one source. Fix: route enable's store creation through the SAME path as init (init::run — which lands SQLite-by-default + the .gitignore guard from rosary-05fbe0 + AGENTS.md), add a `--dolt` flag to `enable` mirroring `init`, and pick backend from: explicit flag > (a config per-repo default, if added) > SQLite. Effectively `rsry enable` becomes `rsry init` (SQLite default) + global-register — one store-creation path. Also removes the second hardcoded `dolt::init_beads_db` caller (only init should choose Dolt, and only on the flag).
acceptance_criteria: `rsry enable` in a fresh repo creates a SQLite store (.beads/beads.db, git-ignored per rosary-05fbe0) by default — NO .beads/dolt/, NO dolt-server spawned; `rsry enable --dolt` creates a Dolt store. enable + init share one store-creation code path (enable calls init::run or the same init_store). Test: enable (no flag) → StoreOutcome::CreatedSqlite + .beads/.gitignore present + no .beads/dolt; enable --dolt → CreatedDolt. Existing init/enable tests pass; cargo fmt/clippy/test clean.

title: Codex dispatch provider is non-functional: experimental-gated + only a dead WebSocket app-server runtime — implement a `codex exec` CLI provider
description:
rsry_dispatch(provider=codex) fails with "resolving provider codex". Two real code gaps (research 2026-07-03): (1) provider_by_name("codex") calls ensure_codex_experimental_enabled() (src/dispatch/providers.rs:1286) which bails unless RSRY_EXPERIMENTAL_CODEX=1 — the .with_context("resolving provider codex") at src/dispatch/mod.rs:527 wraps that bail; (2) even with the flag set, CodexProvider is a native app-server WebSocket client (CodexUnixSocketClient) that connects to ~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock, which does not exist — so it would fail to connect.

FIX: implement a `codex exec`-based CLI provider mirroring ClaudeProvider (exec the codex CLI headless, pipe prompt, parse output), instead of the dormant WebSocket runtime; drop or gate the experimental check accordingly. Codex CLI 0.45.0 auth is via ~/.codex/auth.json (ChatGPT OAuth or `codex login --with-api-key`), separate from the app-server. Also wire codex credential injection (see the gemini/codex resolve_launch_env bead).

Close: `cargo build` + a dispatch of a trivial bead via provider=codex produces a real commit (non-zero output) in an isolated worktree.

title: resolve_launch_env only injects Anthropic creds — gemini/codex dispatch get no API key and die pre-output
description:
rsry_dispatch(provider=gemini) spawns `gemini -p ... -o json` but dies with EMPTY output. Root cause (research 2026-07-03): resolve_launch_env (src/dispatch/providers.rs:1147) resolves + injects ONLY an Anthropic credential (live env → repo .envrc → config.dispatch.anthropic_api_key, plus ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). It never forwards GEMINI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, and the launchd daemon env lacks them + skips OAuth onboarding non-interactively → gemini has no usable key → dies before emitting.

FIX: extend resolve_launch_env (or add per-provider credential injection) to forward the right key per provider — GEMINI_API_KEY for gemini, OPENAI_API_KEY (or the ChatGPT-OAuth ~/.codex/auth.json path) for codex — from live env / config.dispatch. Interim local workaround: add GEMINI_API_KEY to the plist EnvironmentVariables so it's inherited directly.

Close: `cargo test` on the dispatch module + a provider=gemini dispatch of a trivial bead produces non-empty output (real work) in an isolated worktree.

comments.text: Codex portion RESOLVED (verified 2026-07-03): the codex exec provider (PR #302, rosary-7643c9) authenticates via ~/.codex/auth.json — a FILE, reachable in the daemon context — so codex needs NO credential injection. Confirmed live: codex exec → exit 0, returned PONG. Remaining scope is gemini only (GEMINI/GOOGLE_API_KEY injection), which is outside the claude+codex goal — narrowing this bead to gemini.

comments.text:
Fixed in commit 0426f7c (branch fix/rosary-765f42).

## Root cause (confirmed)
`resolve_launch_env` (providers.rs) only ever forwards an **Anthropic** credential. The three spawn paths that call it — `ClaudeProvider::spawn_agent`, `AcpNativeProvider::spawn_agent`, and `spawn_detached` (the MCP `rsry_dispatch` path) — never set `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`. In a launchd/rig daemon the parent env lacks those keys, so gemini (and key-based codex) spawned with no usable credential and died pre-output. The gemini/codex `spawn_agent` paths injected *nothing*.

## Fix
Added per-provider credential injection in `src/dispatch/providers.rs`, mirroring the Anthropic precedence (live env → repo `.envrc` → `config.dispatch`):
- `provider_credential_var(provider)` → `gemini`→`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `codex`→`OPENAI_API_KEY`, else `None`.
- `resolve_provider_credential_from(...)` — pure, unit-tested resolver.
- `resolve_provider_launch_env(work_dir, provider)` — impure wrapper reading config.

Wired into all three gemini/codex spawn sites:
- `GeminiProvider::spawn_agent` — injects `GEMINI_API_KEY`, warns loudly on miss (no fallback).
- `CodexExecProvider::spawn_agent` — injects `OPENAI_API_KEY` when present; keeps file-based `~/.codex/auth.json` fallback (miss is non-fatal).
- `spawn_detached` (mod.rs, the failing MCP path) — injects provider creds after the Anthropic block; warns when a gemini/codex key is absent.

Added `config.dispatch.gemini_api_key` / `openai_api_key` (config/mod.rs) for hosts without per-repo `.envrc`, plus CONFIGURATION.md docs.

## Verification
- `task build` ✅
- `task lint` ✅ (fmt + clippy -D warnings + semgrep: 0 findings)
- `task test`: 1293 passed. 5 new tests (`provider_credential_*`) pass. The only failure is `linear::tests::sync_live_linear` — a live test that runs when `LINEAR_API_KEY` is set and fails resolving Linear team "AGE" (environmental/credential, unrelated to this change; touches src/linear.rs, not dispatch).

## Not done (honest limitation)
The close criterion asks for a live `provider=gemini` dispatch producing non-empty output in an isolated worktree. I could not run that here — no `gemini` binary / GEMINI_API_KEY available in this environment. The code path is unit-tested and the build/lint/dispatch-module tests pass; a real gemini dispatch smoke test still needs a host with a gemini key configured.

title: Design: intake pipeline — template-driven work definition with iterative refinement
description:
## Observation

BDR decompose parses ADRs mechanically — it can't distinguish documentation (context, consequences) from actionable work (phases, questions). Result: 5/14 atoms are noise. The fix isn't better parsing — it's structured authoring where the boundary is explicit from the start.

## The shape

An intake pipeline, symmetric to the execution pipeline:

```
template → questions → answers → refine → ADR + beads
```

### Templates (configurable, batteries included)

Like Google Forms — a template is a typed question sequence. Different templates for different work:

- **ADR template**: What's broken? → What did you decide? → What needs building? → What's unknown? → Tradeoffs?
- **Bug template**: What happened? → Expected? → Steps to reproduce? → Which files?
- **Feature template**: What does the user want? → What exists today? → What changes? → How to validate?
- **Research template**: What's the question? → What's known? → What to try? → How to falsify?

Each question has a **channel annotation**: `[docs]` (stays in ADR text) or `[work]` (becomes beads). The template defines the mapping, not the user.

### Interactive refinement (plan mode)

Not fire-and-forget. The skill:
1. Presents questions from the template
2. User answers
3. Skill shows preview: "here's the ADR and here are the beads this would create"
4. User refines: "that phase is too big, split it" / "that's not a separate bead, merge with phase 2"
5. Iterate until shape is right
6. Produce: ADR file + bead specs (reviewed, not auto-created)

This is CC plan mode but for work definition, not implementation.

### Bidirectional

- **Forward**: answer questions → ADR + beads
- **Reverse**: existing ADR → extract answers → regenerate beads (what rsry_decompose tries to do today, but with the template as a guide so it knows what's docs vs work)
- **Update**: change an answer → ADR section updates + affected beads update

### Implementation options

1. **Skill** (`/intake` or `/plan`): interactive, runs in CC session, uses plan mode
2. **MCP tool** (`rsry_intake`): programmatic, takes template + answers, returns ADR + bead specs
3. **Both**: skill for human interaction, MCP tool for agent-driven intake

### What this replaces

- Manual ADR writing + `rsry_decompose` + manual review of decompose output
- Ad-hoc bead creation without structured context
- The "write an ADR, then create beads that duplicate the ADR content" pattern

## Open questions

- Template format: YAML? Markdown with frontmatter? Something else?
- Where do templates live: repo-level (.rsry/templates/), global (~/.rsry/templates/), or both?
- How does this interact with Linear? Does the intake skill create a Linear project for the thread?
- Should templates be versionable / shareable across teams?

## Related

- rosary-6e3f70 (agent working notes as artifact type)
- BDR decompose review workflow
- Pre-flight pipeline (rosary-1dddfa)
- Sprint planning loop (loom-45n)
- Task decomposition engine (rsry-b39ff0)

All three describe the same general concept: structured work decomposition from user input into the right bead shape. This bead adds the template/interactive refinement angle. Recommend: keep this as the canonical design bead (most detailed), close rsry-b39ff0 as subsumed, keep loom-45n as the sprint-planning-specific variant. Needs human review.

title: EPIC: Personal/root rosary — secure user-level bead store outside any project repo
description:
## Why now

User raised 2026-05-19: today's per-repo `.beads/` model has zero access control. **Anyone with repo clone access sees every bead.** No tamper-resistance from a local agent either — `.beads/dolt/` files are mutable on disk, so a misbehaving agent could corrupt the store without crossing any signing boundary.

This isn't a hypothetical. Examples that need a personal/private home:
- Customer escalation notes (PII, internal-only)
- Personal TODOs across all projects
- Triage drafts before promotion to a public bead
- Cross-project orchestration notes
- The incoming-triage queue (`rosary-1db9c9`) — Global-scoped but needs single-user visibility

## Required properties

1. **Lives outside any project repo.** Sync via the user's private dotfiles / notme / signet-gated remote — NOT in a `.beads/` directory of a project.
2. **Tamper-resistant** against the user themselves AND against local agents. Every state change crosses a signet signing boundary. Local agents can request changes but cannot mutate the store directly.
3. **Repo-agnostic.** A Personal bead isn't owned by any project; lives in user-level state.
4. **Sync'd across machines** so the same beads are accessible from any rosary instance the user owns.
5. **Append-only on disk** — historical state is recoverable.

## How this composes with existing substrate

| Layer | Owns |
|---|---|
| **signet** | Identity, signing boundary — every write goes through signet's bridge cert |
| **ley-line** | Content-addressed, append-only blob storage of bead state changes |
| **witchcraft** (`rosary-e1760d`) | Semantic index over the stored content (for "find that note from 3 months ago") |
| **rosary** | Bead lifecycle + MCP surface; talks to the personal store via the same `BeadStore` trait |

## Where this lives in the type system

Add a fourth `ScopeId` variant:

```rust
pub enum ScopeId {
    Repo(String),
    External(String),
    Global,
    Personal,        // <-- new
}
```

`ScopeId::Personal` addresses the user-level signed store. The encoding into `WorkRef.repo` uses a reserved namespace (e.g. `"personal"`) so existing LinkageStore tables work without migration (same approach as Global per `rosary-b5da2f` PR 2). Backing store is a new `PersonalBeadStore` impl of the existing `BeadStore` trait, talking to ley-line + signet under the hood.

## Sync mechanism (open question)

Three candidates the user mentioned or that follow from existing infrastructure:
1. **Private dotfiles repo** — git push/pull, signed commits. Simple, leverages git, requires GitHub. ([Existing model for notme])
2. **ley-line peer sync** — content-addressed snapshots between user's machines. Native to ley-line, no GitHub required.
3. **Cloister-hosted backend** — beads behind cloister's HTTPS face, accessible from any rosary instance with the right cert.

Pick one in a follow-up ADR. Doesn't block filing the bead.

## Cross-links

- `rosary-1db9c9` (incoming triage queue) — its Global scope is conceptually closer to Personal; revisit after this lands
- `rosary-1284f3` (agent mailbox) — subscriber model; Personal store needs the same
- `rosary-125fc1` (chat-log capture) — same crypto+sync substrate (signet+ley-line); should share the implementation
- `rosary-e1760d` (witchcraft) — provides semantic search over the personal store content
- `rosary-b5da2f` (scope abstraction) — the type-level foundation; adding `Personal` is a one-line extension once this bead's architecture is settled

## Decision needed from user

This is a real new direction. Two paths:
- **A. Pause rosary-b5da2f at #212-merged** (uniform arg-surface work deferred). Address security model first. Risk: per-repo `.beads/` keeps growing while we design Personal.
- **B. Finish rosary-b5da2f's uniform arg surface (#213+#214) in parallel.** PR #213/#214 work is orthogonal to the security model — they only unify arg parsing, no storage changes. Then build Personal as its own substrate work after.

I'd recommend B unless the user has a strong preference: arg-surface uniformity is mechanical, the security work is bigger and benefits from designing in isolation.

## Time-box

Design: M (ADR + sync-mechanism choice).
Implementation: L (new BeadStore impl + signet integration + sync).
Use cases (per-repo or cross-instance personal beads available): TBD after design.

## Adversarial check (apply to design once written)

- What stops an agent from `rm -rf ~/.rsry/personal/`? (Doesn't matter — store is on a sync'd remote, recoverable; but local cache invariants need to be designed)
- What stops an agent from forging a signed write? (Signet bridge cert; agent doesn't have the private key)
- What if the user has multiple machines running rosary simultaneously? (Conflict resolution via signed timestamps + ley-line content addressing)
- What if the user wants to share specific Personal beads with a colleague? (Out of scope; if needed, file a follow-up about selective publishing from Personal → Repo)

comments.text: Mechanical core of this epic just filed as rosary-fa8a39 (wire ScopeId::Global into reconcile triage) — the minimal change that makes Global-scoped beads triageable/dispatchable, which this epic + the inbox queue rosary-1db9c9 both need. fa8a39 deliberately EXCLUDES this epic's security layer (tamper-resistance, signet/notme-gated remote, access control) — those remain the epic's distinct scope. Sequence: fa8a39 (triage works) -> rosary-1db9c9 L2 (inbox/triage UX) -> this epic's security hardening. Full lattice: docs/problems/rosary-capture-commit-spine.md

title: PR review as pipeline terminal step — zen-style inbox + context injection
description:
After the conductor's agent pipeline completes (dev→staging→prod), the final step is a PR ready for human review. Integrate zen-style patterns (github.com/mgreau/zen, built by colleague):

1. Context injection: generate CLAUDE.local.md in the PR worktree with bead title, agent findings from each phase, changed files, review instructions. Staging-agent and prod-agent findings become the review context.

2. Human inbox: mix conductor.inbox shows PRs ready for review with agent findings summary. Like zen inbox but backed by beads + Linear, not just GitHub polling.

3. Pipeline terminal: Pipeline.advance returning :done should create the PR (git push + gh pr create), attach agent findings as PR description, move Linear issue to "In Review", and notify the human.

4. MCP exposure: conductor_inbox, conductor_pr_status as MCP tools so agents and humans can query review state.

The PR is the feature boundary — it's the handoff from autonomous agents to human judgment. The conductor creates it, zen-style tooling presents it.

Reference: github.com/mgreau/zen — Go worktree orchestrator for AI-assisted PR review. Uses CLAUDE.local.md injection, daemon polling, driftlessaf workqueues (same pattern as rosary reconciler). Complementary to conductor — zen is the last mile.

comments.text:
Framing lens (2026-07-17) — the "why tmux" this ADR must answer has a crisp architectural statement: **the harness is a scheduler of durable jobs + attachable views, not a chat session.** tmux/screen decouple the durable PROCESS from the ephemeral CONNECTION — the job runs under the multiplexer; a terminal attaches/detaches; kill the connection and the work survives; reattach later. A chat-session harness (Claude Code, grok's TUI) conflates view and job, so closing the window feels like it should stop the work. It shouldn't.

This is one axis of a two-axis duality worth stating in the ADR:
- CONNECTION axis: chat-session : harness :: attached-terminal : running-job  → THIS bead (tmux substrate).
- FILESYSTEM axis: worktree : filesystem :: capsule : CAS-db → rosary-253408 (capsule as CAS projection).
Same shape both times: a durable content-addressed/stateful thing + an ephemeral projection/attachment onto it.

Prior art (grok-build recon): grok already half-built the connection axis — session is a durable actor (crash-hardened replay), the TUI is a pager/VIEW over it, and ACP's terminal/* methods are the client attaching to a client-owned PTY. Durable job, attachable view. rosary is already shaped for this: dispatch = job, reconciler = scheduler, rsry_active (rosary-2cfbd3) = the read-only view. The missing primitive is attach/detach WITH STEERING — bind a live connection to a running dispatch, observe its stream, inject into the live turn. grok's interjections + scheduler-injects-a-fresh-turn are the prior art for the steer.

Load-bearing symmetry to note in the ADR: steering a running job (connection axis) is the exact analog of capturing edits back into CAS (filesystem axis, rosary-253408). Both are the "write-back" hard part; solving one informs the other. Custody-able creds (rosary-470270) are the enabler — a job can run detached (no interactive login) only if the vault holds the credential, which is why the vault-custody RCA gates this whole model.

title: [tmux-substrate W1] TmuxSpawn primitive — pure tmux wrapper in src/dispatch/tmux.rs
Move leyline-vcs (+ leyline-core, leyline-fs) from private ley-line to public ley-line-open
description:
## Why

rosary is PUBLIC. Its `leyline` feature (off by default per #190) pulls `leyline-vcs` from `agentic-research/ley-line` which is PRIVATE. Until the crates move to public, public clones must build with `--no-default-features` or have private-repo credentials. That's a permanent friction point and undermines the "rosary is open infra" message.

Long-term fix is to move the leyline-vcs crate (and its transitive path deps) to `agentic-research/ley-line-open` (public).

## What's in scope

3 crates totaling ~8000 LOC, all currently in `agentic-research/ley-line/rs/crates/`:

- `leyline-vcs` (1947 LOC) — jj sidecar for SQLite arena versioning + FUSE-backed virtual `.leyline/` time-travel directory. The crate rosary actually consumes.
- `leyline-core` (645 LOC) — `Controller` type used by leyline-vcs.
- `leyline-fs` (5398 LOC) — NFS/FUSE backing, validation, staging graph. Pulled by leyline-vcs.

## Verification done before filing

Scanned all three for proprietary content. **No matches** for: `chacha`, `x25519`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `secret`, `private_key`, `proprietary`, `enterprise`, `paid`, `premium`, `license-only`. The crates are VCS-sidecar / filesystem plumbing, not crypto/IP. Safe to publish.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `leyline-vcs`, `leyline-core`, `leyline-fs` exist in `agentic-research/ley-line-open/rs/crates/` (or wherever fits ley-line-open's layout) at versions matching what rosary currently pins.
- [ ] Old crate locations in `agentic-research/ley-line` either removed (cleanest) or marked deprecated with `[package.metadata.deprecated]` pointer to the new home.
- [ ] rosary `Cargo.toml` updated: `leyline-vcs = { git = "https://github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open", ... }` (URL + tag/branch).
- [ ] rosary `Cargo.toml` flips `default = []` back to `default = ["leyline"]` — public clones now build the integrated path natively.
- [ ] rosary `Taskfile.yml` reverts the temporary `--features leyline` pinning the comment in PR #190 noted.
- [ ] `task install` from a fresh public clone (no credentials) succeeds with the integrated jj sidecar.

## Out of scope

- Repo-level OSS-prep work (LICENSE files, README polish, contribution guide) for ley-line-open — that's its own work.
- FUSE/fuse-t install instructions in rosary README. Once ley-line-open ships the wrapper publicly, document it.
- Removing the temporary `default = []` workaround before the migration completes — keep it until rosary points at the public URL.

## Refs

- PR #190 — the temporary public-build fix this bead replaces.
- Audit notes: 0 red-flag keywords across all 3 crates, ~8000 LOC.

Filed for an out-of-band agent to handle since it's cross-repo work.

Test command: cd ../ley-line-open && cargo test --workspace

title: [tmux-substrate W2a] ClaudeTmux provider — AgentProvider impl wrapping TmuxSpawn
description:
## Scope

New `AgentProvider` impl in `src/dispatch/providers.rs` that spawns `claude -p` inside a TmuxSpawn session. Behind feature flag `dispatch-tmux`; legacy Claude provider stays available.

## Acceptance

- `ClaudeTmux` implements the existing `AgentProvider` trait
- Constructor accepts a bead worktree + agent prompt; creates a TmuxSpawn session named after the bead
- Sends `claude -p <prompt>` (with proper escaping) to the session
- `wait_complete()` polls `is_alive()` AND inspects pane output for the agent's exit marker
- Cleans up the session on completion (configurable: keep alive for human reattach vs auto-kill)
- Per-session worktree means parallel dispatches don't share state — pins the fix for rosary-44a542
- Feature-gated: building without `dispatch-tmux` doesn't include this module

## Tests (TDD, 5-7)

- `claude_tmux_dispatch_creates_session_in_bead_worktree`
- `claude_tmux_dispatch_fails_cleanly_when_tmux_missing`
- `claude_tmux_dispatch_uses_per_bead_worktree` (pin rosary-44a542 fix: parallel dispatches get distinct CWDs)
- `claude_tmux_dispatch_keeps_session_for_reattach_when_configured`
- `claude_tmux_dispatch_kills_session_on_clean_exit`
- `claude_tmux_command_escapes_special_chars_in_prompt` (security/correctness)

Mock the actual `claude` binary in tests — substitute with `echo "agent done"` or similar.

## Files

- `src/dispatch/providers.rs` (add `ClaudeTmux` struct + impl)
- `src/config.rs` (add `dispatch_tmux: bool` config knob)
- `Cargo.toml` ([features] dispatch-tmux = [])

## Risk

- **Command escaping**: claude -p takes a prompt that may contain shell metachars. Use a heredoc or send-keys with `-l` (literal) mode.
- **`claude` binary may not be in tmux session's PATH**: tmux inherits user's interactive shell env, but Brewed claude may need explicit PATH setup. Document in ADR.

## Depends on

- W1 (TmuxSpawn primitive)

## Closes (when shipped + W3)

- `rosary-44a542` (parallel agents share worktree)

## Time-box

M — ~1 day

title: Review→fix pipeline: staging-agent findings should auto-decompose into fix beads
description: Staging-agents (review perspective) find issues but can't fix them — they lack write permissions by design. In control-room, the color audit (control-room-09c52a) found 40+ hardcoded Color literals across 13 files, documented them perfectly in bead comments, but produced zero code changes. The surgical-reviewer found 2 HIGH bugs (data race in NetworkMonitor, unobservable Date.now in StaleBanner) that also need a dev-agent to fix. Current UX is broken: review comments sit as prose, someone must manually create fix beads and dispatch dev-agents. Need a review→fix pipeline where review agent structured output auto-decomposes into scoped fix beads for the next dispatch wave. Related to the @ask concept and ADR-004 dual state machine (verification phase should feed back into execution phase).

comments.text: After reading agents/ and dispatch.rs:agent_pipeline(), the pipeline tiers already define the chain (bug→dev→staging, feature→dev→staging→prod). The gap is: (1) pipeline phases don't auto-advance after agent completion — dispatch.rs:next_agent() exists but the conductor doesn't call it yet, (2) review beads are terminal (review→staging only) with no feedback loop into fix beads, (3) the conductor (ADR-004 Phase 2) is supposed to read phase-N comments and auto-decompose into child beads. The user escalation point should be when the agent can't produce a good enough spec OR when retry count exceeds threshold — not for every review→fix handoff.

title: [tmux-substrate W2b] rsry_active consults tmux ls for live sessions
description:
## Scope
