title: mache: Taskfile + CI still require fuse-t after FUSE backend removal
description:
Branch refactor/remove-fuse-backend removes cgofuse from go.mod but leaves Taskfile.yml and CI workflows requiring fuse-t/libfuse-dev.

Taskfile.yml:
- `check-fuse-t` task still checks for /Library/Frameworks/fuse_t.framework headers (line 23-37)
- `build` and `test` tasks both `deps: [check-fuse-t]` (lines 63, 90) — this BLOCKS builds on machines without fuse-t installed even though cgofuse is gone
- `CGO_CFLAGS` still points at fuse-t headers (line 14): these headers are never included by any remaining .go file; the flag is a no-op that adds noise and confuses people
- `setup` task still installs fuse-t via Homebrew (lines 39-50)

CI workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml, integration.yml, release.yml):
- Matrix includes `fuse_setup: brew install --cask fuse-t` and `fuse_setup: sudo apt-get install -y libfuse-dev`
- ci.yml has a dedicated "Install FUSE" step (line 34: `run: ${{ matrix.fuse_setup }}`) that runs on every build
- lint job has its own `Install FUSE headers` step (sudo apt-get install -y libfuse-dev)

These are now dead infrastructure — they add build time and will confuse contributors. On a fresh macOS machine without fuse-t, `task build` fails with "fuse-t not found" even though the binary no longer needs it.

Fix: remove check-fuse-t dep from build/test tasks, remove FUSE_T_HEADERS CGO_CFLAGS, remove fuse_setup matrix entries from CI workflows, update setup task.

title: [tmux-substrate W2c] Pane capture → cloister blob (closes rosary-125fc1)
description:
## Scope

Periodic `tmux capture-pane -p -S -` of each rsry-* session → content-addressed blob in cloister. Sidecar index maps bead_id + timestamp → blob hash for retrieval. Closes the impl side of `rosary-125fc1` (chat-log capture).

## Acceptance

- A capture worker (timer-based, configurable interval, default 60s) iterates rsry-* tmux sessions and captures each pane.
- Each capture is hashed (BLAKE3 or whatever cloister uses) and written to cloister as a blob.
- A sidecar table records `(bead_id, capture_timestamp, blob_hash, byte_size)` for retrieval.
- On session kill, a final capture is taken before cleanup so the agent's tail is preserved.
- Failure to write to cloister logs an error but does NOT crash the capture worker (the agent must outlive observability).
- Witchcraft (`rosary-e1760d`) can later read the blobs and build a semantic index over them.

## Files

title: mache: .query/ magic dir and semantic search silently broken after FUSE removal
description:
Branch refactor/remove-fuse-backend removes the FUSE backend (internal/fs/root.go) which was the only place that called SetQueryFunc() and SetSemanticSearchFunc(). These features are now dead in the NFS path.

Evidence:
- vfs.Resolver has EnableQuery() at internal/vfs/resolver.go:59 but it is NEVER called anywhere in the codebase after this branch (grep finds zero callers outside the deleted code)
- internal/nfsmount/graphfs.go has no SetQueryFunc, no SetSemanticSearchFunc, no EnableQuery call
- mountNFS() in cmd/mount.go wires SetPromptContent but has no .query/ or semantic wiring
- QueryHandler exists in internal/vfs/query.go but its Enabled field stays false for all NFS mounts
- The deleted mountFUSE() had explicit wiring: macheFs.SetQueryFunc(sg.QueryRefs) and macheFs.SetSemanticSearchFunc(...)

The .query/ directory will never appear in any NFS mount even though:
1. The vfs plumbing exists (QueryHandler, EnableQuery, vfs.Resolver)
2. The store backends (SQLiteGraph.QueryRefs, MemoryStore.QueryRefs) still work
3. Internal docs (CLAUDE.md line 70) still list .query/ as a virtual dir feature

This is a silent regression — the feature silently disappears with no error, no log message, no flag change. Users who relied on /.query/ SQL queries via the NFS mount will get ENOENT with no explanation.

Fix: wire EnableQuery + query execution into GraphFS/mountNFS, or explicitly document that .query/ is FUSE-only and removed in v0.7.0.

title: Doc generation as pipeline step — ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG, ADRs from agent work
description:
After agents complete work but before PR creation, a doc generation step synthesizes what changed into human-readable + agent-readable artifacts. This is a pipeline step, not an afterthought.

Outputs:
1. ARCHITECTURE.md updates — if the agent changed module boundaries, exports, or data flow, the architecture doc should reflect it. Agent diffs + mache structural analysis = auto-updated architecture.
2. CHANGELOG entry — what changed, why (from bead title/description), which agent phases it went through.
3. ADR creation — if the change is architectural (new module, new protocol, new dependency), auto-draft an ADR from the bead description + agent findings. BDR can then decompose it into future beads.
4. CLAUDE.md updates — if the agent added new tools, config options, or workflows, update the project instructions so future agents (and humans) know about them.

Design: a doc-agent perspective (or a step mode on existing agents) that runs after implementation but before PR creation. Read-only permissions — it reads the diff and writes docs, doesn't change code.

Pipeline integration:
  bug:     dev → staging → docs → PR
  feature: dev → staging → prod → docs → PR
  task:    dev → docs → PR

The docs step is fast (no compilation/testing) and catches the "code shipped but nobody updated the docs" anti-pattern. It's agentic-first: the docs are written for other agents to consume (CLAUDE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md) AND for humans to skim (CHANGELOG, ADR).

Golden Rule 8 (cite sources): every doc update must cite the bead ID and agent phase that produced it.

title: ACP client crate — native Rust Agent Client Protocol for multi-provider dispatch
description:
## Context

ADR-0002 accepted ACP integration. rosary dispatches agents via `claude -p` (fire-and-forget) which has auth issues from launchd context and no bidi streaming. The Agent SDK uses a stdin/stdout JSON protocol that needs `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `setup-token` for non-interactive auth.

## Goal

Write a Rust ACP client crate in the rosary workspace that replaces the current `ClaudeProvider` shell-out with native protocol support.

## What ACP gives us

- Bidi streaming: send prompts, receive events, send control messages (interrupt, permissions)
- Multi-provider: same protocol for Claude (via claude-agent-acp), Gemini ADK, Codex, local models
- Auth: `setup-token` + `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for non-interactive dispatch
- Session resumption: session_id tracking for continuation
- Permission handling: rosary can answer permission requests programmatically

## Implementation

1. `crates/acp-client/` — Rust crate implementing ACP client (JSON-RPC over stdio)
2. Wire into `dispatch/providers.rs` as `AcpProvider` replacing current `AcpCliProvider` stub
3. `setup-token` integration: read token at startup, pass to spawned agents
4. Preserve workspace on agent failure (no cleanup until post-mortem read)

## References

- ADR-0002 (accepted)
- https://github.com/anthropics/agent-client-protocol-schema
- https://github.com/zed-industries/claude-agent-acp (TS reference impl)
- Python SDK transport: subprocess_cli.py (wire format reference)

title: Design Claude↔Codex cross-provider handoff and communication
description: Follow-on design work for native Codex integration. Define how Rosary can let Claude Code and Codex communicate or hand work to each other through Rosary-owned primitives rather than ad hoc chat: beads, comments, handoff/observation records, agent definitions, phase transitions, thread/session references, MCP-visible context, and provider-native resume/visibility metadata. title: rsry dead-letter CLI surface — list + resolve dead-letter beads
description:
## Scope

Carve-out from rosary-c3034b (closed). The `DeadLetter` state + auto-detection shipped in PR #202; what's missing is a **CLI surface** for the operator side. Today the only way to resolve a dead-letter bead is `rsry bead update <id> --status open` — no listing, no batched resolve, no inspection of forensic detail.

## Acceptance

Two new subcommands under `rsry dead-letter` (or wherever feels right):

1. **`rsry dead-letter list`** — show all beads in `DeadLetter` state across registered repos, with forensic columns (pid, started_at, last_activity, work_dir, reason).
2. **`rsry dead-letter resolve <bead-id> --action {redispatch|close|reopen}`** — transition out of `DeadLetter` to the chosen state. Uses the existing `BeadState::DeadLetter => &[Open, Done]` allowed-transitions.
3. Tests cover both subcommands against an in-memory store.

## Estimate

~2-3h end-to-end. Pure CLI work — backend already supports the transitions.

## Provenance

Filed 2026-06-17 from subagent investigation of the rosary-c3034b family (agent ID aa864001a725f29d0). Original c3034b bead had a CLI requirement in its acceptance list but only the design intent shipped via PR #202.

title: dispatch.dead_session_grace_secs config — prevent false-positive dead-letter on fast finishers
description:
## Scope

Carve-out from rosary-c33e62 (closed). Today `sweep_dead_workers` (`src/dispatch/sweep.rs`) transitions a bead to `DeadLetter` immediately when the worker pid is dead, with no grace window on `last_activity`. Risk: a fast finisher (scoping-agent, or any agent that exits cleanly before the reconciler iterates) races the sweep — its pid is dead, bead is briefly `Dispatched`, gets false-positive dead-lettered.

## Acceptance

1. Add `dispatch.dead_session_grace_secs` to `Config` with default `300` (5 min).
2. Gate `sweep_dead_workers` to skip beads where `last_activity` is within grace_secs even when pid is dead. The reconciler iterates frequently enough that a fast-finisher's *next* iteration sees the bead at `Done` and never sweeps.
3. Test coverage: dead-pid + activity-within-grace → not swept; dead-pid + activity-stale → swept.

## Estimate

~2h.

## Provenance

Filed 2026-06-17 from subagent investigation of rosary-c33e62. Original bead had this as an explicit acceptance criterion that PR #202 didn't address.

title: AI-oriented bead sizing — "1 day = 1 shot" estimation model
description:
Human story points don't translate to agent work. Need an AI-native sizing model:

- "1 shot" = agent can complete in a single dispatch (one CC session, ~10min, one set of file edits + tests)
- "2 shot" = needs handoff between phases or a retry after feedback
- "multi-shot" = needs decomposition into 1-shot beads first

Sizing signals (automatable):
- File count in scope (1-3 files = 1-shot, 4-8 = 2-shot, 8+ = decompose)
- Cross-module changes (same module = 1-shot, cross-module = 2-shot)
- Test existence (tests exist to validate = 1-shot, needs new test strategy = 2-shot)
- Schema changes (no schema = 1-shot, schema + wiring = multi-shot)

This replaces human time estimates. The reconciler could auto-size at triage using file scopes + mache structural analysis. Oversized beads get flagged for decomposition before dispatch.

Related: BDR decompose (produces sized BeadSpecs), dispatch timeout (currently 10min = 1 shot budget), the overnight mode preference for small/mechanical beads.

title: Design: rsry-in-cloister credential model — Linear/3p creds via CredentialVault proxy, identity via lease cert (rsry holds no plaintext)
description:
## Vision
The endgame for rosary's third-party credentials (Linear API key first, then GitHub etc.) when rsry runs as a cloister-hosted bundle: **rsry holds no plaintext credential at all.** Outbound calls route through cloister's CredentialVault, which injects headers and never lets plaintext surface. "Nothing to rotate, nothing to leak."

## This is modeled, not aspirational
cloister `cluster.toml` already declares rosary as a hosted bundle:
```
[[bundles]] name = "rosary"
image = "rosary:0.2.0"
args  = ["mcp","--ipc-socket","/run/cloister-uds/rosary.sock"]
binding = "ROSARY_BUNDLE"   # kind = "external"
```
Trust tiers:
- **cloister-router** (hypervisor tier, singleton): the only external TCP listener; `holdsCredential = ["VAULT_KEK_SOURCE","VAULT_STORE"]`. The CredentialVault DO lives here.
- **notme-identity** (hypervisor tier): Signet master CA + lease-cert mint — the identity/auth substrate.
- **rosary** (lower tier): holds NO credentials.

CredentialVault (`cloister/vault/`, lifted from notme): AES-GCM envelope encryption, `checkAccess` sub-glob matcher, **proxies outbound requests** with identity-scoped checks. `VAULT_KEK_SOURCE` is itself a kek-source URL (`keychain://`/`op://`/`env://`/`http(s)://`, resolved by `leyline-sign-helper`; ADR-0014 + ADR-0019) — i.e. the kek-source scheme is the root of the vault's own trust chain.

## The three gates (why this is "not too optimistic, but gated")
1. **Modeled ≠ running.** Live rsry today is the launchd `com.rosary.serve` HTTP daemon on :8383, not the cloister bundle over UDS. The vault-proxy path doesn't exist for the launchd runtime.
2. **Auth model is the hard part.** lease-cert identity → vault scoped access → cross-DO handoff (ADR-0011 three-criterion / ADR-0012). This is the adversarially load-bearing boundary (bundle-isolation / trust-root / lease-replay reviewers exist for exactly it). "Gate the auth right" is doing most of the work.
3. **Migration.** launchd daemon → cloister external bundle; tracked under the `mcp-transport-canonical` / `daemon-*` decades.

## Sequence (this bead is the endgame)
- now — rsry-5af158 (P0): chmod 0600 + rotate, on the launchd runtime
- bridge — adopt kek-source `keychain://` in `config.rs` (correct in BOTH worlds; on-path, never wasted)
- endgame — THIS: rsry bundles into cloister; Linear key moves to CredentialVault; rsry holds nothing; vault proxies; gated on lease-cert auth

## Relationship
This is rosary-752f9b ("rsry as sole sync hub") taken to its limit: "external systems aren't things agents hold creds for" becomes literally true — rsry never touches the Linear key.

## TODO when picked up
Wire `depends_on` to the concrete (a) rsry-as-cloister-bundle migration bead and (b) lease-cert auth-model bead once those IDs are identified (left unwired here to avoid false-blocking links).

title: notme: CRITICAL — X-Client-Cert header is attacker-controlled, bypasses CA verification
description: In worker/worker.ts:1367, the /token endpoint falls back to X-Client-Cert for identity if no session cookie is present. It calls verifyX509(decodeURIComponent(certPem), "") — passing an empty string as the CA public key. In verify-proof.ts:verifyX509(), the CA is constructed via `new X509Certificate(caPublicKeyPem)` where caPublicKeyPem is "". This will throw or produce a garbage CryptoKey, but critically X-Client-Cert is NOT a Cloudflare-injected header — wrangler.toml has no mTLS configuration. Any attacker can POST to /token with a self-signed cert in X-Client-Cert. Even if verifyX509 throws and returns 401, the code path is structurally broken — an attacker who crafts a cert that passes @peculiar/x509 date checks and whose verifyX509 somehow doesn't throw gets principalId set to the cert's CN (arbitrary string), then getPrincipalScopes is called — if that principal doesn't exist, scopes returns [] and the request continues with no scopes. Attack: POST /token with X-Client-Cert containing a self-signed cert with CN=<victim-principal-UUID>. Even if scopes is empty, the rate limiter fires against the victim's principalId.

comments.text: Verified fixed. worker/worker.ts:1711-1717 has X-Client-Cert path removed (mTLS not configured in wrangler.toml, so the header was attacker-controlled). /token now requires session cookie. Cross-correlated during security sweep — see notme commit 0c5e296.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: HIGH — DPoP htu hardcoded to auth.notme.bot in dpop-handler.ts, bypasses origin validation
description: dpop-handler.ts:54 hardcodes htu: "https://auth.notme.bot/token". The worker.ts /token route correctly derives htu from request origin (line 1397). But dpop-handler.ts (the tested path used in unit tests) hardcodes the production URL. Any self-hosted deploy of notme where the authority URL is different will silently accept DPoP proofs with htu=auth.notme.bot regardless of the actual host — or reject all proofs if the host differs. More dangerously: a proof stolen from auth.notme.bot can be replayed against a self-hosted instance that uses dpop-handler.ts directly, because the htu check passes against the hardcoded value. The fix previously described as "htu derived from origin" only applies to the inline /token route in worker.ts — dpop-handler.ts was not updated.

comments.text: Verified fixed. worker/src/auth/dpop-handler.ts:56 reads htu from input.tokenEndpointUrl (caller-supplied). HandleTokenInput interface (line 21-22) documents the contract. worker.ts derives the URL from the request origin at line 1733: 'htu: `${new URL(request.url).origin}/token`'. No hardcoded auth.notme.bot string remains.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: HIGH — WebAuthn authentication challenge not bound to credential ID, enables cross-credential replay
description: In worker/src/auth/passkey.ts:authenticationOptions() (line 197), the challenge is stored with no user_id: INSERT into passkey_challenges (challenge, type) — no user_id column. In verifyAuthentication() (line 219), the challenge is fetched by type='authentication' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 — takes the most recent challenge regardless of which credential is authenticating. Attack scenario: Alice initiates a login (challenge CA generated, stored). Bob immediately initiates a login (challenge CB generated — now the most recent). Bob completes his authentication using CB. Alice's client, receiving challenge CA, could be tricked by a race into signing CB if the server returns CB. More practically: if two authentication flows are in flight simultaneously, any completion picks up the latest challenge, not the one issued to that specific session. The fix requires binding challenges to a session nonce or credential hint returned to the client during options.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit 0c5e296. verifyAuthentication (worker/src/auth/passkey.ts) was using ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1. New flow: decode the challenge from the assertion's clientDataJSON (base64url JSON, contains the WebAuthn challenge per spec), look it up by exact value scoped to type='authentication' AND created_at within 5 minutes. Returns {verified:false} on miss instead of throwing. Each flow's unique nonce is now its session identifier, so concurrent flows can't stomp each other. 4 new tests under passkey.challenge.session-binding: rejects unknown challenge, malformed clientDataJSON, missing challenge field, regression guard for empty DB. Threat model: 2 new rows added (session-binding, unknown-rejected). Registration flow uses WHERE user_id=? — not affected.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: HIGH — bootstrap reset endpoint uses timing-unsafe string comparison
description: worker/worker.ts:1193 compares bootstrap codes with `body.bootstrapCode !== code` — a direct string equality check that is vulnerable to timing side-channels. An attacker who can make repeated requests to /auth/passkey/reset can measure response latency to infer the bootstrap code character by character. The bootstrap code is a UUID (36 chars), so this is 36 comparison points. The fix is to use a constant-time comparison (crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual or equivalent). Note: the bootstrap code is also logged to wrangler tail in plaintext (signing-authority.ts:605), which is a separate exposure vector for anyone with log access.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit 0c5e296. worker.ts:1480 'body.bootstrapCode !== code' inline compare replaced with 'await authority.consumeBootstrapCode(body.bootstrapCode)'. consumeBootstrapCode runs the comparison through timingSafeEqual (worker/src/auth/timing-safe.ts:25-35) — HMAC-SHA256 digest both sides, constant-time XOR. 5 new tests under passkey.bootstrap.timing-safe: equal/equal, different-same-length, different-length, prefix-vs-full, empty boundary. Threat model: passkey.bootstrap.timing-safe row added.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: MEDIUM — keyIdFromSpki uses djb2 hash, collisions grant wrong-key trust
description: signing-authority.ts:65-73: keyIdFromSpki() generates an 8-hex-char (32-bit) key ID using a djb2 hash over the last 32 bytes of the SPKI. 32-bit hash space means ~1-in-4-billion collision probability — not zero. The key ID is embedded in issued certs (authority.key_id), in the CA bundle (bundle.keyId), and used during revocation checks (revocation.ts:234: token.keyId !== bundle.keyId). If two different CA keypairs hash to the same keyId, a token issued by the old key would pass the keyId check against the new key's bundle. Given that rotation generates a new keypair, a sophisticated attacker who can influence key generation timing could attempt to manufacture a collision. Use SHA-256 truncated to 8 bytes instead.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit 60d2eee. Truncation widened from 4 bytes (32-bit, ~65k birthday-collision threshold) to 8 bytes (64-bit, ~4 billion). Earlier fix swapped djb2 for SHA-256 but kept 4-byte truncation — collision space was unchanged. Algorithm extracted to worker/src/key-id.ts so tests exercise the production code (the previous test reimplemented djb2 and tested itself in isolation). Existing 8-hex keyIds in deployed DOs persist; new key generations produce 16-hex.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: MEDIUM — revocation fails open when bundle has no issuedAt (stale check skipped)
description: revocation.ts:203: the staleness check is gated on `if (bundle.issuedAt !== undefined)`. CABundle.issuedAt is declared optional. If the issuing side (signet Go implementation) omits issuedAt, the entire staleness check is skipped and an arbitrarily old bundle is accepted as valid. An attacker who can write to CA_BUNDLE_CACHE KV (compromised KV credentials) could publish a bundle without issuedAt and a forged-but-valid signature from an old key, and the staleness guard would not fire. The field should be required, and bundles missing it should be treated as invalid rather than trusted.

comments.text: Duplicate of rosary-9bb26b — same staleness fail-open. Closed by notme commit ca47125 (CABundle.issuedAt now required + runtime isBundleStale fails closed for missing/NaN/non-positive). 6 tests under revocation.bundle.staleness.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: MEDIUM — /token DPoP JTI stored after mint, creates TOCTOU window for replay
description: worker/worker.ts:1404-1419: the /token route checks the DPoP JTI for replay (line 1406), then mints the token (line 1411), then stores the JTI (line 1419). There is a window between the check and the store where a concurrent request with the same DPoP proof will also pass the replay check (KV GET returns null for both), both will mint tokens, and only one will store the JTI. The result is two valid access tokens issued for one DPoP proof. In a DO context this is hard to exploit at scale, but KV is eventually consistent — two Worker invocations on different CF edge nodes can race on the same KV key. The JTI should be stored atomically before minting, or the entire operation should be serialized inside the SigningAuthority DO.

comments.text: Stale — worker.ts /token already stores JTI BEFORE mint (line 1790). Bead description claimed line 1419 had the bug but the actual code (verified during rosary-9b969c work) is correct. The companion bead rosary-9b969c covered the real divergent path in dpop-handler.ts.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: MEDIUM — /cert/gha rate limiter uses non-atomic KV read-increment-write, parallel requests bypass limit
description: worker/worker.ts:100-117: the GHA cert rate limiter reads the counter (KV GET), increments in memory, checks against the limit, then writes back. Two concurrent requests for the same repo will both read count=N, both increment to N+1, both pass the limit check if N+1 <= RL_MAX, and both write N+1. The effective limit is 2*RL_MAX for concurrent requests. With RL_MAX=10 and a burst of 10 parallel CI jobs, all 10 can race past the counter. Same issue exists in /token (lines 1382-1390). KV does not support atomic increment; move rate limiting into the SigningAuthority DO using DO storage transactions, or use a DO as a rate limit coordinator.

comments.text: Stale — /cert/gha rate limiter migrated to CF's atomic rate-limit binding (worker.ts:360-366 uses platform.rateLimit which wraps env.CERT_LIMITER.limit() — see platform.ts:192-197). Comment in code: 'Rate limit — atomic, edge-fast (replaces KV-based TOCTOU-vulnerable limiter).' Closing.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: LOW — canGrant() in principals.ts is defined but never called, scope delegation not enforced
description: principals.ts:143 defines canGrant() which checks that the grantor has authorityManage AND the scope being granted. The invite creation flow in worker.ts:1038-1041 re-implements this check inline. canGrant() is never called anywhere in the codebase. The risk is that future code paths that grant capabilities (e.g. a future admin API) may skip the check and call grantCapability() directly, silently granting unauthorized scopes. Either remove canGrant() and keep the inline check, or wire canGrant() into grantCapability() so the invariant is enforced at the data layer.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit c9bb3b9. /invites POST now uses canGrant() instead of the inline check, killing the duplication. 5 new tests pin the predicate's behavior. The function is no longer dead code.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme: LOW — verifyAccessToken does not validate iss, aud, or nbf claims
description: token.ts:93-139: verifyAccessToken() checks signature and exp only. It does not validate iss (issuer), aud (audience), or nbf (not-before). A token minted for audience "attacker.com" will pass verification when checked by a resource server for "victim.com" if they share the same public key. The cnf.jkt claim is also not validated by this function — callers must remember to check DPoP binding themselves. This is a library function used by resource servers downstream; incomplete claim validation at the verification layer is a class of bug that tends to be exploited when callers forget the extra checks.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit ed5600d. SDK verifyAccessToken now delegates to shared validateClaims (covers exp/nbf/iat/iss/aud/sub uniformly). New audience and issuer options on VerifyAccessTokenOptions. Also activated 52 dormant SDK tests by extending worker/vitest.config.ts to glob ../gen/ts/__tests__ — they're now under CI signal. Test count: 150 → 207 (5 new + 52 newly-activated).
comments.author: jamestexas

title: Observation fold ignores terminal-fail: Deadletter/Fail bead folds to highest non-fail verdict (R4b flip blocker)
description: Surfaced by rsry lattice audit on the real store (PR #298): rosary-11214e persisted=blocked but folded=PrOpen. title: Bead files field: make required on create, backfill existing beads via mache
description:
## Problem

0/200 beads have `files` populated. This blocks blast radius dedup (ADR-003), pre-flight validation, and scoped agent dispatch. The field exists in the schema but nothing enforces it.

## Stage 1: Enforce on create

Update `rsry_bead_create` MCP tool and `bd create` CLI to require `files` for actionable issue types.

**Required for**: bug, task, feature, chore (implementation work — must know what code to touch)
**Optional for**: epic, design, research, review (may not reference specific files yet)

Semantics: `files` is "what this bead intends to change." Can be file paths, directory paths, or module names. At least one entry required for actionable types.

**PATCH vs MERGE consideration**: `rsry_bead_comment` and future `rsry_bead_update` should NOT require files — they're patching an existing bead, not replacing it. Only `rsry_bead_create` enforces the requirement. If we add an `rsry_bead_update` tool later, it should be PATCH semantics (only update fields that are provided, leave others unchanged). Don't require re-specifying files to add a comment or change status.

### Changes
- `src/serve.rs`: validate `files` is non-empty for actionable issue_types in `tool_bead_create`
- `src/cli.rs`: same validation for `bd create` 
- Return clear error: "files required for {issue_type} beads — specify which code this bead touches"

## Stage 2: Backfill existing beads

Use mache MCP to derive file scope from bead descriptions, dogfooding rsry's own tools.

For each bead without `files`:
1. Parse description for code references (file paths, function names, module names)
2. Call `mcp__mache__search` to resolve references to actual symbols
3. Call `mcp__mache__find_callers` / `find_callees` (depth 1) for blast radius hints
4. Write back via rsry MCP (`rsry_bead_update` or direct Dolt if update tool doesn't exist yet)

This should be dispatched as an agent task — a dev-agent scanning beads across repos using mache projections. One bead per repo (rosary: 139, mache: 29, etc.) or one bead for the whole backfill.

**Important**: beads for repos other than rosary need mache projected against THAT repo, not rosary. The agent needs to `mache get_overview` per repo.

### Depends on
- Stage 1 (enforce on create) should land first so new beads don't add to the backfill pile
- mache must be running and projected for each target repo

## Related
- ADR-003 (blast radius dedup — files field is prerequisite for Layers 2 and 3)
- rosary-1dddfa (pre-flight pipeline — validates files are scoped before dispatch)
- rsry-acab33 (bead schema: add files and test_files fields — already done/closed)

comments.text: Starting Stage 1: enforce `files` on `rsry_bead_create` for actionable issue types. Reading serve.rs and cli.rs to understand current implementation.

title: Dead dispatches/pipelines inflate 'active' forever — no reaper runs + list_active_pipelines has no terminal filter
description:
Found by dogfooding: the statusline showed 14 'active' agents but ZERO live workers — all corpses in the shared ~/.rsry/backend.db (13 pipeline rows + 1 dispatch, oldest from 2026-07-04). Manually reaped (UPDATE dispatches SET completed_at WHERE completed_at IS NULL; DELETE FROM pipelines) to unstick it.

Two coupled defects:
1. list_active_pipelines (src/store_sqlite.rs:459) returns ALL rows of the `pipelines` table with NO WHERE filter on phase_status — so a pipeline row is counted 'active' forever until it's DELETEd via clear_pipeline (only called on legitimate completion). A dispatch that dies without completing leaves its row lingering indefinitely. Fix: filter out terminal phase_status ('done','deadletter') in the query, OR ensure dead-dispatch detection calls clear_pipeline.
2. The reaper (dispatch/sweep.rs orphan-sweep + janitor-agent dead-session detection) ONLY runs inside a reconcile iteration. With no `rsry serve`/reconcile daemon running, nothing ever reaps — corpses accumulate permanently. This is worsened by the shared-backend/multi-writer topology (CLI + MCP + multiple chats all write one backend.db): failing dispatches from any context (e.g. the concurrent ley-line-open chat dying on 'Not logged in', rosary-b1495c) each leave a stale row, and the 'active' count only grows.

Fix direction: (a) terminal-filter list_active_pipelines; (b) run the orphan/dead reap on MCP-server startup and/or opportunistically inside rsry_active (a read that reports N active should first reap the provably-dead), so a standalone `rsry_active`/statusline is self-healing without a full reconcile daemon; (c) optionally a `rsry reap` CLI. Relates to rosary-b1495c ('Not logged in' dispatch failures that generate the corpses).

Also note: 39 dead session-registry worktrees remain under ~/.rsry/worktrees (needs_merge) — separate disk-cruft cleanup; some may hold unmerged branch work, so do not blind-nuke.

title: README as projection: BDR-generated docs from codebase state + mache + beads
description:
## Idea

README.md is a projection, not a hand-maintained document. Generated from actual codebase state using BDR (reverse direction: atoms → markdown) + mache (code structure → mermaid) + bead status.

## Generated sections

| Section | Source |
|---------|--------|
| Architecture diagram | mache get_communities → mermaid flowchart |
| Module map | mache get_overview → table with file counts, symbols |
| Status / progress | rsry status → bead counts, phase progress from loom-2al |
| Agent definitions | agents/*.md frontmatter → role/description table |
| Key source files | mache list_directory → file purpose table |
| Recent activity | git log + bead close history → changelog |

## Static sections (preserved by BDR)

Intro paragraph, installation, license, contributing — hand-written, BDR marks them as atoms it doesn't regenerate.

## Command

`rsry render readme` or `rsry docs` — renders README.md from current state. Could run as a pre-commit hook or GHA step.

## BDR reverse direction

BDR currently: markdown → atoms (decompose). New: atoms → markdown (compose). The README template defines the structure, BDR fills in generated sections, preserves static sections.

## Mache mermaid integration

Depends on the mache mermaid bead for bidirectional diagrams. Mache projects code structure as mermaid, README embeds it. Edit the mermaid in README → mache could theoretically update code structure (stretch goal).

## Why this matters

The README is the most-read file and the first thing that goes stale. Making it a projection means it's always accurate. "The docs ARE the system" — same philosophy as beads (work items in repos, not external trackers).

comments.text: Simpler than originally scoped. Mache already has bdr-schema.json (beads as FS), markdown-schema.json (markdown with write-back), and the code schemas. The README is just a mache projection — mount beads + code, render template from the mount. BDR's role is only the ADR→beads direction. Mache handles the reverse (structured data → markdown). Depends on mache-ml2 (mermaid output) and mache-85t (beads schema with mermaid deps). Implementation is a schema file + a small render script, not a Rust feature.

title: Dolt auto-start port race (TOCTOU) — flaky tests + real multi-repo production race
description:
RTFM'd the Dolt flake instead of waving it away. Root cause in DoltClient::connect (src/dolt/mod.rs): the ephemeral-port allocation binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads the port, DROPS the listener, then spawns 'dolt sql-server -P <port>'. Classic TOCTOU: between drop and Dolt binding, another concurrent connect() can grab the same just-freed port → the two servers collide → intermittent startup/query failure.

Manifested as: migrate_repairs_partial_005 (+ other Dolt tests) flaky under parallel 'cargo test' (many connect() calls racing). But it's also a REAL production race — rosary auto-starts a Dolt server per repo, and connecting to multiple repos concurrently hits the same window.

Fix (no new dependency): serialize the alloc→spawn→ready window with a process-global tokio::sync::Mutex in a OnceLock (tokio because we .await the readiness wait inside). One startup at a time; the port is held by a live server before the next allocation runs. Verified: full suite 1296/0 across 4 consecutive runs (was intermittently failing 1).

Uses std + tokio (already deps).

title: Audit ART primitives (ley-line, mache, tropo) for pipeline schema reuse
description:
Before designing the pipeline schema / handoff layer between Rust (rsry) and Elixir (conductor), audit existing ART ecosystem primitives to avoid reinventing IPC:

- **ley-line**: Content-addressing (ChaCha + CAS). Handoff artifacts could be CAS objects — immutable, content-addressed, verifiable. Already used for VCS layer.
- **mache**: Structural code intelligence. Pipeline DAG could be visualized via mache (community detection for agent scoping, call graphs for file overlap). Mermaid output (mache-ml2) needed for DAG rendering.
- **tropo**: Transform layer (less mature). Could model handoff transforms — e.g., dev-agent output → staging-agent input as a typed transform.

The goal: the Rust↔Elixir handoff schema should compose from existing primitives, not be a bespoke format. rosary-c5266a (Pipeline as DAG) and rosary-c1d937 (Handoff quality) both depend on this audit to avoid building on sand.

Cross-refs: rosary-c5266a, rosary-c1d937, ADR-004, ADR-005 (reactive store).

title: Conventional commits + GH automation: close the bead↔PR↔files loop
description:
## Idea

Conventional commit scopes map to bead file scope. PR diffs provide ground truth for what files actually changed. GitHub Actions can automate the bead lifecycle from commit/PR events.

## The loop

1. Bead created with estimated `files` scope
2. Agent works, makes conventional commits: `feat(dispatch): wire ACP` with `bead: rosary-xyz` in footer
3. PR opened — actual changed files visible from diff
4. GH Action on PR open: call `rsry_bead_comment` with PR link, update bead `files` from diff
5. PR merged — GH Action on merge: call `rsry_bead_close` via rsry HTTP webhook
6. Bead `files` updated to ground truth (what actually changed, not what was estimated)

## Conventional commit → bead mapping

- `feat(scope)` → issue_type: feature
- `fix(scope)` → issue_type: bug
- `docs(scope)` → issue_type: docs
- `refactor(scope)` → issue_type: chore
- Scope string → module/directory → bead `files` hint
- Footer `bead: rosary-xyz` → links commit to bead

## GH Actions needed

- On PR open: parse bead refs from commit messages, update beads with PR URL
- On PR merge: close linked beads via rsry HTTP endpoint
- On commit push: extract files changed, update bead `files` field

## Related

- rosary-1e137e (PR-as-execution-surface)
- rosary-8284bf (files field enforcement + backfill)
- rosary-13b5df (dogfooding — require bead ref in commits)
- Existing Linear webhook integration (same pattern, different source)

title: Flaky test: detached_child_runs_and_survives_handle_drop races file-exists vs content-written (TOCTOU on marker)
description:
Observed 2026-07-16 failing CI on PR #367 (a license-metadata-only diff — cannot be causal) while passing on #371 minutes earlier with identical dispatch code.

Race (src/dispatch/mod.rs ~1135-1162): the child runs `sh -c 'printf started > marker; sleep 5'`. The shell redirection opens/creates `marker` BEFORE printf writes to it. The test's `wait_for(|| marker.exists(), 2s)` returns on creation, then `assert_eq!(read_to_string(marker), "started")` at mod.rs:1158 can read an empty file on a slow runner → `assertion left == right failed`.

Fix: make the wait condition check CONTENT, not existence — `wait_for(|| std::fs::read_to_string(&marker).map(|s| s == "started").unwrap_or(false), 2s)` — and drop the separate assert_eq (or keep it after the content-wait as a no-op safety). Alternatively have the child write to marker.tmp and rename (atomic publish), but the content-wait is the minimal fix.

A flaky test in the main suite fails EVERY dispatch verify tier (see rosary-59ff84 precedent) and every unrelated PR's task check — worth fixing promptly.

NOTE: this did NOT block the v0.9.0 release PR #397 — that was a separate real failure (server.json version drift), not this test. Priority to fix stands: a flaky test that hard-fails poisons every dispatch's `test` verify tier (rosary-59ff84 pattern).

title: Switch leyline-vcs Git URL: agentic-research/ley-line → agentic-research/ley-line-open
description:
**Follow-up to ley-line-open-889173** (lift on 2026-05-09).

`Cargo.toml:31` currently:
```
leyline-vcs = { git = "https://github.com/agentic-research/ley-line", default-features = false, optional = true }
```

Two issues:
1. `agentic-research/ley-line` is **private**. The crate has been removed from there (lifted to ley-line-open). Once that ley-line commit publishes, fetching from this URL with `--features leyline` either auths-fails (public clones) or finds no `leyline-vcs` package (after the deletion).
2. `agentic-research/ley-line-open` is **public** and now hosts the canonical `leyline-vcs` at `rs/ll-open/vcs/`.

## Fix

Change line 31 to:
```
leyline-vcs = { git = "https://github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open", default-features = false, optional = true }
```

Cargo will discover the `leyline-vcs` package by name within the ll-open workspace.

## Verification

- `cargo build` (no features) still works (default = [] keeps vcs out — already done).
- `cargo build --features leyline` resolves the new URL and pulls the lifted crate.
- `task build` (which passes `--features leyline`) succeeds locally.

## Notes

- The lifted `leyline-vcs` is on the T2.4 Controller API (`current_root: [u8; 32]`); rosary's `src/vcs.rs` uses `JjIntegration` only, which is unchanged by the migration. No rosary code edits expected.
- Wait for ley-line-open commit `feat: lift leyline-vcs + leyline-sign from ley-line` (filed under bead `ley-line-open-889173`) to be pushed to `origin/main` before flipping the URL, otherwise Cargo can't find the package.

title: Safe branch cleanup: janitor agent garbage-collects merged/closed agent branches
description:
Agent dispatches create fix/rosary-* branches on origin that accumulate. Need safe automated cleanup.

Safety rules:
1. Only delete branches whose bead is closed/done (query Dolt)
2. Only delete branches whose PR is merged or closed (query GitHub API)
3. Never delete branches with active dispatches (check rsry_active)
4. Never delete branches that are ahead of main with unmerged commits
5. Dry-run mode that lists what would be deleted without acting

Implementation:
- New janitor task: `rsry cleanup-branches` CLI command
- Queries: list remote branches matching fix/* pattern → cross-reference bead status + PR status + active dispatches
- Uses GitHub App auth (rosary-stringer) for branch deletion API
- Add to janitor-agent.md as a scheduled sweep task
- Reconciler can run this after each iteration (or on a slower cadence)

Testing requirement: needs a disposable git repo to test against. Options:
- Docker container with local git server (gitea/gogs)
- Temp directory with `git init --bare` + worktree
- Sprites container with test repo

The container approach is safest — test cleanup logic against throwaway repos before running on real origin. Could be the first use of the e2e container test infra (bead rosary-a3b2cf).

Risk: deleting a branch that an agent is actively pushing to. The active dispatch check (rule 3) + the "ahead of main" check (rule 4) are the safety net.

4. Open PR via gh CLI (not done — currently ff-merges or manual)

- Multi-phase pipeline (dev → staging → prod)
- OTP supervision + crash recovery
- Concurrent dispatch (3+ agents)
- Remote compute (Sprites)
- Handoff context between phases
- Overnight unattended operation

The free tier is "attended dispatch, one at a time, human reviews PR." The paid tier is "overnight dispatch, multi-agent, multi-phase, wake up to PRs."

description:
After lifting schema-bridge into notme (rosary-1b914d), `task gen:zod` against `notme/schema/identity.capnp` fails with:

  schema-bridge: unmapped capnp construct `annotation` at node id=bea97f1023792be0:
  add a mapping for `annotation` in schema-bridge, or open an issue

Root cause: identity.capnp uses `$Go.package(...)` and `$Go.import(...)` for the Go codegen task. capnp emits the imported `/go.capnp` file's annotation **declarations** (`annotation package(file) :Text;` etc.) as `Node.Annotation` nodes in the CodeGeneratorRequest. schema-bridge currently rejects all `Node.Annotation` nodes at packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs:128-130.

These annotation declarations have zero impact on zod output (they describe Go codegen) but trip the fail-fast policy.

Fix options (need design call):

1. Skip `Node.Annotation` declarations whose containing file is NOT the schema being compiled (i.e., imported ones). Preserves fail-fast for new annotations in your own schema.
2. Allowlist Go's annotation file id (`@0xd12a1c51fedd6c88`) the same way `ANN_JSON_*` constants are tracked. Most explicit.
3. Strip `$Go.*` from identity.capnp and put Go annotations in a sidecar file. Heavy.

Option 2 fits schema-bridge's existing pattern best.

Until this lands, `task gen:zod` in notme is documented-as-failing in the Taskfile comment; the lift itself is complete.

Files:
- packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs
- packages/schema-bridge/tests/integration.rs (new test case)
- gen/ts/identity.zod.ts (will be created once the codegen succeeds)

title: Auto-close beads whose commits already shipped (reconcile bead status from git/PR state)
description:
## Problem

554 open beads, 465 ready. But the bead backlog is fiction — the March 2026 build-out (8,848 prompts that month, top 4 repos: rosary 2367, rig 1728, x-ray 1409, mache 1284) shipped a ton of code without bead-closing discipline catching up. Bead refs in typed prompts didn't exist before March (0 refs Sept-Feb, 56 in March, 54 in May), so most bead-close was happening manually after-the-fact and most didn't happen at all.

Evidence: spot-checks during the chat-corpus analysis (2026-05-17) found beads marked `open` whose IDs appear in merged commits on main. The bead system is younger than half the work it's tracking.

## Proposed behavior

One-time cleanup pass + ongoing reconciler step.

### One-time pass

For each `open` (or `ready`, or `in_progress`) bead:

1. Search every registered repo for commits referencing the bead ID:
   - `git log --all --grep="<bead-id>" --format=...`
   - Match canonical commit-prefix pattern: `[<bead-id>] type(scope): msg`
2. If any matching commit was merged to the default branch → propose closure
3. If the bead has `pr_url` filled and the PR is merged via gh API → auto-close
4. Otherwise leave open

Report mode (`rsry reconcile --dry-run`) lists candidate closures with a one-line justification before doing anything.

### Ongoing reconciler step

Wire the same check into the existing reconciler loop (rosary-c6386e splits this into 3 cadences) so newly-merged commits auto-update bead state without a daily cleanup ritual.

## Why this matters

- The "ready" list is overwhelming because it's not real — many of those beads are already done
- Dispatchers (and humans) pick from `ready`, so false-positive opens waste agent time
- Pairs naturally with the existing `rosary-54145e` (GitHub merge webhook → advance dependents) and `rosary-3eef9c` (write pr_url on webhook match) work
- Unblocks honest dispatch-budget planning — the optimization analysis assumed 50/day dispatch against 465 ready, but the real number is probably closer to 200

## Files (touches)

- `src/reconcile/mod.rs` — add a `reconcile_bead_completion` step
- `src/github.rs` — already has gh CLI integration; reuse the PR-merged check
- `src/cli.rs` — add `rsry reconcile bead-completion [--dry-run]` subcommand
- `src/bead.rs` or `src/bead_dolt.rs` — bead state update plumbing (likely already exists)

## Test plan

- Unit: parse-commit-prefix regex against fixture commits (real bead IDs + adversarial inputs)
- Integration: small temp repo + dolt DB, commit a `[test-bead-abc123]` message, run reconciler, assert bead closes
- Dry-run mode: never mutates dolt

title: Dispatched-agent default prompt: "continue when you can, only stop when you need a real decision"
description:
## Problem

Over 8 months of `~/.claude/history.jsonl` (18,820 typed prompts), the user typed:

- "pls cont" × **115**
- "pls do" × **46**
- "yes pls" × **35**
- "hit it" × **21**
- "lets do it" × **20**
- "pls continue" × **19**
- "lets do'r" × **17**
- "oops go ahead" × **11**
- "try now?" × **10**

That's ~300 nudge prompts where the user is unblocking an agent that paused unnecessarily. Each one is a round-trip context-switch cost.

The agents are asking permission they didn't need — typically after finishing a step where the next step was obvious from the original prompt.

## Proposed change

Add a sentence to every dispatched agent's system prompt (rosary owns these via `agents/*.md` + the dispatch wrapper that builds the final prompt):

> "When you finish a step and the next step follows directly from the original task description, continue without asking. Only stop when you need a decision the user hasn't already made, when you've completed the task, or when you've hit a real blocker."

Audit the existing per-agent definitions in `agents/dev-agent.md`, `scoping-agent.md`, `pm-agent.md`, etc. — some may already have stronger autonomy guidance; this is the fallback default.

## Why this matters

- Direct elimination of the 300+ nudge prompts is the largest single workflow tax in the user's 8-month history
- Doesn't change behavior on real blockers (the agent should still stop when genuinely stuck)
- Composes with the `continue-when-context-running-out` pattern from rosary-1e137e (full feature pipeline)

## Risk

Over-autonomous agents might charge ahead when they should stop. Mitigation:
- Keep "stop on real blockers" explicit in the prompt
- The existing `continue-if-needed` decision is already happening; this just biases the default
- Easy to roll back — single-line prompt change

## Files

- `agents/dev-agent.md`
- `agents/scoping-agent.md`
- `agents/pm-agent.md`
- `agents/architect-agent.md`
- `agents/janitor-agent.md`
- `agents/staging-agent.md`
- Any dispatch wrapper that composes the final system prompt (`src/dispatch.rs` or `src/dispatch/providers.rs`)

## Test plan

- Manual: dispatch a multi-step bead and observe whether the agent pauses for permission mid-task
- Quantitative: re-run the history.jsonl nudge-prompt analysis after 30 days; expect "pls cont"/"pls do"/etc. counts to drop ≥50%

title: Auto-wrap exploration-style dispatches with `mache build` + mount the .db
description:
## Problem

Subagent analysis (2026-05-17) on 1446 subagent transcripts found:

- 17.3% of subagents are **runaway** (>100 turns)
- 50 of those are in the "Explore X repo and summarize" cluster — agents that grep/glob the filesystem instead of using mache projection
- 26 subagents are explicitly labeled *"session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context"* — these consume **20% of all subagent wall time** (163h of 819h total)
- 5 of those continuations are *mache agents exploring mache itself* via filesystem rather than via the .db

This is darkly ironic: mache exists to solve exactly this problem (structural code intelligence via pre-built SQLite), and the agents we dispatch aren't using it.

## Proposed change

When dispatching an agent whose task description matches exploration patterns ("explore", "summarize", "audit", "understand the codebase", "find usages", "trace data path of", "walk me through"), the dispatcher:

1. Runs `mache build <target>` against the relevant repo (or finds an existing .db in `~/.mache/cache/` keyed by repo+commit)
2. Mounts/serves the .db
3. Prepends the agent prompt with: *"A mache .db is mounted at `<path>` and a mache MCP server is serving at `<url>`. Use the mache tools (find_callers, find_definition, search, list_directory, read_file) instead of Bash/Glob/Grep for code exploration."*

Skip wrap when:
- Task description explicitly says "no mache" or "use grep"
- Repo has no go/python/rust/typescript files (mache won't help)
- A recent .db already exists (cache hit)

## Why this matters

- The 26 context-overflow continuations are ~163 hours of agent wall time that could be eliminated
- Mache is the answer to ill-scoped exploration; we just need to wire it into dispatch by default
- Pairs with `mache-fbb736` (schema-by-name presets) — once that lands, mache picks the right schema automatically

## Risk

- Adds a build step to every exploration dispatch (~10-60s overhead)
- If mache build fails, dispatch falls back to filesystem (warn + log)
- Wrong schema selection could give the agent worse data; mitigate by defaulting to FCA inference until mache-fbb736 lands

## Files

- `src/dispatch.rs` — wrap dispatch with exploration-pattern detection
- `src/agents/prompts.rs` (or wherever agent system prompts get composed) — inject the mache-mounted notice
- New: `src/mache_wrap.rs` — encapsulates the build+mount lifecycle

## Test plan

- Unit: exploration-pattern detector regex against real subagent titles from the 50-runaway cluster
- Integration: dispatch a fixture "explore repo X" task against a small test repo, assert `mache build` ran and the .db path is in the system prompt
- Skip path: dispatch with `--no-mache` flag, assert no build runs

## Depends on

- `mache-fbb736` (schema-by-name) would simplify the schema-selection logic; not blocking, but cleaner once it lands

title: connect_bead_store auto-starts dolt sql-server on connect — read paths (cross_repo_search, doctor future) need a no-spawn connect mode
description:
Surfaced by the #371 fresh-eyes review (2026-07-16), not introduced by that PR: for a Dolt-mode repo with no live server and no port-info file, DoltClient::connect (src/dolt/mod.rs ~329+) auto-starts a `dolt sql-server` subprocess. That's fine for write paths, but cross_repo_search (src/main.rs) documents itself as read-only ("never created") and can now touch every registered Dolt repo in one command — a search from a random cwd could spawn N dolt servers as a side effect. Connect timeouts are bounded (3s/10s) so no hang, but process-spawning is a mutation.

Fix direction: add a `ConnectMode::ReadOnlyNoSpawn` (or a `connect_bead_store_readonly`) that attempts the existing server / SQLite file and returns Err instead of spawning; use it from cross_repo_search (skip-with-warning already handles Err) and from any future doctor deep-check.

title: SqliteBeadStore under-reads bd-created beads.db: misses closed beads + most comments (data-loss risk on export)
description:
Discovered while live-testing rsry bead export on ley-line-open (a pre-1.0 bd-created SQLite beads.db). rosary's SqliteBeadStore does NOT fully read a bd-created store:

Raw beads.db (direct sqlite3): 229 issues (96 open + 133 closed), 155 comments on 99 issues, deps present.
rosary via SqliteBeadStore:
- `rsry bead export --status all --jsonl` → 96 beads (ONLY the open ones; all 133 closed missing), 4 of 155 comments, 70 deps.
- `rsry bead list --status all --json` → count: 0 (!) — inconsistent with the export's 96 in the same session (possible separate flakiness / WAL / repo_name resolution).

Impact: a rosary-driven export of a bd-created beads.db LOSES closed beads + ~151 comments — directly contradicts the "don't lose data" goal (ADR-0014). My earlier claim that "rosary reads LLO's 227 beads fine" was WRONG; it reads 96 open.

Likely root: rosary's SqliteBeadStore schema/queries (src/bead_sqlite.rs) assume rosary's OWN SQLite schema; bd's pre-1.0 SQLite schema differs (column/table names, or list_beads excludes closed, or a default LIMIT). Needs: (1) confirm whether list_beads is supposed to return closed at all (and why export --status all only got open); (2) reconcile reading bd's issues/comments/dependencies tables faithfully, OR detect a foreign schema and read it correctly; (3) explain the export(96) vs list(0) inconsistency.

Data is SAFE meanwhile: ley-line-open/.beads backed up to scratchpad (ley-line-open-beads-backup-20260624), and the beads.db is intact. For a lossless LLO export NOW, a direct-SQL → bead-contract-JSONL extraction (bypassing SqliteBeadStore) works.

Test: against a bd-created beads.db fixture with closed beads + comments, `rsry bead export --status all --jsonl` returns ALL beads (open+closed) and ALL comments.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED — NOT a schema mismatch. rosary reads bd's SQLite `issues` table fine (columns align). The cause is LIST_BEADS_SQL: `WHERE i.status NOT IN ('closed','done')`. list_beads is an active-beads query (correct for triage/dispatch). Export reuses it, so it can't see the 133 closed beads, and never fetches their comments → ~151 comments (on closed beads) missed, only ~4 (on open) survive. Secondary: list_beads does `.filter_map(|r| r.ok())` = silent drop of any unparseable row.

FIX (implementing now): add BeadStore::list_all_beads (no status filter) to both backends; repoint the export path at it; make export enumeration fail-loud instead of silently dropping rows. Leave list_beads' open-only filter for triage. Also verify the `bead list --status all → 0` anomaly.

title: Elixir conductor: OTP supervision layer for agent lifecycle
description:
Thin Elixir app in conductor/ that connects to rsry HTTP (:8383/mcp), gets dispatch decisions from rosary's triage, and supervises agent processes via OTP.

Replaces in Rust: active HashMap, check_completed polling, recover_stuck_beads, wait_and_verify, timeout detection, phase advancement collection. Keeps in Rust: triage scoring, verification pipeline, Dolt persistence, Linear sync, BDR decomposition, MCP tools.

Architecture: DynamicSupervisor with one AgentWorker GenServer per bead. Port monitoring gives instant :DOWN messages (no polling). Phase advancement is synchronous within GenServer handler (no lost continuations). Pipeline state persisted to Dolt (survives crashes).

New rsry MCP tools needed: rsry_triage, rsry_verify, rsry_pipeline_update, rsry_bead_set_owner.

Migration: 4 phases — observer only → conductor dispatches → delete Rust lifecycle → add triage/verify tools.

Ref: OpenAI Symphony (github.com/openai/symphony-framework) for OTP patterns.

title: Triage model: split severity (bugs/chores) from value-horizon (features) — priority inflation is total
description: Observed: of the top-50 open rosary beads, 33/33 features+designs+epics are P0 or P1 — 100% priority inflation. Root: one urgency scale (P0-P4) is applied to two fundamentally different kinds of work. Bugs/chores have SEVERITY (how bad, how soon — P is right for them). Features have VALUE/HORIZON (how much they move the product, where in the roadmap — P is wrong for them, so every aspirational feature collapses to P0/P1 and the scale carries no signal). James' framing: features want an F{0-4} (value/horizon) tier, distinct from bug/chore P{0-4} (severity). Proposal: two axes keyed on issue_type — keep priority=severity for bug/chore/task; add a value/horizon tier for feature/design/epic. Then 'what to do' = high-severity P + current-horizon F + the compounding-hygiene cluster (leverage-now, orthogonal to both). Also enables meaningful thematic THREADS (e.g. the cf* build-profile hygiene cluster) instead of a flat P0/P1 wall. Deliverable: a triage-model ADR + bead-schema change (F-tier field or type-scoped priority semantics) + re-triage the backlog against it.

Since the workflow is fully agentic (agents commit + open PRs, human is out of the loop), this must be deterministically enforced at commit time: reject any commit not matching '[bead-id] <type>(<scope>)!?: <subject>' (type in feat|fix|docs|chore|refactor|test|perf|build|ci|style|revert), keeping merge/revert/initial/fixup escapes. Downstream falls out: squash subject carries bead-id -> auto-close; conventional history -> mechanical changelog/semver. Add the conversion row to the friction doc. Per gitattributes(5) a driver only runs for paths carrying the matching merge= attribute, so the driver was INERT in 5 of 7 repos with a tracked export — git line-merges the JSONL and shreds bead records, the exact failure merge_jsonl exists to prevent. hooks status already reported 'driver is inert' but install never wrote what it diagnosed. Also: the canonical BEADS_GITIGNORE template never denied dolt.bak/, which migrate --commit creates and never deletes. Acceptance: git check-attr merge -- .beads/beads.jsonl reports beads-jsonl after hooks install; cargo test gitattributes passes.

title: obs-registry-and-fold: field/algebra registry + deterministic fold
description:
Phase 1 of ADR-0010, Layer 2. Sequential after all Layer 1 algebra impls land.

**FieldRegistry** (registry.rs): maps FieldName → Box<dyn Algebra>; per-process singleton via OnceLock following src/plugin.rs pattern.

**algebra_flat.rs**: FlatLatticeAlgebra<T> with Bot | Single(T) | Top { values: Vec<T>, sources: Vec<Source> }. Distinct values join to Top carrying witnesses. Used ONLY for cross-source `status` derivation, NOT as a primitive field algebra. Its placement here (with registry+fold) reflects that it's a cross-source-fold concern, not a base algebra.

**fold.rs**: fn fold(log: &ObservationLog) -> DerivedView. Per-WorkRef, per-field, dispatches to registered algebra. DerivedView is a struct of per-field results plus a per-source derived_status plus a cross-source Status flat-lattice value.

**Inline tests** (covers ADR-0010 invariants 9, 10, 14):
- reorder_invariance: fold(perm(O)) = fold(O) for any permutation, all field types
- cross_source_status_conflict_is_top: when two sources' derived status disagree, cross-source result is Top with witnesses
- convergence_under_partition: fold(O₁ ∪ O₂) = fold(fold(O₁), fold(O₂))

**Test command**: cargo test --lib 'observation::registry::|observation::fold::|observation::algebra_flat::'

**Estimate**: ~350 LOC across three files.

Refs: ADR-0010 (PR #186).

Test command: cargo test --lib 'observation::registry::|observation::fold::|observation::algebra_flat::'

title: Phase 1: Blast radius derivation — mache integration at rsry_bead_create
description:
When rsry_bead_create is called, derive blast radius from the description:

1. Parse description for file paths, function names, module references

3. Expand via `find_callers` / `find_callees` (depth 2) to compute blast radius

title: rsry MCP: bead_link parameter names undocumented; agent had to guess
description:
## Problem
While filing the 12 substrate-IDL leaves and linking dependencies, the `rsry_bead_link` MCP tool's parameter schema is not self-documenting:

Attempt 1: agent passed `from_id` + `to_id` + `link_type` → error: "id required"
Attempt 2: agent passed `id` + `to_id` + `link_type` → error: "depends_on required"
Attempt 3 (worked): agent passed `id` + `depends_on` → success

Three round-trips of guess-and-error to discover the real parameter shape (`id`, `depends_on`). The MCP schema discovery surface should make this single-shot. Either:
1. The MCP tool's input schema should expose the param names (current schema visible to the MCP client may not match the validator)
2. The error message on missing param should list which params are accepted ("got: from_id, to_id, link_type — expected: id, depends_on")
3. Both the documented common names (`from_id`/`to_id`/`link_type`) and the internal names (`id`/`depends_on`) should be accepted as aliases

## Acceptance criteria
- `rsry_bead_link` either: (a) accepts the common shorthand `{from_id, to_id, link_type}` alongside `{id, depends_on}`, OR (b) the InvalidParams error response lists the accepted parameter names in the error message.
- Add an integration test in `src/serve/handlers_test.rs` (or wherever bead_link tests live) verifying the error message names the expected params.

## Inputs
- src/serve/handlers.rs (MCP tool implementations — 31 tools incl. bead_link)
- src/serve/mod.rs (MCP server setup, schema export)
- src/store_dolt.rs (LinkageStore backend that bead_link writes through)

## Output shape
PR against rosary. Touches handlers.rs (param parsing/aliases) + a test file. Net diff <100 lines.

## Scope boundary
bead_link parameter clarity only. Same audit on other rsry MCP tools is a follow-up bead.

## Failure mode
Existing tests pass but new test (asserting error message names params) is missing.

## Time-box
S

## Why this matters
The substrate-IDL workflow expects agents to file beads + link dependencies in one session via MCP. If every MCP tool needs N error-rounds to discover its param shape, agent budget burns on schema discovery rather than work.

comments.text:
Current schema at src/serve/tools.rs:177-189 is technically complete (`repo_path`, `id`, `depends_on`, `remove`) — required fields are declared. The friction is the *description*: "Bead ID that depends on another" / "Bead ID that must complete first" doesn't read clearly without context. Fix:
1. Punchier description with an example block (`rsry_bead_link(id="rosary-abc", depends_on="rosary-xyz")  // abc blocked until xyz done`)
2. Same treatment on other relational tools (rsry_thread_assign, rsry_thread_reparent) while we're in there
3. ~10 line patch to tools.rs

Pair-shippable with rosary-98ee93 (cross-repo bead_link) + rosary-992e79 (thread_create / decade_create MCP tools) as one "MCP surface completeness" PR — all three are tools.rs + handlers.rs work against already-existing backend traits.

title: Phase 3: Tropo sheaf analysis for flagged duplicate pairs
description:
For pairs flagged by Phase 1 (blast radius Jaccard > 0.40) or Phase 2 (cosine > 0.80), run tropo sheaf analysis on the overlapping subgraph.

1. Extract mache subgraph for overlapping files (callers/callees within the shared scope)
2. Build tropo sheaf complex: 0-cells = files, 1-cells = call edges, 2-cells = cycles
3. Compute H1 Betti number (cycle detection), containment check, violation detection
4. Return structured relationship: `near-duplicate`, `scope-contained`, `circular-dependency`

This is the layer that catches what cosine and Jaccard miss: structural coupling between beads with different descriptions.

## Integration
- tropo crate already in the workspace (../tropo or as dependency)
- mache provides the call graph data
- Results stored as bead comments or a new `relationships` field

## Test plan
- Two beads touching same cyclic subgraph → H1 > 0, flagged as circular-dependency
- Bead A's files ⊂ bead B's files → flagged as scope-contained
- Unrelated beads → no sheaf analysis triggered (only runs on flagged pairs)

## Parent epic: rosary-984b20
## Depends on: Phase 1 (blast radius data required)

title: Phase 4: Validation — re-run experiment, measure recall against ground truth
description:
Re-run the dedup experiment (experiments/run_dedup.py) after Phases 1-3 are implemented. Measure recall against the 8 ground truth pairs.

## Success criteria
- Combined recall > 50% (4/8 ground truth pairs caught)
- Each layer adds value: structural catches pairs cosine misses (or vice versa)
- False positive rate manageable (< 20 spurious pairs flagged)

## What to measure
- Layer 1 (cosine) recall and precision
- Layer 2 (blast radius Jaccard) recall and precision — the delta over cosine alone
- Layer 3 (tropo sheaf) recall and precision — the delta over Jaccard alone
- Which ground truth pairs each layer catches vs misses
- Whether the sheaf layer is justified (does it catch anything Jaccard doesn't?)

## If sheaf adds nothing
Strip Layer 3. Two layers (cosine + Jaccard) is simpler and sufficient. The experiment proves or disproves the sheaf hypothesis — don't ship complexity that doesn't earn its keep.

## Depends on: Phases 1, 2, 3

title: rsry: bead_link rejects cross-repo dependencies (blocker for multi-repo coordination)
description:
## Problem
Attempting to link a cloister bead's `depends_on` to a signet bead failed:

```
rsry_bead_link(repo_path=cloister, id=cloister-963a5c, depends_on=signet-9605a3)
→ Error: bead not found: signet-9605a3
```

`signet-9605a3` exists; it was created in this session in signet's `.beads/`. The bead-id namespace prefix correctly identifies the source repo, but `bead_link` apparently scopes the lookup to the calling `repo_path`'s `.beads/` only, so cross-repo dependencies can't be expressed.

This is a meaningful gap given the substrate-IDL track's whole premise: 8+ repos that need to coordinate releases. Per ADR-0009 (cross-repo linkage) the model exists in concept; what's missing is the MCP surface honoring it.

## Acceptance criteria
- `rsry_bead_link --id=<bead-in-repo-A> --depends_on=<bead-in-repo-B>` succeeds when both beads exist in their respective `.beads/` stores
- Cross-repo dependencies are persisted via `LinkageStore` (per ADR-0009 stratified acyclicity)
- A new integration test exercises the cross-repo path (signet-X → cloister-Y direction)
- `rsry_list_beads --status blocked` correctly surfaces a bead blocked by a cross-repo dependency

## Inputs
- src/serve/handlers.rs (bead_link MCP impl — must resolve the dep-bead via repo registry, not just local store)
- src/store.rs (LinkageStore trait)
- src/store_dolt.rs (Dolt backend impl)
- src/dolt.rs (Dolt client; cross-repo lookups)
- src/pool.rs (connection pool for multi-repo Dolt access — already exists, leverage)
- docs/adr/0009-cross-repo-linkage.md (the design)

## Output shape
PR against rosary. Touches bead_link handler + LinkageStore methods + adds integration test. Net diff <400 lines.

## Scope boundary
bead_link cross-repo only. Other tools (bead_search, list, dispatch) that also need cross-repo awareness are follow-up beads.

## Failure mode
Test asserting cross-repo link succeeds returns false; OR blocked-bead listing doesn't see cross-repo deps.

## Time-box
M

## Why this matters
The substrate-IDL track filed today has L9 (cloister) → L8 (signet) as a real dependency: L9's GHA workflow uses cosign with `tlog-upload=true`, which is what L8's signet docs specify. Without cross-repo link support, the dependency is informal (only in the bead description prose), and rsry's automatic "ready vs blocked" classification mis-classifies L9 as ready.

## Workaround in use today
Dependency documented in L9's bead description prose ("Depends on L8 (signet-9605a3)") — humans can read it but rsry's dispatcher cannot.

**Full fix still requires scope abstraction** (`rosary-b5da2f`) so non-canonical bead ids and external scopes route correctly. Leaving this bead OPEN until that lands — the dependency edge already wires it through.

title: rsry MCP: no thread_create / decade_create tools — BDR hierarchy can't be populated by agents
description:
## Problem
The BDR hierarchy is Decade ⊃ Thread ⊃ Bead. rsry exposes 4 MCP tools for it:
- `rsry_decade_list` (read)
- `rsry_thread_list` (read)
- `rsry_thread_assign` (assign existing bead to existing thread)
- `rsry_thread_reparent` (move existing thread to different decade)

There is no `rsry_thread_create` or `rsry_decade_create` tool. An agent cannot file a new bead AND put it in a properly-named new thread/decade in one session via MCP — only assignment to existing ones is possible.

The CLI has `rsry decompose` which parses ADR markdown and emits beads inside an auto-populated decade+thread structure, but that's ADR-shaped input, not a general-purpose decade/thread creation tool.

## Real-world manifestation (this session)
Just filed 12 substrate-IDL leaves across cloister + signet. They naturally group into 5 threads (schema-bridge, substrate-manifest, capability-conformance, supply-chain-wiring, identity-vocabulary) under a "substrate-idl" decade that doesn't yet exist. With no `thread_create` MCP tool, the 12 beads are sitting un-threaded in the default decade. Agent cannot complete the grouping the user explicitly requested.

## Acceptance criteria
- `rsry_decade_create(id, title, source_path?)` MCP tool exists; creates a decade row
- `rsry_thread_create(decade_id, id, title, source_path?)` MCP tool exists; creates a thread under the named decade
- Both tools return the created entity's metadata
- Both refuse if id already exists (idempotent: if title+source_path match, return existing; if they don't, error)
- Integration test exercises end-to-end: create decade → create thread under it → file bead → assign bead to thread

## Inputs
- src/serve/handlers.rs (where the new tools register)
- src/store.rs (HierarchyStore trait)
- src/store_dolt.rs (Dolt-backed HierarchyStore impl)
- src/observation/tree_fold.rs (BDR Decade ⊃ Thread ⊃ Bead catamorphism — must stay consistent)
- crates/bdr/src/decompose.rs (existing decompose pipeline that already creates these implicitly)

## Output shape
PR against rosary. Adds 2 MCP tool handlers + HierarchyStore methods + integration test. Net diff <500 lines.

## Scope boundary
Create-only. Updating decade/thread metadata after creation is a separate bead. Deleting is also separate.

## Failure mode
New tools missing from `rsry serve --transport stdio` tool list; OR creating a duplicate-id returns success silently; OR test asserting end-to-end flow fails.

## Time-box
M

## Why this matters
User explicitly asked for proper BDR hierarchy on the substrate-IDL leaves. Without these tools, every "file N beads grouped by thread" workflow is stuck with manual SQL inserts or `rsry decompose` (which expects ADR markdown, not bead-spec lists).

## Workaround in use today
Beads land in the default decade/thread; user has to manually edit Dolt rows to group them.

title: Doc-drift validator: ensure cited paths in docs actually resolve
description:
## Problem
This session surfaced repeated doc-staleness issues:

1. `agents/docs/prior-art/_baseline.md` cited `signet/pkg/sigpol/` — actual path is `signet/pkg/policy/` (CLAUDE.md uses "sigpol" colloquially; directory doesn't match). Found only because the problem-decomposer subagent grepped the path and reported the mismatch.
2. ADR-0022 referenced by three prior-art entries — file doesn't exist in `cloister/docs/adr/` (numbering hole between 0021 and 0023). Found only by an explicit `ls docs/adr/` ground-truth pass.
3. `notme/.github/workflows/gha-identity.yml` cited in baseline — never verified to exist this session (marked `[unverified]`).

User flagged this directly: "docs are stale af and we need a way to validate it better."

The pattern is general: docs (ADRs, READMEs, specs, decompositions, prior-art entries) cite file paths, ADR numbers, and external URLs. Some are stale. Today there's no automated check.

## Proposal
Build a doc-drift validator that:
1. Walks all markdown files in a target tree (or a configured set)
2. Extracts cited paths: `/repos/...`, relative paths in code-blocks, `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` references, URLs
3. Resolves each:
   - Local path → does the file exist?
   - ADR reference like `ADR-NNNN` → does `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` exist?
   - URL → returns 2xx (optional / configurable)
4. Reports a per-doc table of broken citations
5. Can run as a pre-commit hook OR a CI gate OR a one-shot audit

Could be a new rsry MCP tool (`rsry_doc_drift_audit --path=<dir>`) OR a standalone skill in jamestexas/agents/skills/doc-drift-validator/ OR both (skill calls the rsry tool).

## Acceptance criteria
- New tool/skill emits a structured report listing every broken citation across a target tree
- Detects at least: missing file paths, missing ADRs (by number), missing markdown anchors
- Returns exit code ≠ 0 when any citation breaks (CI-gate compatible)
- Has a `--ignore <pattern>` flag for known-broken citations
- Tested against `agents/docs/prior-art/_baseline.md` — should catch the `pkg/sigpol/` vs `pkg/policy/` mismatch had this existed (verifying past mistake)
- Tested against `cloister/docs/adr/` — should catch the ADR-0022 hole

## Inputs
- src/serve/handlers.rs (if rsry MCP tool)
- src/main.rs (if rsry CLI subcommand)
- ~/github/jamestexas/agents/skills/ (if skill)
- ~/github/jamestexas/agents/docs/prior-art/_baseline.md (test corpus — known to have had drift)
- ~/remotes/art/cloister/docs/adr/ (test corpus — known to have ADR-0022 hole)

## Output shape
PR against rosary OR new skill in jamestexas/agents. Either way: <500 lines including tests.

## Scope boundary
Citation resolution only. Not "is the cited content semantically correct" — just "does the cited thing exist." Semantic drift (a doc saying "X uses Y" when X no longer uses Y) is a separate, harder problem.

## Failure mode
Validator runs against a known-broken doc and reports 0 issues.

## Time-box
M (~1 week to ship usable v0; rich pattern-matching iterates after first real use)

## Why this matters
The substrate-IDL track has 12 bead specs each citing 5-10 file paths. If any of those go stale, the bead becomes un-runnable for the dispatched agent. Catching drift at write-time (or pre-commit) keeps the dispatch surface honest.

Pairs with the prior-art-cartographer's `[unverified]` discipline — same idea: don't let citations rot silently.
