title: Define ART service boundaries: rsry vs conductor vs BEAM layer
description:
## Problem
Unclear whether conductor (Elixir/OTP) should remain separate, migrate to Gleam, use Rustler, or get absorbed into rsry. Need to define service boundaries explicitly.

## Context
- Conductor owns OTP process supervision (~2500 LOC Elixir)
- rsry owns state (Dolt), dispatch logic, MCP server, Linear sync
- Gleam offers type-safe OTP on same BEAM runtime
- Rustler (Rust NIFs) is wrong — conductor's value IS the process model
- codebase-memory-mcp and mache could help discover/enforce service boundaries

## Questions to resolve
1. Is the rsry/conductor boundary right? (state vs process mgmt)
2. Should conductor stay Elixir, migrate to Gleam, or be absorbed?
3. Should mache grow service boundary detection (HTTP routes, cross-repo call graphs)?
4. How do apko/melange/krust fit into the build/deploy boundary?

## Approach
Architect-level analysis: map actual call patterns, data flow, and failure domains. The right boundary is where failure domains differ.

comments.text: Business model input: conductor may be the free/open offering (AGPL3), ley-line is deliberately closed source. This means the rsry/conductor boundary isn't just technical — it's a product boundary. Conductor as the open-source orchestration layer anyone can use, ley-line as the closed crypto/content layer. This argues strongly for keeping conductor separate (not absorbing into rsry) and making the interface clean enough that third parties can plug in their own backends. The Gleam vs Elixir question is still open but secondary to the product boundary.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: notme/worker: bootstrap reset does not consume code — repeated passkey wipe possible
description: In worker.ts `/auth/passkey/reset`, the bootstrap code is compared directly via `body.bootstrapCode !== code` (line 1196) without calling `consumeBootstrapCode`. The code is never marked `used = 1` in the bootstrap table after a successful reset. An attacker who learns the bootstrap code (e.g. from a log leak) can call `/auth/passkey/reset` repeatedly, wiping all registered credentials each time with the same code. Fix: after a successful reset, call `authority.consumeBootstrapCode(body.bootstrapCode)` instead of the inline comparison, or add `DELETE FROM bootstrap WHERE id = 'code'` in `resetPasskeyData()`. Repo: notme/worker, files: worker/worker.ts, worker/src/signing-authority.ts.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit 0c5e296. worker.ts /auth/passkey/reset now calls authority.consumeBootstrapCode(...) instead of inline !==. consumeBootstrapCode (signing-authority.ts:707) atomically validates AND marks the code used; a second /reset returns false → 403 'invalid or expired bootstrap code'. This combined fix also closes rosary-8067c1 (timing-safe HMAC compare via timing-safe.ts). Threat model: passkey.reset.single-use row added to THREAT_MODEL.md.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: ley-line-open: arena VERSION mismatch error message is opaque ("invalid arena header")
description: In rs/ll-open/fs/src/lib.rs SqliteGraph::from_arena (and from_arena_writable in graph.rs), the ArenaHeader::active_buffer_offset call returns None on VERSION mismatch (layout.rs:41 checks `self.version != Self::VERSION`). The caller surfaces this as the generic string "invalid arena header" (context call at lib.rs:105, graph.rs:223). A V1 arena handed to a V2 binary gets this unhelpful error rather than a clear "ArenaHeader VERSION mismatch: file has v1, binary expects v2" message. Compare to Controller::open_or_create which emits a detailed, actionable message. The arena read-path needs the same treatment — active_buffer_offset should return a typed error or the caller should inspect the version field before calling it. Without a specific error, operators and automated monitors cannot distinguish corruption from a legitimate cutover gap.

title: notme/revocation: null seqno bypasses rollback protection in RevocationAuthority
description: In revocation.ts `RevocationAuthority.handleSeqno`, the `seqno` value from the POST body is not validated to be a positive integer. Sending `seqno: null` causes `null < last` and `null > last` to both be false (JavaScript null comparison), so neither branch fires and the function returns `{ ok: true }` — approving the bundle without advancing the counter. A rollback attack using `seqno: null` passes the seqno check. Fix: add `if (typeof seqno !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(seqno) || seqno < 1) return Response.json({ ok: false, reason: 'invalid_seqno' }, { status: 400 })` at the top of handleSeqno. Additionally, the `issuerId` is fully caller-controlled — in a multi-tenant rig deployment one tenant could poison another tenant's seqno. Repo: notme/worker, file: worker/src/revocation.ts.

comments.text: Verified fixed. worker/src/revocation.ts:93-95 has the exact validation from the bead: 'if (typeof seqno !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(seqno) || seqno < 1) return invalid_seqno, 400'. The multi-tenant issuerId concern is a separate, broader design issue — current single-tenant deployment uses fixed issuerId='notme.bot' (line 230). Closing the seqno-validation issue.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: ley-line-open: set_current_root is public + unfenced; can produce torn reads of current_root
description: Controller::set_current_root (rs/ll-core/core/src/control.rs:200) is still a public method. It writes 32 bytes of current_root without bumping the sync counter (no Release-store). Readers in current_root() do an Acquire-load on the sync counter to fence their byte reads — but if a writer calls set_current_root instead of set_arena_with_root, the sync counter is never bumped, so readers doing Acquire can observe a stale counter value and still read their cached root bytes. The root bytes are committed to mmap, but there is no happens-before edge established between the write and any concurrent read that hasn't loaded a new counter value. The doc comment says "do not call from the snapshot critical path in production yet" but the method is public and callers in tests (e.g. current_root_round_trips_through_set, current_root_does_not_collide_with_existing_fields) exercise it. Either deprecate+seal it, or bump the sync counter inside it to maintain the fence contract.

title: notme/token: empty audience allowed — DPoP tokens with no audience restriction issued
description: In worker.ts `/token` handler, the audience allowlist includes `""` (empty string) with comment "legacy compat" (line 1349). This means any authenticated user can obtain a DPoP-bound access token with no audience restriction by omitting the `audience` field from the POST body. An audience-less JWT is valid for any resource server. This defeats the DPoP sender-constraint model. The token is still key-bound (cnf.jkt), but there is no audience to reject it. Fix: remove `""` from ALLOWED_AUDIENCES, require a non-empty audience, and deprecate the no-audience path. If legacy clients exist, give them a migration window. Repo: notme/worker, file: worker/worker.ts.

comments.text: Verified fixed. worker/worker.ts:1674-1687 — ALLOWED_AUDIENCES no longer contains empty string (comment: 'Empty audience no longer allowed'). Lines 1682-1683 explicitly reject missing audience with audience_required/400. Cross-correlated during security sweep.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: ley-line-open: race test satisfiable with zero contention — does not prove race-safety
description: test_op_reparse_snapshot_race_publishes_well_formed_root (rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/integration.rs:2688) fires 6 reparses + 6 snapshots concurrently and asserts "at least one non-zero root was published." This assertion is satisfiable by a single successful snapshot with no actual contention. A scheduler that serialises all ops (deadlock-free but no true concurrency) passes the test trivially. The test does check for ok:true on all 18 tasks and a final "ready" phase, which catches outright deadlocks and panic propagation — but the "≥1 non-zero root" predicate is not a race-safety proof. A genuine race-safety test would assert that after N concurrent snapshots, the final root is consistent with some valid serialization, or that the controller never transitions through a partial-write window observable to a reader. Consider adding a concurrent-reader goroutine that validates every root it sees against BLAKE3(active_buffer), analogous to the monotone regression check in the control.rs unit test.

title: notme/token: rate limiter is non-atomic — concurrent requests bypass 20/hr limit
description: In worker.ts `/token` handler (lines 1386-1395), the rate limit is implemented as read-from-KV → check → write-to-KV. Two concurrent requests from the same principal can both read `count=19`, both pass the `>= 20` check, and both get tokens. The KV write is not atomic. The JTI store correctly uses write-before-mint, but the rate limiter has a classic TOCTOU race. Fix: move the rate-limit counter into the SigningAuthority DO SQLite with `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO rate_limits ... RETURNING count` so the increment is serialized within the DO, which processes requests one at a time. Alternatively, use a DO alarm-based counter. Repo: notme/worker, files: worker/worker.ts, worker/src/signing-authority.ts.

comments.text: Stale — /token rate limiter no longer uses KV read-increment-write. worker.ts:1763-1766 now uses env.TOKEN_LIMITER.limit() (CF's atomic rate-limit binding). Closing.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: ley-line-open: from_arena passes full buf_size slice to SQLite, not buf[..data_size]
description: In rs/ll-open/fs/src/lib.rs:108-111 (SqliteGraph::from_arena) and graph.rs:226-229 (SqliteGraphAdapter::from_arena_writable), verify_arena_root correctly hashes buf[..data_size] against current_root, but then calls from_bytes(buf) / from_bytes_writable(buf) with the full buffer_size slice — which includes trailing zero-padding beyond data_size. sqlite3_deserialize handles trailing zeros gracefully today (SQLite uses page_count from its own header to determine valid pages), so this is not a current correctness bug. But the semantic contract is violated: the substrate promised that BLAKE3(buf[..data_size]) == current_root, yet the deserializer gets a different byte range. If a future backend is not SQLite-tolerant of trailing zeros, this will silently fail. The fix is to pass &buf[..header.data_size as usize] to from_bytes, consistent with what the verifier hashed.

title: notme/verify-proof: verifyX509 called with SPKI PEM instead of X.509 cert PEM — always 401
description: In worker.ts `/connections` POST handler (line 983), the CA key is fetched via `authority.getPublicKeyPem()` which returns an SPKI-format PEM (`-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----`). This is passed as `caPublicKeyPem` to `verifyProof` → `verifyX509`. Inside `verifyX509` (verify-proof.ts line 171), this string is wrapped in `new X509Certificate(caPublicKeyPem)`. An SPKI PEM is not a valid X.509 certificate — this constructor call will throw, and the catch in worker.ts returns 401. Result: the `/connections` endpoint with `type: "x509"` proof is permanently broken. The CA parameter type name suggests a key but the implementation expects a certificate. Fix: either pass `await authority.getCACertificatePem()` at the call site, or fix `verifyX509` to accept a raw public key (SPKI) and use `crypto.subtle.importKey` directly for verification. Repo: notme/worker, files: worker/worker.ts, worker/src/auth/verify-proof.ts.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit c120b9a. /connections (worker.ts:1295) now calls authority.getCACertificatePem() instead of getPublicKeyPem(). The earlier SPKI 'PUBLIC KEY' PEM threw inside new X509Certificate(...) and silently 401'd every legitimate x509 connection. New regression test under oidc.x509.ca-pem-shape guards the dispatcher path.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme/dpop-handler: JTI stored after mint — replay window in handleToken path
description: In dpop-handler.ts `handleToken`, the JTI replay check (step 5, line 63) and JTI store (step 7, line 80) bracket the token mint (step 6, line 70). Two concurrent requests with the same DPoP proof both pass the replay check, both mint tokens, then both store the JTI. The direct `/token` handler in worker.ts correctly stores JTI before minting (worker.ts line 1417). The `dpop-handler.ts` path is currently used only in tests, not in the production `/token` route, but it is exported and could be wired in. The divergence between two implementations of the same flow (one correct, one not) is itself a hazard. Fix: in `handleToken`, call `storeJti` before `mintAccessToken`, consistent with the worker.ts pattern. Repo: notme/worker, file: worker/src/auth/dpop-handler.ts.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit 95ef0dd. handleToken steps reordered: store JTI BEFORE mint, matching worker.ts /token (which already had the correct order at line 1790). Existing routes-dpop.test.ts test inverted to assert the new order — stub storeJti to throw, verify mint never runs.
comments.author: jamestexas

title: notme/revocation: staleness check skipped when issuedAt is missing — old bundles accepted
description: In revocation.ts `checkRevocation` (line 203), the staleness check is wrapped in `if (bundle.issuedAt !== undefined)`. A CA bundle without an `issuedAt` field — possible for bundles generated before the field was added, or bundles from a Go signet implementation that doesn't include it — bypasses the 5-minute staleness window entirely. Combined with a valid signature, this means an arbitrarily old bundle can be served from KV without triggering `bundle_stale`. Fix: treat missing `issuedAt` as stale (fail closed), or require `issuedAt` in the CABundle type. Repo: notme/worker, file: worker/src/revocation.ts.

comments.text: Fixed in notme commit ca47125. Two-layer fix: (1) CABundle.issuedAt now required at type level, (2) runtime isBundleStale() returns true for missing/NaN/non-positive — fail-closed boundary. 6 new tests under revocation.bundle.staleness. Behavior unchanged for legitimate producers (signing-authority.ts always set issuedAt).
comments.author: jamestexas

title: ADR-0016 V0 — smell rule: forbid raw process exec outside the sanctioned dispatch seam
description:
ADR-0016 D9 / V0 (the cheap guard, lands first). Add a committed structural rule that flags std::process::Command / tokio::process::Command::new (and Command::spawn) OUTSIDE the one sanctioned dispatch seam (src/dispatch/providers.rs). Re-introducing a raw host spawn is the exact regression ADR-0016 exists to prevent — make exec-out a gate failure, not a habit. Implement as either a mache smell rule JSON in docs/smell-rules/ (JSON-of-SQL over the _ast, like long_file_rosary) or a semgrep rule in the lint gate. Allowlist the legitimate current spawn sites (providers.rs claude/gemini/codex spawn) via the rule's scope or a baseline entry, so it ratchets NEW exec-out only. Note: dispatch legitimately execs today (that's what ADR-0016 fixes) — the rule guards against SPREADING the anti-pattern to new call sites while the cloister migration lands.

Ref: docs/adr/0016-dispatch-via-cloister.md D9. Relates to ADR-0018 (smell gate).

title: rsry MCP/CLI: optional include_closed flag for list_beads + search (default off)
description:
## Problem

`rsry_list_beads(status="closed")` and `rsry_list_beads(status="done")` both return **zero beads** — closed beads are invisible to MCP consumers regardless of the requested status filter. `rsry_bead_search` similarly hides them. CLI `rsry bead list --status closed` returns "No beads found".

This is the correct DEFAULT (closed work isn't actionable, agents shouldn't trip over it), but it prevents real questions:

- "How many beads have we closed total?" — can't answer
- "Did we close X already, or is it just buried?" — have to know the ID to retrieve
- "What changed in the last cycle?" (closed vs newly-opened delta) — impossible to compute
- Cross-session memory: an agent picking up work in a fresh session can't audit what its predecessors disposed of

## Proposed fix

Add `include_closed: bool` (default `false`) to:

- `rsry_list_beads` (MCP tool)
- `rsry_bead_search` (MCP tool)
- `rsry bead list` (CLI flag `--include-closed`)
- `rsry bead search` (CLI flag `--include-closed`)

When `true`, the SQL filter on bead status drops the implicit "exclude closed" clause. Behavior matrix:

| `include_closed` | `status` arg | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `false` (default) | unset | open + in_progress + blocked + ready |
| `false` (default) | `"open"` / etc. | same as today |
| `false` (default) | `"closed"` / `"done"` | empty (today's behavior — no surprise change) |
| `true` | unset | everything |
| `true` | `"closed"` / `"done"` | actually returns closed beads |

## Why default off

The MCP-driven agent flow is "do work" not "audit history." Default-off keeps the active queue tight; closed-bead reads are an explicit operator/audit-time action, not the inner loop.

## Surfaced from

Cloister adversarial-cycle 2026-06-22 close-out session (2026-06-23). User asked "how many closed do we have?" and the CLI/MCP returned 0, but `rsry_status.total - rsry_status.open = 5` says SOMETHING is closed and just hidden. Conversation thread is part of the rosary bd-adoption pivot (see related: rosary ADR-0012 rewrite around bd server-mode-over-socket).

## Acceptance

- Add `include_closed` param to both MCP tool schemas + handlers
- Add `--include-closed` flag to both CLI subcommands
- Test: `rsry_list_beads(repo="cloister", status="closed", include_closed=true)` returns the 9 cloister-9339c0 / 938b32 / 93b0c2 / 93d674 / 92e846 / 936890 / 93132f / a2809a / a2971b beads closed 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-23.
- Doc: README or CLAUDE.md note on the audit pattern

title: rsry has no id-preserving jsonl->store restore (bd-free) — store recovery needs hand-crafted SQL
description:
Hit live during ley-line-open store recovery (2026-07-22): a stash-pop reverted LLO's beads.db, dropping 82 beads that survived only in the git-tracked beads.jsonl. Restoring them SHOULD be a one-liner, but:

- `rsry bead import` DELIBERATELY re-keys (src/import.rs:136: 'does NOT preserve the original id'). Using it would have re-keyed ley-line-open-4aeb4f, dangling the cross-repo edge rosary-6edb56 -> 4aeb4f, and broken all inter-bead deps + commit refs.
- The documented id-preserving path is `bd init --from-jsonl` (src/import.rs:140) — but bd is FORBIDDEN (ADR-0014; bd mis-routing caused prior LLO data loss).
- The verbatim-write primitives EXIST (bead_migrate.rs restore_status/restore_dependency) but are wired only to Dolt->SQLite migration (a BeadStore source), NOT to a jsonl file.

So the only bd-free recovery was a hand-crafted direct-SQL insert (issues + dependencies + comments, original ids, verbatim status). That worked (347 beads, field-verified on a copy first, committed as ley-line-open accb05c) but it should be a first-class rsry primitive, e.g. `rsry bead restore --from-jsonl <file>` reusing restore_status/restore_dependency + a restore_bead_full that writes the id verbatim. This is the inverse of `bead export --jsonl` and the bd-free completion of ADR-0014's 'own the store'. Note the export it consumes currently drops acceptance_criteria (rosary-a18a1f) — restore inherits that gap until a18a1f is fixed.

title: Docker compute provider (local container execution)
description:
## What
Add a Docker provider alongside Local and Sprites. Agents run in containers instead of bare processes. Like Local but with isolation — no VM provisioning cost like Sprites.

## Why
Local provider has no isolation. Sprites requires external API. Docker is the middle ground: container-level isolation, local execution, no external dependency. Also aligns with krust OCI builds (rosary-735446) — if we're building OCI images, running them locally via Docker is the obvious local dev/test path.

## How
Implement Provider behaviour in conductor:
- provision: docker run with repo mounted or cloned
- spawn_process: docker exec or attach to running container
- exec_sync: docker exec
- deprovision: docker rm -f
- checkpoint: docker commit or workspace checkpoint via mount

Could share container networking config with Sprites (network_allowlist pattern).

title: Active dedup: agent verifies bead uniqueness before starting work
description:
## Problem
Current dedup is passive — jaccard similarity + file overlap in epic.rs filters at triage time. But AI-created beads duplicate easily, and the heuristic misses semantic duplicates with different wording. As agents manage more work, this gets worse.

## Proposal
Make dedup an active, concrete step in the agent workflow:
1. Before an agent starts work on a bead, it searches for similar beads (rsry_bead_search)
2. Agent evaluates whether work is genuinely unique vs already covered
3. If duplicate: agent closes the bead with a comment linking to the original
4. If related but distinct: agent links them (rsry_bead_link) and proceeds

## Additional: backlog limits per issue type
Cap open beads per type (e.g., max 10 open features, max 20 open bugs). When at capacity, new beads of that type must either replace an existing one or be rejected. Forces consolidation.

## Where this lives
- Agent prompt (dispatch.rs task_framing or AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT): explicit dedup verification step
- Triage phase (reconcile.rs): enforce backlog limits before dispatch
- epic.rs: tighten similarity thresholds or add LLM-based semantic comparison

comments.text:
Witchcraft (dropbox/witchcraft — Rust XTR-WARP semantic search, SQLite-backed library) is the right primitive for the "semantic duplicates with different titles" failure mode. Jaccard catches lexical overlap but misses paraphrase. Hybrid semantic + BM25 (witchcraft's built-in) handles both.

New witchcraft-integration bead filed; this bead becomes a downstream consumer of that one. `epic::is_dominated_by` would call witchcraft for similarity score, falling back to jaccard when index isn't available.

The e2e_colocated_workspace_isolation test (workspace.rs) passes but only tests single-agent scenarios. Need a concurrent multi-agent isolation test.

title: Observation lattice: non-deterministic LWW tie-break + status pre-fold ignores observed_at (cross-machine divergence)
description:
Found by theoretical-foundations review (2026-06-23) of the ADR-0010 lattice. Two real correctness defects that can make two machines fold the same observations to DIFFERENT state:

1. src/observation/algebra_lww.rs (~lines 109-130): LWW winner is `max by (observed_at, source.as_str())`. Two DISTINCT values sharing the same (observed_at, source) compare Equal → resolution falls to first-seen (slice order). Not a strict total order over elements → cross-machine divergence when folding unordered slices or pre-persist. FIX: extend the key to (observed_at, source, payload_hash) so it's strict-total over the elements.

2. src/observation/fold.rs (~lines 113-129): the cross-source Status pre-fold comment says "LWW by observed_at" but the code resolves within-source by iteration order (and_modify last-wins over the dedup-key order), NEVER reading observed_at. Can surface an OLDER status. Deterministic but semantically wrong + disagrees with every other single-valued field. FIX: resolve within-source by observed_at LWW (reuse LwwRegisterAlgebra per source), then join_per_source.

Both are determinism/convergence bugs in the CvRDT fold. Verdict from review: lattice is otherwise lawful; these two must be fixed before relying on cross-machine convergence.

comments.text: FIXED → PR #231 (branch worktree-lattice-determinism-a38fca). Both defects fixed with TDD: (1) algebra_lww.rs LWW key now (observed_at, source, payload_hash) — strict total order; (2) fold.rs status pre-fold now resolves within-source by (observed_at, payload_hash) LWW instead of iteration order. 2 new regression tests; full observation suite (100) + whole suite (1167+21+1+4) green; clippy/fmt clean. Not self-merged — P1 bug fix, holding for review.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: Observation lattice review follow-ups: G-set naming, tautological invariant-14 test, join-preserving compaction, pin payload_hash canon, write-once invariant
description:
Non-blocking caveats from the theoretical-foundations review (2026-06-23), companion to the P1 determinism bug:

1. algebra_orset.rs is an ADD-ONLY G-set, not an OR-set (no remove/tombstone). Rename to reflect that, OR document that when remove lands it MUST be add-wins with tombstones keyed by (source, source_event_id) — else lawfulness breaks.
2. The invariant-14 "partition" test (fold.rs ~325-387) asserts fold(set)==fold(same set), which is tautological for a BTreeMap G-set and does NOT prove the partition property fold(O1∪O2)=merge(fold O1, fold O2). Either implement a real merge(DerivedView,DerivedView) and test it, or downgrade the claim.
3. Compaction/retention (ADR-0010 90-day) must be JOIN-PRESERVING: don't delete observations that change the fold (chain-max, LWW winner, live G-set members); first materialize a synthetic dominating snapshot observation.
4. Pin/version the payload_hash canonicalization (over (source, field, value)) — changing it changes dedup identity → double-count on replay.
5. Document the load-bearing invariants (ADR-0012 D8): observations are write-once (no UPDATE); Dolt merges only the append-only log, never the derived projection. This is what makes syntactic (Dolt) and semantic (lattice) merge coincide.

comments.text: ADD (folded here to avoid a dup, since item #4 already owns payload_hash canonicalization): switch the observation content hash from sha2/sha256 → BLAKE3. Do this together with pinning the canonicalization (item #4): pick blake3 + a versioned canonical encoding of (source, field, value) in one change so dedup identity is stable and ecosystem-consistent. Files: add to src/observation/mod.rs + wherever payload_hash is computed + Cargo.toml (blake3 dep, drop sha2 if unused elsewhere).

title: rsry_dispatch broken by Claude Code harness changes (compat debt in providers.rs)
description:
## Problem
`rsry_dispatch` doesn't work today (user-confirmed 2026-05-18 during substrate-IDL bead-filing session). This is the most fundamental gap in the BDR-driven workflow:

- File 12 substrate-IDL leaves ✓ (rsry_bead_create works)
- Establish dependency graph ✓ (rsry_bead_link works after parameter-discovery friction)
- **Dispatch agents to execute the beads ✗ (broken)**

Without working dispatch, every leaf becomes "manually do this work or use Claude Code's general-purpose subagent" — losing the per-bead workspace isolation, state transitions, and audit trail that rsry was supposed to provide.

## What "broken" looks like (need user to clarify scope)
- Does `rsry_dispatch` error out?
- Does it succeed but no agent actually starts?
- Does an agent start but never write back results?
- Does the dispatch record save to Dolt but the agent execution layer is missing?

User to fill in symptom; this bead records that the *capability* is non-functional regardless of the precise mode.

## Why this matters
The substrate-IDL track has 12 well-scoped bead specs. The whole point of the decomposition exercise was that each leaf is dispatchable — passing all 7 dispatchability properties from `skills/problem-decomposer/DISPATCHABILITY.md`. If the dispatcher itself doesn't work, the dispatchability discipline at write-time pays no return at execution time.

Pairs with `rosary-98ee93` (cross-repo deps), `rosary-992e79` (no thread_create), and `rosary-98b11d` (bead_link param schema). Together these say: **bead creation works, bead lifecycle and execution don't**. The right shape of rosary is in scope; the implementation has gaps.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `rsry_dispatch` call against a known-good bead (e.g., a bead in cloister with `dispatchable: true` and a clear acceptance criteria) results in an actual agent context window opening and doing the work
- The dispatch record persists in Dolt and is queryable via `rsry_dispatch_history`
- Dispatched work lands in an isolated workspace (worktree) per `src/workspace.rs`
- On success, the bead transitions `Dispatched` → `InReview` (per ADR-0004 dual state machine)
- Integration test exercises end-to-end against a synthetic bead

## Inputs
- src/dispatch/mod.rs (Agent dispatch, pipeline mapping, execution)
- src/dispatch/providers.rs (AgentProvider trait — claude / gemini / plugin-kind="dispatch" backends)
- src/dispatch/sweep.rs (Orphan-dispatch detection — exists but may not be reachable)
- src/workspace.rs (Git/jj worktree creation and isolation)
- src/serve/handlers.rs (MCP rsry_dispatch handler)
- docs/adr/0004 (dual state machine — what state transitions should fire)

## Output shape
PR against rosary. Touches dispatch + handlers + workspace. Net diff probably <800 lines if it's primarily wiring; could be more if a provider needs rewiring. Add integration test.

## Scope boundary
Make dispatch *work*. Pipeline phase tuning, semantic dedup improvements, dispatch history visualizations — separate beads.

## Failure mode
Dispatch a synthetic test bead. If no agent context opens / no work happens / no state transition fires → fail.

## Time-box
L (this is the most plumbing-heavy of the rsry friction beads; could split into "make stdio dispatch work" vs "make Claude provider work" vs "make state transitions fire")

## Workaround in use today
For the 12 substrate-IDL leaves, falling back to Claude Code's `Agent` tool with `general-purpose` subagent. Each subagent gets the bead's full spec as prompt, does the work in its own context, reports back. Loses rsry's tracking + workspace isolation but produces the work product.

comments.text:
**User clarification 2026-05-18:** the dispatch breakage is due to Claude Code harness changes — not a rosary-internal bug. rosary's dispatch wiring assumed a specific Claude Code SDK/CLI shape that has since evolved.

Implication: fix likely lives in `src/dispatch/providers.rs` (the Claude provider) — needs to adapt to the current Claude Code invocation surface. Possible touch points:
- The CLI args/flags used to spawn a Claude session
- Stdin/stdout transport assumptions
- Env vars passed through to the dispatched agent
- Workspace mount semantics

So this is compat debt, not a regression in rosary's logic. Reframing for the fix-PR description: "adapt Claude provider to current Claude Code harness."

Workaround for substrate-IDL leaves: continue using Claude Code's `Agent` tool with `general-purpose` subagent (foreground via Task tool). Bead spec → subagent prompt → work product. Loses rsry's tracking + worktree isolation but produces output.

comments.text: RESOLVED by PR #226 (rosary-b1495c), merged 2026-06-23. The "dispatch doesn't work" root cause was credential propagation to the spawned claude (not TTY/PTY — empirically disproven this session). #226 fixed auth injection across all spawn paths (spawn_agent, spawn_detached, verify, bdr_enrich). Verified live: real `rsry_dispatch` of a throwaway bead succeeded end-to-end (workspace created, agent ran on claude-opus-4-8, is_error:false, bead auto-closed). Dispatch works today. Closing. title: Map bead file scopes to agent write permissions at dispatch
description:
## Problem

Dispatched agents can modify files outside their bead's declared `files` scope. Case in point: bead signet-8915ba declared files `["pkg/git/identity.go", "pkg/git/sign.go", "cmd/signet-git/main.go"]` but also modified `pkg/attest/x509/localca.go`, which could conflict with a parallel bead (signet-882eca) working in the same package.

The `has_file_overlap()` check (epic.rs:386-393) prevents concurrent dispatch but doesn't enforce the scope at runtime — the agent's `--allowedTools` include unrestricted Write/Edit access.

## Proposal

When dispatching an agent, translate the bead's `files` + `test_files` into Write/Edit path restrictions:

1. Agent can **read** anything (needs context)
2. Agent can only **write/edit** files listed in `files` + `test_files` + any NEW files in those directories
3. If the agent tries to modify an out-of-scope file, the tool call is denied with a message explaining the scope boundary

## Implementation options

- **Claude Code hooks**: `pre_tool_use` hook that checks Edit/Write file paths against bead scope
- **--allowedTools regex**: Claude Code supports path-scoped tool permissions
- **Agent prompt instruction**: Softer — tell the agent its scope and trust it (current approach, clearly insufficient)

## Why

- Prevents merge conflicts between parallel beads
- Enforces the contract that `files` scope defines
- Caught by review but should be caught at write time

title: workspace_dir() mkdirs as a side effect — 20,435 leaked dirs in ~/.rsry/worktrees since March; plus basename collision lets one repo reuse another's workspace
description:
Found while spiking jj-lib workspace creation (rosary-efd300).

SYMPTOM: ~/.rsry/worktrees/ currently holds 20,435 EMPTY directories (18 MB), accumulating since 2026-03-16 — four months. Almost all are named .tmpXXXXXX (they are hidden, so a plain `ls` shows only ~16 entries and the pile is invisible). None contain a .jj or .git — they are pure empty shells.

CAUSE (src/workspace/sweep.rs:13-23): `workspace_dir()` is a PATH-COMPUTING function with a filesystem side effect:

    pub fn workspace_dir(repo_path: &Path, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let repo_name = repo_path.file_name()...;              // repo BASENAME
        let home = dirs_next::home_dir()...;
        let ws_root = home.join(".rsry").join("worktrees").join(&repo_name);
        let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(&ws_root);             // <-- mkdir just to compute a path
        ws_root.join(id)
    }

Every caller that merely wants the path — including the existence CHECK in Workspace::create — creates the directory. The test suite passes tempfile::TempDir paths whose basename is a random .tmpXXXXXX, so each test run leaks one permanent directory into the developer's REAL home directory. Tests are not hermetic: they write outside their TempDir.

SECOND, MORE SERIOUS BUG — BASENAME COLLISION: ws_root keys on the repo BASENAME, not a unique repo identity. Two different repos with the same basename (~/work/api and ~/other/api, or any two checkouts named "rosary") share ~/.rsry/worktrees/<basename>/<bead-id>. Combined with the reuse branch in Workspace::create:

    if existing_ws.exists() && vcs != VcsKind::None { return Ok(reused) }

...an agent dispatched in repo A can silently REUSE a workspace directory belonging to repo B, and Workspace::create returns it as a valid isolated workspace. The reuse branch also never verifies the directory is actually a registered VCS workspace — it trusts existence alone, so a stale plain directory is handed back as if it were a jj workspace. This is a concrete instance of rosary-6e5fc1 (repo addressing has no canonical identity).

HOW IT SURFACED (worth recording — it is a test-isolation lesson): the jj-lib spike test passed when run alone and FAILED in the full suite, with before=["default"] after=["default"] — no jj workspace registered, yet Workspace::create still "succeeded". The isolated run had left ~/.rsry/worktrees/repo/spike-1 behind; the suite run found it existing and took the reuse branch. A test that passes alone and fails in-suite was the only reason any of this was noticed.

FIX SKETCH:
1. Make workspace_dir PURE (no mkdir). Create the directory only in the code paths that actually materialize a workspace.
2. Key the root on a canonical repo identity, not basename (rosary-6e5fc1 seam), so two same-named repos cannot collide.
3. Make the reuse branch VERIFY the existing directory is a real registered workspace for this repo (jj: registered in the store; git: a valid worktree), not merely present.
4. Make tests hermetic — redirect the workspace root (env var or injected root) so no test writes into the real $HOME.
5. One-off: garbage-collect the existing ~20k empty dirs.

comments.text:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF PR #405 — VERDICT: CHANGES NEEDED. The headline claim is FALSIFIED. Recording so the next session does not merge it believing the fix is complete.

1. THE LEAK IS RELOCATED, NOT FIXED (the big one). The PR claimed "22766 -> 22766, zero new directories". That measured $HOME only. The reviewer measured $TMPDIR: 145 dot-prefixed roots in $TMPDIR/rsry-test-worktrees after ~16 runs — ~9 per run, the SAME rate the PR claimed to eliminate, with the SAME invisibility (`ls` shows 0, `ls -a` shows 145). `ensure_workspace_root` (sweep.rs:70-73) still mkdirs a per-repo root that no cleanup path removes. Open question worth answering first: does `git worktree add` / `jj workspace add` create leading dirs itself? If yes, DELETE both ensure_workspace_root calls and the fix becomes structural.

2. sweep_orphaned STILL USES THE LEGACY PATH (sweep.rs:414-421) — builds home/.rsry/worktrees/<basename> by hand, ignoring workspace_root, the digest, WORKTREE_ROOT_ENV, and the cfg!(test) redirect. It is the ONLY orphan-reclaim mechanism (reconcile/mod.rs:481), so after this PR orphan reclaim is a permanent no-op for every new workspace, AND it would remove_dir_all real $HOME dirs from test builds.

3. UNACKNOWLEDGED MIGRATION HAZARD. Every pre-existing workspace becomes unreachable at merge:
   - lifecycle.rs:47 resume-after-death misses it -> second worktree on a fresh fix/{id} branch.
   - dispatch/sweep.rs:133-140 -> sweep_orphan_dispatches reverts a LIVE Dispatched bead to open (called on every rsry_status poll, handlers/mod.rs:309) -> duplicate dispatch onto a repo an agent is actively editing.
   - serve/review.rs:180 -> rsry_review reports workspace:null for beads that have one.
   - reconcile/orchestration.rs:327 -> crash recovery cannot find .rsry-orchestrator.json.
   Exposure on this machine is currently ~nil, so "merge when no dispatches are active" + a stated note may suffice — but it must be STATED.

4. unsafe { set_var } SAFETY COMMENT IS FALSE (tests.rs:1033/1064). I wrote "single-threaded test scope"; cargo test is multi-threaded. std is explicit: "the only sound option is to not use set_var/remove_var in multi-threaded programs at all". Concurrent tests (concurrent_worktree_isolation, e2e_colocated_workspace_isolation, git_worktree_has_source_code_not_just_beads) call workspace_root and could land in this test's TempDir, which is then dropped under them. remove_var is not panic-safe either. Repo already has the right pattern: codex_gate_test_lock (dispatch/tests.rs:13-28) + a Drop guard. Latent, not reproduced in 16 stress runs.

5. HASHES to_string_lossy() NOT A NORMALIZED PATH (sweep.rs:44). "/a/b/" and "/a/b" are Path-EQUAL everywhere else in this codebase but hash to different roots. Hash components() instead.

6. DESIGN CONTRADICTION I SHOULD ANSWER, NOT HAND-WAVE. The PR argues against canonicalizing because ~/github -> ~/remotes are "deliberately distinct" — but scanner.rs:68-77 (canonicalize_repo_path, rosary-617010) exists PRECISELY so those aliases compare EQUAL for repo matching. Under the new key the same physical repo reached via two aliases gets two isolated workspace roots. That contradicts an existing invariant and needs a decision, not a comment.

NITS: docs/CONFIGURATION.md:251 still documents the old path and :235 omits RSRY_WORKTREE_ROOT; stale comments at reconcile/orchestration.rs:324-326 and dispatch/sweep.rs:9; ensure_workspace_root is pub but only used in sweep.rs.

CONFIRMED GOOD (do not redo): workspace_dir IS pure (sweep.rs:31-33); the two ensure_ calls are the only creation sites; nothing breaks from the removed implicit mkdir; 8 hex is sufficient (~1e-7); content_hash is BLAKE3 and stable (pinned by golden vectors); the basename-collision bug is real (lifecycle.rs:47-61 reuses on .exists() alone); the restore/tests.rs clippy drive-by is legitimate.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING: I verified the fix by measuring the location I had just moved the problem OUT of. The measurement was real; the scope was self-serving. Measure the invariant ("no directory is created anywhere that nothing cleans up"), not the symptom's old address.

comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-07-22 — R4b is blocked on something other than what the plan says.

`rsry lattice audit` on rosary's own store:
    lattice audit [rosary]: beads=1117 comparable=0 agree=0 diverge=0
      (no foldable observations yet — the corpus fills as dispatches run post-R4b-step-1)

comparable=0. Not "close to equivalent", not "diverging" — NO DATA AT ALL across 1117 beads.

WHY (verified by grep over src/, excluding src/observation/ and tests):
  - No `.record(` / `record_observation` / ObservationLog call anywhere in production code.
  - `persist_status` does NOT record an observation alongside its write.
  - `SqliteObservationLog` is NEVER CONSTRUCTED outside tests.

So the ADR-0010 substrate is entirely DARK: the algebras, the fold, tree_fold, quarantine, shadow-compare and `lattice audit` are all built and unit-tested, and none of it is connected to the running system. The audit will report comparable=0 forever, because nothing ever writes an observation.

THIS INVERTS THE STATED PLAN. audit.rs:2-5 frames R4b as "compare the lattice-derived status against persist_status; if divergence is small or zero, the fold is proven equivalent and persist_status can be deleted." That is unreachable: there is no corpus and no mechanism to accumulate one. The blocker is not EVIDENCE, it is the WRITE PATH.

CORRECTED SEQUENCE:
 1. R4b step 1 (THE actual blocker): dual-write. Every place that calls persist_status also records an Observation carrying its `source`. Cheap, additive, changes no behavior — the lattice stays shadow. This is the ONLY thing between "no data" and "corpus fills".
 2. Let dispatches run; the corpus accumulates.
 3. `rsry lattice audit` now produces real numbers -> the equivalence evidence the plan wants.
 4. Flip the source of truth; delete persist_status.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND R4b (context from 2026-07-22 session): the lattice is the fix for three separate live problems, all currently worked around:
  - DUAL STATE (user's requirement): per-source Observations mean branch-local state and global-store state COEXIST instead of one clobbering the other. `Observation.source` already models exactly this.
  - LOSSY MERGE: the JSONL sync (rosary-4ebf52) needs a conflict rule because it merges a MUTABLE SNAPSHOT. Observations are append-only and form a G-SET (mod.rs:278) — G-sets union trivially, so there is nothing to conflict.
  - THE MERGE DRIVER (rosary-f9516f) exists only to make that snapshot safe. Under an op-log it is deletable, which is also prior-art recommendation #1 in docs/prior-art/state-sync-sota.md (git-bug/Radicle/beads/Entire all store an append-only log outside the working tree, none needs a merge driver).

So R4b step 1 — a dual-write that is additive and behavior-neutral — is the highest-leverage unblocked item in this cluster. Everything above is waiting on a write call that does not exist.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
CORRECTION + MEASURED BACKFILL VIABILITY (2026-07-22).

I previously said the ~1778 done beads' provenance was unrecoverable because the `events` table is empty of status transitions (10 rows total: 5 pr_url, 5 github_merge). That was wrong about the CONCLUSION — git history is a high-fidelity backfill source.

MEASURED over the last 400 commits on origin/main (rosary):
  197  squash merges matching `[bead-id] <type>(<scope>): <subject> (#N)`
  159  distinct bead ids referenced
  157  of those resolve in the bead store   -> 98.7% JOIN RATE
    2  referenced in git but absent from the store (dangling)

So the corpus R4b needs largely ALREADY EXISTS, encoded by the commit contract the commit-msg hook has been enforcing all along. Each squash merge yields exactly the shape of an Observation:
    source           = git (or github, for the PR event)
    work_item        = the [bead-id]
    field            = Status
    value            = done
    observed_at      = commit/merge timestamp
    source_event_id  = commit sha (or PR number — both are stable, dedup-able)
    actor            = commit author
That is BETTER provenance than a forward-only dual-write would produce, because it carries the merge event and its author, not just "status changed".

REVISED R4b SEQUENCING (supersedes the "dual-write only" plan in my previous comment):
 1. BACKFILL from git history — walk `git log` per registered repo, parse `[bead-id] ... (#N)`, emit one Observation per merge into the lattice. Retroactive, high-fidelity, and it makes `rsry lattice audit` immediately comparable instead of comparable=0.
 2. DUAL-WRITE for new transitions (still needed — git only witnesses MERGES, not open->in_progress->blocked).
 3. Audit -> equivalence evidence -> flip -> delete persist_status.
 The backfill is what makes step 3 reachable in one pass instead of waiting months for a forward-only corpus to accumulate.

CAVEAT worth stating: git witnesses only the terminal merge event, so backfilled beads get a Status=done observation and nothing about their intermediate lifecycle. That is sufficient for the equivalence audit (which compares DERIVED status vs persist_status) but it is not a full history. Do not claim the backfill reconstructs the lifecycle — it reconstructs the outcome.

SIDE FINDING: the 2 dangling refs (in git, absent from store) are direct field evidence for rosary-225c94 — the commit-msg hook validates bead-id FORMAT but not EXISTENCE. Predicted earlier today from reading the hook; now measured in this repo's own history.

title: EPIC: Agent-native workflow state-machine substrate (PR/CI/review as kafka-esque events, GHA as one backend)
description:
## User's framing (2026-05-19)

Recurring pattern the user manually types every PR:

> "Pls watch for Copilot's review / respond if appropriate or resolve. Once all are resolved or responded report back to me if you need my input, or otherwise if CI passes merge once things are resolved."

That's a **state machine encoded as a one-shot prompt**, every time. Entities (PR, review thread, CI run, bead, agent worker) have states (open/replied/resolved, queued/running/passed). Transitions are caused by events (Copilot posted, CI finished, agent committed). Policies are "when X is in state Y AND Z is in state W, then action A."

Today this state machine lives in **GHA + GitHub UI + the user's head**. Goal: extract it into a substrate.

## Architectural insight

> "It feels kafka-esque... but we can be better because we are designing for agentic / AI native, not humans."

Key distinctions:
1. **State machine is the primitive.** Not "watch this PR" — a generic substrate any entity registers against.
2. **GitHub is one backend, not THE backend.** GHA is an actor that drives transitions. Local CI (reading GHA workflow files), tmux-spawned agents, webhooks, etc. can all be equivalent actors.
3. **Provenance via cloister + signet + ley-line, not GitHub.** Each transition is a signed attestation; the chain is recoverable. GitHub becomes a write-through cache, not source of truth.
4. **Agent-native UX != human UX.** Humans need rich UI to drive state machines (point-and-click). Agents need declarative policies + observable events. No clicking.

## What this is NOT

- Not "replace GitHub" — it's "GitHub is one observer/actor"
- Not "no CI" — it's "CI is a thing that emits state-transition events"
- Not "build our own k8s" — it's "the reconciler pattern, but for agent workflows"

## Plausible primitive shape

```toml
# rosary-self.toml or similar
[[policy]]
name = "auto-merge-when-clean"
when = "pr.checks.passed AND pr.reviews.all_resolved AND pr.merge_state=clean"
do = "gh pr merge $pr.number --squash"

[[policy]]
name = "auto-reply-copilot"
when = "pr.review.copilot.unresolved AND pr.review.copilot.body matches '^Addressed'"
do = "gh api repos/.../comments/$id/replies POST 'See latest commit'"
```

Plus an **event source** abstraction: GHA webhooks, GitHub poll, local CI process, tmux pane output, MCP tool calls. The reconciler matches events against policies + dispatches actions.

## Why this is its own EPIC, not part of existing beads

| Existing bead | Adjacent but different |
|---|---|
| `rosary-cdd522` (Guardrail trait) | pre-merge invariants; this is workflow state-machines |
| `rosary-75555d` (tmux substrate) | spawn primitive; this is the policy layer above it |
| `rosary-792ed6` (Personal/root rosary) | storage substrate; this is the execution substrate |
| `rosary-b65745` (Plugin kind=mcp outbound) | one event source; this is the matcher above it |

This bead is the architectural umbrella that ties them all together for the PR-management use case the user actively wants today.

## Possible homes

- **rosary** — bead lifecycle is already a state machine; extending to PR/CI is a natural fit
- **cloister** — already has attestation/signing infra; could host the policy substrate as one of its MCP-hosted tools
- **a new project** — if the substrate generalizes beyond rosary/cloister concerns

User's lean (implicit): probably cloister, since attestation infra is already there. Not yet committed.

## Open questions

- Policy DSL design — TOML declarative vs Rhai/script vs WASM
- Event-source plug-in shape — how do new sources (GHA webhook, GitHub poll, tmux pane) register
- Conflict resolution — what if two policies match same event with different actions
- Personal vs shared — policies that are user-personal (auto-merge my PRs) vs team-shared (CI required before merge)
- Local CI replay — read GHA workflow file, run locally (act-style?), emit same events

## First experiment (proposed)

Pick the ONE most-typed prompt and encode it as a single hardcoded policy:

> "Watch PR #X. When Copilot's review is on a stale SHA AND HEAD has commits since, post `@copilot review` comment. When all review threads resolved AND CI green, auto-merge --squash. Report back if any review has `Needs changes` state."

Implement as a `rsry pr autopilot <pr-number>` subcommand. Hardcoded policy, hardcoded event sources (GitHub poll). One concrete shipping artifact. If it tightens the loop, expand to declarative policies.

## Time-box

Design: M (ADR + first-experiment scope decision)
First experiment: M (~1 week)
Full substrate: L+ (months)

## User observation (2026-05-19, end of session)

> "rosary-5dc9b0, rosary-a7f18e, rosary-e1760d all seem related + the like pipeline abstraction? They appear to be parallelizable as well so long as they are scoped out properly."

The user spotted the unifying shape. All three are **pipeline-flavored primitives**:

| Bead | Pipeline shape |
|---|---|
| `rosary-5dc9b0` (rsry_ticket_load) | **Fan-in aggregator** — pulls Linear+GH+Zendesk+bead, composes one view |
| `rosary-e1760d` (witchcraft chat search) | **Indexer pipeline** — ingest → embed → query → results |
| `rosary-a7f18e` (Dolt port race) | **Process lifecycle / supervision** — process-pool primitive |

Plus the recurring "watch PR → respond → resolve → merge" prompt: a **reactor / event-driven policy** loop.

Rosary already has a "pipeline" concept (bead dispatch → triage → verify). The user is asking: does that generalize to handle ALL pipeline-shaped work, not just bead dispatch?

## Rust ecosystem options (web search 2026-05-19)

Researched: "temporal.io-like + fs watchers + reactor in Rust"

**Workflow engines / durable execution:**
- **[Sayiir](https://dev.to/yacineb_45/sayiir-a-durable-workflow-engine-in-rust-simple-with-python-nodejs-bindings-5gd7)** — embeddable durable workflow engine in Rust. Checkpoint-based recovery, no deterministic replay, no separate server. Simpler than Temporal. **Closest fit** for embedding into rosary as a substrate.
- **[Temporal Core SDK](https://temporal.io/)** — Rust-implemented core; TS/Python/.NET/Ruby SDKs all wrap it. No first-party Rust-app SDK, but the engine itself is in Rust. Heavier, full Temporal semantics.
- **Inngest** — open-source durable primitives; serverless-shaped.

**Reactor + fs watchers:**
- **`notify` crate** — standard Rust filesystem watcher.
- **tokio reactor + `mio`** — the underlying event-demultiplex layer; what rosary already uses indirectly via tokio.
- **`async-watcher`** — higher-level async fs notification.

**Source: [Temporal at Replay 2026](https://thenewstack.io/temporal-replay-2026-news/)** — they explicitly called out "durable execution for AI agent workflows" as the new positioning. So others are validating the same insight.

## Recommendation for this EPIC

Don't build a Temporal clone. Don't depend on Sayiir directly (yet — evaluate it but the user's primitives are narrower). Instead:

1. **Use `notify` + tokio for the event source layer.** No reinvention.
2. **Use a checkpoint-style "policy state machine"** (similar to Sayiir's approach but rosary-specific). Each policy run is a function call that produces an event log; resumption replays the log + skips completed steps.
3. **Generalize rosary's existing `pipeline` concept** to handle PR/CI/review events alongside bead dispatch. The `tool_pipeline_upsert` / `tool_pipeline_query` MCP surface already exists — extend the entity types it knows about.
4. **Parallelize the three observed beads** (5dc9b0, a7f18e, e1760d) once the substrate stub exists — they share the substrate but operate on different domains, so they can ship independently.

## Cross-link in this EPIC's first-experiment

The first experiment in this EPIC (`rsry pr autopilot <pr-num>`) is exactly the "event-driven reactor + policy state machine" shape. Sayiir's approach (checkpoint each output, resume on failure) is what `pr autopilot` wants: if the user closes the laptop mid-flow, resuming should pick up where it left off, not redo Copilot review checks.

title: [investigate] dolt sql-server instances leak — 10+ orphaned servers (~6.5GB) contributed to an OOM
description:
Observed 2026-06-26 on the operator's machine during a lectio session: 10+ `dolt sql-server` processes running concurrently (`dolt sql-server -H 127.0.0.1 -P <port>` on distinct ports, ~28-35MB RSS each, several GB total). This was half of a machine OOM (the other half was a separate lectio-daemon memory issue, handled in the lectio repo).

Hypothesis: rosary/bd spawns a `dolt sql-server` for the beads Dolt DB and does not reliably reap them — repeated bd/rsry MCP operations accumulate orphaned server instances (distinct ports = missing singleton guard / race) that never exit.

Investigate:
1. Where rosary starts `dolt sql-server` (per-repo daemon? per bd command? rsry MCP lifecycle?) and what owns shutdown.
2. Why old instances aren't reaped (no PID tracking? no idle timeout? crash leaves orphan? duplicate-on-same-DB race).
3. Whether concurrent servers on the SAME beads Dolt dir risk lock contention / corruption.

Fix direction: singleton-per-repo reuse (attach to existing server on known port instead of spawning), idle-timeout/auto-shutdown, and/or a reaper + a `bd`/rsry command to list+reap stray dolt servers.

Repro: run many bd/rsry ops over a session, then `ps aux | grep 'dolt sql-server' | grep -v grep | wc -l` — count grows unbounded instead of staying ~1 per active repo.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (investigated; live evidence: 37 dolt sql-server procs running, one at 4GB, ~6.5GB total).

Three compounding causes:
1. NO runtime reaper / Drop. rosary spawns 'dolt sql-server' in two places (src/dolt/mod.rs:402 for DoltClient, src/store_dolt.rs:89 for the orchestrator store) but NEVER kills them at runtime — the only libc::kill(SIGTERM) is inside a test's cleanup (store_dolt.rs:1381). There is no impl Drop for DoltClient/pool/store. So every server outlives the rsry process that started it.
2. Ephemeral port per spawn → no reuse guarantee. Each spawn picks a fresh free port (port=0). Re-connects find the live server via .beads/dolt/.dolt/sql-server.info (+ legacy dolt-server.port). When that file is stale/missing/racy, connect() spawns a NEW server on a NEW port instead of reusing → accumulation. Evidence: 37 servers on 37 DISTINCT ephemeral ports = 37 non-reused spawns.
3. Many independent entry points each connect+maybe-spawn: every rsry CLI call, MCP reconnect, dispatched agent, and test run. The code even acknowledges it (dolt/mod.rs:352 tells the user to 'pkill -f dolt sql-server' for stale servers).

Contribution to the OOM: ~37 procs × ~30MB + one runaway at 4GB (a long-lived server that accumulated state) ≈ 6.5GB. Same pressure that caused disk-full mid-session.

RECOMMENDATIONS (each its own fix bead):
A. Add a REAPER — a sweep (rsry startup + periodic, or a ) that kills orphaned dolt servers: pid dead, repo gone, or not the pid in the current sql-server.info. Fold into the existing workspace sweep (src/workspace/sweep.rs / dispatch/sweep.rs).
B. Guarantee REUSE — connect() must not spawn when a live server exists for this db (robust sql-server.info read; single-flight spawn). Verify the pool.rs:302 sql-server.info staleness fix actually prevents duplicate spawns.
C. Decide LIFECYCLE — dolt servers should be either launchd-supervised long-lived daemons (one per repo, like the MCP service) OR process-scoped (killed on rsry exit via Drop). Today they orphan (neither). Given rsry = short-lived CLI + long-lived MCP daemon, a supervised shared model + reaper is the fit.
D. Investigate the 4GB runaway separately — is it a dolt memory leak, a huge working set, or an unbounded long-lived server? 

Immediate reclaim: 'pkill -f dolt sql-server' frees the ~6.5GB now, but forces respawn on next connect (and would kill the rosary self-store server the live MCP uses — do it when safe, not mid-session).
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by mapping servers→repos: each server serves a DISTINCT repo, 1:1, NOT orphaned/duplicated — reuse works). The real cause: RepoPool::from_config (src/pool.rs:94, 'connect to all repos in the given config') EAGERLY connects EVERY configured repo at MCP server startup (called from serve/mod.rs:611 HTTP, ipc.rs:115 stdio, serve/mod.rs:720). Each connect_bead_store → for a Dolt repo → spawns/attaches a dolt sql-server. 34 configured repos (incl. 19 assay-* worktrees) → 34 heavyweight MySQL server processes → ~6.5GB, with rosary's own store the 4GB busiest. pool.get() is &self — a lookup into the pre-connected map, so the pool is EAGER not lazy. FIX: make RepoPool lazy — from_config records config only (names/paths/beads_dirs), and get()/get_client() connect-on-demand + cache (interior mutability, return Arc<dyn BeadStore>). Then a single-repo op touches 1 server, not 34; startup spawns 0. Also worth: many of the 34 (esp. assay-* worktrees) should be SQLite (no server) per the CLAUDE.md default (rosary-cf6e38 SQLite-first). The reaper idea (rosary-cce7bc) is voided — symptom not cause.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified for why multiple dolt sql-server instances accumulate; fix (singleton-per-repo reuse and/or idle-timeout/reaper) implemented; after a session of repeated bd/rsry operations, `ps aux | grep 'dolt sql-server' | grep -v grep | wc -l` stays bounded (~= active repos), not growing unbounded.

title: Hierarchical repo-oriented config substrate for agentic tools (.gitconfig-style, TOML, cross-tool)
description:
## User's framing (2026-05-19)

> "I am almost thinking that we need to expose less CLI options and have a config file (that is repo oriented and global, like how .gitconfig works hierarchically)."
> "Not sure if that's a cobra thing so we dont repeat the world."
> "I also lowkey... love toml."

Recurring pattern across rosary, mache, and (soon) cloister: each tool ships its own ad-hoc config story. Each has CLI flags. Each has env vars. None has a clean `.gitconfig`-style hierarchy where:

- system defaults → user config (`~/.<tool>/config.toml`) → project config (`<repo>/.<tool>/config.toml`) → env vars → CLI flags

Each tool reimplements bits of this. None gets all of it right.

## What the user wants

- **TOML** (explicit preference)
- **Repo-oriented** (project config travels with the repo)
- **Hierarchical** (project > user > system, like `.gitconfig`)
- **Cross-tool consistency** (rosary + mache + cloister all use the same pattern)
- **Less CLI flag duplication** — most options should live in config; flags are overrides

## Where this lives (open question)

Two plausible homes:

1. **A shared crate** that rosary + mache (and others) import. Lives somewhere central. Rust: `crates/agentic-config`. Mache uses Go though — would need a Go equivalent or a JSON-shaped wire format both consume.

2. **Each tool independently uses the same convention.** Rust tools use `figment` or `viper`-equivalent; Go tools use viper. Config schemas vary per tool but the loading pattern is unified.

3. **Cloister-hosted.** Cloister already does identity + access control via MCP; could expose a `tool_config_get(tool, key)` MCP that any tool queries. Heavier; requires cloister to be running.

User's hint: "Maybe this is ANOTHER project. Maybe it belongs in cloister." But also "Not sure if that's a cobra thing so we dont repeat the world" — implying the standard library answer is probably right.

## What today's rosary has (partial precedent)

- `~/.rsry/config.toml` (global user config)
- `rosary.toml` (project config)
- `rosary-self.toml` (self-management)
- Mixed env vars + CLI flags

The hierarchy isn't enforced rigorously and flags don't uniformly override. Refactor target.

## What today's mache has

User says: similar story, also wants this. Mache is Go; would need viper.

## Recommended shape

**For Rust tools (rosary, eventually cloister-rs bits):** `figment` crate with the Toml + Env + Serialized layers stacked.
**For Go tools (mache):** `spf13/viper` (already the standard, supports TOML + env + flags + hierarchical).

Define a **shared config-file naming convention**:
- `~/.<tool>/config.toml` for user-level
- `<repo>/.<tool>/config.toml` for project-level
- `<repo>/<tool>.toml` for project root (e.g. `rosary.toml`)

Document this in a cross-repo ADR (probably lives in cloister since it's substrate-wide).

## Acceptance (minimum useful)

- Per-tool config loader uses figment/viper with hierarchy: system → user → project → env → flags
- Most CLI flags become optional (override config)
- Config schema documented per tool with TOML keys mapped to flags
- Cross-tool ADR documents the convention
- Backward compat: existing flag-only callers still work

## Time-box

S — per-tool figment/viper setup is ~½ day each.
M — including the cross-tool ADR + naming convention.

## Cross-link

- This might be the right home for: scope abstraction's "name → path resolver" (so `scope: \"repo:rosary\"` can look up the path from config without explicit `repo_path`)
- `rosary-185bca` (AIO consolidation) — repo discovery probably goes here
- mache and rosary both want this; cross-repo bead candidate

title: Dolt sandbox test port-allocation race in SandboxBeads::new — intermittent flake
description:
## Symptom

Tests in `src/dolt/tests.rs` (Dolt sandbox tests) intermittently fail with port-collision errors:

- `migrate_repairs_partial_005_when_marked_applied` fails one run, passes on re-run
- Other sandbox tests show the same behavior under load (full `cargo test --bin rsry` rather than single-test invocation)

## Why

`SandboxBeads::new` allocates an ephemeral port via `TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")` → `local_addr().port()` → drops listener → starts dolt sql-server on that port. There's a window between the listener drop and dolt's bind where another process (or another concurrent test) can claim the same port.

When you run the full suite in parallel (cargo test default), multiple sandbox tests can race on this.

## Fix options

1. **Serialize sandbox tests.** Add `#[serial_test::serial]` to the dolt sandbox tests. Cheapest fix; throughput penalty.
2. **Retry on bind failure.** Loop the ephemeral allocation + dolt-start sequence with a backoff if the port is taken. Modest complexity.
3. **Use Dolt's own port-allocation.** Have dolt sql-server bind to port 0 itself + read back the port from its stdout/logs. Removes the race entirely. Most correct.

## Confidence

Medium. The flake reproduces on busy machines, doesn't on quiet ones — symptom matches a race. Option (3) is the right architectural answer but requires understanding what dolt sql-server logs when bound to port 0.

## Time-box

S — option (1) is 10 lines. (3) is ~1 hour.

## Why now

Surfaced 2026-05-19 during rosary-b5da2f PR #214 conversion testing: the `migrate_repairs_partial_005_when_marked_applied` test failed in the full-suite run but passed in isolation. No code change in the test or its dependencies. This is the second time the same flake class has bitten in two days.

## Files

- `src/dolt/tests.rs` — SandboxBeads::new
- `src/dolt/mod.rs` — connect() ephemeral port allocation

title: rsry pr: record pr_url event at creation (not just merge) so open PRs carry bead provenance
description: Today Command::Pr just runs 'gh pr create' + prints the URL; the structured pr_url event is only logged at MERGE time by close-merged/the GitHub webhook (parsing [bead-id] … (#N)). So an OPEN PR has no stored bead→PR pointer — only the [bead-id] string in its title. A /pr-board (lives in ~/github/jamestexas/agents, adjacent) that queries beads for pr_url therefore sees only merged PRs. Fix: capture the created PR URL from 'gh pr create' output in Command::Pr and store.log_event(bead_id, 'pr_url', url) right there, keyed off .rsry-bead-id / the branch. Then open PRs carry their bead immediately and the board reads provenance (derived_from BDR source, handoff chain, CI/review state) straight off the bead + joins lectio memory. Enables the pr-board provenance surface — which is also structural medicine for the discovery-first failure class (cf. the cloister leyline-sign RCA: designing work that already shipped, because provenance wasn't queried first). Board-side fallback works today: gh pr list → parse [bead-id] → join beads.

comments.text: CORRECTION on mechanism (checked github_webhook.rs): recording in Command::Pr is the WRONG primary layer — it only fires for 'rsry pr', so an agent using raw 'gh pr create' / the gh MCP tool / the web UI is missed (the exact 'agent has to remember' trap). The right layer is the GitHub pull_request webhook rosary ALREADY receives (src/serve/github_webhook.rs): it verifies HMAC, parses the [bead-id] from the PR (bead-id extractor at line ~50), but filters to action=='closed' (line 197) and ignores 'opened'. FIX: handle action=='opened' (and 'reopened') → extract bead id from title → store.log_event(bead, 'pr_url', pr.html_url). Server-side + caller-agnostic = captured no matter HOW the PR was created, zero agent cooperation. ~15 lines. Command::Pr recording becomes an optional local fallback for tunnel-less setups; a reconcile sweep (gh pr list open → match [bead-id] → record) is the belt-and-suspenders catch-all when the webhook isn't reachable. Retitle intent: 'webhook: record pr_url on pull_request.opened (+ reconcile fallback)'.

title: MCP + CLI: rsry_bead_comment_update / rsry_bead_comment_delete (with audit-trail columns)
description:
## Motivation

The rsry MCP today exposes `rsry_bead_comment` (append) and `rsry_bead_update` (description-only). There is no way to **edit or delete a comment** via the public API. Consumers who need to scrub a comment have three bad options today:

1. Append a "ignore the previous comment" follow-up (cluttered audit trail; leaked content stays in the binary).
2. Drop to direct dolt SQL (`UPDATE comments SET text = ...`) — bypasses the abstraction; one-off scripts; not auditable.
3. Live with the leak.

This recurs **whenever** a comment needs to be revised: typos, wrong commit hashes, accidental absolute-paths, leaked credentials, content the author later wants to clarify or correct.

Surfaced 2026-05-09 from cloister's OSS-prep PII sweep. cloister had two comments containing `/Users/jamesgardner/...` (the author's home dir, which leaks the real-name portion). The MCP couldn't fix them; SQL was the only path. Direct SQL ran into auto-mode tool-classifier guardrails (correctly — destructive bead-history mutations shouldn't bypass the abstraction).

This is a **rosary-level gap**, not a cloister-specific issue. Every rsry consumer faces it.

## Proposed surfaces

### MCP

```
rsry_bead_comment_update(repo_path, comment_id, body[, reason])
  - Replaces text of an existing comment.
  - `comment_id` selects which comment (need a stable id; today comments
    have (issue_id, created_at, author) which is composite — adding a
    surrogate `comment_id` column may be required).
  - `reason` (optional) is recorded in the audit trail.
  - Returns the updated comment + a hash/version of the prior text.

rsry_bead_comment_delete(repo_path, comment_id[, reason])
  - Marks the comment deleted. Soft-delete preserves audit trail; hard-
    delete only via a separate flag (or via a CLI-only operation, not
    exposed through MCP).
```

Both should require the caller to be the comment's author OR a privileged role (TBD — for now, author-or-anyone-on-a-trusted-host is fine; cloister-style cert-scope check comes later).

### CLI

```
rsry bead comment update <issue-id> <comment-id> --body "<new text>" [--reason "<why>"]
rsry bead comment delete <issue-id> <comment-id> [--reason "<why>"] [--hard]
rsry bead comment list <issue-id>          # need this anyway, to find comment_ids
```

### Schema migration

The `comments` table currently has `(issue_id, text, author, created_at)`. Need to add:

- `id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT` (or UUID) — surrogate primary key, makes update/delete addressable.
- `edited_at DATETIME NULL` — last edit timestamp; NULL means never edited.
- `edit_reason TEXT NULL` — optional reason captured on update.
- `original_text TEXT NULL` — the very first text (preserved on first edit, immutable thereafter; gives a clean "what was this originally" audit trail without storing every revision).
- `deleted_at DATETIME NULL` — soft-delete timestamp.

Soft-delete + first-original-text is enough for v1. Full revision history can come later if needed.

## Why "audit trail" matters

The whole rsry premise is that bead history is the durable record. Mutations that erase audit trail (hard-delete) defeat that. Soft-delete + original-text preserved + edit-reason recorded keeps the property: any future reviewer can see (a) something was edited, (b) why (if reason given), (c) what the original said.

Hard-delete should exist (for honest credential-leak scenarios where the original literally must not persist) but should be CLI-only, with a `--confirm`-style guard, never via MCP.

## Cross-repo impact

After this lands:

- **cloister**: scrub the 2 comments containing `/Users/jamesgardner/...` paths via the new MCP surface. No more SQL workaround.
- **Other rsry consumers**: have a clean primitive whenever they need to revise a comment.
- **Discipline doc** (separate, not this bead): note in agent-loaded docs (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md across repos) that home-dir paths and other accidentally-leaky strings shouldn't go in bead comments in the first place — this feature is a corrective tool, not a license to be sloppy.

## Out of scope

- Full revision history (every edit kept, not just first-original). v2 if needed.
- Per-comment ACLs beyond "author can edit own." cloister-style scope checks land when ADR-0007 lease verification reaches rosary.
- Bulk pattern-scrub utility (`rsry bead comment scrub --pattern X --replace Y` across all beads). Useful but distinct primitive — file separately if the use case proves recurring.
- Modifying `rsry_bead_comment` (append) — this bead only adds new endpoints and the schema migration.

## Files (best guess; implementor may differ)

- `src/bead.rs` — core comment storage interface
- `src/bead_dolt.rs` and/or `src/bead_sqlite.rs` — backend-specific impls (rosary supports both)
- `src/serve/handlers.rs` — MCP request handlers
- `src/cli.rs` — CLI subcommands under `rsry bead comment`
- `src/migrations/00X_comment_audit.sql` (or equivalent) — schema migration
- `tests/` — unit + integration tests for update/delete + audit-trail invariants

## Success criteria

- `rsry_bead_comment_update` and `rsry_bead_comment_delete` available via MCP.
- CLI subcommands work (`rsry bead comment update/delete/list`).
- Schema migration applies idempotently; existing comments migrate cleanly.
- Soft-deleted comments hidden from `list` by default; visible via `--include-deleted`.
- Audit-trail columns populated on every update/delete.
- After cloister-side test: `dolt sql -q "SELECT * FROM comments WHERE text LIKE '%/Users/jamesgardner%'"` returns 0 rows when the new MCP surface is used to scrub.

## Refs

- Surfaced from cloister PII sweep, 2026-05-09 (commit `5abf290` and the conversation around it)
- Related rosary issue: `rsry_bead_search` doesn't search comments — also a gap surfaced during this audit; if separate bead is filed, link.

comments.text:
PR opened: https://github.com/agentic-research/rosary/pull/188

Implements all four surfaces (MCP + CLI + schema migration + trait extension) with audit-trail preservation:
- `rsry_bead_comment_list/update/delete` MCP tools
- `rsry bead comment add/list/update/delete [--hard]` CLI subcommands (nested under `comment`)
- Migration 005_comments_audit_columns (UUID id PK + edited_at + edit_reason + original_text + deleted_at)
- Both Dolt and SQLite backends; comment_id is opaque String (UUID for Dolt, stringified int for SQLite)

Tests: 866 unit + 18 integration green; clippy unchanged at 19 errors vs main. Live smoke-test on this bead in the PR description shows the full edit + soft-delete + restore-via-include-deleted lifecycle.

Unblocks cloister-aa6a71 (PII scrub via the new MCP surface) once this lands.

title: rsry_bead_search should match against comments, not just title/description
description:
## Motivation

Surfaced 2026-05-09 during cloister's OSS-prep PII sweep. After verifying with `strings` that the cloister dolt binary contained `/Users/jamesgardner/...` references, I tried to find the affected beads via:

```
rsry_bead_search(repo_path="/.../cloister", query="jamesgardner")
→ count: 0
```

Yet the strings were demonstrably present in the dolt store. Cause: `rsry_bead_search` only matches against bead **title and description** fields, not against **comments**. Since most active rsry workflows record the bulk of context in comments (progress, commit hashes, audit trails), this is a real coverage gap — search misses the majority of the bead's textual content.

## Proposed change

Extend `rsry_bead_search` to also match against `comments.text`:

```sql
-- conceptually
SELECT b.* FROM beads b
WHERE b.title LIKE ? OR b.description LIKE ?
   OR EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM comments c
     WHERE c.issue_id = b.id AND c.text LIKE ?
   )
```

Return shape stays the same (bead rows). Optionally add a `match_in` field to the result indicating where the match was found (`title|description|comment`) so callers can tell whether it was a comment hit.

## CLI parity

`rsry bead search "..."` should behave identically — extending the same query underneath.

## Performance

Comments table grows much faster than beads. For repos with thousands of comments, a naive LIKE scan can be slow. v1: just do the LIKE; document expected size limits. v2: full-text index on comments.text if needed.

## Out of scope

- Boolean / fielded search syntax (`title:foo` etc.). Defer.
- Returning matching comment snippets in the search result. Defer.
- Indexing across deleted comments — depends on rosary-XXX (the comment_update/delete bead) landing first; the soft-delete column will need to be respected here too.

## Sibling bead

This pairs naturally with `rsry_bead_comment_update / _delete` (the comment-edit feature surfaced from the same audit). The comment-edit bead is the higher priority; this one is "search should reach into comments" — useful but lower-stakes.

## Files (best guess)

title: feat(vault): wire KEK_HELPER schemes (secret-tool/op/apple-password/keyring) into buildKekSource()
description:
Follow-up to rosary-54ad76. The `vault/wrangler.toml.example` and `vault/README.md` originally documented four KEK source schemes — `secret-tool://` (Linux libsecret), `op://` (1Password CLI), `apple-password://` (macOS Passwords app), and `keyring://` (generic cross-platform) — but `buildKekSource()` in `vault/src/kek-source.ts` only dispatches `env://`, `file://`, `keychain://`, and `http(s)://`. Configuring any of the four extra schemes throws at runtime with `kek-source: unsupported URL scheme`.

Per Copilot review on notme PR #22, the docs were trimmed to match what the dispatcher actually accepts, with an explicit note that these four schemes are deferred and tracked separately. This bead is that follow-up.

## What needs to happen

1. Extend `buildKekSource()` in `vault/src/kek-source.ts` to route the four schemes through `HelperKekSource` — same path as `keychain://`. The helper-side work (the `scripts/kek-helper.mjs` sidecar interpreting the URL into a backend call) lives in cloister; see cloister ADR-0019 for the design.
2. Each scheme needs a small input-shape validator (analogous to `EnvKekSource`'s alphanumeric var-name check) — e.g. `op://VAULT/ITEM` requires both segments, `apple-password://NAME` requires a non-empty name.
3. End-to-end test per scheme via the existing `KEK_HELPER` fake-Fetcher pattern in `vault/src/__tests__/kek-source.test.ts` — assert the spec is forwarded verbatim to `GET /resolve?url=<encoded>`.
4. Restore the docs (wrangler.toml.example + README) once the dispatcher accepts the schemes.

## Files

- `vault/src/kek-source.ts` — dispatcher
- `vault/src/__tests__/kek-source.test.ts` — per-scheme acceptance tests
- `vault/wrangler.toml.example` — restore scheme list
- `vault/README.md` — restore scheme table

## Cross-link

PR #22 (`feat/vault-wire-kek-source-rate-bucket`) addresses Copilot's doc/dispatcher mismatch by trimming the docs; this bead is the inverse direction (extend the dispatcher to match the original doc intent).

title: epic: agent-attested LSP gateway — LLO + cloister + notme + CC plugin
description:
Cross-repo coordination bead. CC sessions consistently report stale rust-analyzer diagnostics because the IDE's LSP server never receives didChange after Claude's Edit-tool writes. Fix: route LSP through cloister (MCP gateway), backed by LLO (fresh data), via notme-proxy (attested local IPC over UDS).

Standards-unified design — every layer is MCP-shaped + UDS-local, no protocol churn:

  Claude Code
      │ MCP HTTP
      ▼
  cloister (workerd) ── service binding ──▶ notme (identity)
      │
      │ HTTP-over-UDS via notme-proxy
      ▼
  notme-proxy (mTLS bridge, UDS listen)
      │ UDS
      ▼
  LLO daemon (LSP/parse/vec — already UDS-native)

Attestation surface: AF_UNIX peer creds (uid/pid/cmdname) + bridge cert (Ed25519). LLO stays unaware of attestation — it just sees authenticated UDS requests.

Children:
- notme: notme-proxy UDS listen support (~50 LOC; flag already documented)
- ley-line-open: LLO HTTP MCP transport on UDS (~200 LOC, mirrors rsry serve --transport http pattern)
- cloister: register lsp_* route → forward via notme-proxy UDS to LLO (~30 LOC)
- cloister: CC plugin — route LSP through cloister, hook Edit/Write for stale-didChange (~plugin scaffolding)
