title: Fix handoff chain_hash to use hash-linking instead of path-linking
description:
WHO: Orchestrator (rosary reconciler/conductor). WHEN: Every pipeline phase handoff. BLAST RADIUS: handoff.rs + any code reading chain_hash.

The current Handoff::chain_hash() includes artifacts.previous_handoff as a file path string (".rsry-handoff-0.json"), not the actual SHA-256 hash of the previous handoff's content. This means replacing the previous handoff file does NOT invalidate the current handoff's hash — the chain is path-linked, not hash-linked.

Fix: Add previous_chain_hash: Option<[u8; 32]> to Handoff. The orchestrator computes handoff_0.chain_hash() and passes it to handoff_1 during construction. Update chain_hash() (or add chain_hash_v2()) to include the actual previous hash bytes instead of the file path.

This is Phase 1 of the agent provenance lattice specification (docs/design/agent-provenance-lattice.md Section 7.1).

Backward compatible: field is Option with skip_serializing_if, so old handoffs remain valid.

comments.text: Created from theoretical foundations analysis of agent provenance lattice. The full specification is at docs/design/agent-provenance-lattice.md (Section 3.2 details this specific fix). The chain_hash() method in src/handoff.rs:103-122 hashes artifacts.previous_handoff as a file path string, not the SHA-256 of the previous handoff content. Fix: add previous_chain_hash: Option<[u8; 32]> field, populate it from the orchestrator, and include the actual hash bytes in the chain computation.

Clean fixes, pick one: (a) generate the baseline IN CI — coverage.yml on push-to-main runs --write + commits the baseline back, PRs run --check; or (b) build a filtered toolchain dir (symlink all of /opt/homebrew/bin EXCEPT dolt+jj) so they're truly NotFound → tests skip like CI, generate baseline from that; or (c) --ignore-filename-regex the env-dependent integration files (dolt/*, store_dolt, bead_dolt, vcs) so the ratchet covers only deterministic-coverage code. Then re-add .github/workflows/coverage.yml (drafted in the 69fdde branch history). Follow-up to rosary-69fdde.

title: Anthropic direct ModelProvider adapter — /v1/messages via API key (x-api-key), the sanctioned direct path
description:
The direct-API adapter for Anthropic, completing rosary-c79331 slice 3's provider set. Distinct from OpenAiCompatProvider — Anthropic is NOT OpenAI-compatible (its own /v1/messages wire format).

WHY API-KEY, NOT THE SUBSCRIPTION TOKEN (settled by rosary-470270, live-validated 2026-07-17): the Max/Pro subscription OAuth (sk-ant-oat…) is harness-bound by policy + billing — its sanctioned programmatic use is the claude -p / Agent SDK path (which bdr_enrich already uses), NOT raw direct /v1/messages. Direct calls require a real Console/Platform API KEY (sk-ant-api…, pay-as-you-go) with credits. So this adapter authenticates with Credential::ApiKey → the `x-api-key` header (NOT Authorization: Bearer, which is the OAuth/subscription shape). A dispatched multi-tenant use must use an API key per policy, never the operator's subscription seat.

SCOPE (new file src/anthropic_provider.rs, mirrors src/openai_compat.rs structure):
- AnthropicProvider<M: TokenMinter> impl ModelProvider (kind=Anthropic).
- build_body (pure, tested): normalized ChatRequest → Anthropic body { model, max_tokens (required), messages: [{role, content}], system? }. Anthropic splits `system` out of messages (unlike OpenAI) — map a Role::System message to the top-level `system` field, not into `messages`. Merge provider_options["anthropic"] verbatim.
- parse_response (pure, tested): Anthropic response { content: [{type:"text", text}], stop_reason, usage:{input_tokens, output_tokens} } → normalized ChatResponse; concat text blocks; warn-not-error on missing stop_reason.
- generate(): bearer()→ but Anthropic API key goes on `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` headers (add an apply_auth that routes ApiKey→x-api-key vs OAuth→Bearer by credential shape, rosary-1be3b8). POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages.
- Register Anthropic in the model_provider registry alongside the OpenAI-compat one.
- #![allow(dead_code)] until a consumer wires it (matches the slice convention). Keep the file under the 500-line smell floor.

Dispatchable to a local agent: new file, bounded, pure-fn tests, no network. Relates rosary-c79331 (ModelProvider), rosary-470270 (why API key not subscription OAuth), rosary-1be3b8 (header-by-token-shape).
acceptance_criteria: cargo test --bin rsry anthropic_provider:: passes with pure-fn tests: build_body maps a System message to the top-level `system` field (not into messages) + sets max_tokens + merges only the anthropic-namespaced options; parse_response extracts concatenated content[].text + usage and warns on missing stop_reason; a shape test asserts ApiKey routes to x-api-key (not Authorization). clippy --bin rsry clean; file under 500 lines.

title: ModelProvider eval harness — behavioral ground truth from the bead-store history (Greptile pattern), differential vs claude -p
description:
An eval harness that validates a ModelProvider (esp. the new direct-API-key path, rosary-c79331 + the Anthropic adapter bead) produces outputs equivalent-or-better than the incumbent `claude -p` shell-out BEFORE any consumer (bdr_enrich, goal-verifier, scoping) migrates onto it.

GREPTILE'S LESSON (researched 2026-07-17, zenml.io/llmops-database greptile writeup + greptile.com/blog): they tried LLM-as-judge (a 2nd LLM rating quality 1-10) and it was "NEARLY RANDOM" for subjective criteria + added latency — they SCRAPPED it. Their north-star was BEHAVIORAL ground truth: the "address rate" = did a developer actually act on the comment in a later commit (scanned from diffs). Their quality distribution: ~19% good (addressed), ~79% nits (correct-but-not-actionable), ~2% wrong. Takeaway: capture behavioral ground truth, NOT model judgments; the dangerous metric is the small wrong-fraction, not the noise.

ROSARY'S ADVANTAGE — the bead store IS a behavioral ground-truth corpus. Build the golden set from rosary's own history, not synthetic labels:
- bdr_enrich (atom extraction): real ADRs → the atoms/beads they actually produced → which got CLOSED (the address-rate analog). Metric: did the direct-path extraction yield the same dispatchable, eventually-closed beads?
- goal-verifier gate (rosary-d4592f / the independent-verification-gate decade): past dispatch verdicts → did a "complete/pass" bead stay closed or REOPEN? FALSE-PASS rate (a "pass" that reopened) is the load-bearing metric — the 2%-wrong analog, and the dangerous one. Correctness here is behavioral, not judged.
- scoping agent: predicted file scopes vs the files the dispatched agent ACTUALLY touched (git diff) — objective overlap, no judge needed.

DESIGN (avoid Greptile's trap):
- DIFFERENTIAL: run the direct-API-key ModelProvider AND the claude -p baseline on the same golden inputs; gate = direct must match-or-beat baseline on each task's metric before migration. Deterministic where possible (JSON-schema-valid? file-overlap match? bead-reopened?) — do NOT use an LLM to judge subjective quality (Greptile's random-judge finding).
- Report the good/wrong/noise distribution per task + the differential; headline the FALSE-PASS rate for the goal-verifier.
- Keep it offline/replayable (no live dispatch) — replay recorded inputs/outcomes from the store.

Scope: new module (src/eval/ or tests/model_provider_eval.rs) + a golden-set builder that reads the bead-store history. Local-agent-dispatchable. Relates rosary-c79331, rosary-470270, rosary-d4592f, the Anthropic-adapter bead.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes with an offline eval that: (1) builds a golden set from recorded bead-store history (no live dispatch/network), (2) runs the direct ModelProvider vs a recorded claude -p baseline on ≥1 task (atom-extraction or scoping), (3) reports per-task correctness via a DETERMINISTIC/behavioral check (schema-valid, file-overlap, or bead-reopened) — not an LLM judge, (4) emits a good/wrong/noise distribution incl. a false-pass metric, and gates on direct >= baseline.

title: Centralize time handling — 4+ silent timestamp-corruption sites across both backends (now() vs epoch fallbacks)
description:
Surfaced while building LWW sync (rosary-4ebf52). Fixing ONE silent-timestamp bug in src/bead_sqlite/mod.rs revealed the same class in at least four more places, with THREE different wrong answers and no shared owner:

  src/bead_sqlite/mod.rs   parse_datetime -> Utc::now()   [FIXED in rosary-4ebf52]
  src/bead.rs:751          parse_datetime -> unwrap_or_default() = EPOCH 1970
  src/dolt/observations.rs:157  created_at -> unwrap_or_else(|_| Utc::now())   [LIVE]
  src/dolt/query.rs:106,201     updated_at -> unwrap_or_default() = EPOCH      [LIVE]
  src/store_dolt.rs:967         started_at -> unwrap_or_default()              [LIVE]

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the two failure directions are mirror images under last-writer-wins. A now() fallback makes a corrupted row WIN every comparison forever; an epoch fallback makes it LOSE every comparison forever. dolt/query.rs corrupts `updated_at` specifically — the exact LWW key — so a Dolt-read bead with an unparseable timestamp silently never syncs. Neither failure raises anything; both look like successful reads.

There is also NO shared notion of the wire/storage format. Formats currently in play: the store's canonical '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', a T-separated variant, RFC3339 (what `bead export --jsonl` emits), SQL `datetime('now')`, and bare `.parse()`. That mismatch is exactly what produced the rosary-4ebf52 bug — the SQLite reader rejected RFC3339, i.e. it could not read rosary's OWN export contract, and the failure was invisible because it fell through to now().

PROPOSED: a single `src/time.rs` (or similar) owning:
  - parse(s) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>>  accepting all contract shapes, never defaulting
  - format_for_store(dt) -> String     the one canonical write format
  - a single now() seam (also makes time testable/injectable)
Then route every backend reader through it and delete the ad-hoc fallbacks. A grep-gate (like the ADR-0021 drift gate) can keep new `unwrap_or_else(|_| Utc::now())` / `unwrap_or_default()` on timestamps from reappearing.

Relates to ADR-0021 (single-source the field lifecycle) — this is the same disease on the *time* axis: N surfaces each re-deciding how to parse/format/default a field.

title: beads.jsonl export is not deterministic — blocks content-addressing and signing
description:
The contract export can produce different bytes for identical bead state, so BLAKE3(beads.jsonl) is unstable. Two independent causes, both verified in source:

1. Dependency arrays are unordered. src/dolt/deps.rs:157 `SELECT depends_on_id FROM dependencies WHERE issue_id = ?` and deps.rs:122 have no ORDER BY; bead_sqlite/mod.rs:1139 get_dependencies likewise. Row order is engine-dependent, so the deps array can permute between runs.

2. The export does not order beads. src/import.rs:98 export_beads_contract_jsonl iterates the caller-supplied slice and emits one line per bead with no sort, so line order depends on whatever query produced it.

NOT affected (verified, so don't chase these): comments are ordered (ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC in both backends); serde_json is built without preserve_order so Map is a BTreeMap and JSON field order is stable; no wall-clock is stamped into the export (the Utc::now at import.rs:306 is on the import path, not export).

Why it matters, one present cost and one blocking:
- Today: a re-export can produce a spurious git diff for unchanged bead state — noise in every repo that now tracks beads.jsonl as the shared source of truth (the ley-line-open 8d47b2 migration made this the sharing mechanism).
- Blocking: ley-line-open workstream S1 landed a RootSigner (Ed25519 over a BLAKE3 digest). Signing beads.jsonl locally so one key covers every repo's beads requires a canonical export — an unstable hash makes the signature unverifiable for logically identical state.

Fix: add ORDER BY to the dependency selects (depends_on_id ASC, issue_id ASC), and sort beads by id inside export_beads_contract_jsonl rather than trusting the caller's ordering.

Filed from the ley-line-open S1 session; found by reading the export path, not by observing a failure — so a regression test that fails before the fix is the important half.

title: rsry_dispatch agents die silently — worktree created, agent never starts
description:
rsry_dispatch creates a worktree and returns success but the spawned agent process dies immediately without producing any work or errors. The bead stays in 'dispatched' status forever. This has happened consistently across multiple repos (rig, signet, rosary) over multiple sessions.

Symptoms:
- dispatch returns pid + work_dir
- rsry_active shows 0 running agents moments later
- worktree exists but has no new commits
- no error in bead comments
- needs_merge shows bead as 'dead'

rsry_run_once (dry_run=false) may work differently — untested.

Likely causes: agent binary not found in PATH, permission issue, or the claude CLI command construction is wrong. The dispatch command shown in the response uses a specific --allowedTools flag that may be malformed.

comments.text: Confirmed root cause extends to Claude Code sub-agents too (not just rsry_dispatch). Background agents hang on Edit/Bash/Write permission prompts they can't interact with. The agent reads files fine but dies the moment it needs to write. This affects both rsry_dispatch AND the Agent tool with run_in_background=true.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Root cause analysis complete (5-whys). Two critical causes, three contributing factors:

CRITICAL 1: dry_run defaults to true in MCP handler (handlers.rs:108). `.unwrap_or(true)` means any missing/malformatted arg silently neuters dispatch. Tool schema also declares default:true.

CRITICAL 2: println! in reconcile/ corrupts MCP stdio transport. 26+ println! calls write non-JSON to fd 1, which IS the JSON-RPC channel. Client sees garbled output.

MODERATE: backend:None in MCP path (handlers.rs:226 via ..Default::default()). CLI passes cfg.backend; MCP does not. No pipeline persistence.

MINOR: SessionRegistry not populated by reconciler — rsry_active can't see agents spawned by run_once.

MINOR: Targeted dispatch still filtered by needs_refinement(), severity_floor, etc. Silent triage rejection with no error in response.

Fix plan: (1) change unwrap_or(true) to unwrap_or(false), (2) replace all println! with eprintln! in reconcile/, (3) pass cfg.backend, (4) exempt targeted beads from soft triage filters. Full analysis in _agent_log/theoretical-foundations-analyst_2026-03-23_agent_log.md.

title: Fail-loud on missing claude auth; add --bare for explicit headless mode
description:
## Symptom

Dispatched `claude -p` subprocesses die ~84ms in with `Not logged in · Please run /login`. Result: `health: dead` across every recent dispatch (observed: control-room, signet, ley-line-open, ley-line, rig, cloister, rosary itself — ~30 dead sessions in `rsry_active`'s `needs_merge` list). No work done. No clear error surfaced to the dispatcher.

## Root cause

`src/dispatch/providers.rs:102-132` resolves an auth token via `resolve_auth_token(work_dir)`, which checks (in order):
1. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var
2. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var
3. `<work_dir>/.envrc` for `export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...` or `export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...`

When all three fail (common case — user's shell doesn't export these, and the worktree at `~/.rsry/worktrees/<repo>/<bead>/` doesn't have its own `.envrc`), `auth_token` is `None`. **The spawn proceeds anyway.** The subprocess tries to read keychain OAuth credentials it cannot see from a non-interactive context (per Claude Code's headless docs, June 15 2026 default-on `--bare` makes this explicit), fails, exits 84ms in. Caller sees `health: dead` with no actionable error.

## Fix (3 changes, ~20 LOC total)

### 1. Fail-loud when auth resolution fails

`src/dispatch/providers.rs:102` — change `resolve_auth_token` from `-> Option<String>` to `-> Result<String>` (or wrap at the call site). Refuse to spawn when no token resolves:

```rust
let auth_token = resolve_auth_token(work_dir).ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(
    "no auth credential found for spawned claude subprocess. \
     Set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your shell, \
     or add an `.envrc` exporting one at the dispatch repo root. \
     Subprocess cannot read keychain; missing credential causes silent \
     death observed across all recent dispatches."
))?;
cmd.env("CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN", &auth_token);
```

### 2. Pass `--bare` for explicit headless intent

`src/dispatch/providers.rs:105-114` — add `"--bare"` to `base_args` between `prompt` and `"--allowedTools"`. Per [Claude Code headless docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless): `--bare` skips OAuth + keychain reads, becomes the default for `-p` in a future release. Makes our intent explicit and reduces the failure surface — if env var IS set, `--bare` adds nothing; if it ISN'T, claude errors with a cleaner message before death.

### 3. Mirror in `build_command` and add a test

`src/dispatch/providers.rs:144-165` — add `"--bare"` to the same position in `args`. Add a unit test asserting the produced args contain BOTH `-p` and `--bare` in the right order.

## Falsifiability gates

**Gate 1 (silent failure eliminated).** Unset both env vars, remove `.envrc` from the worktree root, attempt `rsry_dispatch` on any open bead.
- ✅ pass: dispatch returns an error before spawning the child process. Error message includes "no auth credential found".
- ❌ fail if the spawn still happens and the child dies silently.

**Gate 2 (working path unbroken).** Set `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to a valid value, dispatch a real bead.
- ✅ pass: spawn succeeds, subprocess does work, stream shows non-zero progress, branch gets commits.
- ❌ fail if dispatch errors when auth IS available.

**Gate 3 (`--bare` semantics).** Inspect the spawned command line via `eprintln!` or strace equivalent.
- ✅ pass: `--bare` appears in the argv before `--allowedTools`.

**Gate 4 (regression — `bdr_enrich.rs` and `verify.rs` parity).** Same changes to those two other `claude -p` call sites (`src/bdr_enrich.rs:54`, `src/verify.rs:313`). Existing tests for those modules stay green.

## Non-goals

- Don't add new credential sources (keep the three: env, env, `.envrc`).
- Don't try to detect "logged in interactively but spawn can't see it" — that's the bug we're surfacing, not solving.
- Don't pre-flight a `claude --version` check; the spawn IS the check.

## Why this matters more than the auth bug itself

Every dead session in the past month of dispatches is wasted compute + opaque debugging. The fix is small. The discipline shift is "spawn should refuse rather than spawn-and-pray." Worth landing before next dispatch wave.

comments.text:
EMPIRICAL ROOT-CAUSE (2026-06-22, CLI 2.1.186). Ran a controlled 3-cell spike of `claude -p 'reply SPIKE_OK' --output-format json --allowedTools ''`:

| cell | env | PTY | result |
|------|-----|-----|--------|
| A | full inherited (nested-CC: CLAUDECODE=1, CHILD_SESSION=1) | no | ✅ SPIKE_OK, exit 0 |
| B | clean (`env -i HOME PATH`) | no | ❌ "Not logged in", exit 1 |
| C | clean (`env -i HOME PATH`) | **yes** (real PTY via `script -q /dev/null`) | ❌ "Not logged in", exit 1 |

Conclusion: the failure is **credential/env propagation, NOT TTY/PTY**. PTY made zero difference (C == B). The differentiator is whether the spawned process's env carries usable creds. So:
- Context #3 (nested in claude-code): already works — inherits creds.
- Context #2 (rig OTP daemon / launchd, clean env): fails — this is the actual broken path.

Web corroboration: multica#3728 ("Not logged in through daemon, works in my shell with same env" — daemons filter CLAUDE_CODE_*/ANTHROPIC_* out of the subprocess); anthropics/claude-code#34917 (tokens copied from interactive sessions are session-bound → "Not logged in" headless).

FIX (small, not the tmux epic): mint a long-lived token with `claude setup-token` (1yr OAuth), inject as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN into the spawned env in ALL launch contexts (rig→rosary AND rosary→claude). Audit `resolve_auth_token()` — it may be scraping a session-bound token that fails headless. NB: same mechanism (env injection of ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/AUTH_TOKEN) is what a Qwen/Kimi/local model-swap needs.

comments.text:
FIX IN PROGRESS — commit 87ff142 on branch `worktree-tmux-substrate` (isolated worktree, branched fresh from origin/main e4134ba so it doesn't collide with the root-worktree agent).

What landed (TDD, 4 new unit tests, full suite 1152+21+1+4 green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean):
- New pure resolver `resolve_launch_env_from(getenv, envrc_contents)` in dispatch/providers.rs — forwards CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL passthrough (the Qwen/Kimi/local model-swap hook). Priority env > .envrc > global config. Tests cover: no-creds signal, OAuth forward, model-gateway passthrough, .envrc fallback.
- Impure wrapper `resolve_launch_env(work_dir)` (env + .envrc collection + global-config fallback).
- Wired into: main ClaudeProvider spawn (was best-effort silent → now injects token+endpoint and WARNS loudly on no-creds); verify.rs and bdr_enrich.rs (these had ZERO auth injection before — guaranteed-broken in any clean-env context).

Keychain-aware design: no-creds is a WARNING not a hard fail, because the spike showed interactive/nested-CC contexts auth via Keychain with no env token — hard-failing would regress those.

REMAINING (follow-up, intentionally out of this commit to bound blast radius):
1. ACP provider (providers.rs:368) + detached spawn (dispatch/mod.rs:749) still call resolve_auth_token (single-token, not structured env). Migrate them too.
2. True dispatch-level fail-loud: parse the stream-json result for "Not logged in" and mark the dispatch failed (vs warn-and-spawn). Bigger change.
3. OPERATOR ACTION (the other half — can't be done in code): run `claude setup-token` to mint a non-session-bound 1yr token, set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in rig's EnvironmentFile / launchd plist so the daemon→rosary→claude chain carries it. A session-bound token (anthropics/claude-code#34917) won't work headless.

Not closing — needs #3 to verify end-to-end green in the rig context, plus review.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
UPDATE — commit 7f45632 (branch worktree-tmux-substrate). Found the critical gap: MCP `rsry_dispatch` → tool_dispatch → `spawn_detached` (dispatch/mod.rs), NOT ClaudeProvider::spawn_agent. spawn_detached still used the single-token resolve_auth_token, so the *primary nested-claude-code path* was uncovered by the first commit. Now wired to resolve_launch_env (token + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL passthrough + loud no-creds warning).

EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION (live Max auth, CLI 2.1.186, nested-CC context):
- Added 2 #[ignore]d e2e tests exercising the REAL spawn paths; both PASS (is_error:false, no "Not logged in"):
  - claude_spawn_agent_end_to_end_authenticates_and_completes (reconciler path)

title: Enforce mechanical bead-closure on agent shutdown — "tools deterministic, agents not"
description:
## User framing (2026-05-19)

> "I need a way to like enforce bead closing before agent shutdown or some shi, and this goes back to the like 'mechanical tool calling' vs 'agent calling' as the determinism is possible with tools today."

The recurring failure mode: an agent finishes work, commits, makes a PR — but never **closes the bead**. State drifts. `rsry_active` shows stale `in_progress`. Operators have to manually reconcile.

**Why this is hard to fix with agent judgment alone:**
Agents forget to call `rsry_bead_close` for the same reasons humans forget to file expenses — it's the LAST step, no follow-up consequence catches them. Asking "remember to close" in the system prompt isn't deterministic. A **tool-level enforcement** is.

## The "mechanical vs agent" insight

| Layer | Determinism | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| **Tool calls** (MCP, CLI) | Deterministic — tool either executes or errors | Pre-conditions, post-conditions, gating |
| **Agent calling** (judgment, intent) | Non-deterministic — agent decides | Pattern-matching, summarization, creativity |

The bead-closure problem is properly a TOOL-level concern. It should be enforced by the dispatch substrate, not by hoping the agent remembers.

## Acceptance

Bead lifecycle MUST include a closure step that the agent CANNOT skip. Concretely:

1. **At dispatch time**, the bead state transitions to `Dispatched` and a "completion contract" is registered (what's required for closure — test green, PR merged, or explicit `--force`).
2. **At process-exit time**, the dispatch substrate checks: is the bead still `Dispatched` or `InProgress`? If yes, refuse to mark the dispatch as Completed; instead transition to `Deadletter` with a `closure_missing` reason.
3. **Operator visibility**: `rsry_active` surfaces `closure_missing` beads with explicit "agent exited without closing" status. No silent staleness.
4. **Bypass path**: explicit `rsry bead close <id> --no-test` or `--force` for legitimate non-impl beads (docs, design); audit log records the bypass.

## Related to

- `rosary-a761df` (Agent-native state-machine substrate) — closure is one state transition in the bigger machine
- `rosary-75555d` (Tmux spawn substrate) — tmux pane exit is the natural "agent done" signal; closure check fires on pane-close
- `rosary-792ed6` (Personal/root rosary security) — closure attestation could be signed by signet for provenance
- `rosary-c3034b` (Dispatch dead-letter) — closely related; this bead extends the dead-letter trigger condition
- `rosary-ba011e` (34 dead worktrees) — the EXISTING evidence of this failure mode

## Why now

User noticed: "the backlog is relevant to all of this as some of it doesn't belong in LLO." The closure problem isn't unique to one repo; it spans the whole agent-dispatch substrate. Belongs at rosary's substrate layer.

## Time-box

S — IF the tmux substrate is in place, this is a ~½ day addition to the pane-exit handler.
M — without tmux, ~1 day to add lifecycle hooks at process exit.

## Files

- `src/dispatch/sweep.rs` — already does orphan-dispatch detection; extend
- `src/dispatch/mod.rs` — add closure-contract registration at dispatch time
- `src/bead.rs` — `BeadState::Deadletter { reason: ClosureMissing | ... }` variant detail
- `src/main.rs` — `rsry bead close --force` CLI flag handling

title: BDR decompose: schema-driven with success criteria, cross-repo routing, dependency parsing
description:
## Problem
rsry_decompose does naive markdown section → bead mapping. Can't handle:
- Cross-repo ADRs (sheaf cache → ley-line, onboarding → rosary, integration → mache)
- Inter-document dependencies (ADR-B depends on ADR-A)
- Spec vs actionable work distinction
- Success criteria generation
- Duplicate detection against existing beads

## Requirements
1. Parse dependency graph between ADRs (frontmatter: Depends on, Relates to)
2. Route beads to correct repo based on file/crate references in the ADR
3. Distinguish specification sections (algorithm pseudocode, data structures) from actionable work
4. Generate verifiable success criteria per bead (not just "done")
5. Deduplicate against existing beads (rsry_bead_search before creating)
6. Schema-driven output: repo, depends_on, success_criteria, acceptance_test fields
7. Support mache AST parsing for structural validation of decomposition

## Immediate driver
4+ ADRs (sheaf-cache, merkle-sheaf-sync, structural-onboarding, integration-surface, product-tiers) need decomposition and the current tool produces garbage on them.

comments.text:
Enrichment pipeline clarification:

1. **mache** (deterministic, structural): resolve atom references to actual files via find_definition, search, get_communities. mache has community support + LSP support (ley-line inserts into its DB). This is the code-reader that sets file scopes.

2. **haiku** (cheap LLM, validation): validate + enrich mache's structural data against the BDR atoms. Questions haiku answers:
   - Are the resolved files correct for this atom?
   - Is this actually one bead or should it be split?
   - Is this a dupe of an existing bead? (semantic comparison)
   - Does the decomposition make sense given the code structure?

3. **Pre-flight**: before decompose runs, verify mache is indexed for the target repo, rsry is accessible, .beads/ exists, Dolt is running. Without pre-flight, the enrichment pipeline can't run.

mache = source of truth. haiku = reviewer. BDR parse = raw extraction. The pipeline: parse → mache resolve → haiku validate → enriched BeadSpecs.

Phase 1 (this PR): frontmatter parsing, success criteria, cross-repo routing, target_repo, depends_on. No mache/haiku yet.
Phase 2: mache file resolution + haiku validation pass.
Phase 3: pre-flight checks.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
## Architecture Analysis: BDR Enrichment Pipeline (ADR-0007)

Produced full architecture at `docs/adr/0007-bdr-enrichment-pipeline.md`.

### Key Design Decisions

1. **4-stage pipeline**: Symbol Resolution (mache) -> Dedup Check (sqlite-vec + epic.rs) -> LLM Validation (haiku) -> Materialization (Dolt). Each stage has explicit fallback behavior.

2. **Dedup formalization**: Composite score = max(token_jaccard, embedding_cosine * 0.9, structural_overlap * 0.7). Three-tier decision: auto-dedup (>0.85), flag-for-review (0.60-0.85), allow (<0.60). Two beads are "the same work" iff semantic equivalence OR scope subsumption OR structural identity.

3. **Cross-repo routing**: Symbol-based routing via mache resolution + explicit frontmatter routing. Multiple mache instances (one per repo, Option B) for multi-repo enrichment.

4. **Dependency boundary**: rosary accesses embeddings through mache MCP, NOT direct ley-line dependency. This respects the AGPL/closed-source boundary. New mache tool `mache_embedding_similarity` needed.

5. **Pre-flight**: 3 required checks (Dolt, ADR parseable, repo in config) + 3 optional (mache, embeddings, haiku). Graceful degradation at each stage.

### Theoretical Issues Identified

- Jaccard is insufficient for paraphrase detection (two beads saying the same thing differently)
- The composite dedup score violates triangle inequality -- acceptable for threshold classification but NOT for clustering
- sqlite-vec 384D MiniLM is sufficient for paraphrase detection but cannot capture structural relationships -- this is why we need the structural overlap signal as a separate feature
- O(n^2) pairwise dedup will bottleneck at ~1000 beads per repo; sqlite-vec ANN handles embedding search but token Jaccard does not scale

### Implementation Beads Created

5 phases decomposed into separate beads with file scopes verified against codebase structure. See child beads.

title: Cross-repo deps with severity: blocking thresholds for reconciliation
description:
## Problem
Cross-repo dependencies today are binary (blocked or not). But a P0 bug filed in repo A that blocks a feature in repo B should trigger reconciliation — the dependency severity determines whether it's a hard block, a soft warning, or just informational.

## Proposal
- Dependencies carry severity/priority from the blocking bead
- A bug (high severity) dependency blocks dispatch of the dependent bead
- A task (lower severity) dependency may allow dispatch with a warning
- Reconciler checks dependency severity during triage, not just existence
- This enables: "a bug filed means we can reconcile" — filing a blocking bug in one repo triggers re-triage in dependent repos

title: Cross-repo monorepo aspiration — cloister, notme, etc. but moving is a PITA
description:
## User framing (2026-05-19, end of long session)

> "It's like I need a monorepo, but all of the repos that would go in (cloister, notme, etc) would be a real PITA to move."

The recurring friction: rosary, cloister, notme, ley-line-open, signet, mache, crumb, rig, witchcraft (sidecar) all interact. Beads link across them. Changes in one ripple to others (e.g. LLO's `text_search` op required rosary to wire up `leyline-chat-embed`). Today this is ~12 repos with bespoke per-repo CI, per-repo bead stores, per-repo task config.

## What a monorepo would solve

| Pain today | Monorepo equivalent |
|---|---|
| 12 sets of `.beads/dolt/` to keep in sync; cross-repo deps need LinkageStore | One `.beads/dolt/` for everything; deps are local |
| Each repo has separate `Taskfile.yml`, separate CI workflows, separate version cadence | Shared CI, shared task runner, atomic version bumps |
| Refactor that touches signet+cloister+rosary needs 3 PRs across 3 repos with merge ordering | One PR, atomic landing |
| `task install` per-repo; reinstall after every cross-repo change | One install, everything updated together |
| `rosary-a7bfdc` (cross-tool config substrate) becomes trivial | Config substrate is just one file |

## What it doesn't solve

- Public/private boundary (`rosary-public_private_repos` memory): some repos are private (ley-line, cloister, notme); a monorepo would force all-public or all-private. Or sub-projects with selective visibility.
- Migration cost: rewriting git history across 12 repos to fold into one is technically possible (`git filter-repo`, `git subtree`) but operationally painful — every open PR breaks, every external link to a commit SHA dies.

## The honest trade-off

A monorepo would solve a real ergonomic pain but the migration cost is genuinely high. **The user is correctly torn.** The pragmatic middle paths:

1. **Stay multi-repo, invest in cross-repo tooling.** Rosary's scope abstraction (just shipped) is part of this. Add: shared CI workflows via reusable workflows. Shared config substrate (`rosary-a7bfdc`). Cross-repo PR groups (a la stacked PR tooling).

2. **Selective monorepo merge for the tightest-coupled subset.** rosary + ley-line-open + cloister might be tight enough to merge while signet/notme stay separate. Smaller migration cost; partial win.

3. **Federated monorepo via cloister.** cloister already hosts MCP servers behind one HTTPS face; could host bead stores too. Each "sub-repo" becomes a cloister bundle with its own visibility. Bigger architecture; might be the right end state for `rosary-792ed6` (Personal/root rosary).

## Recommendation (filed, not acted on)

Don't migrate today. Instead, **invest in cross-repo tooling** so the multi-repo pain decreases without the migration cost:

- Cross-repo bead_link (already done — `rosary-98ee93` closed)
- Hierarchical config substrate (`rosary-a7bfdc`)
- Cross-repo CI via reusable workflows
- Stacked-PR tooling

Re-evaluate monorepo when one of these is clearly true:
- A specific refactor genuinely requires atomic cross-repo landing 3+ times in a month
- Migration cost is amortized (tooling exists to make it cheap)
- The public/private boundary is no longer load-bearing

## Time-box

XL — DON'T DO IT NOW. This bead is to track the consideration so it doesn't repeatedly resurface as "we should just monorepo." Re-evaluate per the conditions above.

## Cross-link

- `rosary-792ed6` (Personal/root rosary) — federation model could obviate monorepo need
- `rosary-a7bfdc` (Cross-tool config substrate) — partial pain reliever
- [[project-public-private-repos]] (memory) — the visibility constraint

## Files

(no implementation; tracking-only bead)

title: Reconciler multi-tenant scoping bug: all_user_repos() returns ALL users
description:
Surfaced during Notion research session (2026-03-31). The reconciler's `all_user_repos()` function returns repos for ALL users, not scoped to the current tenant. In a multi-tenant WfP world this is a critical isolation violation.

Needs investigation:
- Where is `all_user_repos()` called?
- What data does it access? (KV? D1? DO state?)
- Is this only a problem in the WfP context or also single-tenant?
- Fix: scope all repo queries to the authenticated user/tenant ID

comments.text:
INVESTIGATION (2026-06-21): this is STALE — the described leak was already fixed before the bead was filed.

EVIDENCE:
- Scoping gate landed 2026-03-25 in commit 89583e6 (PR #123 "scope remote repo loading to user_id"). This bead was filed 2026-03-31 — 6 days AFTER the fix, during a Notion research session that didn't know #123 had shipped.
- Data layer is correctly scoped: list_user_repos(user_id) filters `WHERE user_id = ?` in BOTH backends (src/store_sqlite.rs:653, src/store_dolt.rs:787). Isolation is TESTED at src/store_sqlite.rs:1399-1430 (user-2 gets empty list, user-1 sees only its own).
- The actual multi-tenant entry point (MCP handler) is scoped: src/serve/handlers.rs:2407 calls list_user_repos(user_id), not the all-users variant.
- all_user_repos() has only 2 non-test callers, both intentional: reconcile/mod.rs:358 (local-mode fallback, gated behind `match config.user_id` — None => all-local = single user's own repos) and migrate.rs:272 (backend->backend migration, legitimately copies all).

RESIDUAL (not a P0, not a leak today): ReconcileConfig.user_id (reconcile/mod.rs:64) defaults to None and is never set to Some — no setter, no caller wires it. So the reconciler's *scoped* branch is currently dead code and it always takes the all_user_repos() local path. This is NOT an isolation violation because there is no multi-tenant reconciler deployment; the reconciler is single-tenant/local where all-local == own repos. It becomes a gap ONLY if a hosted multi-tenant reconciler is ever run, at which point the missing work is "plumb authenticated user_id into ReconcileConfig."

RECOMMENDATION: close as already-fixed (data + MCP layer scoped + tested via #123). Move the reconciler-user_id-wiring residual to the multi-tenant epic rosary-39fbb2 as a P2/P3 design item, NOT a P0 bug. No code change warranted on the reported issue.

title: Beads store must survive git stash pop / branch switch on a shared checkout
description:
The live beads store gets reverted/corrupted by ordinary git operations, causing bead loss. Concrete incident (2026-07-22, LLO session): `git stash pop` applied a DIFFERENT branch's stashed `.beads/` state (a "beads.db working state" stash), creating a DU conflict on `.beads/beads.db`; combined with branch switches on the shared `~/github`↔`~/remotes` checkout (one physical tree via two symlinked aliases), the live store reverted, losing 82 beads. Manually recovered (superset re-export, integrity ok, original 265 untouched), but this is a recurring footgun — prior memory notes it caused ~3× beads.db loss.

The store must be resilient to: (1) `git stash`/`git stash pop` touching `.beads/` (a stash from one branch must never overwrite another branch's live store), (2) branch switches reverting `.beads/` working-tree files on the shared checkout, (3) `git rm --cached`/checkout on `.beads/` not destroying live data.

The user reports moving rosary to a NEW store backend that should help — this bead is to VERIFY that fixes it and harden the rest. Candidate hardening: keep the live store entirely OUTSIDE the git working tree (so no git op can touch it — e.g. a per-machine store dir keyed by repo identity, not `.beads/` under the worktree), with the git-tracked `beads.jsonl` as a pure export/import boundary; make import idempotent + superset-preserving (never regress ids); and/or a pre-stash/pre-checkout guard that refuses to stash/revert `.beads/`.

Close condition: a falsifier — create N beads, run `git stash -u && git checkout <other-branch> && git checkout - && git stash pop` (and a cross-branch stash-pop that carries a stale `.beads/`), then assert all N beads still resolve by id with 0 regressions. The new-store backend passes this where the old one lost data.

title: Adversarial review gate: spawn reviewer agent on each changeset, loop until consensus
description:
## Problem

Changes ship without adversarial review. The staging-agent persona exists but isn't invoked systematically during development. Bugs slip through (pipeline didn't progress, enable produced "unnamed", list_beads crashed at 686K).

## Design

After each logical code change (pre-commit), spawn a reviewer agent that:
1. Reads the diff
2. Checks against Golden Rules
3. Tests adversarial scenarios (what if input is empty? null? huge? "."?)
4. Reports findings
5. Developer fixes or justifies
6. Loop until reviewer approves

This is the staging-agent pipeline phase, but applied to the development session itself.

## Implementation options

A) Claude Code hook (PostToolUse:Edit) — auto-spawn reviewer after file edits
B) Pre-commit hook — reviewer runs before commit (like cargo clippy but semantic)
C) Manual invocation — `/review` skill that spawns the adversarial agent
D) Task decomposition — each changeset gets a review task, tracked in session

Option C is simplest to start. Option A is the automation goal.

## Tracks

- rosary-dc8b05 (5-whys gate — related pre-implementation review)
- rosary-fb78a4 (test harness — the tests ARE the adversarial check, codified)

title: Systematize Rosary trusted kernel before broader agent fanout
description:
Goal: make Rosary safe enough to use as the source of truth for multi-agent work across Claude Code and Codex without relying on convention or LLM obedience.

Problem statement:
Rosary has real value and is now used for task management, but its ambition is close to exceeding the guarantees enforced by the code. The risky zone is dispatch/runtime truth: CLI, MCP, daemon, installed binary, provider abstraction, close conditions, PR/review state, and task verification can drift. When those drift, agents can appear productive while bypassing the actual system of record.

Trusted-kernel framing:
1. Bead spec is durable input.
2. Close condition is mandatory for implementation work.
3. Dispatch is provider-neutral and does not shell out on the native path.
4. Provider sessions emit typed events.
5. Runtime state is derived from event/store truth, not stale process memory or tool descriptions.
6. `task check` is the canonical verification gate.
7. Fake-provider harness proves the state machine without live AI.
8. Claude Code and Codex integrations are adapters over the same contract.

Deliverable:
A small set of implementation beads, each with explicit close conditions, that harden the trusted kernel before broader fanout/dogfooding.

Suggested decomposition:
- Runtime truth: daemon/tool schema/build hash/install drift detection and repair.
- Verification truth: enforce `task check` as the one composed gate everywhere.
- Dispatch truth: dispatch refuses implementation beads without close conditions.
- Provider truth: fake native provider harness covers session/event/grant behavior.
- Codex/Claude parity: provider feature matrix with tests around the shared contract.
- Backlog truth: define ready/dispatchable semantics so 600+ ready beads do not mean "safe to fan out".

Claude Code handoff instruction:
Do not start by adding features. First inspect existing beads and PRs, then create or reuse child beads under decade `trusted-kernel`, thread `trusted-kernel/dispatch-determinism`. Every implementation bead must include a runnable close condition such as `task check`, a focused `cargo test ...`, or both.

title: Generic rosary: decouple bead identity from repo_path (scope abstraction)
description:
## Why now

Recurring friction this week:

- `rosary-98ee93`: bead_link rejects cross-repo deps because `repo_path` is the lookup key
- substrate-IDL multi-repo premise needs L9 (cloister) → L8 (signet) links
- Future composition needs (zen PR ingestion, cloister-hosted MCP sources) want bead identity that isn't tied to a local git checkout

## The change

`repo_path: &str` → `scope: ScopeId`, where `ScopeId` is:
- `Repo(name)` for current model (resolved to local path via config)
- `External(uri)` for non-repo sources (zen inbox, cloister bundle, ad-hoc)

title: Mechanical merge gate: all PR review comments resolved or replied
description:
## Pattern

Sibling to `rosary-99f891` (doc-drift validator) and `rosary-cdd522` (Guardrail trait substrate). Same idea: **pre-merge invariants the substrate can check without judgment**.

## This gate

Block bead → `done` (or PR → merge) until every review comment thread on the bead's PR is either:
- marked resolved on GitHub, OR
- has a reply from the bead's author that the reviewer hasn't pushed back on

## Why it matters

We routinely hit "agent committed fix, PR has unresolved comments, bead closes anyway." The 34 needs_merge beads in `rsry_active` include several where reviewer said "Needs changes" but the worker died and the bead never advanced. A mechanical check catches this class.

## Implementation sketch

- Verify-tier plugin (per `rosary-541568` Assay pattern): `gates-review-comments`
- Query: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` + GraphQL `reviewThreads.isResolved`
- Pass when: zero unresolved threads, OR all unresolved threads have a newer comment from the bead's author
- Hook: `pipeline.verify`

## Related

- Blocks-on-pattern: `rosary-cdd522` (Guardrail trait — the substrate)
- Sibling gate: `rosary-99f891` (doc-drift)
- Surface that motivates: `rosary-ba011e` (34 dead worktrees, several with unresolved review feedback)

title: Plugin kind="mcp" outbound runtime — call other MCP servers as bead sources / verify gates
description:
## Status quo

`src/plugin.rs` declares the plugin kind axis: `hook | mcp | dispatch | state_sink`. Only `hook` is wired. The `mcp` variant — outbound MCP client where rosary calls into another MCP server — is **declared but no runtime**.

## What it unlocks

Rosary becomes a substrate that composes with other MCP-speaking tools without bespoke integration:

1. **Zen as PR ingestion source** — call `zen_inbox` periodically, create beads for review-needed PRs
2. **Cloister-hosted tools** — cloister hosts MCP servers behind one HTTPS face; rosary can consume any of them
3. **Other agents' MCP outputs** — anything that speaks MCP becomes a potential source / gate / sink

## Acceptance

- `~/.rsry/plugins/foo.toml` with `kind = "mcp"` registers a remote MCP server (stdio command or HTTP URL)
- Pipeline hooks can call any tool on the registered server
- Failures don't crash reconciler (one bad MCP source ≠ whole system down)
- Optional: a `pipeline.source` hook variant that periodically pulls candidates → beads

## Composes with

- Zen integration bead (filed separately)
- `rosary-b5da2f` (scope abstraction — needed once external sources create beads)
- Cloister's substrate-portability story (ADR-0009 on cloister side)

title: Zen MCP integration: register as outbound source, ingest zen_inbox PRs as beads
description:
## Motivation

`https://github.com/mgreau/zen` exposes 9 MCP tools (zen_inbox, zen_pr_details, zen_pr_files, zen_worktree_list, zen_agent_status, zen_who_am_i, zen_config_repos, zen_review, zen_review_resume). Installed locally via `claude mcp add --scope user zen -- zen mcp serve` on 2026-05-18.

Zen handles "what PR needs human review attention." Rosary handles "dispatch a reviewer and track the result." Composed: zen as upstream source, rosary as downstream orchestrator.

## Blocked by

Filed-but-unwired outbound `kind = "mcp"` plugin runtime (separate bead).

## Acceptance

1. `~/.rsry/plugins/zen.toml` registers zen as an MCP source via `kind = "mcp"`
2. Reconciler periodically calls `zen_inbox`, dedups against existing beads, creates new beads for PRs not yet tracked
3. New beads carry `ProvenanceRef::GitHubPR { repo, number }` (requires new variant in bdr/provenance.rs)
4. Bead routes to a `code-reviewer` / `pr-review` agent pipeline
5. On close: optionally call zen's `zen_review` to open the prepared worktree

## Open question

Should rosary's reviewer-agent open the zen-prepared worktree (zen does this well) or its own? Likely zen's, with rosary tracking the dispatch state.

title: Unify signing/attestation on leyline-sign (dsse.rs sha256+ed25519 → LLO CMS/cert/attestation)
description: The signing-unification the hashing centralization pairs with (raised alongside rosary-bf9cbf). dsse.rs hand-rolls DSSE/in-toto attestation with sha2::Sha256 subject digests + keyids + an ed25519 stack. LLO ships leyline-sign (CMS signing, cert chains, sha256 fingerprints, attestation claims — sign/src/cms.rs, cert_chain.rs). Centralize rosary's bespoke signing/attestation onto leyline-sign so it's one signing boundary, not a reinvented one — mirroring how bf8121 put content-hashing on leyline-core. NOTE: DSSE subject digests stay sha256 by external spec; the unification is about using LLO's signing/attestation primitives, not changing the wire algorithm. Candidate #4 from the rosary-41e98b hashing audit. Independent of the content-address foundation (own boundary); do after the hashing thread lands.

comments.text: Investigated → WON'T DO (decision, not code). dsse.rs is DSSE/in-toto (payloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json, PAE 'DSSEv1', in-toto Statement/v1, ed25519 over PAE, keyid=hex(sha256(pubkey))). leyline-sign is CMS/PKCS#7 (RFC 5652, X.509 cert chains, signer identifiers). These are DIFFERENT signing formats for DIFFERENT purposes: DSSE = supply-chain attestation (SLSA/sigstore interop); CMS = X.509 cert-chain/trust-root signing. Swapping DSSE→CMS would BREAK rosary's in-toto attestation interop. And there's nothing to centralize at the primitive level: rosary and leyline-sign BOTH use ed25519-dalek + sha2 directly — the crypto is already shared; only the (correctly-different) envelope format differs. So unlike the hashing centralization (blake3→leyline-core, a true dedup), signing has no valid centralization here. Keep DSSE. If a future need arises for CMS/cert-chain signing (e.g. signet trust-root integration), THAT would use leyline-sign — a new capability, not a swap of the DSSE path.

title: rsry_active: rename `needs_merge` — dead sessions are not "needing merge"
description:
## What's wrong

`rsry_active` returns a `needs_merge` array. Looking at it today on a working machine, ~30 entries are listed there across control-room, signet, rosary, ley-line, rig, cloister, ley-line-open. **Every single one has `health: "dead"` with `last_activity: null` and `last_comment: null`.** These sessions died at startup (e.g. our 2026-05-16 LLO dispatches died 84ms in with `Not logged in`). They do not need a merge — they need to be discarded.

A human reading "needs_merge" reasonably infers "agents that finished work and want their changes pulled in." The actual semantic is closer to "workspaces that exist on disk and haven't been cleaned up." That's a different concept and should have a different name.

## Why this matters

When a new agent looks at `rsry_active` to triage state, the `needs_merge` count gives a wildly inflated picture of in-flight work. We have zero pending merges right now; we have ~30 dead worktrees on disk. The UX bug is conflating those two.

## Fix

Two paths, pick one:

### Option A — split the field

Return two arrays in `rsry_active`:
- `needs_merge`: only sessions with `health` ∈ {`completed`, `running`} AND `last_activity != null` AND uncommitted work / unmerged branch
- `dead_workspaces`: sessions with `health: dead` (eligible for janitor cleanup)

Most caller code paths only care about one or the other; this makes the intent explicit.

### Option B — rename + filter

Rename `needs_merge` → `workspaces`, add a `health_filter` parameter (defaults to "all", can be "alive", "dead"). Callers that wanted the "merge me" semantic pass `health_filter=alive` and check the per-entry `health` field themselves.

I'd prefer (A) — separation of concerns. Two arrays, no parameter.

## Falsifiability

- ✅ pass: after fix, `rsry_active` on the current machine returns 0 entries in `needs_merge` and ~30 in `dead_workspaces` (or whatever the new shape is). Counts agree with the actual on-disk state.
- ❌ fail if dead-health sessions still appear in the merge-shaped slot.

## Scope

Touches `rsry_active` handler (`src/serve/`) + the response struct + the tool schema description. Caller code (`mache` and friends) doesn't need updates if they were already filtering by `health` field; if not, this is a clean break worth doing.

## Why parallel-safe with `rosary-b1495c`

Different files. `b1495c` touches `src/dispatch/providers.rs` + `src/bdr_enrich.rs` + `src/verify.rs`. This bead touches `src/serve/`-side response shaping. No overlap.

title: Janitor: retroactive cleanup of confirmed-dead worktrees (~30 stale entries)
description:
## Symptom

`rsry_active` currently returns ~30 entries with `health: "dead"` across control-room, signet, rosary, ley-line, rig, cloister, ley-line-open. All have `last_activity: null` and `last_comment: null` — they died at startup and never produced any work. The worktrees still exist on disk at `~/.rsry/worktrees/<repo>/<bead-id>/`. Branches exist on those worktrees pointing at main.

These are not active work. They are orphan worktrees from failed dispatches — most caused by the auth bug ([[rosary-b1495c]]).

## Why this is its own bead

Two separate concerns:
- [[rosary-b1495c]] fixes the cause of NEW orphans going forward (fail-loud on missing auth + `--bare`)
- This bead cleans up the EXISTING orphan inventory and adds a janitor primitive to do it on a schedule

Without this, every `rsry_active` call drowns the real state in dead history.

## Scope

Two pieces:

### 1. Manual one-shot cleanup (immediate)

Walk `~/.rsry/worktrees/`. For each worktree:
- Read `.rsry-stream.jsonl` (single line for a dead session)
- If only line is a `result` event with `is_error: true` AND `last_activity` (via session.rs metadata) is null AND the worktree has no uncommitted changes (no work to preserve): delete the worktree via `git worktree remove`, delete the branch, mark the session row archived in the dolt store.

Conservative: only auto-clean confirmed-dead-with-no-work cases. Anything ambiguous (e.g. session that started but didn't comment) gets reported for human review, not auto-deleted.

### 2. `rsry_janitor` MCP tool

A new tool callable from MCP that runs the above cleanup logic on demand and returns:
```json
{
  "scanned": N,
  "cleaned": M,
  "skipped_ambiguous": K,
  "skipped_with_uncommitted_work": L,
  "errors": [...]
}
```

Cron-friendly: a daily run keeps the inventory honest.

## Falsifiability

- **Gate 1**: after running the manual cleanup, `rsry_active`'s dead-or-needs_merge count goes from ~30 to 0 (or to the count of genuine in-progress sessions).
- **Gate 2**: re-running the janitor a second time on the same state is a no-op (idempotency).
- **Gate 3**: drop a deliberately-stale `.rsry-stream.jsonl` with an `is_error: false` `result` event (simulating a successful but un-merged session). Janitor must NOT delete it; instead report it under `skipped_with_uncommitted_work`.
- **Gate 4**: drop a fake worktree with an actual uncommitted change. Janitor must NOT delete; reports under `skipped_with_uncommitted_work`.

## Non-goals

- Don't auto-clean sessions that committed work, even if dead — those might be valuable artifacts the user wants to recover.
- Don't touch the dolt store schema for sessions; just add an archive flag if needed.
- Don't try to be smart about "maybe alive" — if `health != "dead"`, leave alone.

## Why parallel-safe with [[rosary-b1495c]] and [[rosary needs_merge rename]]

Different files. `b1495c` touches dispatch/providers. The rename bead touches serve/. This touches janitor/cleanup logic + a new tool registration. Three independent surfaces.

title: rsry serve processes should be distinguishable (session ID, repo, transport in process name)
description:
## Problem

`ps aux | grep rsry` shows identical lines for every stdio session:
```
rsry serve --transport stdio
rsry serve --transport stdio
rsry serve --transport http --port 8383
```

No way to tell which Claude Code session owns which rsry process. Can't selectively kill, can't debug, can't relate to conversation context.

## Proposal

Add identifying info to the process title or argv:
- `rsry serve --transport stdio --session <short-id>` (or use prctl/setproctitle)
- Include repo context if available (which project's .mcp.json spawned it)
- The HTTP daemon could show `rsry serve --transport http --port 8383 [daemon]`

This also relates to observability — if rsry is the daemon pattern (OTP-style), its child processes need identity.

## Context

Observed 2 stdio + 1 HTTP process running. Both stdio sessions were legit (attached to live claude PIDs) but indistinguishable without tracing parent PIDs manually.

title: 5-whys: rsry daemon architecture — channels, plugins, OTP pattern alignment
description:
## Problem

Before building more features (SQLite migration, channels, session continuity), we need to answer foundational questions about rsry's daemon architecture. The pattern is emerging but not explicitly designed:

- rsry HTTP daemon runs persistently (PID stays alive across sessions)
- stdio sessions are ephemeral per-conversation
- Claude Code plugins may provide a channel mechanism for agent↔rosary communication
- Conductor in rig uses OTP-style supervision — is rsry converging on the same pattern?

## 5-Whys to answer

1. **What is rsry's process model?** — daemon + ephemeral workers? OTP supervisor tree?
2. **How do agents communicate back to rsry?** — currently: MCP tool calls only. What about long-running status, heartbeats, intermediate results?
3. **What are "channels" in this context?** — Claude plugins? WebSocket subscriptions? Dolt branch events? ley-line reactive store?
4. **How does this relate to conductor's OTP?** — is rsry the local supervisor and conductor the remote one? Or are they the same thing at different scales?
5. **What's the session lifecycle?** — stdio sessions live/die with conversations. HTTP daemon survives. What state belongs where?

## Why this blocks SQLite migration

It doesn't directly block — but understanding the daemon model informs WHERE state lives (process memory vs SQLite vs Dolt) and HOW state flows (polling vs channels vs reactive). Doing SQLite first is fine, but this thinking should happen in parallel.

## Related

- rosary-49145f (local/remote MCP transport fallback)
- rosary-13af35 (reactive persistent store — "local firebase" for agent IPC)
- ADR-005 (ley-line as reactive store)
- conductor OTP pattern in rig

title: Parallel-LLM coordination: prevent docker / workspace / branch contention across concurrent sessions
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from a real session incident in ley-line-open (PR #3 work).

## What happened

User had 4 concurrent LLM sessions running, each operating on a different rosary-managed repo (LLO, rosary itself, notme, mache). The LLO session was building OCI images via `task image`. Concurrent observations during ~1 hour:

1. **Docker daemon contention** — multiple `melange build` invocations queued on the docker daemon, none making progress. Symptoms: log goes silent for 5+ min after `populating workspace`. No timeout, no error — just stuck.
2. **Workspace tmpdir leak** — melange's default `--source-dir` = `dirname(melange.yaml)` = repo root. Each interrupted run leaks 8-30 GB to `/var/folders/.../T/melange-workspace-XXXXXX`. After 4 stalled+killed runs: ~80 GB across 10 leaked dirs.
3. **Process tree confusion** — `pkill -f "task image"` from one session would have killed work in the other 3 sessions. The user explicitly stopped the cleanup mid-way ("omg why are you killing it all lol") to avoid losing live work.
4. **Branch lifecycle confusion** — PR #4 in LLO was misclicked closed instead of merged. The other LLM sessions had no awareness this was happening; if any of them had started follow-up work assuming PR #4 was on main, that work would have been built on a phantom commit.

This isn't an LLO problem — it's a rosary infrastructure problem. The dispatch layer routes work to repos, but doesn't guard against concurrent sessions stomping on shared host resources (docker daemon, /var/folders/T, the user's git config).

## Possible interventions

### Per-LLM scratch isolation
- Each LLM session gets a unique tmpdir prefix (`/var/folders/.../T/llm-<session-id>-melange-workspace-*`)
- Tools that take `--workspace-dir` / `--out-dir` / `--cache-dir` flags get session-prefixed defaults
- Cleanup on session end is per-session, not global
- Pro: isolation guaranteed
- Con: requires every tool to be opt-in to the convention OR rosary intercepts at dispatch

### Shared-resource lockfiles
- Tools that contend for docker daemon (melange, docker build, docker run with --name) acquire a flock on `~/.rosary/locks/docker-daemon` before invoking
- Lock is held for the duration of the operation, released on exit/kill
- Pro: serializes cleanly without coordination
- Con: subtle bugs around lock timeouts; one stuck session blocks all
- Variant: per-image-name lock (so `task image` on LLO doesn't block `task image` on a different repo using a different tag)

### "Claim a repo" convention
- Each LLM session claims (via rosary) which repo it owns
- Other sessions filing beads or reading state from that repo are read-only until the claim releases
- Pro: explicit
- Con: doesn't help when an LLM works on multiple repos in one session (cross-repo coordination is exactly the case where most stomping happens)

### Just don't run concurrent sessions on the same repo
- Document it. Lean on the user to know.
- Pro: zero engineering cost
- Con: that's the status quo, and it didn't work today

## Recommend

Hybrid: per-LLM scratch dirs (cheap, immediate) + shared-resource lockfile for docker daemon specifically (the one-time pain we hit was ALL docker-daemon-mediated). Skip the "claim a repo" convention — it's the heavy answer for a problem that the first two solve.

## Related: branch/PR lifecycle awareness

Separate sub-question: should rosary surface "PR #N just closed without merging" as an event other sessions consume? Today, a misclick on the GH UI is invisible until the next session manually checks. A rosary "watch active PRs across all repos" subscription could push these events.

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded (which interventions to ship)
- ADR or design doc in rosary's `docs/`
- One or more follow-up beads filed for the implementation
- Real test: spawn 4 concurrent sessions running `task image` on the same repo, confirm no contention / no leaks

## Cross-link

Filed from LLO PR #3 session — see `ley-line-open-2b255c` for the full incident timeline (the workspace leak + docker stall, including 80GB of orphan tmpdirs we eventually swept).

title: Scheduled tasks vs pipeline tasks — cron-style recurring work
description:
Rosary needs a concept of "scheduled tasks" distinct from pipeline tasks. Pipeline tasks are bead-driven (scan → triage → dispatch). Scheduled tasks are time-driven crons: "find things to do", "find improvements", "clean up stale beads", "sweep orphaned workspaces", etc.

Key questions:
- Can we use an OSS scheduler (e.g. cron, tokio-cron-scheduler, apalis) or build on Dolt events?
- Should these be event-streamed or polled? Depends on volume — low-frequency crons (hourly/daily) can poll, high-frequency (per-commit) should stream.
- Cron beads vs config-defined schedules? Beads are the unit of work, but recurring schedules feel more like config.
- The Elixir conductor's OTP supervision tree is a natural fit for this (GenServer timers), but the Rust reconciler needs it too for the single-process path.

Examples of scheduled tasks:
- Hourly: scan repos for new work, clean up orphaned workspaces
- Daily: reconcile Linear sync, find improvement opportunities, prune stale beads
- On-event: post-merge verification, dependency update checks

title: bead migrate verify treats owner ''↔NULL as a mismatch — blocks signet migration entirely
description:
Found during the fleet Dolt→SQLite sweep (rosary-aa8c6d). `rsry bead migrate --to sqlite --json` on ~/remotes/art/signet fails its own dry-run verify:

    {"repo":"signet","source_backend":"dolt","verify":"failed","committed":false,
     "error":"bead signet-a7c3ae: owner mismatch after migration (None != Some(\"\"))"}

Ground truth from the Dolt source:

    select count(*) total, sum(owner is null) null_owner, sum(owner='') empty_owner from issues;
    -> total=68, null_owner=0, empty_owner=67

So 67 of signet's 68 beads carry owner = '' (empty string). The Dolt reader yields Some(""), the SQLite round-trip yields None (empty string normalized to NULL on write or read). Semantically identical — "no owner" either way — but `verify_migration` compares the Option directly, so it reports a field mismatch and refuses to migrate.

Impact: signet can never be migrated off Dolt without --force or a code fix. It was the ONLY repo of the 15 swept that tripped this; the other 14 verified clean and were committed. Migration was correctly HALTED on signet rather than forced.

Fix: normalize empty-string ↔ NULL for nullable text fields (owner at minimum, likely the whole optional-text family: branch, pr_url, external_ref, scope, jj_change_id) on one side of the comparison in verify_migration, so semantically-equal-but-differently-encoded emptiness doesn't read as data loss. Related to ADR-0021's single-source-the-field-lifecycle thesis: this is a per-field encoding rule that each surface currently re-invents.
acceptance_criteria: `cd ~/remotes/art/signet && rsry bead migrate --to sqlite --json` reports verify=ok with beads=68, and a unit test in src/bead_migrate.rs covers the ''↔NULL equivalence for nullable text fields.

title: Staging-agent must review + run new tests before pipeline passes
description:
When a dev-agent writes new tests (especially integration/E2E), the pipeline currently just runs them. There's no gate that checks:

1. **Leakage/safety**: Does the test clean up after itself? Does it touch real state (filesystem, network, Dolt)? Does it leak temp dirs, worktrees, branches? Are there race conditions with concurrent test runs?
2. **Actually runs the test**: The staging-agent should explicitly execute the new test and verify it passes — not just trust that it compiles.

This is somewhere between a golden rule and a pipeline design decision:
- **Rule aspect**: "New tests must be reviewed for resource leakage before marking pass" → belongs in GOLDEN_RULES.md or staging-agent.md
- **Design aspect**: The pipeline should enforce this — staging-agent's verification should include running new/modified test files specifically, not just `task test`. Could diff HEAD to find new test functions and run them targeted.
- **Operational aspect**: Integration tests that touch git/jj/Dolt/filesystem need extra scrutiny. A checklist: tempdir cleanup, worktree cleanup, no hardcoded paths, no network calls, idempotent.

Concrete actions:
- Add "test safety review" to staging-agent.md perspective
- Consider adding a verify tier that identifies and runs only new/changed tests
- Golden rule: "integration tests must be self-contained — no leaked state across runs"

title: Handoff quality: structured context transfer between pipeline phases
description:
When dev-agent finishes and staging-agent picks up, the context transfer needs to be high quality. Currently handoff.rs exists but the prompt integration may not give the next agent enough structured context about what was done, what was tested, what to watch for.

Review handoff format, ensure it includes:
- What changed (files, approach)
- What was tested vs not tested
- Known risks or edge cases
- Review hints for the next phase

The agents ARE the pipeline phases (they don't need pipeline awareness), but the handoff between them is the critical seam.

title: Hot-swap running MCP servers to a newly installed binary (nginx-style re-exec over preserved stdio)
description:
User wish (2026-07-16, after v0.7.0): `task install` updates the binary + restarts the launchd HTTP service, but every ALREADY-RUNNING stdio MCP server (one per Claude Code session) keeps serving the old version until its session restarts. Today that also means a stale RepoPool (see reference_rsry_repo_tier memory — repos registered mid-session don't resolve by scope).

## Difficulty: moderate (~1-2 days), no protocol changes needed

The trick is the classic nginx/envoy binary-upgrade pattern adapted to stdio: `exec()` preserves fds 0/1/2, so the MCP client (Claude Code) keeps talking to the same pipes and never notices the process image swap.

Mechanism sketch:
1. **Drift detection**: `rsry serve --transport stdio` remembers its own RSRY_BUILD_HASH. On a timer (or opportunistically between requests) it stats the canonical install path (resolve argv[0] → ~/.local/bin/rsry) and cheap-compares mtime+len; on change, confirm by running `<new-binary> --version` (subprocess) and comparing hash.
2. **Quiescence gate**: only swap when no JSON-RPC request is in flight and stdout is between complete frames (a partial frame write followed by exec = corrupted stream = client hangs). Serialize via the existing request loop.
3. **Re-exec with session resume**: `exec()` the new binary with a `--resume-stdio-session <fd-or-env>` carrying the tiny negotiated state (protocol version, client info from initialize). New process skips waiting-for-initialize and continues serving on the inherited fds. RepoPool intentionally NOT carried — rebuilding it from config is the point (fixes stale-pool for free).
4. **Fail-safe**: if exec fails, the old process keeps serving (exec only replaces on success); if the new binary crashes within N seconds... (it can't fall back post-exec — mitigate by validating `--version` + a `--selfcheck` subcommand pre-exec).

Risks/edges: in-flight sampling/notifications mid-swap (rosary's server is request-response only today — low risk); signal handling across exec; Keychain/launchd env inheritance (env is preserved by default exec).

Phases: (1) drift detect + clean idle re-exec + resume flag + integration test driving a fake MCP client over pipes through a swap; (2) HTTP transport equivalent is NOT needed (launchd restart covers it) — explicitly out of scope.

Related: reference_rsry_repo_tier (stale RepoPool), rsry doctor drift warning (the detection logic can be shared).
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: spawn `rsry serve --transport stdio` via pipes, complete initialize + one tool call, swap the binary on disk for one with a different build hash, next tool call is served by the NEW hash (verify via a version-reporting tool) over the SAME pipes with no client-side reconnect; cargo test passes

title: Test safety linter — codifiable rules as a verify tier (tropo candidate)
description:
The reasoning we apply when reviewing new tests is codifiable:

- Does the test use tempdir and hold the guard? (leaked filesystem state)
- Does it create git worktrees/branches and clean them up?
- Does it spawn processes and ensure they're killed?
- Does it bind ports and release them?
- Does it touch real Dolt and clean up?
- Are assertions checking the RIGHT thing (not just "it didn't crash")?
- Is it idempotent (can run twice without the second run failing)?

This is a linter. Not a style linter — a **safety linter** for test code. It could be:
1. A verify tier in the pipeline (runs after staging-agent, before merge)
2. A tropo transform (test code → safety checklist → violations)
3. A mache query (find_callees from test functions → check for cleanup patterns)

The key insight: these rules are the same ones a senior dev applies when reviewing test PRs. They're heuristic but consistent enough to automate. False positives are fine — flag for human review, don't block.

Connection to tropo: this is exactly the kind of "structural transform" tropo was designed for — take code structure, apply domain rules, emit findings. Not AST rewriting, but AST analysis with domain-specific safety rules.

Cross-refs: rosary-c1d89b (staging-agent test review), rosary-870ae4 (tropo audit)

title: Dispatch dead-letter: failed workers must surface, not silently drop
description:
## Problem

Today when a dispatched worker dies (crash, OOM, timeout, exit-nonzero, SIGKILL), the bead stays at `dispatched`/`in_progress` forever. No alert, no automatic recovery, no triage surface. Work silently disappears.

Two failure modes already observed today (2026-05-11):

1. **Stuck `in_progress`** — `rosary-ba9893` smoke test: agent ran 41s, completed successfully, exited. Bead remained `in_progress` because the prompt told the agent "Do NOT close the bead — the reconciler verifies and closes it" but no reconciler daemon was running to advance it. Without `rsry run` actively iterating, every successful dispatch is a leak.

2. **Orphan `dispatched`** — `cloister-a30e40` from another session: dispatched ~20min ago, no live worker visible in `rsry_active`'s `running` list, status stays `dispatched`. `dispatch::sweep::sweep_orphan_dispatches` only fires on a NEW dispatch into the SAME repo; cross-repo orphans persist indefinitely.

The user's read: "things die → should dead-letter. This smells like an issue causing us to drop things intermittently." Correct.

## What we have today

- `~/.rsry/sessions.json` (session registry) tracks: bead_id, repo, pid, started_at, last_activity, last_comment, work_dir.
- `health` is computed at read-time via `is_pid_alive(pid)` — values: `healthy`, `idle`, `stuck`, `dead`.
- `rsry_active` reports both `running` and `needs_merge` (the dead-pid sessions).
- `dispatch::sweep::sweep_orphan_dispatches` exists but only sweeps the dispatching repo, only on a fresh dispatch.

## What's missing: dead-letter lifecycle

Beads need a `dead_letter` status (or label) that:

1. **Triggers automatically** when the dispatched worker dies without successfully closing the bead.
2. **Captures forensics**: exit signal/code (if recoverable), last_activity timestamp, last_comment, stream log path, work_dir, dispatch generation. So operators can decide retry vs. mark-resolved vs. investigate without diving into logs.
3. **Surfaces in tooling**: `rsry status` shows dead-letter count alongside `active`/`blocked`. `rsry list-beads --status=dead_letter` returns them.
4. **Resolves explicitly**: operator commands to (a) re-dispatch with clean worktree, (b) re-dispatch resuming the existing worktree, (c) close as won't-fix, (d) merge any partial work and close.

## Required machinery

- **Periodic janitor**: a job (cron / scheduled task / part of `rsry run` iteration) that walks the session registry, checks pid liveness, and moves stale `dispatched`/`in_progress` beads to `dead_letter` if no live pid AND no recent activity (configurable window, e.g. 5min).
- **Cross-repo scope**: the sweep must touch every registered repo, not just the one being dispatched into now. (Implementation task — see `rosary-XXXXXX` to be filed.)
- **Status transition table** — when a bead is `in_progress` AND pid dead AND last_activity > N minutes ago → `dead_letter`. When `dispatched` AND no live pid AND no worktree → `dead_letter` (the existing sweep currently reverts these to `open`, which is the WRONG default — losing the dispatch attempt history).
- **Reconciler integration**: the existing reconciler loop should run the janitor each iteration, so operators running `rsry run` get DLQ behavior for free.

## Out of scope

- Auto-retry policies (let operators decide; "retry on dead-letter" is a separate bead).
- Worker output forensics beyond what's already in `.rsry-stream.jsonl` + `.rsry-stderr.log`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New `BeadState::DeadLetter` status (or equivalent persisted label)
- [ ] Janitor function detects dead sessions and transitions bead status
- [ ] `rsry status` and `rsry list-beads` surface dead-letter count and entries
- [ ] At least one CLI command to resolve a dead-letter bead (re-dispatch / close)
- [ ] Test: spawn a worker, kill -9 it, run janitor → bead is dead-letter with kill signal captured
- [ ] Implementation tasks file linked beads

## Refs

- `src/session.rs` — SessionRegistry, is_pid_alive
- `src/dispatch/sweep.rs` — existing sweep_orphan_dispatches (the seed of the right idea, narrower scope)
- `src/serve/handlers.rs::tool_active` — current health categorization
- Today's symptom: `rosary-ba9893` (in_progress, agent done), `cloister-a30e40` (dispatched, orphan)

comments.text:
## Closing — design intent shipped via PR #202; CLI ergonomics carved out

Subagent investigation 2026-06-17 (agent ID aa864001a725f29d0) confirms the core design — `BeadState::DeadLetter` + automatic detection + forensics + Linear mirroring — shipped fully in PR #202 (commit `d4759ca`, +854/-9 across 7 files):

- `BeadState::DeadLetter` with transition table (`src/bead.rs:40-78`)
- Linear round-trip mapping (`bead.rs:108-128`, `linear_tracker.rs:263-270`)
- `sweep_dead_workers` + `LivenessSweepReport` + `DeadWorkerCandidate` (`src/dispatch/sweep.rs:194-257`)
- `Reconciler::liveness_sweep` wired into `iterate()` Phase 1.8 (`reconcile/mod.rs:699`, `reconcile/persistence.rs:211-298`)
- Forensic detail captured (pid, started_at, last_activity, work_dir)
- 9 round-trips of Copilot review baked into commits

Remaining ergonomic gap (CLI surface to list + resolve dead-letter beads) carved out as separate follow-up bead. Closing this parent design bead pointing at PR #202.
