title: Janitor: auto-advance stuck in_progress beads when worker pid is dead
description:
Implementation subset of rosary-c3034b (dead-letter design).

**Symptom**: agent finishes work (commit posted, bead comment added) but bead stays `in_progress` forever because the agent prompt says "do not close — reconciler verifies and closes" and no reconciler is running. Today's example: rosary-ba9893 sat in_progress after the spawned agent exited cleanly at 20:31Z.

**Scope**:

1. New function `janitor::sweep_dead_in_progress` that walks `SessionRegistry` and for each entry where:
   - `pid` is set AND `is_pid_alive(pid) == false`
   - bead status is `in_progress`
   - `last_activity` is older than `dispatch.dead_session_grace_secs` (default 300)

   → transitions bead to `dead_letter` (new status from rosary-c3034b) with metadata captured from the registry entry.

2. Call sites:
   - End of each reconciler iteration (`reconcile::iterate`)
   - Beginning of each `rsry_dispatch` call (extends existing `sweep_orphan_dispatches`)
   - Standalone CLI: `rsry janitor` (one-shot, for manual triage)

3. Add `dispatch.dead_session_grace_secs` config field. Operator can tune; default 300 (5 min) so quick-running agents like scoping-agent don't get false-positive'd.

**Tests**:

- Sandboxed Dolt + a fake "agent" subprocess that we spawn, record in registry with bead_id=X status=in_progress, then SIGKILL → run janitor → assert bead status is dead_letter and registry entry retained for forensics.
- Live-pid case: sleep-100 subprocess + janitor → bead status unchanged.
- Recent-activity case: dead pid but last_activity within grace window → bead unchanged.

**Files**:
- `src/dispatch/janitor.rs` (new) — sweep_dead_in_progress + tests
- `src/dispatch/mod.rs` — re-export, wire into existing dispatch flow
- `src/reconcile/mod.rs` — call from iterate()
- `src/main.rs` — `rsry janitor` subcommand

Depends on rosary-c3034b for the DeadLetter status definition.

comments.text:
## Coverage gap confirmed (2026-05-11)

Re-read of the reconciler shows the load-bearing miss: `src/reconcile/mod.rs:474` calls `workspace::sweep_orphaned` (filesystem worktree cleanup) but NOT `dispatch::sweep::sweep_orphan_dispatches` (bead-status cleanup). The dispatch-status sweep only runs from `serve/handlers.rs::tool_dispatch` (MCP entry, on a per-repo basis at dispatch time).

So even with a `rsry run` daemon iterating continuously, bead statuses don't get reconciled — only worktrees on disk do. That's why "things die silently": the daemon was never wired to inspect in-progress bead state.

**Hardened acceptance criterion for this bead**: the janitor function MUST be invoked from `reconcile::iterate`, not just from `tool_dispatch`. Add an integration-shaped test in `src/reconcile/tests.rs` that:

1. Sets up a bead in state `in_progress` with a `SessionRegistry` entry pointing at a dead pid (sleep + kill OR a never-spawned synthetic pid)
2. Runs one iteration of the reconciler
3. Asserts the bead status transitioned to `dead_letter` (per rosary-c3034b)

Without this test, the janitor lives in isolation and the failure mode silently returns.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: Cross-repo orphan sweep: sweep_orphan_dispatches must walk all registered repos
description:
Implementation subset of rosary-c3034b (dead-letter design).

**Symptom**: `cloister-a30e40` was dispatched ~20min ago, its worker is gone, but the bead stays at `dispatched` because the existing `sweep_orphan_dispatches` only fires when a NEW dispatch happens INTO the same repo. Cross-repo orphans persist indefinitely.

**Scope**:

1. Refactor `dispatch::sweep::sweep_orphan_dispatches(client, root, repo_name)` to a top-level `sweep_orphan_dispatches_all_repos()` that walks the global repo registry (~/.rsry/repos.toml) and runs the per-repo sweep against each.

2. Behavior change: instead of reverting orphans to `open` (current), transition them to `dead_letter` per rosary-c3034b. The dispatch attempt history is forensically valuable — losing it to a status revert was the wrong choice. Operators can re-open from dead_letter explicitly if they want to retry.

3. Wire into:
   - The reconciler iteration (so the daemon does it periodically)
   - Standalone CLI: `rsry sweep` (one-shot)
   - Optional: extend `rsry_dispatch` to do a global sweep before its current per-repo sweep — current per-repo behavior is too narrow

**Tests**:

- Multi-repo fixture: dispatch a bead in repo A, kill the worker, then dispatch a bead in repo B → global sweep transitions A's orphan to dead_letter.
- Single-repo regression: existing per-repo sweep behavior preserved for the per-repo entry point.

**Files**:
- `src/dispatch/sweep.rs` — add global entry point + adjust transition target
- `src/reconcile/mod.rs` — wire global sweep into iterate()
- `src/main.rs` — `rsry sweep` subcommand

Depends on rosary-c3034b for the DeadLetter status definition.

title: [ADR-0001] ContextProvider trait + build_prompt wiring
description:
Define the `ContextProvider` trait — the abstraction layer for injecting external document context into agent prompts at dispatch time.

**Trait definition** (`src/context.rs`, new file):
```rust
#[async_trait]
pub trait ContextProvider: Send + Sync {
    /// Search for documents relevant to the given bead's file scopes and description.
    /// Returns Markdown-formatted context, truncated to `max_tokens`.
    async fn fetch_context(&self, bead: &Bead, max_tokens: usize) -> Result<Option<String>>;
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
}
```

**Config addition** (`src/config.rs`):
- Add `context_providers: Option<Vec<ContextProviderConfig>>` to `Config`
- `ContextProviderConfig` has `provider: String` (e.g., "notion"), provider-specific sub-config
- Add `[notion]` section: `oauth_token_env`, `workspace_filter`, `max_context_tokens` (default 2000)

**Prompt wiring** (`src/dispatch.rs`):
- `build_prompt()` accepts `&[Box<dyn ContextProvider>]`
- Calls each provider's `fetch_context()`, injects results into `<product-context>` XML section
- Graceful degradation: if no providers configured or all return None, omit the section entirely

**Reconciler wiring** (`src/reconcile.rs`):
- `Reconciler` struct gets `context_providers: Vec<Box<dyn ContextProvider>>`
- Factory function `context_providers_from_config()` instantiates providers from config

This is the foundational trait — NotionContextProvider (separate bead) implements it. Pattern follows existing ComputeProvider / AgentProvider / IssueTracker traits.

ADR: docs/adr/0001-notion-byon-integration.md (in rig repo)

title: [ADR-0001] NotionContextProvider implementation
description:
Implement `NotionContextProvider` — the concrete `ContextProvider` that fetches product context from a customer's Notion workspace via the hosted Notion MCP server.

**Notion MCP client** (`src/notion.rs`, new file):
- Connect to Notion MCP server at `mcp.notion.com` using customer's OAuth token
- Implement key operations: `search_pages(query)`, `retrieve_page(id)`, `retrieve_database(id)`
- All responses are Markdown — parse and truncate to token budget

**Relevance matching**:
- Extract keywords from bead title, description, and file scopes
- Call `notion_search_pages` with derived query terms
- Rank results by relevance (title match > content match > recency)
- Return top N results concatenated as Markdown, within `max_context_tokens` budget

**Token budget enforcement**:
- Default: 2000 tokens max (configurable via `[notion] max_context_tokens`)
- Truncate per-page content proportionally if total exceeds budget
- Include page title + URL as attribution even when content is truncated

**Caching**:
- Cache Notion search results with TTL (default 5min) to avoid rate limit issues
- Notion API rate limit: 3 req/sec per integration
- Cache key: hash of (workspace_id, search_query)

**Error handling**:
- OAuth token expired → return None, log warning (graceful degradation)
- Notion API error → return None, log error
- Never block dispatch due to Notion failures

Depends on: rosary-c4104a (ContextProvider trait)

title: [ADR-0001] DocCoverageCheck verify tier
description:
Implement `DocCoverageCheck` — a new `VerifyTier` that compares code entities modified by the agent against Notion documentation references. Flags stale docs after code changes.

**VerifyTier implementation** (`src/verify.rs`):
- `DocCoverageCheck` implements `VerifyTier` trait
- Inserted after `DiffSanityCheck` (Tier 3), before `ReviewCheck` (Tier 4)
- Configurable mode: `warn` (VerifyResult::Partial) or `block` (VerifyResult::Fail)
- Default: `warn` — flags stale docs but doesn't block merge

**Algorithm**:
1. Read git diff from agent's work (already available in verify context)
2. Extract changed code entities: function names, type names, module paths
3. Query Notion via `notion.rs` for pages referencing those entities
4. For each matching Notion page:
   - Compare page `last_edited_time` against commit timestamp
   - If page last edited BEFORE code change → flag as potentially stale
5. Generate coverage report as VerifyResult detail

**Report format** (added to bead comment):
```
Doc Coverage: 3 entities changed, 2 documented, 1 stale
  ✓ process_bead() — documented in "Pipeline Architecture" (updated 2026-03-18)
  ✓ ContextProvider trait — documented in "Integration Guide" (updated 2026-03-20)
  ⚠ verify_agent() — documented in "Verify Pipeline" (last updated 2026-03-01, code changed 2026-03-20)
```

**Optional: Notion AI agent trigger**:
- If customer has Notion Business ($20/mo/member), Notion's AI can auto-update pages
- Call `notion_update_page` with a comment requesting AI curation
- Gated behind `[notion] auto_curate = true` config flag

title: Sync bead dependencies/blockers to Linear relations API
description:
The Linear sync currently pushes status + labels but completely ignores dependency edges. Beads have a dependencies table (issue_id, depends_on_id) and cross_repo_deps, but none of this flows to Linear.

Linear has a relations API with blockedBy/blocks/related relation types. We should:
1. Push: when a bead has dependencies, create corresponding Linear relations
2. Pull: when a Linear issue gets a blocker added, create a bead dependency
3. Handle cross-repo deps (bead in repo A blocks bead in repo B) via external_ref mapping

This matters because blockers are invisible in Linear today — you can't see the dependency graph in the UI.

title: Decouple task tracker from dispatch/scheduling — rsry installable as just-the-tracker
description:
## User framing (2026-05-19, end-of-session)

> "Ensuring that the task manager is installable w/o the agent scheduling thing.
> As I need to work on the scheduling thing more."

User wants to evolve dispatch/scheduling without it being load-bearing for everyone who just
wants the bead tracker. Today `rsry` is a monolith: install rosary, you get the tracker AND
the dispatch loop AND the reconciler AND the agent-provider machinery. That's fine for the
dogfood case but it's a barrier for:

1. **Other agents/humans who want bead tracking only** — they shouldn't have to configure
   Sprites/Fly/Claude providers, pipeline mappings, or workspace lifecycle to use the issue
   tracker.
2. **The user themselves while iterating on dispatch** — the scheduling work shouldn't
   destabilize people's task tracking. Today a bug in `dispatch/` can break `rsry status`.

## What "installable without scheduling" means concretely

- `rsry install --minimal` (or a separate binary `rsry-track`) that excludes dispatch,
  workspace, agent providers, sweeps, Linear push.
- The minimal install gives: `rsry bead create/update/list/search/close/comment`,
  `rsry scan`, `rsry status`, MCP server with the 14 bead-CRUD tools.
- The dispatch + reconcile + workspace + provider tools become an **opt-in extension**
  enabled by a config flag or a separate feature compile.

## Honest assessment

Today this is a refactor, not a clean split. Cardinal coupling points:

- `src/main.rs` wires everything in one CLI
- `src/serve/mod.rs` registers all 31 MCP tools unconditionally
- `src/reconcile/` and `src/dispatch/` share types with `src/bead.rs` and `src/store_dolt.rs`
  but the *reverse* shouldn't be true — the bead store should not need to know about
  dispatch
- `src/observation/` is consumed by both — that's fine, it's substrate
- The pipeline plugin system is dispatch-side; bead-only install can ignore it

The right approach is probably **Cargo features**, not separate binaries:
- `default = ["dispatch", "linear", "github"]`
- `minimal = []` — just bead CRUD + MCP server + scan + status
- Feature-gate `mod dispatch`, `mod reconcile`, `mod workspace`, `mod plugin`,
  `mod linear`, `mod github_mirror`, `mod sync`

## Why it matters

User explicitly says **they need to work on the scheduling thing more**. Today every
scheduling change risks regressing the tracker. Separation gives the user a stable tracker
floor to iterate dispatch on top of. Also opens "rosary-as-issue-tracker" as a standalone
offer (lower barrier for adoption, public/private boundary friendlier).

## Sequencing

Filed as **post-P1-prioritized-work**:
1. `rosary-5dc9b0` (ticket_load) — user's stated highest priority
2. `rosary-a761df` (state-machine substrate)
3. `rosary-792ed6` (personal/root rosary security)
4. **THIS bead** + `rosary-5ead7e` (MCP Apps substrate) — substrate cleanup, do together

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cargo build --no-default-features --features minimal` produces a working `rsry` binary
- [ ] Minimal binary exposes: bead-CRUD CLI, `scan`, `status`, MCP server with bead tools only
- [ ] `cargo build` (default features) is identical to today's behavior — no regression
- [ ] CI gate: build minimal feature in addition to default to prevent feature-drift
- [ ] Documentation: `INSTALL.md` section explaining when to use minimal vs full

## Time-box

L — ~2 days. Feature-gating touches a lot of imports + module boundaries. Test matrix doubles.
Not hard, just careful.

## Files (preliminary, expect drift during exploration)

- `Cargo.toml` — feature definitions
- `src/main.rs` — feature-gated CLI subcommands
- `src/lib.rs` — feature-gated module declarations
- `src/serve/mod.rs` — feature-gated tool registration
- `src/serve/handlers.rs` — feature-gated handlers
- `src/reconcile/mod.rs`, `src/dispatch/mod.rs`, `src/workspace.rs`, `src/plugin.rs` — all
  fall behind `#[cfg(feature = "dispatch")]`
- `src/linear.rs`, `src/linear_tracker.rs`, `src/github_mirror.rs`, `src/sync.rs` — fall behind
  their respective features
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add `--no-default-features --features minimal` build matrix
- `INSTALL.md` (new) — minimal vs full install guide

## Cross-links

- `rosary-a761df` (state-machine substrate) — the scheduling work this clears the path for
- `rosary-5ead7e` (MCP Apps UI substrate) — same "post-P1 substrate cleanup" cohort
- `rosary-b306e5` (monorepo aspiration tracking) — feature-gates are a multi-repo-friendly
  alternative to a monorepo merge for the dispatch-vs-tracker boundary

title: Split reconciler into observer + dispatcher + linear-sync loops (3 cadences)
description:
## Problem

`Reconciler::iterate()` fuses **three** concerns with very different operational profiles. The fix isn't just observer-vs-dispatcher (the original framing) — Linear sync is a third axis with its own cadence + failure modes.

### Loop 1: Observer (passive, safe, always-on, local-only)
- `scan` — read open beads from each repo's `.beads/`
- `scan_vcs` — walk jj/git logs for `[bead-id]` references → advance bead state
- `poll_pr_status` — `gh pr view` on `pr_open` beads → close on MERGED, log review feedback
- Writes only to local bead DB. No network beyond `gh`.

### Loop 2: Dispatcher (active, side-effectful, opt-in, local-but-spawns)
- `triage` — score beads + apply filters
- `dispatch` — spawn agents (writes to git, costs $, spawns subprocess)
- `verify_completed` — run verify tiers on completed work
- `assemble_feature_prs` — open PRs (network side effect)

### Loop 3: Linear sync (network, rate-limited, external API, fragile)
- `persist_status` to Linear via `IssueTracker` — push bead state transitions to Linear issues
- Pull Linear webhook events (in HTTP serve) → drive local bead state changes
- Today: fused into `persist_status` which is called from observer-style code paths
- Has its own failure modes (rate limits, API errors, OAuth expiry) that should NOT affect local bead state

## Why all three are separate

| Loop | Cadence | Network | Side effects | Failure blast radius |
|------|---------|---------|--------------|----------------------|
| Observer | 30s | local + `gh` | local DB writes | nil |
| Dispatcher | 1-30min | local subprocess | spawns agents, costs $$, opens PRs | wide |
| Linear sync | 1-15min | Linear API | network calls | external only — should never block local |

Fusing them today means: a Linear API rate-limit can stall observer iterations. A dispatcher crash can interrupt Linear writes. A network blip stops bead-state observation.

## Manifest of the issue surfaced today

`rsry serve` running for 3 days, but neither `rsry run` nor `rsry start` is — so none of the three loops fire. Result: 32 beads stuck in `needs_merge` because their merged PRs were never observed by `poll_pr_status` AND their Linear status never advanced. Diagnosed in conversation 2026-05-09.

## Proposed shape

### Three iteration methods

```rust
pub async fn observe_iteration(&mut self) -> ObserveSummary {
    // scan + scan_vcs + poll_pr_status + local persist
    // NO dispatch. NO Linear. NO verify.
}

pub async fn dispatch_iteration(&mut self) -> DispatchSummary {
    // triage + dispatch + verify_completed + assemble_feature_prs
}

pub async fn linear_sync_iteration(&mut self) -> LinearSyncSummary {
    // push pending state changes to Linear
    // pull Linear webhook deltas
    // independent of observer/dispatcher cadence
}
```

`Reconciler::iterate()` becomes a thin scheduler: each loop fires at its own interval.

### Three service surfaces

- `rsry serve` — auto-spawns Observer task in background. Default-on. Cheap. No surprises.
- `rsry serve --with-dispatcher` — opts into Loop 2.
- `rsry serve --with-linear-sync` — opts into Loop 3 (if Linear configured).
- Or all three as separate launchd plists if user wants to control individually.

### Wiring

- `ReconcilerMode { ObserveOnly, ObserveDispatch, ObserveLinear, All }` — or three boolean toggles
- Each loop gates on its own config flag
- Failures are isolated: a Linear outage doesn't stop the observer

## Why now

The user just noticed `rsry serve` running for 3 days but no reconciliation, leading to 32 stalled beads. "Just running serve" should keep state coherent without risking auto-dispatch and without making local state contingent on a network round-trip to Linear.

This is also the kind of subtle bug they've been worried about — three semantically distinct loops jammed into one means one failure mode masks another.

## Files

- `src/reconcile/mod.rs` — split iterate into 3 methods
- `src/linear_tracker.rs` / `src/linear.rs` — extract Linear sync into its own iteration
- `src/main.rs` — add per-loop flags to `rsry run`
- `src/serve/mod.rs` — auto-spawn observer; gate dispatcher + linear-sync
- `scripts/com.rosary.serve.plist.template` — possibly siblings for dispatcher + linear-sync

## Tests

- `observe_iteration_does_not_dispatch` — assert active map unchanged
- `observe_iteration_polls_merges` — feed merged-PR fixture, assert close
- `observe_iteration_skips_linear_sync` — assert no Linear API call when Linear-sync loop is off
- `dispatch_iteration_skips_observe_only_repos` — verify mode gating
- `linear_sync_failure_does_not_stop_observer` — Linear API mock returns 429, observer iter still completes

## Related

title: Release batching: aggregate completed beads into reviewable releases
description:
## Problem
Currently human reviews individual PRs (5-10/day). Goal is to move to "human reviews a release" — batch completed pipeline outputs into a single release candidate.

## What
A release aggregation layer on top of the dispatch pipeline:
1. Overnight: agents work on N beads across M repos
2. Morning: completed beads (all pipeline phases passed) are batched into a release candidate
3. Release candidate runs cross-bead integration tests
4. Human sees one release with changelog: 3 bugs, 2 features, 1 hotfix
5. Human approves → coordinated merge across repos → deploy

## Multi-repo as virtual monorepo
In a monorepo this is straightforward. For multi-repo (ART ecosystem), repos must be declarable as a cohesive unit with "sections" / "groupings" — analogous to sheaf cells / communities. A release spans multiple repos but is presented as one coherent change set. The grouping structure (which repos form a release unit) should be configurable in rosary.toml.

## Phases
1. Human reviews PRs (today)
2. Human reviews releases (this bead)
3. Human creates work, agents handle everything else (future)

## Reference
- gstack /ship skill: atomic release coordination, test bootstrapping, coverage audit
- Rosary pipeline already does per-bead verification — this extends to cross-bead release verification
- sheaf-core / hotsheaf for structural grouping primitives

title: ModelProvider abstraction: typed Credential union + per-request auth resolver + registry middleware — synthesized from AI SDK / LiteLLM / genai
description:
Design synthesis (2026-07-17) from a 3-crate prior-art sweep (Vercel AI SDK LanguageModelV4, LiteLLM BaseConfig+Vertex load_auth, Rust genai vs rig) + the vault-custody RCA (rosary-470270). Grounds a small `ModelProvider` abstraction for rosary's lightweight direct-model-call gap.

CONTEXT / correction: rosary makes NO direct model API calls today. bdr_enrich/capture/decompose shell out to `claude -p` (CLI). Dispatch is converging on NATIVE RUNTIME protocols (codex app-server JSON-RPC in codex_runtime/transport.rs; ACP-native claude path rosary-5a9a88/5118b7) — a persistent, steerable session (the "durable job + attachable view" model). So there are THREE layers, one shared substrate:
  Credential   — typed union, vault-backed        (SHARED by both below)
  ModelProvider — direct model call (generate/stream) — NET-NEW; enrichment, classification, goal-verifier (rosary-d4592f), scoping agent
  RuntimeProvider — native runtime protocol (app-server JSON-RPC, ACP) — full dispatch, already converging

KEY DECISIONS (convergent across all three sources):
1. Credential = typed tagged UNION, not a dict/HashMap (LiteLLM Vertex load_auth dispatches on a `type` field; genai has MultiKeys+async resolver but leaves it unwired; both punt on OAuth — that's our exact gap to fill). The RCA's per-provider split IS the variants:
     enum Credential {
       ApiKey(SecretString),                                  // claude: token-elsewhere, header shape-routed
       OAuth { client_id, client_secret: Option<SecretString>, refresh_token, access: RwLock<Option<Cached>> },
     }                                                        // codex = OAuth{secret:None}; gemini = OAuth{secret:Some}
   with `async fn bearer()` = refresh-if-expired + cache (LiteLLM `_ensure_access_token` caches the minted bearer separately from the long-lived cred). Collapses codex/gemini/claude to one call site.
2. Auth resolved PER-REQUEST (genai AuthResolver: async closure ModelIden->AuthData), NOT baked at client build (rig bakes a static header — strictly worse for us). Lazy resolution gives refresh for free. AI SDK does the same via a headers-function closure.
3. Auth scheme routed by TOKEN SHAPE where one provider has multiple modes (Anthropic OAuth-prefix -> Bearer vs x-api-key) — this is rosary-1be3b8 already; LiteLLM + AI SDK both confirm it generalizes.
4. ModelProvider trait: object-safe via #[async_trait] (boxed futures) so the registry holds Box<dyn ModelProvider> keyed by ProviderKind. rosary has a CLOSED provider set so genai's enum-dispatch fits, but the dyn seam is cleaner for the registry + middleware. generate()/stream() as TWO methods over one normalized request/response (AI SDK: streaming is a method, not a flag). Stream = Pin<Box<dyn Stream<Item=Result<ChatStreamEvent>>+Send>> normalizing every provider's SSE (both Rust crates do this).
5. Registry = strict "provider/model" string split -> HashMap<ProviderKind, Box<dyn ModelProvider>>; distinct errors for unknown-provider (list available) vs bad-id-format. A registry-level MIDDLEWARE WRAPPER around every returned model (AI SDK wrapLanguageModel) = THE hook for rosary's feedback-contract/observation logging around every call — both external lenses independently flagged this. Bolt observation (ADR-0010) + the independent-gate here.
6. THE VAULT-PROXY IS A PROVIDER, not a separate thing. AI SDK's "gateway" is just a remote Provider satisfying the same seam (authMethod api-key|oidc, mints short-lived tokens). cloister /vault/proxy (OpenAI-compatible, OIDC, vault-minted bearer per ADR-0042) = a `VaultProxyProvider` behind the identical trait. So N-adapters vs gateway was a false choice: local direct providers AND a vault-proxy gateway coexist in one registry; call sites never know. This is "1:1 at the seam, adapter-shaped inside" made concrete — the vault holds the per-provider Credential bundles; rosary talks one OpenAI-compatible seam. Prefer routing rosary's own calls through vault-proxy so credentials never sit in the rosary process.

ADAPTER METHOD SET (copy LiteLLM BaseConfig, absorb difference behind these): supported_params, map_params (common->native rename, e.g. max_tokens->max_output_tokens), auth_headers/sign_request (SigV4-style escape hatch), complete_url (model-in-path providers), transform_request/transform_response.

AVOID (LiteLLM/rig warts): 137-arm if/elif provider chain (use trait-object map); overloading the model string with special-cases (cohere_chat/anthropic_text/double-openrouter) — keep provider/model strictly 2-part, variant selection in config; untyped credential_values dict; silent drop_params (use a warnings: Vec<Warning> on the response — degrade honestly, not error). Route provider-by-PARSED-HOST never substring (LiteLLM had a GROQ_API_KEY exfil via substring match).

BUILD ORDER: (1) the Credential union + async bearer()/refresh() (buildable now, directly settles the RCA into a type; the vault holds these). (2) ModelProvider trait + one adapter (anthropic or openai-compatible) + the registry + middleware hook. (3) VaultProxyProvider (route enrichment through it). (4) migrate bdr_enrich/capture/decompose off `claude -p` onto ModelProvider.

Deliverable: docs/design/model-provider.md (or an ADR) with the trait sketch + the three-layer framing + the Credential union + the vault-proxy-as-provider decision. Clones for reference at scratchpad/provider-research/{ai,litellm,genai,rig}.

comments.text:
Slice 1 built (2026-07-17): src/credential.rs — the Credential substrate, the RCA (rosary-470270) turned into a type. Registered as `mod credential` in main.rs.

Shipped:
- `Secret` newtype with redacting Debug (`Secret(***)`) — verified by test that neither the secret nor a whole Credential leaks via Debug.
- `Credential` enum: `ApiKey(Secret)` (claude: token-elsewhere) | `OAuth(OAuthCredential)`. Constructors `codex(client_id, refresh)` [public client, secret=None], `gemini(client_id, secret, refresh)` [confidential, secret=Some], `api_key(token)` — the three RCA rows as variants.
- `bearer(&minter, now) -> Secret`: ApiKey returns as-is (never mints); OAuth refresh-if-expired + caches, 60s skew, injected `now` clock. Cache lock is scoped so it's never held across the refresh await.
- `TokenMinter` trait (RPITIT + Send, no async_trait dep) with `HttpMinter` (reqwest POST refresh_token grant, form incl. client_secret only when present) + a `FakeMinter` in tests.
- Endpoints baked: codex=auth.openai.com/api/accounts/oauth/token, gemini=oauth2.googleapis.com/token (RCA-confirmed).

Tests (4, all green, no network): refresh-when-expired-and-cache (mint on 1st call, cache within expiry, re-mint past skew-adjusted expiry — asserts exact mint count); api_key-never-mints; Debug-redaction; codex-public vs gemini-confidential shape. `cargo clippy --bin rsry` clean (public surface #![allow(dead_code)]-annotated as next-slice API surface).

NOT yet: ModelProvider trait + registry + middleware hook (slice 2), VaultProxyProvider (slice 3), migrating bdr_enrich off `claude -p` (slice 4). Uncommitted — awaiting go on commit/PR.

title: Installed git hooks carry no version — a stale hook is indistinguishable from a current one (PR #408's guard protected nothing)
description:
Shipping a hook FIX does nothing until someone manually re-runs `rsry hooks install`. There is no version marker in an installed hook, so a stale one is indistinguishable from a current one — silently.

PROVEN, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. PR #408 added two guards to docs/git-hooks/pre-commit that refuse an export which would wipe the bead record. It merged hours ago. Measured just now:

    docs/git-hooks/pre-commit  (template):  6 guard markers
    .rsry-hooks/pre-commit     (installed): 0 guard markers   <-- BEFORE reinstall

So the guard protected NOTHING. PR #411 (mache pin bump) was authored in a worktree during that window and its diff is `.beads/beads.jsonl +0/-1119` — the ENTIRE bead record zeroed, exactly the rosary-599778 wipe the guard was written to stop. It reached a green PR. `task install` does not run `hooks install`, so installing v0.10.0 did not refresh it either.

Additionally `.git/hooks/pre-commit` still exists and is STALE, inert only because `core.hooksPath` points at `.rsry-hooks/`. If hooksPath were ever unset, the old unguarded hook silently becomes live again.

FIX (user's proposal, and it is the right shape):
1. STAMP A VERSION into every generated hook — e.g. `# rsry-hooks v<crate-version> <template-digest>` inside the rsry-managed marker block. An installed hook must be able to say what it is.
2. `rsry hooks status` compares installed digest vs the compiled-in template and reports STALE loudly, per hook.
3. Make staleness ENFORCED, not advisory. Options: `task install` runs `hooks install`; and/or the hooks themselves warn on stderr when their digest != the installed binary's template; and/or `rsry doctor` fails on drift (doctor already reports binary-vs-repo-vs-service version drift — this is the same class and belongs there).
4. Remove or neutralize the stale `.git/hooks/*` left behind when hooksPath is adopted, so there is no dormant unguarded copy.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS BUG: rosary's guards live in hooks (commit-msg bead-ref contract, close-merged, the export guard, the merge driver). Every one of them silently degrades to "not installed" with no signal. A guard you cannot verify is running is not a guard. This is the same disease as rosary-6832d7 (tooling that does not disclose itself) and the parse_datetime/empty-store class: a missing thing that looks identical to a working one.

comments.text: Root cause confirmed on main after #414: hook installation renders only __RSRY_BIN__; managed blocks have no crate version or template digest. hooks status treats any marker as current, doctor does not inspect hooks, and task install does not reinstall them. Beginning TDD fix against acceptance criteria, including stale dormant .git/hooks handling when core.hooksPath is active.

title: BDR enrichment Phase 1: type-state framework + EnrichedBeadSpec + pipeline skeleton
BDR enrichment Phase 2: symbol resolution via mache MCP (Stage 1)
description:
## What

Implement Stage 1 of the enrichment pipeline: resolve backtick references and symbol names to actual files via mache MCP tools.

### Process

1. Classify each reference in BeadSpec.references:
   - Symbol name (no path separators) -> `mache search(pattern)`
   - File path (contains `/` or known extension) -> `mache list_directory` validation
   - Repo-qualified (`repo:symbol`) -> split, lookup repo in rosary.toml, query target mache
   - URL -> preserve as-is

2. For resolved symbols, expand blast radius:
   - `mache find_callers(symbol)` -> up to 2 hops
   - `mache find_callees(symbol)` -> up to 2 hops
   - Union all file paths into BeadSpec.files

3. Separate test files matching `*_test.*`, `tests/`, `test_*` into test_files

### MCP client

Rosary already has agent-client-protocol. Build a lightweight mache MCP query wrapper:
```rust
pub struct MacheClient { /* MCP endpoint */ }
impl MacheClient {
    pub async fn search(&self, pattern: &str) -> Result<Vec<Symbol>> { ... }
    pub async fn find_callers(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<Vec<Caller>> { ... }
    pub async fn find_callees(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<Vec<Callee>> { ... }
}
```

### Fallback
If mache returns no results for a symbol, mark as Unresolved. Do NOT guess file paths. Continue pipeline with partial scope.

### TDD
1. Test: symbol reference resolves to file path (mock mache response)
2. Test: file path reference validated as-is
3. Test: repo-qualified reference splits correctly
4. Test: unresolved symbol marked in resolution_map
5. Test: blast radius expansion unions callers + callees into files
6. Test: test files separated from source files
7. Test: 2-hop depth limit enforced

### Complexity
O(R * D) where R = references, D = call graph depth. ~200 mache queries per ADR. ~10s latency.

title: BDR enrichment Phase 3: embedding-based dedup via mache + composite scorer
Unified query layer: BeadQuery struct consumed by MCP, CLI, REST, and mache
description:
## Problem
MCP tools, CLI, and future REST API all query beads differently. No shared query abstraction. Adding a filter (priority, type, status) means changing 3 places.

## Solution
One BeadQuery struct:
```rust
struct BeadQuery {
    text: Option<String>,
    priority: Option<u8>,
    issue_type: Option<String>,
    status: Option<String>,
    repo: Option<String>,
    limit: usize,
}
```

Consumed by:

- CLI rsry bead list --priority 0 --type bug
- REST /api/beads?priority=0&type=bug (hosted endpoint)
- mache schema projection (beads as browsable filesystem)

## Bigger picture
Define as OpenAPI spec. mache parses OpenAPI specs and projects them as schemas (check mache/examples for type-based schema definitions). This makes any API a mache data source — GitHub, Linear, Stripe, rosary. Schema-to-schema translation via FCA lattice.

Related: ADR-0006 (declarative tool registry), mache-c0n (schema-driven projection from external type systems)

title: BDR enrichment Phase 4: haiku LLM validation (Stage 3)
description:
## What

Implement Stage 3 of the enrichment pipeline: call Claude Haiku to validate decomposition quality.

### Structured prompt

Send to haiku:
- Bead title, description, file scope, source ADR, source atom kind
- Similar existing beads (from Stage 2)
- Ask for: quality_score (0-1), should_split (bool), split_suggestion, title_revision, overlap_verdict, notes

### Response parsing

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct HaikuValidation {
    pub quality_score: f64,
    pub should_split: bool,
    pub split_suggestion: Option<String>,
    pub title_revision: Option<String>,
    pub overlap_verdict: String,  // "new_work" | "partial_overlap" | "duplicate"
    pub notes: Option<String>,
}
```

### Retry and fallback

- On API error: retry once with exponential backoff
- On malformed JSON: attempt partial parse, fall back to defaults
- On timeout (>5s): skip validation, set quality_score = 0.5, validation_status = Skipped
- On missing API key: skip entirely (pre-flight catches this)

### Cost model

~500 tokens input, ~200 tokens output per bead. At haiku pricing (~$0.25/1M in, ~$1.25/1M out): $0.0004 per bead, $0.004 per ADR. Negligible.

### TDD
1. Test: valid haiku response parsed correctly
2. Test: malformed JSON falls back to defaults
3. Test: quality_score < 0.3 with should_split=true returns split suggestion
4. Test: missing API key skips validation gracefully
5. Test: timeout handling returns neutral score

title: close-merged blind spots: hook needs absolute rsry path + --local should match [bead-id] commits without a recorded pr_url
description:
Observed 2026-07-15 during a 15-PR multi-repo session where every bead was manually closed because BOTH auto-close paths silently no-oped:

1. The rsry-managed post-merge hook guards on `command -v rsry` and swallows everything with `|| true`. In PATH-restricted shells (Claude Code sandboxed Bash, any environment without ~/.local/bin) the hook silently does nothing. Fix: `rsry hooks install` should embed the ABSOLUTE path of the installing binary (it knows argv0) with command -v as fallback, and the failure should at least print one stderr line instead of vanishing.

2. `rsry close-merged --local` reported "0 closed (checked=0)" even with a fresh `[ley-line-open-e5addb] chore(release): … (#229)` squash commit on trunk and the bead open — it only walks open beads with a recorded pr_url event. Beads created via MCP and merged by a session that never calls bead_update with the PR URL are invisible to it. The --local mode's whole point is parsing `[bead-id] … (#N)` from git log; it should close on commit-message evidence alone (the bead id IS in the commit), using pr_url only as enrichment.

Verification: on a repo with an open bead and a trunk squash commit `[<bead-id>] … (#N)` and NO pr_url event, `rsry close-merged --local --repo <repo>` closes the bead; hook fires correctly from a shell without ~/.local/bin on PATH.

comments.text:
Both fixes implemented on branch `fix/close-merged-blind-spots` (worktree off `main`). Strict TDD, not pushed, no PR, bead left open per instruction.

ROOT CAUSE (fix 2 was deeper than "no pr_url"): `run_close_merged --local` already closed on commit evidence without a pr_url (landed in #319). The real reason `[ley-line-open-e5addb] … (#229)` showed `checked=0` was `vcs::valid_bead_id`: it split the bead-id on the FIRST dash and forbade `-` in the prefix, so a multi-segment repo prefix (`ley-line-open`) parsed as prefix="ley"/suffix="line-open-e5addb" and was REJECTED — the release commit never became a closure, so `closures` was empty and the sweep short-circuited before incrementing `checked`. title: BDR enrichment Phase 5: pre-flight checks + materialization + rsry_decompose wiring
description:
## What

Implement the pre-flight check protocol and Stage 4 (materialization), then wire the complete enrichment pipeline into the rsry_decompose MCP tool and rsry decompose CLI.

### Pre-flight checks

```rust
pub struct PreflightReport {
    pub dolt_ok: bool,
    pub adr_atom_count: usize,
    pub repos_resolved: Vec<String>,
    pub repos_unresolved: Vec<String>,
    pub mache_available: bool,
    pub mache_repos: Vec<String>,
    pub embeddings_populated: bool,
    pub embedding_count: usize,
    pub haiku_available: bool,
    pub degraded_stages: Vec<String>,
}

pub async fn preflight(
    adr_path: &str,
    config: &Config,
) -> Result<PreflightReport> { ... }
```

Required checks (abort on failure):
1. Dolt server reachable (SELECT 1)
2. ADR parseable (atoms.len() > 0)
3. Target repo in rosary.toml

Optional checks (degrade gracefully):
4. mache MCP available (get_overview)
5. Embedding index populated (count query)
6. Haiku API key set (env var check)

### Materialization (Stage 4)

- AutoDedup: skip creation, return reference to existing bead
- quality_score < 0.3 AND should_split: return split suggestions, do not create
- Otherwise: create bead via Dolt with all enriched fields

### Wiring

Update `rsry_decompose` MCP tool in serve.rs:
```
Before: parse_adr -> decompose -> create_beads
After:  preflight -> parse_adr -> decompose -> enrich_pipeline -> create_beads
```

Add `--enrich` flag to `rsry decompose` CLI (default: true, `--no-enrich` to skip).

### TDD
1. Test: preflight with Dolt down returns dolt_ok=false
2. Test: preflight with empty ADR returns atom_count=0
3. Test: materialization skips AutoDedup beads
4. Test: materialization creates Allow beads with full enrichment
5. Test: FlagForReview beads created in backlog state with comment
6. Test: rsry_decompose with --no-enrich bypasses pipeline

title: Provider abstraction: add Qwen, Codex/Copilot, and local-vs-remote dispatch
description:
AgentProvider trait already supports Claude, Gemini, ACP. Need to add:

1. QwenProvider — qwen CLI or API. Key angle: ley-line enables interruptibility on hosted instances (checkpoint arena to R2, resume elsewhere). This is a unique selling point for hosted Qwen dispatch.

2. CodexProvider / CopilotProvider — for users on those platforms. Likely wraps their CLI/API with our prompt format.

3. Local vs remote dispatch abstraction — ComputeProvider already has LocalProvider and SpritesProvider. Need to formalize: local dispatch = subprocess on user's machine, remote dispatch = Fly Machine or Sprites VM. Ley-line's arena provides the data bridge: agent writes to arena locally → ley-line syncs to R2 → next agent on remote reads from R2.

The provider config in rosary.toml:
```toml
[dispatch]
provider = "claude"  # or "gemini", "qwen", "codex"
# Future: per-pipeline-stage provider (adversarial review on different model)
adversarial_provider = "gemini"
```

Relates to: ley-line-2a289e (R2 arena backend), ley-line-598681 (BYO-R2)

comments.text:
Proposed decomposition for Codex-ready dispatch isolation, kept under existing thread `agent-dispatch/compute-providers`:

Core abstraction: Rosary should not abstract over provider CLI commands. It should abstract over `AgentRun`s over leased work. Rosary owns bead selection, file-scope overlap, workspace lease, phase/pipeline state, MCP/tool grants, and observation/handoff recording. Provider-specific code owns only harness execution and event translation.

Suggested abstractions:
1. `RunSpec`: bead id, repo, phase agent, prompt/system prompt, model hint, permission profile, MCP/tool grant, workspace lease id/path, chain hash.
2. `WorkspaceLease`: isolated jj/git worktree + branch/bookmark + file-scope overlap lock + cleanup/checkpoint hooks.
3. `AgentHarness`: provider-native interface (`start`, `poll/wait`, `interrupt/kill`, optional `resume`) returning an `AgentRunSession`, not a subprocess command.
4. `AgentEvent`: normalized stream (`started`, `tool_call`, `file_change`, `assistant_message`, `final`, `error`, `usage`) that all harnesses translate into.
5. `ToolGrant`: provider-neutral capabilities mapped to Claude allowedTools, Codex sandbox/approval/MCP config, ACP permission answers, etc.
6. `Observation/Handoff`: append-only result contract for pipeline transitions and audit.

Potential child beads after design approval:
- Design ADR: provider-native AgentHarness + RunSpec + AgentEvent contract.
- Codex seam audit: identify stable Rust API surface from jamestexas/codex (`codex-rs/exec`, app-server-client/protocol/core) and required upstream shim if needed.
- Provider-neutral permission/tool grant mapping (remove Claude-specific assumptions from dispatch surface).
- WorkspaceLease hardening: assert isolated Codex runs cannot overlap/trample file scopes and record chain hash.
- CodexHarness native adapter with fake/in-process tests; explicitly forbid durable `codex exec` shell-out path.
- Live ignored Codex dispatch smoke test proving a bead can run in isolation and produce expected Rosary observations.
- Prompt/agent definition audit for Claude Code assumptions; make agent prompts harness-neutral where appropriate.

title: Design personal operating picture aggregation over observational sources
description:
Problem:
Lectio/Rosary/Mache provide useful observational sources, but the larger personal/project operating picture is still missing. For a personal project there may be no Slack or external org substrate, so aggregation cannot assume team chat as the central narrative layer.

Question to answer:
How should Rosary/Lectio turn many local observations into an actionable bigger picture: current goals, active risks, decisions, stale threads, next best work, and why the system believes those claims?

Constraints:
- Rosary remains authority for beads/dispatch/state.
- Lectio remains witness/recall/evidence graph, not authority.
- Aggregation must work for solo/local projects without Slack.
- Outputs must cite underlying observations/beads/PRs/sessions.
- Aggregates should be derived/regenerable, not hand-maintained summaries.

Likely design direction:
Define an operating-picture layer that periodically derives project-level views from local sources: beads, threads, decades, git/PR history, session transcripts, task check results, and docs/ADRs. It should produce small typed summaries such as current objective, active work, unresolved decisions, risk register, drift alerts, and suggested next actions, each backed by evidence links.

Deliverable:
A design proposal that defines the aggregation primitives, source priority, confidence/evidence model, and how agents consume the operating picture during dispatch/review.

title: EPIC: `rsry review` — agent-native review-and-integration substrate (PR-as-residue, bead-as-stable-identity)
description:
## Problem statement

PRs are the wrong tool for agentic work — they conflate **integration mechanism** with **human review surface**, and they key on `(branch, commit-sha)` which is unstable under rebase/rewrite. The substrate fights agents at every step: comments orphan on force-push, the reasoning trail is lost at squash-merge, the diff-against-base is unreadable past 10 commits.

The deeper truth from a 5-whys descent: the **identity of the work** needs to be stable across implementation rewrites. jj solved this at the VCS layer with stable `change_id`s. Rosary already solved it at the work-item layer with bead IDs. What is missing is a **review-and-integration mode** that uses these primitives as its anchor — instead of borrowing GitHub PR mechanics.

## Decision (the framing)

Add `rsry review` as a first-class rosary mode. It is **not** a wrapper around `gh pr review`. It is the canonical review surface for agent-produced work, with PRs becoming an export view for external collaborators rather than the system of record.

The reviewable unit is `(bead, evidence-chain, change-set)`:
- **bead** — stable identity (bead ID, survives all rewrites; jj `change_id`s of contributing commits are the file-level analogue)
- **evidence-chain** — observations (ADR-0010 lattice), gate-check outputs (Guardrail trait, rosary-cdd522), structured handoffs, the comment audit-trail
- **change-set** — the actual code change, sliced for review (jj-style sliced atomic changes, not one big diff-against-base)

Integration is a **derived consequence** of bead completion + passing gates, not a separate merge-button decision. PRs are produced as an export-view for external eyes (OSS contributors, customers, Linear stakeholders without rosary access).

## Why now

Six already-filed beads are independently reaching for pieces of this:

- rsry-8c31a5 (jj events trigger bead transitions, P0 EPIC) — supplies the change_id primitive
- rosary-a761df (agent-native state-machine substrate, P1 EPIC) — review is one state transition in the bigger machine
- rosary-5ead7e (MCP Apps UI substrate, P2) — the human review surface (React-in-iframe = ideal review-panel renderer)
- rosary-cdd522 (Guardrail trait, P1) — the gate-check substrate
- rosary-b29e00 (enforce closure at agent shutdown, P2) — the integration-completion certificate
- rosary-5d7141 (Linear-escalation-triage EPIC, P1) — Linear as the integration-exterior surface for non-rosary users

This EPIC re-frames the six as **phases of one larger thing** instead of disconnected ideas. None of them should ship in isolation without coherent positioning under this umbrella.

## What rosary already has (lit dimly)

| PR concern | Rosary primitive | State |
|---|---|---|
| Stable identity of work | Bead ID | shipped |
| Reasoning trail | Bead comments + ADR-0010 observation lattice + structured handoffs | shipped |
| Phase-to-phase transfer | dev → staging → prod → feature pipeline | shipped |
| Gate checks | `pipeline.verify` + Guardrail trait | partial (rosary-cdd522 open) |
| Cross-repo dependency | `depends_on` + LinkageStore | shipped |
| VCS-event → state transition | — | open (rsry-8c31a5) |
| Sliced review unit | — | gap |
| Comment durability across rewrites | — | gap |
| Integration / merge mechanism | borrowed from GitHub PR | gap |
| Human review surface | Linear (today) | gap (rosary-5ead7e planned) |

## Scope of this EPIC

In:
- `rsry review` CLI mode + the MCP tool counterpart
- Branch-state inspection backed by jj when available (git fallback)
- Sliced-changes view backed by jj `change_id`
- Evidence-panel composition (bead + observations + gates + handoffs + comments)
- Comment anchoring to bead change_id (durable across implementation rewrites)
- Integration-step delegation (bead reaches Completed → rosary performs the merge)
- MCP Apps render target for the evidence panel (rosary-5ead7e becomes the renderer)

Out of scope (separate EPICs):
- The state-machine substrate itself (rosary-a761df)
- The full MCP Apps host implementation (rosary-5ead7e)
- jj-VCS-driven lifecycle generally (rsry-8c31a5) — this EPIC consumes its outputs

## Acceptance shape

This EPIC is done when:

1. An agent finishing work files a bead with code change + evidence chain.
2. A reviewer (human or another agent) opens `rsry review <bead-id>` and sees: sliced change-set, evidence panel, comment thread, gate status — all anchored to bead/change_id, surviving any subsequent rewrite.
3. When gates pass + review approves, rosary triggers the integration step (jj squash or git merge to base, GH mirror as export view).
4. GitHub PRs are produced as a derived export, not as the system of record. The bead remains the canonical handle.

## Cross-links

- Parent of (will be re-parented under this): rosary-5ead7e, rosary-b29e00, rosary-cdd522, partially rosary-5d7141
- Depends on: rsry-8c31a5 (jj primitive), rosary-a761df (state-machine substrate frame)
- Related design docs: docs/design/capnp-issue-type-substrate.md (PR #216, rosary-5ad4b0) — evidence-chain shape lives here

## Provenance

Filed 2026-06-17 from a conversation that descended through 5-whys on "we hate PRs and they aren't the right tool for the job." User explicitly framed as "review mode in rosary where state of branch and whatnot happens — integrated deeply into the supposed design of rosary." Companion blog post by user (jj-flow framing) in progress.

comments.text:
Framing captured from design thread (2026-07-01): user articulation — 'we need a PR locally; the GitHub PR is just a container.' This is the same primitive as this epic's 'PR-as-residue, bead-as-stable-identity', now with a concrete home: ADR-0015 execution-lineage capsules (merged, PR #251). Mapping:
- bead = stable identity (the durable authority)
- capsule = the LOCAL review + proof + lineage container (handoff chain, verify evidence, decisions) — lives outside the worktree, in the orchestrator store
- GitHub PR = disposable PROJECTION of the capsule for human review; GH stays the safe transport, review contents live locally
Siblings: rosary-d18be8 (PR review history as rosary-owned artifact, GH as projection), rosary-d298a3 (invert CI: PR as review container, task ci as rosary-owned verification). Natural next build after the Codex integration lands. No Linear — GH-only per user.

title: Reap orphaned dolt sql-servers — kill servers not referenced by any registered repo's sql-server.info
description: Fix A from the rosary-a7a668 investigation. rosary spawns 'dolt sql-server' but never reaps them → 36+ orphans, ~6.5GB, one 4GB runaway, contributing to OOM/disk-full. Add a reaper: enumerate running 'dolt sql-server' pids (pgrep -f), compute the set of LIVE/expected pids from every registered repo's .beads/dolt/.dolt/sql-server.info, and SIGTERM the running pids not in that set (orphans from dead sessions / test runs). Safe by default: dry-run reports orphans; an explicit --kill flag actually reaps, so it can't nuke a live server the MCP is using (those are referenced by a repo's sql-server.info and spared). Wire as a CLI command (rsry doctor surfaces the count; a reap subcommand does the kill). Close: dry-run lists orphans; --kill reclaims them; live/registered servers untouched; a unit test over the pid-set diff.

comments.text: VOIDED — wrong approach. The servers aren't orphaned/duplicated: each maps 1:1 to a distinct repo (reuse works). Root cause is RepoPool::from_config (src/pool.rs:94) EAGERLY connecting ALL configured repos on every MCP server start (serve/mod.rs:611, ipc.rs:115), spawning a dolt sql-server per Dolt repo — 34 repos → 34 servers → 6.5GB — even for a single-repo op. A reaper would just clean up after a broken lifecycle. The real fix is LAZY per-repo connect (rosary-<lazy>). Closing this as won't-do.

title: [review P0] `rsry review <bead-id>` — shape-proof MVP composing (bead, evidence, change-set) from existing primitives
description:
## Phase 0 of rosary-ccd5a2 (rsry review substrate)

The minimal shape-proof: `rsry review <bead-id>` shows the reviewer what's there today, without inventing new primitives. Integration delegation, comment anchoring, jj-aware slicing all defer to later phases.

## Behavior

```
$ rsry review rosary-a761df
```

Outputs (text mode; structured JSON via `--json`):

```
BEAD          rosary-a761df  P1 design  open
TITLE         EPIC: Agent-native workflow state-machine substrate

WORKSPACE     ~/.rsry/worktrees/rosary/state-machine-substrate
BRANCH        feat/state-machine-substrate  (3 commits ahead of main)

CHANGE-SET (sliced)
  ─ 7a1f2b  feat(state-machine): scaffold StateMachine trait
  ─ 9e0c44  feat(state-machine): wire pr-autopilot first-experiment policy
  ─ b88aa1  test(state-machine): table-driven policy transitions

EVIDENCE
  observations  : 12 (status, files_touched, dispatch_record × 3, gate × 7)
  gates         : tests=pass clippy=pass coverage=82% doc_drift=clean
  handoffs      : 1 (dev → staging at 2026-06-15T14:22Z)
  comments      : 4

DEPENDS_ON    rosary-e5e8a0 (ADR-0014, open)
BLOCKED_BY    none ready
```

## Acceptance criteria (TDD-shaped)

RED tests must precede each:

- [ ] `rsry review <bead-id>` returns bead summary + workspace + branch + change-set + evidence summary in a single call.
- [ ] Works for beads with an associated workspace and beads without (`WORKSPACE  none — no agent dispatched yet`).
- [ ] Change-set listing reads from git (`git log base..HEAD --oneline`); jj support deferred to Phase 1.
- [ ] Evidence summary aggregates from existing rosary store: observation count by field, latest gate result per Guardrail, handoff count, comment count.
- [ ] `--json` output validates against a documented schema (capnp candidate).
- [ ] Tests assert deterministic output ordering — reviewers must see the same thing across runs unless state changed.
- [ ] 100% line coverage on the new module.

## What this MVP intentionally does NOT do

- No comment anchoring (Phase 1)
- No jj-aware change_id slicing (Phase 2 — depends on rsry-8c31a5)
- No integration delegation / merge action (Phase 3)
- No MCP Apps rendering (Phase 4 — depends on rosary-5ead7e)

title: jj workspace isolation for all dispatch — CC worktrees bypass rosary's jj support
description:
Critical: Two isolation systems conflict. Rosary workspace.rs creates jj workspaces (preferred). Claude Code --worktree creates git worktrees at .claude/worktrees/. The conductor dispatches claude -p without --worktree (runs in-place). None of these paths use jj workspaces consistently.

Problems:
1. CC git worktrees don't have Dolt access (rsry MCP fails)
2. Stale .claude/worktrees/ accumulate with broken MCP configs
3. jj change IDs from vcs.rs scanning don't map to CC worktree branches
4. The bead.jj_change_id field is never populated by CC-dispatched agents

The fix: conductor should create jj workspaces via rosary workspace.rs BEFORE dispatching the agent. The agent runs inside the jj workspace (cd to workspace path). jj handles isolation, not CC's --worktree. This means:
- Conductor calls rsry to create workspace (jj workspace add)
- Dispatches claude -p with cd to the workspace path
- On completion, jj commit + bookmark the work
- jj workspace forget to clean up

This is what workspace.rs already does for rsry run. The conductor just needs to use it instead of relying on CC's git worktrees.

Ref: matthewsanabria.dev/posts/running-jujutsu-with-claude-code-hooks/

comments.text:
Design review complete. The bead's framing ("conductor runs in-place") is outdated — both dispatch paths already create jj workspaces via Workspace::create(isolate=true). The real bugs are:

1. **MCP dispatch leaks workspaces**: tool_dispatch() drops AgentHandle (and its Workspace) at function return. No Drop impl → orphaned .rsry-workspaces/ dirs.
2. **jj_change_id never populated**: Workspace::jj_commit() and jj_bookmark() exist but are never called. on_pass() goes straight to cleanup_workspace() without checkpointing.
3. **Workspace changes destroyed on cleanup**: jj workspace forget deletes workspace changes before they land in the main repo. No squash/merge step.
4. **MCP dispatch has no verify/advance cycle**: tool_dispatch() is fire-and-forget. No completion detection, no verification, no pipeline advancement, no cleanup.

Fix design: (1) checkpoint before cleanup (jj_commit + jj_bookmark + squash to main), (2) MCP dispatch lifecycle via reconciler enqueue or background polling, (3) startup sweep for orphaned workspaces.

title: Dynamic prompt enhancement: agent .md files as templates, bead-specific context injection
description:
## Problem
Agent prompts (agents/*.md) are static. task_framing() in dispatch.rs picks a hardcoded string per role. The prompt doesn't adapt to the specific bead — a dev-agent reviewing a 3-line rename gets the same prompt as one tackling a cross-file refactor.

## Proposal
Apply the enhance-prompt pattern (skills.sh/google-labs-code/stitch-skills/enhance-prompt) to agent dispatch:

1. **Assess**: analyze bead scope — files, complexity, community, callers/callees
2. **Integrate**: pull structural context from mache (like enhance-prompt pulls from DESIGN.md)
3. **Enhance**: fill agent .md template with bead-specific details. "Fix this function" → "Refactor `fn X` in `file:line` — 3 callers, complexity: high, community: `parse`"
4. **Structure**: consistent output schema — CONTEXT, SCOPE, TOOLS, CONSTRAINTS blocks

Agent .md files become templates with slots. Enhancement step fills slots from mache + bead metadata. Template defines reign (tools, zoom level). Enhancement fills scope (specific code, structural context).

## Progression
- PR #17: static task_framing() per agent type
- This bead: dynamic prompt enhancement per bead
- Future: scope/reign derived from hierarchy position

## Reference
- enhance-prompt skill: https://skills.sh/google-labs-code/stitch-skills/enhance-prompt
- gstack /plan-eng-review: architecture-aware prompt enrichment

title: spawn_detached: launchd-spawned claude fails with "Not logged in" (auth not propagating)
description:
## Real-world data point

Symptom observed 2026-05-11 during cloister-be36ea dispatch (via the new server-side spawn from PR #200):

- Worker spawned at PID 33960 ✓
- Exited 61ms later with `result: "Not logged in · Please run /login"`
- `total_cost_usd: 0`, no work attempted
- Process gone, worktree empty, bead stuck at `dispatched`

The new server-side spawn (rosary-748f07) works at the process level. The failure is one level deeper: the spawned `claude -p` inherits an env that lacks the Claude OAuth credentials, hits Keychain access (denied for launchd children), and bails immediately.

This is the **exact failure class** the existing memory `feedback_dispatch_http_env.md` named ("MCP HTTP dispatch can't spawn claude — launchd env too restricted. CLI dispatch works.") — the cause is well-understood; the new spawn path just didn't account for it.

## Root cause

`src/dispatch/providers.rs::resolve_auth_token(work_dir)` checks (in priority order):

1. `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var
2. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var
3. `.envrc` in `work_dir`
4. `.envrc` in the git repo root
5. `dispatch.anthropic_api_key` in `~/.rsry/config.toml`

When rosary runs as a launchd service:
- env vars #1 / #2 are not set (launchd plist doesn't have them)
- `.envrc` files exist in dev checkouts but launchd's cwd at start is `/` or whatever the plist says, so the worktree-relative lookups can succeed IF the worktree has a `.envrc` — but for newly-created dispatch worktrees in `~/.rsry/worktrees/<repo>/<bead>/` there's no `.envrc`
- The git repo-root fallback (#4) requires the bead worktree to be inside a git repo with `.envrc` at its root; works for self-hosted dev checkouts, may not for wasteland-cached remote clones
- `~/.rsry/config.toml`'s `dispatch.anthropic_api_key` is the operator-explicit fallback (#5) — works if set, often unset on dev machines that rely on Keychain locally

When all 5 fail, no `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set on the spawned child. macOS Claude CLI falls back to Keychain OAuth — but launchd-spawned children can't read the user's Keychain → "Not logged in".

## Possible fixes (pick one or combine)

1. **At spawn time, refuse to spawn if no token resolved AND rosary itself is running under launchd**. Surface a clear error: "no OAuth token available; set `dispatch.anthropic_api_key` in `~/.rsry/config.toml` or add `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to your launchd plist." Cleanest from a user-experience standpoint — fails loudly at MCP request time instead of after the worker silently dies.

2. **Auto-populate the launchd plist with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`** at `task install` time, reading from the operator's current shell env. The user-facing tradeoff: token now lives in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.rosary.serve.plist` (filesystem-readable to the user).

3. **Make the dispatch process query the user's Keychain via a helper binary that has TCC privileges** (signed with the right entitlements). Heavier engineering; closer to "correct" but a much bigger change.

The deadletter sweep landing in this branch (rosary-c33e62 / c3034b) catches the symptom — `cloister-be36ea` would have moved to `dead_letter` on the next reconciler iteration after the 61ms death — but doesn't fix the root cause.

## Reproduction

1. Have rosary running as a launchd service (`com.rosary.serve` plist active)
2. From an MCP client (CC, conductor, etc.), call `rsry_dispatch` on any bead in any registered repo
3. Observe: response includes `pid` + `stream` (server-side spawn worked)
4. `head .rsry-stream.jsonl` → `"result": "Not logged in · Please run /login"`, `duration_ms < 200`
5. Bead stays at `dispatched` (without the deadletter sweep) or moves to `dead_letter` (with it)

## Refs

- `feedback_dispatch_http_env.md` — pre-existing memory naming this class
- `src/dispatch/providers.rs:371-420` — `resolve_auth_token` priority chain
- rosary-748f07 / PR #200 — introduced the server-side spawn that surfaces this
- rosary-c3034b — deadletter design that catches the symptom
- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.rosary.serve.plist` — the launchd env this spawn inherits

comments.text: RESOLVED by PR #226 (rosary-b1495c), merged 2026-06-23. Root cause was exactly as described here — spawned claude -p inherits an env lacking OAuth creds; Keychain denied for launchd children. #226 made spawn_detached (the MCP/server-side path) inject auth+endpoint via resolve_launch_env, with a loud warning on no-creds. Verified live this session: a real rsry_dispatch of a throwaway bead ran end-to-end on the Max account (model claude-opus-4-8, is_error:false, 0× "Not logged in"). Closing as done.

description:
Implements the schema and surfacing layer for ADR-0009 (cross-repo linkage). Deferred behind mache-iegm landing — federation pattern lands first; this layers on top with the modal calculus.

ALTER TABLE cross_repo_deps:
  - evidence_tier ENUM('asserted','derived','conjectured') NOT NULL
  - source        TEXT NOT NULL

## Surfacing

2. CLI: rsry bead link <from> <to> --cross-repo --type blocks

- cargo test -p rosary linkage::ttl_janitor passes (sweep demotes stale Derived edges)

title: First-time setup story: rename + relocate GETTING_STARTED, standardize on brew + Brewfile, fix tap auth friction
description:
## User framing (2026-05-21)

> "we need to file a bead for rosary wrt first time setup vs 'getting-started.md' and the same is true for other repos as we need a good way to install deps on Mac at least (brew? ʅ(´⊙◞⊱◟⊙｀)ʃ)"

The shrug is load-bearing — brew is the *current* path but not obviously the right one. This bead does the rosary-specific work AND opens the cross-repo design question.

## Current state (rosary, audited 2026-05-21)

- `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` — 321 lines. Nested under `docs/`, **underscore**-named. Diverges from mache + cloister convention (`GETTING-STARTED.md` at root, **hyphen**-named).
- README.md — doesn't surface a "first 5 lines" quick start; readers have to find their way to `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` manually.
- Brew path EXISTS in the doc but assumes the reader knows about `agentic-research/tap` (private, needs SSH or PAT — see homebrew-tap/README.md for the auth dance).
- Dep list in the doc is *manual*: rustup, task, capnp, dolt, jj, fuse-t — each one a separate `brew install` line. No `Brewfile` to `brew bundle install` from.

## Current state (ecosystem-wide, audited 2026-05-21)

| Repo | Getting-started doc | Location | Naming |
|---|---|---|---|
| **rosary** | ✅ | `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` | `GETTING_STARTED.md` (underscore) |
| **mache** | ✅ | root (`GETTING-STARTED.md`) | `GETTING-STARTED.md` (hyphen) |
| **cloister** | ✅ | root (`GETTING-STARTED.md`) | `GETTING-STARTED.md` (hyphen) |
| **ley-line-open** | ❌ | — | — |
| **crumb** | ❌ | — | — |
| **signet** | ❌ | — | — |

`~/remotes/art/homebrew-tap/Formula/` has formulas for: `rosary.rb`, `leyline.rb`, `mache.rb`. Missing: crumb, signet, ley-line-open (different from `leyline`?). Tap is **private** — every new contributor has to set up SSH access or a PAT before `brew tap` works.

## Proposal for rosary (this bead's scope)

### Phase 1: rosary-side fixes (no design dependency)

1. **Rename + relocate**: `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` → `GETTING-STARTED.md` (root, hyphen). Match mache + cloister. Update any cross-links (rosary's CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md).
2. **README quick-start**: top of README gets a 5-line block — `brew tap agentic-research/tap && brew install rosary && rsry status`. Link to `GETTING-STARTED.md` for the deep version.
3. **Ship a `Brewfile`** in repo root declaring runtime + build deps (rustup, task, capnp, dolt, jj, fuse-t). One command from there: `brew bundle install`. Replaces the line-by-line `brew install` walkthrough in the current doc; the doc just says `brew bundle install` and points at the file.
4. **Distinguish "use rosary" vs "develop rosary"** — the current doc front-loads the build toolchain (rustup, capnp). For users who only want `brew install rosary && rsry`, that's irrelevant friction. Split the doc into "Use" (brew install path, 3 commands) and "Develop" (build toolchain, dolt config, codesign).

### Phase 2: design question (cross-cutting)

The cross-repo question is: **is `brew + Brewfile + private tap` the right answer for the ecosystem, or is there a better Mac-first tool?**

Options to weigh in a separate design bead (NOT this one):

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **brew + Brewfile** (current) | Mac-native, low LoE — formulas already exist | Private tap = auth friction; no language-version pinning |
| **mise** (asdf successor) | Pinned tool versions per repo; works across languages | New dep to install before any other deps |
| **nix flake** | Reproducible, ecosystem-friendly | Steep learning curve; nix-on-mac story is rough |
| **devcontainer** | Cloud-portable | Overkill for "I just want to run the CLI on my laptop" |
| **Public tap + `brew install`** | One-line setup | Requires making the tap public (security review) |

My quick read: ship Phase 1 (cleanup that doesn't depend on the choice above), then file a separate design bead to decide Phase 2. The shrug means we haven't decided — don't pretend we have.

## Cross-repo follow-ons (to file as sibling beads, not in scope here)

1. **ley-line-open**: add `GETTING-STARTED.md` + `Brewfile`. Confirm `leyline.rb` formula in homebrew-tap actually corresponds to ll-open (naming drift: `leyline` vs `ley-line-open`).
2. **crumb**: add `GETTING-STARTED.md` + `Brewfile` + formula in homebrew-tap.
3. **signet**: same — and signet is identity-shaped so the install path probably has more dependencies (signet-agent, OS keyring access).
4. **homebrew-tap**: decide public vs private (security review needed if going public). Document the SSH+PAT auth path more cleanly until then.
5. **template-go / template-rust**: those existing templates should ship a `Brewfile` + `GETTING-STARTED.md` skeleton so new tools start with the standard surface (links to cloister-c1b77e, the tools-repo template work).

## Files

- `GETTING-STARTED.md` (new, root) — replacing `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md`
- `Brewfile` (new, root)
- `README.md` — add quick-start block
- `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` — delete (or leave a one-line redirect for 1 week, then delete)

## Severity / priority

P2. Real onboarding friction but no production impact. Phase 1 is small (~half a day); Phase 2 needs a design conversation before any code.

comments.text:
## 2026-05-21 — scope tightening from user

Two constraints landed after the initial filing:

### Constraint 1: zero local deps ideally

Original bead leaned toward "ship a Brewfile listing rustup + task + capnp + dolt + jj + fuse-t". User wants the opposite — **a brew install with zero local toolchain deps needed.**

This is achievable because rosary's formula (`homebrew-tap/Formula/rosary.rb`) already downloads a pre-built binary (`rsry-darwin-arm64`) — no rustup/cargo/capnp needed at install time. The only remaining runtime dep is **dolt** (rosary requires it for cross-repo orchestration).

Two ways to honor zero-deps:

- **Option A (preferred):** Default rosary to SQLite-only mode (`bead_sqlite.rs` exists, `bead_dolt.rs` is the alternative). Single-repo bead operations work fully on SQLite — no dolt needed. Dolt becomes opt-in via `rsry enable --dolt` for users who want cross-repo orchestration / web UI.
- **Option B:** Have the formula declare `depends_on "dolt"` so brew installs it automatically. User still doesn't run `brew install dolt` themselves, but dolt does land on disk.

A is the right answer — matches the user framing exactly ("zero" deps, not "we install them for you"). B is the fallback if A is more refactor than this bead's worth.

The Brewfile idea is therefore deprioritized — there's nothing for it to install if the formula's pre-built binary covers the runtime. Keep `Brewfile` as an *optional* dev-toolchain bundle for the "Develop rosary" path (rustup, capnp, task), but it's not the first-time-setup surface.

### Constraint 2: scope = public repos + ley-line

Cross-repo follow-on table corrected:

| Repo | Public? | In scope today? |
|---|---|---|
| rosary | public | ✅ this bead |
| mache | public | ✅ (already has GETTING-STARTED.md; needs zero-deps audit) |
| cloister | public | ✅ (already has GETTING-STARTED.md; needs zero-deps audit) |
| ley-line-open | public | ✅ (no GETTING-STARTED yet; needs one) |
| ley-line | private | ✅ user explicit include |
| crumb | private | ❌ not today |
| signet | private | ❌ not today |

ley-line-open also has the naming/formula question: homebrew-tap has `leyline.rb`, but the public repo is `ley-line-open`. Need to confirm whether `leyline.rb` corresponds to ll-open or to the private ley-line repo. If it's the private repo, ll-open needs its own formula.

### Revised Phase 1 (rosary)

1. Rename + relocate `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` → `GETTING-STARTED.md` (unchanged).
2. README quick-start: `brew tap agentic-research/tap && brew install rosary && rsry status` — that should be the whole first-time path. If SQLite-only default lands, this works zero-deps; if not, mention `brew install dolt` (one extra line, still one-shot).
3. Audit + decide SQLite-default vs dolt-depends_on (Option A vs B above). Probably needs a sibling design bead to confirm SQLite mode is fully functional for single-repo use.
4. Brewfile becomes "developing rosary" (optional), not "using rosary" (default).
5. Update the doc to reflect the split: "Use" path = 1 command; "Develop" path = the existing 30-line walkthrough.

Wrap handoff JSON in a DSSE envelope (https://github.com/secure-systems-lab/dsse) with in-toto Statement format. Zero DSSE/in-toto code exists in rosary today.

title: APAS L2: provision agent bridge certs during dispatch
description:
Dispatched agents commit with `git commit` but don't sign commits. For L2, agents need signet bridge certs provisioned during workspace setup.

Need to:
1. During dispatch workspace creation, call `signet auth register --agent {agent_name} --scope {bead_scope}` to get an agent-scoped bridge cert

title: Detect and heal rsry MCP service binary drift after local builds
description:
Dogfood finding: when Codex/agents work on rosary, the repo may contain a newer `target/release/rsry` or source tree than the long-running launchd HTTP MCP service is actually running. Today `task install` kickstarts the service, but agents have to remember to run it and cannot easily see drift from MCP itself.

Desired behavior: expose a deterministic way to compare running MCP server identity against the installed/local binary (version, build hash, path, mtime or content hash), and either warn loudly or provide a safe auto-heal path that restarts/kickstarts onto the latest installed binary. This should compose with launchd and not require shelling out from MCP request handling unless an explicit installer/service-management path owns that side effect.

Close condition: add tests for the drift detector/contract and verify with `env RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo test --bin rsry <mcp-binary-drift-test>` plus `env RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER= task check`.

comments.text: Filed from Codex dogfood after PR #315: `task install` is the manual recovery path today. After reinstall/kickstart, direct HTTP MCP `initialize` returned `serverInfo.buildHash: cba0745`, proving the daemon moved from the old main hash to the current PR commit. The gap remains that agents/users must remember to run install and compare this manually; this bead should make drift detection/healing deterministic.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Concrete drift-detection design (from a live incident this session: repo hit 0.4.0 while the installed + running rsry stayed 0.3.0, so the :8383 MCP server served a stale binary and the session never saw current tools).

Two deterministic surfaces, no Actions:
1. post-merge hook check — when `git pull` lands a Cargo.toml version bump, compare `rsry --version` to the repo version and warn (`⚠ rsry X installed, repo bumped to Y — run task install`). The pull that carries the release IS the trigger. Optionally offer auto-install.
2. `rsry doctor` — reports the full runtime-truth picture: installed binary version+SHA vs repo HEAD version vs the running launchd service's reported version (via a /version health endpoint), flags any mismatch, and prints the fix. This is the 'observable + drift-detectable' half of this bead.

Permanent cure is cloister (bundle lifecycle re-resolves from server.json packages[].oci, #323/rosary-4fe10a) — these two are the pre-cloister mitigation.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: Auto-closed by rsry close-merged --local: PR #329 merged

acceptance_criteria: A deterministic test proves rsry can detect when the running MCP service identity differs from the installed/local binary identity, and the operator-facing output tells agents exactly how to heal it or auto-heals via the sanctioned install/service path.

title: Investigate headless AskUserQuestion handling via PreToolUse hooks for claude agent provider
description: Claude 2.1.85 introduced the ability for `PreToolUse` hooks to satisfy `AskUserQuestion` by returning `updatedInput` alongside `permissionDecision: "allow"`. Since `rosary` dispatches agents headlessly via `claude -p`, we should investigate using a `PreToolUse` hook to automatically handle or pipe AskUserQuestion to the Dolt database/UI, preventing the headless agent process from hanging while waiting for user input.

title: Agent escalation: structured @ask mechanism to break infinite loops
description:
Agents loop indefinitely on hard problems (race conditions, subtle bugs) without a stopping point. Need a structured escalation mechanism where an agent can tag in a specialist (@reviewer, @adversarial-reviewer, @architect) via the orchestrator.

Escalation format (write to file, then re-read):
1. Problem statement citing code/paths/deps
2. What you think the cause is
3. What you've tried
4. Desired end goal
5. Cite sources for all above

Implementation options:
- MCP tool: rsry_escalate that creates a bead with structured fields + dispatches specialist
- Agent rule in GOLDEN_RULES.md: "after N failed attempts, escalate don't loop"
- Handoff variant: agent writes structured escalation file, orchestrator reads and dispatches

This is the inter-agent communication primitive — agents today can only talk to the orchestrator, not to each other. The @ask mechanism lets them request help from a specific perspective.

comments.text:
Escalation routing follows the agent hierarchy — @ask always goes UP one level:

- dev-agent @ask → feature-agent (feature orchestrator handles most escalations)
- staging-agent @ask → feature-agent
- feature-agent @ask → orchestrator (reconciler)
- orchestrator @ask → human

So @ask is not a global broadcast — it's a structured "I'm stuck, hand this to my supervisor." The feature-agent becomes the primary escalation handler since it already has cross-file context within a repo. Only truly cross-repo or architectural questions bubble up to the orchestrator/human.

title: Make PR review history a Rosary-owned artifact, with GitHub as projection
description: Design how Rosary should preserve PR review history without treating GitHub as the source of truth. Motivation from PR #247 workflow: Codex fresh-eyes review ran locally via `pr-review-kit` and was recorded as a bead comment, while GitHub PR metadata/checks live separately. Desired model: Rosary stores review artifacts (reviewer identity/agent, PR/work ref, commit SHA reviewed, matrix findings, verification commands, verdict, timestamps, links to handoffs/dispatch records) as first-class observations or review records; GitHub comments/reviews are optional projections for collaboration, not canonical state. Must preserve history even if GitHub threads are resolved/edited/deleted or the repo moves. Relates to ADR-0010 observation lattice and capnp issue-type substrate cross-source drift notes.

title: Crate metadata + README hygiene: workspace inheritance, publish gates, tool-count drift, badges
description:
