title: Make Taskfile the single source of truth for verification gates
description:
Taskfile should be the executable source of truth for local and CI verification. Today the contract is split:

- `task all` composes `fmt`, `check`, `lint`, `test`.
- `task ci` redefines raw `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` inline and skips semgrep wrapper behavior from `task lint`.
- GitHub Actions runs `task check` and `task test` as separate jobs, while pre-commit independently runs its own hooks.
- Docs tell agents/humans to run several different combinations (`task check`, `task test`, `task lint`, `task all`).

Desired invariant: Taskfile target definitions own the semantics; CI and agents invoke named Taskfile targets only. Composite targets should be explicit and non-duplicative, e.g. `task check` as the fast compile gate, `task lint` as fmt/clippy/semgrep, `task test` as tests, and a single higher-level gate (`task verify` or `task ci`) that composes those named targets instead of reimplementing raw cargo commands. If `lint`, `verify`, `check`, and `ci` differ, the differences must be intentional, documented, and mechanically composed.

Close condition: add/update Taskfile + GitHub Actions + docs/tests so the verification contract is centralized in Taskfile and CI invokes the composite Taskfile target(s). Verify with `task --list`, `env RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER= task check`, and the chosen composite gate (`task ci` or `task verify`).

Then made `task check` the canonical composed gate (`taskfile-contract`, `compile`, `lint`, `test`), made `task ci` and `task all` aliases, collapsed GitHub Actions to install prerequisites then `task check`, and updated README/design docs. Verified with `task --list`, `bash scripts/check-taskfile-contract.sh`, and escalated `env RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER= task check` passing end-to-end (contract, compile, fmt/clippy/semgrep, unit tests, CLI integration, IPC Docker e2e, note-skill routing).

title: bead_link auto-route mis-identifies legacy `rsry-` prefixed beads as cross-repo
description:
## Symptom

Linking `rosary-ccd5a2 depends_on rsry-8c31a5` while passing `repo_path: /Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/rosary` still produces `{"cross_repo": "rsry/rsry-8c31a5", "action": "added", "evidence_tier": "asserted"}` — the auto-router treats the `rsry-` prefix as a separate "rsry" repo even though `repo_path` was explicit and `rsry-8c31a5` actually lives in `rosary` (confirmed by `rsry_bead_search` returning `"repo": "rosary"` for it).

## Why this matters

There is no registered repo called "rsry" — it is a **legacy prefix** from before the project rename to "rosary". A non-trivial number of older beads carry it: `rsry-8c31a5` (jj events EPIC, P0, open), `rsry-9b0d64` (pause/play arch, P0), `rsry-988505` (feature branch lifecycle, P0), `rsry-68f6a9` (dispatch by bead ID, P0), `rsry-8cbbe7`, `rsry-8c9fab`, `rsry-8c7af6`, `rsry-8c585f`, `rsry-8cde66` (all rosary repo). Any depends_on edge into these gets stored as a cross-repo asserted link to a phantom "rsry" repo — LinkageStore traversal will fail to resolve the target.

## Repro

```
rsry_bead_link(
  repo_path: "/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/rosary",
  id: "rosary-ccd5a2",
  depends_on: "rsry-8c31a5"
)
# expected: same-repo dep
# actual:   cross_repo: "rsry/rsry-8c31a5"
```

## Root cause (hypothesis)

The auto-route prefix-rule in `LinkageStore` derives target repo from `bead_id.split('-')[0]` without consulting either the explicit `repo_path` arg or a "this prefix is an alias for that repo" table. Explicit `repo_path` should override prefix auto-detection.

## Fix shape

Two complementary fixes:

1. **Honor explicit args.** When `repo_path` (or `scope`) is provided AND the dep target is locatable in that repo's `.beads/`, do not auto-route cross-repo — just write a same-repo dep. The cross-repo path is for when the dep target genuinely cannot be found locally.
2. **Prefix-alias table.** Allow config-level registration of legacy prefix aliases: `[bead_id_prefixes] rsry = "rosary"` in `~/.rsry/config.toml`. The auto-router consults this before treating an unknown prefix as a new repo.

Pick (1) as the must-fix; (2) is a nice-to-have to prevent the same problem if anyone else has legacy-prefixed beads.

## Acceptance

TDD-shaped:

- [ ] RED: integration test where `bead_link(repo_path=rosary, id=rosary-X, depends_on=rsry-Y)` asserts same-repo dep + fails before fix.
- [ ] GREEN: explicit-arg path takes precedence over prefix auto-detect.
- [ ] Regression: cross-repo case (`bead_link(repo_path=rosary, id=rosary-X, depends_on=cloister-Y)` where `cloister-Y` is NOT in rosary's local store) still routes cross-repo via LinkageStore.
- [ ] All previously-mis-routed legacy `rsry-`-prefixed deps in the linkage table get a one-shot migration to same-repo (script + manual review).

## Discovery

While filing dependencies for `rosary-ccd5a2` (review-substrate EPIC) → `rsry-8c31a5` (jj-events EPIC) on 2026-06-17. Caught in MCP tool output. Filed immediately rather than leaving as silent inconsistency.

## Cross-links

- Touches scope-abstraction saga work (rosary-b5da2f closed) — the same `LinkageStore` surface.
- Related to `rosary-cd5d2a` (review Phase 0 MVP) which will want correct dep traversal to show evidence panels.

title: Harden feedback contract with an independent gate — self-report never closes a bead (grok-build goal-verifier pattern)
description:
From the grok-build recon (2026-07-16). Their agent's `update_goal{completed:true}` BLOCKS on an adversarial classifier verdict (Achieved/NotAchieved{attempt,max}/Stalled/Blocked) — the model's self-report never ends the goal. Plus a regex stop-detector (goal_stop_detector.rs) that catches premature bail phrasing mid-turn ("unable to proceed", "VERDICT: PASS", "ready for review") and re-nudges while todos are pending.

This is a stronger version of rosary's feedback contract (PipelineEngine::dispatch_left_feedback downgrades pass→retry when no native feedback run-event exists at/after run start). Ours already refuses to trust a bare pass; the grok pattern adds: (1) an independent verdict gate rather than presence-of-event, (2) a cheap regex bail-phrase detector as a first-line nudge before the expensive classifier.

Scope: evaluate folding a bail-phrase detector into the verify tiers (src/reconcile/verify.rs) as a pre-classifier nudge, and consider whether the adversarial `review` tier verdict should be structured (Achieved/NotAchieved/Stalled/Blocked) rather than pass/fail so retry vs deadletter decisions get more signal. Do NOT copy grok code (see the exfil caveat — read-only repo); reimplement the pattern.

Ref: grok goal.rs:1937, goal_stop_detector.rs. Relates to rosary-0908bc (feedback contract), the artifact steal-list.

title: Scoping agent: LLM pre-dispatch validation (5 whys as pipeline phase -1)
description:
Scoping agent: dispatch-time enrichment via search + analyze + plan.

Every dispatched agent gets a pre-flight enrichment step (haiku, ~30s):

1. **Web search**: relevant APIs, docs, known issues for the bead's domain
2. **Mache analysis**: repo topology, file call graph, related code
3. **Structured plan**: steps with exit criteria, injected into dispatch prompt

This prevents the 'guess and deploy' anti-pattern where agents trial-and-error against production because they didn't check the API docs first.

Example failure this prevents: Clerk auth agent tried sso() (wrong API), then authenticateWithRedirect with wrong params, then checked SDK version, then found the right API. 3 prod deploys wasted. A 30-second haiku search would have found 'SDK 4.73, use authenticateWithRedirect({strategy, redirectUrl, redirectUrlComplete})' immediately.

Implementation:
- agents/scoping-agent.md with ReadOnly perms + web search + mache
- Runs as pipeline phase 0 (before dev-agent)
- Output: enriched prompt JSON with search results + file map + plan
- dev-agent receives enriched prompt, not raw bead description
- Costs ~$0.01 per dispatch (haiku). Saves $0.50+ per bad dispatch.

The scoping agent is model-agnostic — it enriches the prompt regardless of which provider executes the work (claude, gemini, qwen)."

title: Include commit SHA/jj change_id in Handoff::chain_hash()
description:
Handoff::chain_hash() currently hashes phase, from_agent, bead_id, summary, files_changed, and previous_chain_hash — but NOT the commit SHA or jj change_id. This means the provenance chain doesn't bind to the actual artifact produced.

Fix: Add commit SHAs from Work.commits to chain_hash(). Also include jj_change_id from Vcs when available (jj change IDs survive rebase, making them more stable provenance anchors than git SHAs).

This is an APAS L2 prerequisite — the hash chain must bind to artifacts, not just metadata.

title: Per-dispatch bridge cert: rosary requests signet cert for each agent session
description:
Currently rosary dispatches agents with no cryptographic identity binding. For APAS L2, each dispatch should:

1. Request a short-lived bridge cert from signet authority (per-dispatch, 5-min lifetime)
2. Pass the cert to the agent's environment (for git commit signing)
3. Record the cert fingerprint in the dispatch manifest (Identity.signet_cert_hash)
4. Include cert fingerprint in the APAS predicate (runDetails.orchestrator.identity)

This creates the identity chain: user's master key → orchestrator bridge cert → agent session → signed commits.

Depends on: signet-353e7e (CA bundle deploy) for verifiers to validate the certs.

comments.text: Reviewed in context of multi-tenant serve-path work (2026-03-25). This bead is the right long-term identity anchor — per-dispatch bridge certs bind user+repo+bead cryptographically, replacing the string-based user_id scoping we just landed in PR #123. Short-term path: wire CallerIdentity::User(id) → ReconcilerConfig.user_id in serve.rs. Long-term path: cert CN replaces the string. These are sequential, not competing.

title: DSSE-sign handoffs with Ed25519 (APAS L2 completion)
description:
Wrap handoff JSON in a DSSE (Dead Simple Signing Envelope) signed with the orchestrator's Ed25519 key via ley-line-sign. This makes handoffs tamper-evident to EXTERNAL observers.

Format:
- payloadType: application/vnd.in-toto+json
- payload: base64(handoff JSON wrapped in in-toto Statement/v1)
- signatures: [{keyid: sha256(pubkey), sig: ed25519(payload)}]

Signing uses ley-line's Rust CMS crate. Consider a thin Rust → Go FFI bridge via signet-sign, or call ley-line-sign as a subprocess.

This is the final piece of APAS L2: attestations exist (L1) AND are cryptographically signed (L2).

title: Report upstream: beads `bd init` .gitignore template omits .beads-credential-key
description:
UPSTREAM-REPORT (tracking, not a rosary code fix). The `beads` CLI (`bd`, Homebrew formula `beads` v1.0.0) generates a 32-byte (256-bit) machine-local secret at .beads/.beads-credential-key on init, but the .gitignore template `bd init` writes does NOT ignore it — so it sits untracked-but-uncovered and a stray `git add -A` would commit a credential. Confirmed across ~25 art repos: the file only exists in assay/mache/rosary (NO leaks anywhere; nothing committed or in history). mache and rosary already carry the rule; older inits (incl. assay's original) don't.

ROOT CAUSE: upstream in the `beads` tool's bundled .gitignore template — not rosary/assay code. Durable fix already applied locally: `.beads/.beads-credential-key` added to ~/.gitignore_global (covers every repo, present + future, any branch) + assay's .beads/.gitignore on main (assay-lqr) + a .git/info/exclude belt-and-suspenders in assay.

ACTION: report to the upstream `beads` maintainers (Homebrew formula `beads`) to add `.beads-credential-key` to the .gitignore template `bd init` writes, so the fix lands at the source for all clones/machines/users. Then the latent gap in the other ~22 art repos (no credential file present today → no current exposure) closes on re-init. Severity: low (mitigated locally, no leak), but worth upstreaming.

title: Session continuation: capture + resume session IDs across retries and phases
description:
Dispatched agents start cold on every retry and phase transition. claude -p supports --resume SESSION_ID to continue with full context from a previous attempt. The conductor's AgentWorker has session_id in state and AcpClient.resume() exists, but the CLI fallback doesn't use them.

Fix: (1) capture session_id from claude -p JSON output on first dispatch, (2) store in Pipeline history, (3) pass --resume on retry, (4) pass --continue for phase advancement within same worktree. This means a retried agent picks up where it left off instead of re-reading the codebase.

For ACP mode: session resume is built into the protocol (session/prompt with existing sessionId). For CLI mode: need to parse session_id from --output-format json response and pass --resume on next invocation.

title: Worktree-per-feature model: one worktree = one PR, agents work inside it
description:
Current model: agents run in-place on main or in ad-hoc CC worktrees. Target model: one jj worktree per feature/bead, all agent phases run inside that worktree, the worktree becomes the PR.

Flow: (1) conductor creates jj workspace for a bead, (2) all pipeline phases (dev, staging, prod, docs) run inside that workspace, (3) on pipeline completion, jj bookmark + git push + gh pr create, (4) human reviews the PR, (5) merge closes the bead.

This aligns with zen's model (worktree = review unit) and CC's --worktree flag (session isolation). The difference: rosary owns the worktree lifecycle via jj, not CC. CC just runs inside the directory rosary provides.

The conductor's AgentWorker needs to: create workspace before first dispatch, pass workspace path as work_dir for all phases, clean up on pipeline completion or deadletter. workspace.rs already has create/cleanup for jj — the conductor just needs to call it via a new rsry MCP tool (rsry_workspace_create, rsry_workspace_cleanup).

Related: rosary-cd9cbb (jj vs CC worktree conflict), rosary-793652 (PR as pipeline terminal step).

title: Cross-repo "until ready" dependency primitive (first-class block-on-upstream)
description:
Filed 2026-05-11. Workflow gap surfaced today during LLO ↔ mache coordination.

## Pattern we keep reinventing

Today's session hit it 4+ times. mache has 3-4 beads gated on LLO landing X + tag. We encode it like this:

```
"Cross-repo gate update (2026-05-10): the LLO bead this blocks on was re-scoped.
Original gate: ley-line-open-a373ba. Replaced by ley-line-open-b631c8 (A-2) landing
+ LLO release tag pushed."
```

Free-text in bead comments. Doesn't show up in `rsry_list_beads`. Doesn't surface in dispatch decisions. The dispatcher will happily try to run a bead whose upstream hasn't shipped yet, because the dependency is invisible to the tool.

`rsry_bead_link` exists but per the earlier note in this session: *"rsry_bead_link operates within one repo's .beads DB"*. So within-repo `depends_on` is a graph edge the tool understands; cross-repo is a comment.

## What a real primitive looks like

```
rsry_bead_create(
  ...,
  blocked_until={
    "upstream_bead": "ley-line-open-b631c8",  
    "upstream_event": "merged_and_tagged",  # or "merged" | "closed" | "released:<semver>"
  },
)
```

Dispatcher gates the bead behind that upstream event. When upstream merges (or tags, or releases), the bead becomes dispatchable.

## Why this matters now

Today's incident from the user, paraphrased:
> "It does make me feel like... I need a way to pass off things like this. Like an 'until ready' for a thing."

This came from a mache LLM session where they had to manually stop cron-watching an LLO PR, and the user had to tell them verbally to wait on a specific LLO release. The "wait for X" knowledge lives in human chat, not in the bead graph.

## Sketch of the primitive

Three things:
1. **Schema:** `blocked_until` field on bead, structured per above
2. **Dispatcher logic:** before assigning a bead to an agent, check if any `blocked_until` is unsatisfied → skip
3. **Surface:** `rsry_list_beads(blocked=true)` returns beads waiting on upstream events, with the missing event named. `rsry_status` shows "N beads blocked" alongside "N open"

## Why "merged_and_tagged" is a real event-type

Today's mache dance is *specifically* gated on the LLO release tag, not just main-branch merge. mache's `go.mod` reference resolves only after `git tag` + push. A bead that says "blocked on LLO PR merge" but proceeds before the tag will fail with `go get` 404 — exactly the mess we hit with the PR #4 misclick.

## Why this is a rosary bead, not LLO/mache

The pattern is rosary-infrastructure. LLO and mache are CONSUMERS of the bead graph; the bead graph itself needs the new primitive. Filed here so the design conversation lives where the implementation will live.

## Adjacency

Probably related to `rosary-bd32bd` (parallel-LLM coordination) — both are about making cross-session work-state legible to the dispatcher rather than only legible in chat.

title: typed-dep add_dependency fails on richer/bd Dolt schemas (created_by NOT NULL; redundant dep_type vs existing 'type')
description:
Discovered wiring the context-substrate thread deps. The typed-dep feature (rosary-649660, #331) assumes rosary's MINIMAL dependencies schema (issue_id, depends_on_id, dep_type). But bd-created / richer Dolt stores — e.g. rosary's OWN self-store — have extra columns: 'type' varchar(32) DEFAULT 'blocks' (bd's dep-type!), created_by varchar(255) NOT NULL (no default), metadata json, thread_id.

Two bugs:
1. add_dependency_typed INSERT omits created_by -> 'ERROR 1105: Field created_by doesn't have a default value' -> rsry_bead_link fails on richer stores. (The pre-#331 INSERT IGNORE silently swallowed the same error, so deps were silently dropped before; #331's ON DUPLICATE KEY at least surfaces it.)
2. Migration 007 added a REDUNDANT dep_type column when the store already had bd's 'type' column. get_children queries dep_type IN ('parent-child','discovered-from') and would MISS any data in bd's 'type' -> the containment gate is blind on bd-schema stores.

Why CI missed it: tests build rosary's own minimal BEADS_SCHEMA (fresh SQLite/Dolt), never a bd-richer store.

Repro: on the rosary self-store, INSERT INTO dependencies (issue_id, depends_on_id, dep_type) VALUES (...) without created_by -> 1105.

Fix: (a) populate created_by (+ tolerate other NOT-NULL cols, e.g. via a schema-aware insert or a sensible default like 'rosary'); (b) reconcile dep_type vs the pre-existing 'type' column — prefer reading/writing the existing 'type' when present, or coalesce, rather than a parallel column. Add a test against a bd-shaped schema (created_by NOT NULL + a 'type' column) so this class is covered.

Close: rsry_bead_link succeeds on the rosary self-store; get_children sees containment edges regardless of which column (type/dep_type) holds them; a bd-schema regression test exists.

title: Golden Rule: pre-implementation 5-whys gate
description:
Every implementation session surfaces cascading product decisions that should have been answered upfront. Pattern observed across multiple sessions (rig security review → infra → auth → onboarding → CF plans → capability model).

Proposed Golden Rule for agents/rules/GOLDEN_RULES.md:

Before any implementation bead is dispatched, the agent MUST answer:
1. WHO is this for? (hosted user, CLI user, agent, operator)
2. WHAT does the onboarding look like? (zero-step, one-step, multi-step)
3. WHEN does this become a problem? (measurable trigger, not "eventually")
4. HOW MUCH does this cost? (infra cost, complexity cost, maintenance cost)
5. WHAT'S THE BLAST RADIUS? (who/what breaks if this is wrong?)

If any answer is "I don't know" → research bead first, not implementation bead.

Retry: previous attempts failed bead_ref verification. Now fixed with core.hooksPath + .rsry-bead-id injection in worktree."

comments.text:
Pre-dispatch observation: "dispatch" is overloaded in the codebase and conversation.

Three distinct meanings:
1. Agent dispatch — rosary picks bead + provider, runs agent (dispatch.rs, reconcile.rs)
2. Compute dispatch — WHERE the agent runs (LocalProvider, SpritesProvider, FlyMachinesProvider, DockerProvider, FirecrackerProvider)
3. Platform dispatch — CF Workers for Platforms routing to per-user Workers (env.DISPATCHER.get)

The 5-whys gate should clarify WHICH dispatch is being discussed. The nono sandbox (rosary-394890) is specifically about #2 (compute substrate security), but the capability contract touches #1 (bead scopes) and potentially #3 (per-user Worker isolation in CF).

title: Rename ambiguous [backend] config section to [orchestrator] — reads as 'my bead store backend', is actually orchestrator-only
description:
`~/.rsry/config.toml` has a bare `[backend]` section:

    [backend]
    provider = "sqlite"
    path = "~/.rsry/backend.db"

The name does not say WHOSE backend. rosary has TWO unrelated stores, and CLAUDE.md explicitly warns "Beads = per-repo ... Orchestrator = ~/.rsry/backend.db SQLite. Never conflate":

  1. ORCHESTRATOR state — pipeline, dispatches, cross-repo deps — one global ~/.rsry/backend.db. THIS is what `[backend]` configures.
  2. PER-REPO BEAD STORES — `.beads/beads.db` (SQLite) or `.beads/dolt/` (Dolt), configured per repo in `.beads/metadata.json`, NOT here.

`[backend] provider = "sqlite"` therefore says nothing about what backend any repo's beads use. Reading it as "all my beads are SQLite" is wrong — and it is the natural reading.

EVIDENCE THIS MISLEADS: the user reports being confused by it more than once, and it misled ME in this session — asked to make repos "consistent with the store type in global config", I had to stop and disambiguate which store `[backend]` even referred to before acting. Two independent readers, same misreading.

SUGGESTED FIX:
- Rename the section to `[orchestrator]` (or `[orchestrator.backend]`) so the scope is in the name. Keep `[backend]` as a deprecated alias that still parses, with a warning, so existing configs do not break.
- Add a comment in the generated/default config stating plainly that this is orchestrator-only and that per-repo bead backends live in each repo's `.beads/metadata.json`.
- Update docs/CONFIGURATION.md to say the same, and cross-reference the per-repo setting.
- Consider having `rsry doctor` print both explicitly — "orchestrator backend: sqlite (~/.rsry/backend.db)" and a per-repo bead-backend column — since doctor already surfaces the per-repo mismatch class (rosary-21e2d4) and is where someone goes when confused.

This is the same disease as rosary-6832d7 (tooling disclosure): the interface names a thing in a way that does not disclose what it is, so callers guess by analogy and guess wrong.
acceptance_criteria: The global config section is named for its scope (e.g. [orchestrator]) with [backend] accepted as a deprecated alias that warns; the default/generated config and docs/CONFIGURATION.md state it is orchestrator-only and point at .beads/metadata.json for per-repo bead backends; rsry doctor prints orchestrator backend and per-repo bead backend as distinct labelled lines

title: Canonicalize bead status at the write boundary + auto-migrate; fix Deadletter→dead_letter read bug
description:
The literals review found real drift: the retry-exhausted terminal state was written as both 'blocked' and 'dead_letter' (distinct BeadState variants), 'closed' vs 'done', 'deadletter' vs 'dead_letter'. The From<&str> parser ABSORBED aliases at read time (bad — every reader carries the alias table forever, storage stays dirty). And a real bug: derived_status returned 'blocked' for a Deadletter verdict → false audit divergence (persist writes 'dead_letter').

Fix (transform early, store canonical, migrate all backends):
1. Write boundary canonicalizes: SqliteBeadStore + DoltBeadStore update_status persist BeadState::from(s).to_string(), never the raw input. update_status already parsed for validation then threw the transform away and wrote the raw string — the smoking gun.
2. Auto-migration on connect: canonicalize_statuses() rewrites legacy aliases (closed→done, deadletter→dead_letter) to canonical, derived generically from BeadState so it can't drift from the parser. Idempotent.
3. derived_status: Deadletter → 'dead_letter' (canonical), not 'blocked'.

Tests: connect_canonicalizes_legacy_status_aliases, derived_status_deadletter_is_terminal_dead_letter. Suite 1296/0.

Follow-on to R4b (a66b3a) + persist_status ratchet (rosary-301b6c). Dolt existing-row migration is a follow-up (write boundary already prevents new Dolt drift).
acceptance_criteria: Resolved when the linked PR merges — rosary's default close signal (the GitHub merge webhook advances the bead). Set a specific acceptance_criteria to override.

title: Firecracker microVM compute provider — local isolation without Docker
description:
## What
Add Firecracker as a ComputeProvider alongside Local and Sprites. MicroVMs provide container-level isolation with VM-level security, sub-second boot, and no Docker daemon.

## Why
- Local provider has zero isolation (agents share filesystem)
- Docker requires daemon, heavy images, slow on macOS
- Sprites requires external API + network
- Firecracker: VM isolation, 125ms boot, runs on Apple Silicon via UTM/QEMU or native Linux

## Reference
- https://u3n.medium.com/the-future-of-development-is-here-running-firecracker-microvms-on-your-macbook-pro-m3-ad6fd3e5092c
- Firecracker on M3 via Ubuntu VM + KVM nested virtualization
- Same ComputeProvider trait as Local/Sprites
- krust (rosary-735446) builds the OCI image, Firecracker runs it

## Implementation
- provision: create microVM with repo mounted via virtio-fs
- spawn_process: exec agent binary inside microVM
- exec_sync: SSH or vsock into microVM
- deprovision: kill microVM (instant cleanup, zero leaks)
- checkpoint: snapshot microVM state (optional, for pause/resume)

title: task install: launchd WatchPaths doesn't fire on atomic-rename — use launchctl kickstart instead
description:
## Symptom

`task install` rebuilds + replaces `~/.local/bin/rsry` but the running `com.rosary.serve` launchd service often does NOT restart on the new binary. Observed in production: PID 45877 ran from Tuesday (~5 days) across multiple `task install` events until I `launchctl kickstart -k`'d it manually.

## Root cause

The plist sets `WatchPaths` on `~/.local/bin/rsry`. macOS launchd's `WatchPaths` is documented to fire on path modifications, but in practice it does NOT reliably fire on **atomic-replace renames**:

```
cp target/release/rsry /tmp/rsry-staged
codesign /tmp/rsry-staged
mv /tmp/rsry-staged ~/.local/bin/rsry     # ← atomic rename, new inode
touch ~/.local/bin/rsry                    # ← workaround, also unreliable
```

The `mv` replaces the file (new inode), and the `touch` updates mtime — but launchd's FSEvents subscription on the original inode/path combination doesn't always fire after the inode swap. The Taskfile comment acknowledges this:

```
# macOS WatchPaths doesn't trigger on rename(2). Touch ensures
# the launchd service restarts after atomic binary replacement.
```

…but `touch` is not sufficient in practice.

## Reproduction

1. `task install` (rebuilds + replaces `~/.local/bin/rsry`)
2. `ps -o pid,etime -p $(launchctl list | awk '/com.rosary.serve/ {print $1}')` — pid hasn't changed, elapsed time keeps growing across multiple installs
3. `rsry --version` shows new binary's commit hash; running process is on old code

## Proposed fix

Replace the `touch` workaround in `Taskfile.yml`'s `install` target with an explicit `launchctl kickstart -k`:

```yaml
- launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.rosary.serve 2>/dev/null || true
```

Guarantees restart with no FSEvents dependency. The `|| true` covers the case where the service isn't loaded yet (first-time install — install-service will load it).

Consider also removing `WatchPaths` from the plist template entirely since it's not load-bearing once kickstart is the canonical restart mechanism. Less moving parts.

## Files
- `Taskfile.yml` — replace `touch ~/.local/bin/rsry` with `launchctl kickstart`
- `scripts/com.rosary.serve.plist.template` — optionally drop `WatchPaths`

## Related
- The reason this was painful today: I'd merged PR #200/#201/#202-in-progress and the running MCP server was on Tuesday's binary the whole time. Took manual `launchctl kickstart` to surface the issue. Future operators shouldn't need to know this.

comments.text: Shipped in PR #262. install-service now kickstarts the loaded service onto the new binary (launchctl kickstart -k), touch + WatchPaths removed; scripts/check-install-restart.sh guards the invariants. Pairs with #250 (load-when-unloaded) for a deterministic launchd lifecycle. Close condition met: bash scripts/check-install-restart.sh.

description: User pain point, directly experienced multiple times this session: running two Claude Code agents (via the Agent tool, dispatched from within a single Claude Code session, not via rsry itself) in the same shared working tree causes real git-level collisions -- staged/unstaged content interfering, smell-baseline regenerations contaminated by other agents' uncommitted WIP, a live race caught mid-commit. rosary ALREADY solves an analogous problem for its OWN dispatch loop via jj workspaces per bead (.rsry-workspaces/{bead_id}/, real checkpoint/teardown lifecycle in src/workspace/{lifecycle,checkpoint,sweep}.rs) -- confirmed real and working via direct source reading this session, not assumed. title: Witchcraft as unstructured-text substrate: power inbox, semantic dedup, transcript recall
description:
## Motivation

`https://github.com/dropbox/witchcraft` — Rust reimplementation of XTR-WARP semantic search, single-file SQLite backing, embeddable as a library. Ships `pickbrain` example that already indexes Claude Code + Codex session transcripts as a skill.

LLO (ley-line) is adopting witchcraft as a backend "like sqlite is" (parallel to the existing sqlite backend). Once that lands, rosary can reuse the same primitive at the work-tracking layer.

This bead fills rosary's "no story for unstructured text" gap surfaced by James 2026-05-18.

## What it unlocks

| Surface today | Witchcraft-powered |
|---|---|
| `rsry_bead_search` substring on title/desc | Hybrid semantic + BM25 over title, desc, comments |
| Jaccard dedup in `epic.rs::is_dominated_by` (rosary-a26a78) | Semantic similarity — catches paraphrased duplicates |
| Inbox / mailbox (rosary-1db9c9) — unbuilt | Witchcraft-backed inbox: write unstructured observations, semantic-recall, promote to bead via LLM extraction |
| Bead comments — accumulate, hard to recall | Indexed; "what was the bead where we discussed X?" |
| Session transcripts | Already pickbrain's job; rosary just consumes the index |

## Acceptance (minimum useful)

1. `~/.rsry/witchcraft.db` — single-file index over all bead titles + descriptions + comments
2. `rsry_bead_search` accepts a `mode: "semantic" | "substring" | "hybrid"` (default hybrid)
3. Index is incremental — write-through from `bead_create` / `bead_update` / `bead_comment`
4. `rsry inbox add "raw text"` — appends to inbox index (separate from beads); `rsry inbox promote <id>` extracts BeadSpec via LLM (already wired in `src/capture.rs`)
5. Active dedup (rosary-a26a78) calls witchcraft for similarity instead of jaccard

## Design pointers

- Witchcraft is a library (Rust → Rust integration, no MCP needed for now)
- Could also be wired via the outbound `kind = "mcp"` plugin runtime (rosary-b65745) once that lands — but library integration is simpler
- Pickbrain is the reference impl: `examples/pickbrain/` in the witchcraft repo
- ley-line side: tracked separately (witchcraft as LLO backend)

## Related / blocks-on

- rosary-1db9c9 (incoming triage queue / mailbox) — direct dependency consumer
- rosary-a26a78 (active dedup with semantic similarity) — direct dependency consumer
- rosary-b5da2f (scope abstraction) — inbox needs Global scope
- LLO-side witchcraft backend bead — file separately in ley-line

comments.text:
## Subagent research report (2026-05-19): LLO has the substrate; rosary-side wiring is the MVP

Subagent dispatched today returned a substantive report. Bottom line: **LLO already ships everything needed for the read side; rosary just needs to wire it in. MVP is ~1 day.**

### What LLO has today (verified)

**(a) `leyline-text-search` crate** — `rs/ll-open/text-search/`
- `TextSearchEngine` trait (`src/lib.rs:96`): `upsert/remove/finalize/search/len/clear/storage_path`
- `NullEngine` (default) — `Error::NotImplemented` for every op
- `WitchcraftEngine` (feature `engine-witchcraft`) — wraps `dropbox/witchcraft` (XTR-WARP + BM25 hybrid). Storage = single SQLite file the engine owns. Sidecar-by-construction; `tests/substrate_non_leak.rs` asserts storage lives outside arena.

**(b) Daemon wire op `text_search`** — `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/`
- `BaseRequest::TextSearch { query, k }` (k default 10) in `wire.rs:113`
- Op handler in `ops.rs:1743`; MCP tool exposed in `mcp.rs:299`
- Engine installed via `DaemonExt::text_search_engine()` (`ext.rs:87`)
- **Open LLO binary ships NullEngine only** (`cmd_daemon.rs:230`) — real engine is a private extension

**(c) `leyline-chat-embed` binary** — `rs/ll-open/chat-embed/`
- *Separate code path*. Uses fastembed (MiniLM L6 v2 Q, 384-dim).
- Reads `~/.claude/chats.db` produced by some `mache ingest claude-chats` path. Schema: `results(id TEXT PK, record TEXT)` + sidecar `chat_embeddings(id, embedding BLOB, content_preview, model)`.
- Subcommands: `chat-embed index <db>`, `chat-embed query "..." <db> -k N`, `chat-embed stats`.
- **`~/.claude/chats.db` exists today with 1531 sessions indexed.** Binary not installed at `~/.local/bin/chat-embed` yet.

### Claude Code transcripts on disk (confirmed)

`~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-uuid>.jsonl` — JSONL, one event per line. Encoded-cwd = absolute path with `/` → `-`. The rosary dir holds ~20+ sessions, 1MB–33MB each.

### LLO task or rosary task?

**Rosary-side wiring is right.** Reasons:
- LLO already shipped the substrate (text_search trait + op + engine impl). LLO deliberately ships NullEngine; the engine is corpus-agnostic.
- The corpus (Claude transcripts) is rosary-domain. Rosary already has `ProvenanceRef::Session { transcript_path }` in `src/capture.rs:32`.
- `chat-embed` already exists as the cheap MVP. Rosary can shell to it today; the witchcraft op is the upgrade path when the private extension ships.

### MVP shape (~1 day)

```rust
// src/chat.rs  (new module, feature-flagged behind `chat-search`)
pub async fn search(query: &str, k: usize) -> Result<Vec<ChatHit>> {
    // Option A (today): shell to chat-embed
    //   chat-embed query --db ~/.claude/chats.db -k <k> <query>
```

title: Methodology: parallel-safe bead authoring (file-scope discipline so N agents can share a branch)
description:
## User framing (recurring, audited 2026-05-19)

> "Ideally the beads are written in a way that I can parallelize agents in same branch at same time."

User types this in many forms. The system has a **defensive** safety net (`epic::has_file_overlap`, `reconcile.rs:372-380`) that REFUSES dispatch on file overlap — that's correct behavior but only fires after the fact. There is **no affirmative authoring guidance** for the bead author.

## What's missing

A documented discipline for authoring beads so they are intentionally non-overlapping:

1. **File-scope rules** — every bead lists touched files; module/file/symbol granularity guidance
2. **"Same-branch parallel" tags** — a label that asserts "I designed this bead to coexist with siblings on the same branch"
3. **Cross-file shared imports/typedefs** — how to handle a `lib.rs`-style file that multiple beads need to extend (proposal: shared add-only sections; each bead adds its own line, no edits)
4. **Test-file granularity** — separate test modules per bead so tests don't merge-conflict
5. **A linter** — `rsry bead lint <id>...<id>` flags overlap before dispatch (today: only `epic::has_file_overlap` at dispatch, which is too late for the author)

## Related (but NOT the same)

- `rosary-44a542` — defensive: parallel subagents step on each other (shared worktree). That's the **runtime** failure; this bead is the **authoring** discipline that prevents queueing such beads in the first place.
- `rosary-75555d` (tmux substrate) — gives each agent its own worktree; orthogonal solution at a different layer.

## Deliverables

1. `docs/methodology/parallel-bead-authoring.md` — the discipline doc with examples
2. `agents/rules/GOLDEN_RULES.md` — a new rule (#12 or insertion) referencing the discipline
3. `rsry bead lint` CLI subcommand — flags overlap pre-dispatch
4. Skill update for `note` skill — invoke lint on every bead create

## Audit source

`session_audit_2026-05-19.md` §4.2.

## Time-box

M — ~1-2 days. Doc + rules + lint command + skill update. The lint logic largely re-uses existing `has_file_overlap`.

title: mache: SliceContent does not guard against negative offset
description: In `internal/graph/graph.go`, `SliceContent(data, buf []byte, offset int64) int` compares `offset >= int64(len(data))` but does not check `offset < 0`. If a caller passes a negative offset, `data[offset:end]` will panic with an out-of-range slice expression. The FUSE and NFS layers do not appear to validate offset before delegating to ReadContent. title: mache: SQLiteResolver.Close now re-openable — undocumented semantics change
description: Before this PR, `SQLiteResolver.Close()` closed all connections but left the `dbs` map non-nil with its stale (now-closed) entries. After this PR, `Close()` reassigns `r.dbs = make(map[string]*sql.DB)`, which causes subsequent `Resolve` calls to silently re-open the database rather than returning an error. This is a semantic change that is not reflected in any caller contract: the existing callers in `cmd/` use `defer r.Close()` as a terminal teardown, not as a reset/checkpoint. The test `TestSQLiteResolver_Close_ClearsPool` explicitly validates and endorses the re-open behavior, but this was not the original design intent. The question is whether `Close` should be terminal (post-close Resolve returns an error) or a pool-flush (idempotent, re-opens). This needs an explicit decision, not an accidental behavior change. File as a design question to resolve before merge.

title: mache: ContentCache RWMutex promotion silently changes lock granularity for WritableGraph and SQLiteGraph
description: The old `contentMu sync.Mutex` in `WritableGraph` and `SQLiteGraph` was exclusive for both reads and writes. The new `ContentCache` uses `sync.RWMutex` with `Get` under `RLock` and `Put`/`Delete` under `Lock`. This is semantically correct for the cache itself, but the promotion changes observable behavior: previously a reader blocked on a concurrent writer (mutual exclusion); now multiple readers can run concurrently while a writer is waiting. This is generally a correctness improvement, but warrants a review pass to confirm no code was relying on the exclusive read behavior — for example, if a caller held the cache mutex to ensure a get-or-insert was atomic. A scan of `resolveContent` in both files confirms the check-then-set sequence was never atomic even under the old Mutex (it unlocked between check and set), so the promotion is safe. However, the PR description does not acknowledge this change at all — the commit message says only "unify ContentCache" without noting the lock promotion. Should be called out explicitly in the PR description.

title: mache: HotSwapGraph tests test MemoryStore, not HotSwapGraph delegation
description: In `internal/graph/hotswap_test.go`, every delegation test (GetNode, ListChildren, ListChildStats, ReadContent, GetCallers, GetCallees, Invalidate, Act) passes data directly to the underlying `MemoryStore` and then calls the HotSwapGraph method. Because HotSwapGraph is pure delegation with no transformation, every test would also pass if `HotSwapGraph` were replaced by `MemoryStore` directly. A regression in `HotSwapGraph` (e.g., forgetting to acquire `mu.RLock` in a new method, or delegating to the wrong field) would not be caught. The tests verify "it compiles and does not panic" more than "delegation is correct." To actually test the wrapper, at minimum one test should pass two different stores — one where the query succeeds and one where it fails — to prove the delegation is going to `h.current` and not some cached copy. The Swap tests do this correctly; the individual delegation tests do not.

title: mache: ContentCache.Delete linear scan is not wrong but has no duplicate-key protection
description: In `internal/graph/graph.go`, `ContentCache.Delete` does a linear scan of `keys` to find and remove the entry, breaking on first match. If `Put` had a bug that allowed duplicate keys (it currently prevents this with the dedup check), `Delete` would only remove the first occurrence, leaving phantom entries. The `break` after the first match is correct given the current `Put` invariant, but the invariant is not documented or asserted. More importantly: if `keys` is empty when `Delete` is called for a key that exists in `entries` (a theoretically impossible state but possible if the struct is constructed directly without `NewContentCache`), `Delete` would remove from the map but the `for` loop would be a no-op, silently corrupting the `keys`/`entries` invariant. Not a production bug today, but the invariant should be documented with a comment or a debug assertion.

title: mache: contentCache RWMutex creates TOCTOU data race in get→miss→put path
description: PR #147 (fix/perf-quick-wins) upgrades contentCache.mu from sync.Mutex to sync.RWMutex. The get() method now acquires RLock and releases it before returning. resolveContent() in internal/graph/graph.go then calls the resolver and calls put() under a separate Lock. Between the RLock release and the Lock acquisition, multiple concurrent goroutines can all observe a cache miss, all call the resolver, and all call put() — redundant work. Worse, the existing put() logic checks `if _, ok := c.entries[key]; ok { c.entries[key] = value; return }` which means the first writer wins and subsequent writers overwrite with the same data, but there's no atomicity guarantee that the FIFO keys slice stays consistent if two puts race on the same key that was already inserted. Under -race this will be reported as a concurrent write to the entries map. The fix requires either promoting RLock→Lock inside get() when a miss is detected (upgrade lock, not available in Go's sync.RWMutex), or wrapping the entire get→resolve→put sequence in a single Lock, or accepting the thundering-herd on miss (correct but slower). File: internal/graph/graph.go lines 842-858, 878-901.

   - phase_status=pending → dispatch
   - bead=done but pipeline exists → stale, clear
   - bead=dispatched with no pipeline → orphan, reset to open
3. Populate Orchestrator.dispatched MapSet from recovered pipelines

TDD: test recovery scenarios in orchestrator_test.exs with MockRsry seeded with various pipeline states.

title: mache: sync.Pool buf recycled before error-path caller is done in render.go
description: PR #147 adds sync.Pool for bytes.Buffer in internal/template/render.go. The buf.String() call (line ~219, ~247) copies the internal byte slice into a new string allocation — that copy is safe. However, the defer bufPool.Put(buf) fires after the function returns the string. On the error path (t.Execute returns an error), the function returns early with `return "", err` — the buffer is still Put back correctly there too via defer. The pool usage is technically safe. HOWEVER: there is one subtle issue. If t.Execute writes partial output before failing, the buffer contains garbage. It gets Put back with Reset() called only at the start of the NEXT Get(), not before Put(). The current code calls buf.Reset() at Get()-time which is correct. But if a caller somehow holds a reference to the underlying byte slice (e.g. via unsafe or via a template func that captures the writer), the reuse would be unsafe. With standard Go text/template this is not a real risk. The real concern is that the error path returns `return "", err` — the buf was partially written, then Put back with its contents intact. The next Get() calls Reset() so this is cleaned up. Net verdict: pool usage is correct, but the Reset() should be documented as the reason the partial-write state is safe. File: internal/template/render.go lines 214-220, 242-248.

mache: EnsureIndexes silently swallows DB errors — index may not exist
description: PR #147 adds EnsureIndexes() to ASTWalker in internal/ingest/ast_walker.go. The implementation is: `_, _ = w.db.Exec(...)`. It discards both the result and the error. If the _ast table does not exist (e.g. the caller passes a DB that does not have ley-line's schema, or the DB is read-only), the index creation silently fails and subsequent queries will do full table scans — the exact performance problem the change is supposed to fix. There is also no test that verifies the index is actually created, and no test that covers EnsureIndexes being called from SetASTWalker (the new call site in engine.go line 243). Additionally, the gen-lsp-fixture tool already creates idx_ast_source on _ast(source_id) — EnsureIndexes creates idx_ast_kind_source on _ast(node_kind, source_id). These are different; the new compound index is not redundant. But IF NOT EXISTS means silent double-call safety is fine. The error-swallowing is the real problem. File: internal/ingest/ast_walker.go line 32, internal/ingest/engine.go line 243.

title: ADR-0012: Personal/root rosary substrate — pick storage + sync + tamper-resistance model
description:
## Parent

`rosary-792ed6` — Personal/root EPIC.

## Decision needed

Pick ONE option per axis, with tradeoffs documented:

### Axis 1: Storage location

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.rsry/personal.db` (SQLite) | dead-simple, no new infra | per-machine; no sync without separate plumbing |
| `~/Library/Application Support/rosary/personal.db` (macOS) + XDG equiv | follows platform convention | same per-machine constraint |
| ley-line peer-replicated blob | sync for free; content-addressed | depends on ley-line stability; harder to introspect |
| cloister-hosted (HTTPS endpoint per user) | multi-machine + multi-agent ergonomic | networked dependency; cloister auth model needs to be load-bearing |

### Axis 2: Sync model

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| Private dotfiles (age-encrypted `~/.rsry/personal.db`) | leverages existing dotfiles workflow | conflict resolution = manual |
| ley-line peer sync | CRDT-style merge | requires LLO daemon up everywhere |
| cloister-hosted (server-side merge) | always-consistent | single point of failure; needs an auth story |

### Axis 3: Tamper-resistance boundary

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| signet-signed append-only log | provable; signet identity is already device-bound | log compaction is non-trivial |
| local FS perms (700) only | simplest | doesn't defend against local agent compromise |
| TEE / Keychain-backed key | strongest local | macOS-only, won't port |

## Acceptance

- `docs/adr/0012-personal-bead-substrate.md` exists, status `accepted`
- One option chosen per axis with explicit rejected-alternative paragraphs
- Acceptance criteria spell out: what new module is added (`src/bead_personal.rs`?), what schema migration is needed, what test surface validates "agent cannot mutate without signet keyholder consent"
- Concrete sequencing: ScopeId::Personal variant → storage module → sync hook → attestation gate

## Time-box

S — ~½ day to write the ADR after the 3-axis decision is made. The decision itself may take a conversation with user, but the writeup is mechanical once made.

## Files

- `docs/adr/0012-personal-bead-substrate.md` (new)
- Optional: `docs/decades/personal-root-rosary.md` (decade-level rollup)

title: signet-signed append-only attestation for Personal beads (blocked on ADR-0012)
description:
## Parent

`rosary-792ed6`. Tamper-resistance layer for Personal beads.

## Premise

The "personal" store must be tamper-resistant against not just other humans but also **local agents**. An agent compromised on this machine should NOT be able to silently mutate a Personal bead.

Mechanism: every Personal-bead-write produces a signed attestation via signet's local Ed25519 master key. Reads validate the attestation chain. Mutations without a fresh attestation (signed within last N minutes) are rejected.

## Why signet (not generic crypto)

- signet already binds a key to the device (per `~/remotes/art/signet`)
- The CMS/PKCS#7 signer (signet-sign Rust crate) is shipped
- notme (signet's control plane) can revoke a compromised device's attestations

## Acceptance

1. Each `bead_create` / `bead_update` / `bead_close` on a Personal-scoped bead requires a fresh signet attestation (≤5 min old) signed by the device's Ed25519 master
2. The attestation is stored alongside the bead (new column `attestation BLOB`)
3. Reads validate the chain (each mutation's attestation references the prior state hash)
4. CLI prompt for fresh signet sig on every write OR cached touch-id session (macOS keychain integration)
5. Audit log: any rejected write logs the reason ("attestation expired", "signature invalid", "no chain root")
6. Test: corrupt a row with `sqlite3` directly → next read fails with `AttestationChainBroken` error

## Out of scope

- Multi-device key recovery (handled by signet/notme)
- Cross-device attestation sync (handled by sync-candidate child)

## Time-box

L — ~2-3 days. Cryptographic surface is small but the integration touches the bead write path, MCP error surface, and CLI UX (touch-id prompt).

## Files

- `src/bead_personal.rs` (new — extended)
- `src/attestation.rs` (new)
- Cargo.toml — signet-sign dependency
- `tests/personal_attestation.rs` (new)

title: ADR-0014: Agent-native workflow state-machine — pick home (rosary vs cloister) + event-source model
description:
## Parent

`rosary-a761df` — Agent-native workflow state-machine EPIC.

## What this ADR decides

The recurring user prompt:
> "Pls watch for Copilot's review / respond if appropriate or resolve. Once all are resolved or responded report back to me if you need my input, or otherwise if CI passes merge once things are resolved."

is a **state machine** encoded as a one-shot prompt every time. This ADR commits to a substrate that lets us declare such a workflow once, then re-run it as data.

## Decisions needed

### Axis 1: Home

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **rosary** | bead lifecycle already a state machine; close to dispatch | broadens rosary's scope; conflicts with `rosary-c5ae10` (tracker-vs-scheduler split) |
| **cloister** | attestation infra + multi-tenancy already there | net-new dependency for a substrate move |
| **new repo** | clean separation | yet another repo |

### Axis 2: Event sources

| Source | Today | If accepted |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Actions / webhook | already in rosary (`src/serve/github_webhook.rs`) | first-class trigger |
| File system | `notify` crate | first-class trigger (covers `rosary-a7f18e` Dolt-sandbox watcher style) |
| Cron-style | exists in CC scheduling skill | first-class trigger |
| MCP tool call | already via `rsry_dispatch` | first-class trigger |
| Linear webhook | exists | first-class trigger |

### Axis 3: Policy representation

| Option | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| Hardcoded Rust per workflow | type-safe, fast | every new workflow = code change + ship |
| TOML/YAML config | declarative, runtime-editable | parser complexity, validation |
| Sayiir or Temporal | mature, durable | runtime dep + new database |
| Custom Rust state-machine on Dolt | reuses our durable journal | DIY parser + DSL |

### Axis 4: Durability

- Where does workflow STATE persist? (Dolt? SQLite? memory + checkpoint?)
- How is replay-after-crash defined?
- What does "I've already acted on this event" deduplication look like?

## Acceptance

- `docs/adr/0014-agent-native-workflow-state-machines.md` exists, status `accepted`
- One option chosen per axis with explicit rejected-alternative paragraphs
- First-experiment proposal: `rsry pr autopilot <pr-number>` with hardcoded policy as the shape-proof (see child)
- Anti-goals listed: NOT building Temporal; NOT building a general-purpose orchestrator; agent-native means LLM-call composition is first-class

## Sources cited in audit / handoff

- Sayiir (github.com/danielepalaia/sayiir) — Rust durable workflow engine
- temporal-sdk-core — official Rust core
- notify crate — fs watcher
- swiftide / graphile-worker patterns

User lean from handoff: **"notify for fs primitives + a small Rust state-machine of our own on Dolt as the durable journal."** Document why if accepted; document why not if rejected.

## Time-box

M — ~1-2 days to write a load-bearing ADR. The decision conversation may take time; the writeup is mechanical.

## Files

- `docs/adr/0014-agent-native-workflow-state-machines.md` (new)

title: Symbol-scoped beads — AST-level dispatch isolation via mache
description:
Currently beads scope work to files (files: ["src/serve.rs"]). This is too coarse — two agents can't work on the same file even if they touch different functions.

Mache already projects the AST with symbols, callers, and callees. Beads should carry symbol-level scope:
  symbols: ["tool_bead_create", "create_bead"]

The file overlap check (epic::has_file_overlap) becomes symbol overlap + transitive caller/callee blast radius, computed via mache find_callers/find_callees at triage time.

Benefits:
- Two agents CAN work on same file (different functions) — more parallelism
- Blast radius is auto-computed from call graph, not manually listed files
- Bead scope is verifiable: mache can confirm the symbols exist and what they touch
- edit-only beads (no refactor) become enforceable: "change this function's behavior, don't move it"

Implementation:
1. Add symbols field to Bead struct (alongside files)
2. At triage, call mache find_callers/find_callees to expand symbol set to transitive closure
3. Overlap check: if any symbol in candidate's closure intersects active bead's closure, defer
4. BDR decomposition produces symbol-scoped BeadSpecs, not just file-scoped

This is the bridge between file overlap detection (today) and blast radius dedup (ADR-003). Mache is the engine.

title: First experiment: `rsry pr autopilot <pr>` — hardcoded policy, shape-proof of state-machine substrate
description:
## Parent

`rosary-a761df` — Agent-native workflow state-machine EPIC.

## Why this experiment first

The user types the same workflow many times per PR:

> "Pls watch for Copilot's review / respond if appropriate or resolve. Once all are resolved or responded report back to me if you need my input, or otherwise if CI passes merge once things are resolved."

Ship the SMALLEST artifact that proves the shape: a single CLI subcommand with a **hardcoded** policy. No DSL, no config file. Validate that the substrate shape is right by running it on 3 real PRs.

If the shape works, child bead lifts the hardcoded policy into data (see "policy-as-data" sibling).

## Scope

`rsry pr autopilot <pr-number> [--repo <name>] [--interval 5m]`

Hardcoded state machine:

```
INIT → POLL_CI ─(passing)─→ POLL_REVIEWS ─(no reviews)─→ MERGE_IF_AUTO
                │                       │
                │                       ├─(comments unresolved)─→ ATTEMPT_REPLY_OR_RESOLVE
                │                       │                                │
                │                       │                                └─(failed)─→ REPORT_TO_USER
                │                       │
                │                       └─(reviews approved)─→ MERGE_IF_AUTO
                │
                └─(failing)─→ REPORT_TO_USER
```

Implementation:
- One file: `src/policy/pr_autopilot.rs`
- Uses existing `gh` CLI + `gh api` for state polling
- Uses existing rosary cron skill (`skills/loop`) or the new `notify` watcher
- Output: stdout progress + a `~/.rsry/autopilot-<pr>.log` audit trail
- On every state transition: print to stdout AND emit a bead comment on any linked bead

## Acceptance

title: mache: JSONMaterializer encodes empty DB as `null` not `[]` — no test coverage
description: In internal/materialize/json.go, buildJSONChildren returns nil when childrenOf has no entries for the root key. enc.Encode(nil) on a []*jsonEntry produces `null\n` as valid JSON output, not `[]`. Consumers expecting a JSON array will panic or error on a null root. There is no test for an empty source DB. The BoltDB materializer silently writes an empty boltdb in this case. The fix is either to initialize root as an empty slice (`root := []*jsonEntry{}`), or document and test the null case explicitly. title: mache: JSONMaterializer silently drops empty-string content, BoltDB preserves it
description: In internal/materialize/json.go line 152: `n.content.Valid && n.content.String != ""` — a node with record="" (empty string, not NULL) has its content field omitted from the JSON output. The BoltDB materializer (boltdb.go line 132) checks only `n.content.Valid`, so an empty-string record is stored as a zero-byte value in BoltDB but silently dropped from the JSON output. If any real schema produces file nodes with empty string content (e.g. placeholder files or virtual nodes), the two backends produce inconsistent output. Should either align the check to `n.content.Valid` only, or document the intentional divergence. Ref: mache PR #146, internal/materialize/json.go:152 vs internal/materialize/boltdb.go:132.

title: MCP tool: rsry_bead_update — PATCH semantics for updating bead fields
description:
## Problem

No way to update a bead's fields after creation. rsry_bead_create creates, rsry_bead_comment adds notes, rsry_bead_close changes status — but nothing updates fields like files, test_files, priority, owner, description.

The backfill task (rosary-8284bf Stage 2) needs to write derived `files` back to existing beads. Can't do that without an update tool.

## Design

PATCH semantics — only update fields that are provided, leave others unchanged.

```json
{
  "name": "rsry_bead_update",
  "params": {
    "repo_path": "/path/to/repo",
    "id": "rosary-abc123",
    "files": ["src/serve.rs"],
    "test_files": ["src/serve_test.rs"],
    "priority": 1,
    "owner": "staging-agent",
    "description": "updated description"
  }
}
```

All fields except repo_path and id are optional. Only provided fields get written to Dolt.

## Changes
- src/serve.rs: add rsry_bead_update tool handler
- src/dolt.rs: add update_bead_fields() (conditional UPDATE SET for each provided field)

## Blocks
- rosary-8284bf Stage 2 (backfill files)
- Any future bead field updates from agents

Approach: (1) DoltClient::update_bead_fields() with PATCH semantics, (2) IssueTracker::update_fields() trait method with default no-op, (3) LinearTracker impl via issueUpdate mutation, (4) rsry_bead_update MCP tool in serve.rs. Backend sync: event log + reconciler/sync picks up field changes (MCP tools don't hold tracker instances).

reopen / review / comment / search / export / import — but NO update/edit. So there is

title: rsry_bead_create claims success but bead doesn't persist in sqlite-backed repos (ley-line-open)
description:
## Repro

Against `/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/ley-line-open` (which has a sqlite-backed `.beads/beads.db` + `.db-shm` + `.db-wal`, not Dolt):

1. **Step 1** — file a bead:
   ```
   mcp tool: rsry_bead_create
   args: {
     repo_path: "/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/ley-line-open",
     title: "Ship server.json at LLO root (MCP Registry spec) — install metadata + env vars",
     description: "...",
     issue_type: "feature",
     priority: 1,
     files: ["server.json", "rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs"]
   }
   ```
   Returns:
   ```json
   { "id": "ley-line-open-81f3cd", "title": "...", "priority": 1, "owner": "scoping-agent" }
   ```
   Looks like success.

2. **Step 2** — attempt to update the same bead:
   ```
   mcp tool: rsry_bead_update
   args: {
     repo_path: "/Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/ley-line-open",
     id: "ley-line-open-81f3cd",
     ...
   }
   ```
   Returns: `Error: bead not found: ley-line-open-81f3cd`

3. **Step 3** — list/search confirms emptiness:
   ```
   rsry_list_beads({ repo: "ley-line-open", limit: 5 })  →  { "total": 0, "count": 0, ... }
   rsry_bead_search({ repo_path: ".../ley-line-open", query: "server.json", limit: 5 })  →  { "count": 0 }
   ```

## Two hypotheses

(a) **rsry_bead_create against a non-Dolt repo writes to a temp/in-memory store that doesn't persist** — returns a synthetic ID that's then unreachable.

(b) **An old/stale MCP server instance is running** that handles `_create` but not `_update`/`_list` against the same backend — user notes "we might have an old mcp running."

Either way: a tool returning `{id: "..."}` on success but with no persisted bead behind it is a silent-failure footgun. Rosary should either:
- Detect the sqlite/non-Dolt path and either route to `bd` CLI OR reject with a clear error, OR
- Persist consistently so subsequent ops can find what was just created

## Surfaced from

cloister session 2026-05-19. User has reported "bead transitioning is a struggle still" anecdotally; this is a concrete capture of that friction. Was in the middle of dispatching a multi-bead parallel pipeline (cloister P1-P5 LLO enablement) when the LLO-side bead disappeared between create and update.

## Workaround used in the session

The P4 agent for LLO got its full bead spec inline in the dispatch prompt instead of via rsry MCP lookup. Pipeline proceeded but the persistence layer is broken.

## Asks

1. Confirm hypothesis (a) vs (b) — is rsry-mcp routing sqlite-backed repos through a different code path than Dolt repos?
2. If (b), document how to detect + restart stale rsry-mcp instances.
3. If (a), either fix the persistence or make `rsry_bead_create` fail loudly on unsupported backends.

## Coordinated with

User noted "we have a rosary bead for it lol" — meaning cross-repo bead transitioning friction is a known issue. This bead is a concrete repro for the persistence-side of that.

title: Worktrees silently get an empty local bead store — git-tracked .beads/ skeleton defeats git-commondir resolution
description:
Found 2026-07-16 while investigating "0/0 beads in a worktree." Cousin of rosary-560953 (#371) but a distinct trigger the #371 gate does NOT catch.

ROOT CAUSE (src/main.rs:869-872):
```
pub fn resolve_beads_dir(repo_root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    if repo_root.join(".beads").exists() {
        return repo_root.join(".beads");   // early return
    }
    // git-commondir fallback (lines 873+) — DEAD CODE in any worktree
```
The doc comment (868) states the intent: "In a worktree, .beads/ lives in the main worktree — resolve via git commondir." But the early-exists return fires first, and `.beads/` ALWAYS exists in a worktree because `.beads/{config.yaml,README.md,.gitignore}` are git-TRACKED (confirmed via `git ls-files .beads/`). So every worktree checkout materializes the skeleton; `.beads/dolt/` is gitignored so it is NOT checked out.

CONSEQUENCE: resolve_beads_dir returns the worktree-local `.beads/` (skeleton, no dolt/) → connect_bead_store sees no dolt/ → SQLite fallback → opens/creates an empty 61440-byte beads.db in the worktree. Any cwd-scoped bead op (statusline, `rsry bead list/create`) reads/writes the EMPTY local store instead of the main Dolt server. `rsry status` masks it (global, reads config by path, not cwd).

WHY #371 DOESN'T CATCH IT: rosary-560953's gate checks `beads_dir.exists()`; here the skeleton makes it exist, so the gate passes and the empty local store is used. A `bead create` in a worktree would write into this orphan store (not fabricated-from-nothing, but diverged-from-real — arguably worse: it looks like it worked).

FIX DIRECTION: resolve_beads_dir must not treat a store-less `.beads/` as authoritative. Options:
(a) Detect worktree first: if `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` != `--git-dir`, we're in a linked worktree → resolve to `<commondir>/../.beads` unconditionally.
(b) Only early-return the local `.beads/` when it actually holds a store (has `dolt/` OR a non-empty/migrated beads.db); otherwise fall through to commondir.
(c) Stop tracking the `.beads/` skeleton (config.yaml/README are bd-era artifacts anyway — ADR-0014 says rosary owns the store; the tracked bd config.yaml is arguably cruft) so `.beads/` doesn't exist in a fresh worktree. Risky — may break clone-onboarding expectations.
Prefer (a)+(b): worktree-aware resolution + a store-presence check, with a test that a bead op from a linked worktree resolves to the main store (dolt) and creates NO local beads.db.

NOTE: connects to the capsule discussion (ADR-0015) — a per-worktree/per-capsule store MIGHT be desirable someday, but if so it must be a real store wired to lineage, not an accidental empty SQLite orphan. This bug is the accidental version; the capsule is the intentional version. Fix the accident; design the capsule separately.

comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE MECHANISM (found while scoping rosary-3a0e19), with the exact code path:

src/bead_sqlite/mod.rs connect_bead_store():
  :153  if .beads/dolt exists -> Dolt branch
  :164  ONE-SHOT drain: if beads.db exists && !beads.db.migrated exists -> drain beads.db into Dolt, rename beads.db -> beads.db.migrated
  :189  else (no dolt/ dir) -> SqliteBeadStore::connect(.beads/beads.db)

The empty-store failure is the interaction of :164 and :189. Once the one-shot drain has run, beads.db.migrated EXISTS, so the drain is permanently disabled. If anything then re-creates a 0-byte beads.db, it is never drained and never cleaned up — it just sits there. Any resolution that reaches :189 without the dolt/ dir (a worktree carrying only the git-tracked .beads/ skeleton) opens that 0-byte file and silently reports ZERO beads.

CONFIRMED IN ROSARY'S OWN STORE RIGHT NOW: .beads/beads.db = 0 bytes, .beads/beads.db.migrated = 73728 bytes, .beads/dolt/ present, dolt sql-server up 12d23h on :55362, 1092 beads live in Dolt.

The existing guard at :186 (unreadable_backend_warning, added for rosary-21e2d4) does NOT catch this: a 0-byte beads.db is readable-but-empty, not 'unreadable', so no warning fires. That is why it is SILENT.

Suggested fix directions: (a) treat an empty/0-row beads.db next to a beads.db.migrated (or next to dolt/) as a hard error, not a valid empty store; (b) have the one-shot drain DELETE beads.db rather than leaving a stub; (c) resolve the store via git-commondir before falling back to a local skeleton.

Keep both: slice 1 fixes read fidelity; this bead fixes the empty-store resolution.

title: Automated doc generation from code + beads + decades
description:
## Problem
As the system grows (4 decades, 13 threads, 30+ organized beads, 6 ADRs, agents, providers), maintaining docs manually is unsustainable. README, CLAUDE.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, glossary all drift.

## Proposal
Generate docs from source of truth:
- Decade/thread structure from Dolt (rsry_decade_list, rsry_thread_list)
- ADR index from docs/adr/*.md frontmatter
- Key source files table from Cargo.toml + module structure
- Agent definitions from agents/*.md frontmatter
- MCP tool list from serve.rs tool_definitions()

Could be a `task docs` command or a pre-commit hook that regenerates sections of README/CLAUDE.md between marker comments. Keeps docs accurate without manual maintenance burden.

title: rsry move <source> <dest>: cross-repo bead relocation (no bd; carries provenance forward)
description:
## Problem

`bd` mis-routes cross-repo bead writes (ADR-0014): on 2026-06-25 a `bd create --repo ley-line-open` reached an empty embeddeddolt dir ("no database selected") and silently mis-filed 4 LLO beads into mache's store as a "fallback". rosary owns the store and must never need bd, but it has no way to *relocate* a bead from one repo store to another. `migrate_sqlite_to_dolt` is backend conversion (same repo); there is no cross-repo move.

## Proposal

Add `rsry move <source-bead-id> <dest-repo>` — generalizes the "promotion carries provenance forward" leaf (L5 in docs/problems/rosary-capture-commit-spine.md) from Global->repo to repo->repo. Operation:
1. Read bead from source store in-process (connect_bead_store; no bd).
2. Re-create in dest store with dest id-prefix (generate_bead_id).
3. Carry derived_from + created_by forward; append a provenance entry recording the move (moved-from: <old-id>).
4. Rewrite cross-repo dependency links that referenced the old id (LinkageStore / store_dolt remove+add).
5. Tombstone/close the source bead as "moved -> <new-id>" (preserve audit trail; soft).

## Acceptance criteria
- `rsry move <id> <dest>` relocates a bead: source closed-as-moved, dest has an equivalent bead with new id + moved-from provenance. Test covers SQLite->SQLite at minimum.
- Dependents pointing at the old id are updated (no dangling cross-repo dep).
- No invocation of the `bd` binary anywhere in the path.

## First dogfood use-case
Relocate mache-lbn6 / lbn6.1 / lbn6.2 (LLO-cousin beads mis-filed in mache) into ley-line-open; correct mache-nr0g (store was never broken; bd was).

## Inputs
- src/main.rs (generate_bead_id, resolve_beads_dir, CLI), src/bead_sqlite.rs (connect_bead_store), src/store.rs (LinkageStore), src/store_dolt.rs (cross-repo dep add/remove), crates/bdr/src/provenance.rs (ProvenanceRef), docs/adr/0014-decouple-rosary-from-bd.md, docs/problems/rosary-capture-commit-spine.md (L5).

Test: cargo test --bin rsry

comments.text: Shipped in PR #244 (5fa12a0): 'rsry bead move <id> <dest>' cross-repo relocation, no bd, provenance forwarded. Closing as already-merged.
