title: Pluggable ExecutionBackend: sprites.dev first, local fallback
description:
## Problem

Rosary dispatches agents as local subprocesses (tokio::process::Command). This couples agent execution to the orchestrator's host. No isolation, no resource limits, no checkpointing, no remote execution.

## Design

Introduce an `ExecutionBackend` trait that abstracts WHERE agent code runs, orthogonal to the existing `AgentProvider` trait (WHICH model runs). The two compose: `AgentProvider` builds the prompt/config, `ExecutionBackend` provides the compute substrate.

```rust
#[async_trait]
pub trait ExecutionBackend: Send + Sync {
    /// Provision an execution environment for a bead.
    async fn provision(&self, bead_id: &str, opts: &ProvisionOpts) -> Result<ExecHandle>;
    
    /// Execute a command in the environment. Returns exit code + output.
    async fn exec(&self, handle: &ExecHandle, cmd: &[&str]) -> Result<ExecResult>;
    
    /// Tear down the environment.
    async fn destroy(&self, handle: &ExecHandle) -> Result<()>;
    
    /// Optional: checkpoint current state (sprites supports this natively).
    async fn checkpoint(&self, handle: &ExecHandle) -> Result<Option<String>> {
        Ok(None) // default: no-op
    }
    
    /// Backend name for logging/config.
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
}
```

### Backends

1. **LocalBackend** — extract current tokio::process behavior. Zero-config default.
2. **SpritesBackend** — provisions a sprite via https://api.sprites.dev/v1, execs agent inside it. Supports checkpoints, resource policies, filesystem access, network isolation.
3. Future: K8sBackend, DockerBackend, etc.

### Sprites.dev API surface (what we use)

- `POST /v1/sprites` — provision
- `WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/exec` — run commands (WebSocket)
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/checkpoints` — snapshot before/after
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/policies/resources` — CPU/mem limits
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/policies/network` — egress whitelist
- `DELETE /v1/sprites/{name}` — teardown
- `GET/POST /v1/sprites/{name}/fs/{path}` — read/write files (inject prompts, extract artifacts)

### Config

```toml
[execution]
backend = "sprites"  # or "local" (default)

[execution.sprites]
token_env = "SPRITES_TOKEN"
default_resources = { cpu = 2, memory_mb = 4096 }
network_allowlist = ["api.linear.app", "api.github.com"]
checkpoint_on_complete = true
```

### Integration with dispatch.rs

`AgentProvider::spawn_agent()` currently returns `tokio::process::Child`. This changes:
- LocalBackend: still returns a local process (backward compat)
- SpritesBackend: provisions sprite → installs agent CLI → execs prompt → streams output via WebSocket → returns exit status

The `AgentHandle` in reconcile.rs wraps an `ExecHandle` instead of a raw `Child`.

### K8s-like patterns

Sprites follows resource-oriented REST (CRUD on sprites, policies, services, checkpoints). Rosary's reconciler already runs a k8s-controller-style desired-state loop. The fit is natural: reconciler declares "bead X needs a sprite", sprites API provisions it, reconciler polls for completion.

## Sub-beads (parallel-safe after trait is defined)

1. ExecutionBackend trait + ProvisionOpts + ExecHandle types
2. LocalBackend — extract from dispatch.rs
3. SpritesClient — HTTP/WS client for sprites.dev API
4. SpritesBackend — trait impl using SpritesClient
5. Config extension — [execution] section parsing
6. Reconciler integration — backend selection + handle type change
7. Checkpoint lifecycle — snapshot on dispatch + on completion
8. Tests — mock sprites server + integration tests with real API

Whether the workspace is local jj or a sprite is rsry's concern, not the conductor's. The trait, client, and config are all still correct. The reconciler integration bead (rsry-e608bb) scope narrows to just exposing MCP tools, not wiring into reconcile.rs dispatch loop.

description:
Standalone HTTP client for the sprites.dev REST API. No rosary-specific logic — pure API wrapper. Lives in `src/sprites.rs`.

## Endpoints to implement

### Must-have (P0)

- `DELETE /v1/sprites/{name}` — destroy sprite
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/exec` — execute command (HTTP variant)
- `WSS /v1/sprites/{name}/exec` — execute command (WebSocket, streaming)
- `GET /v1/sprites/{name}` — get sprite status

### Should-have (P1)
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/checkpoints` — create checkpoint
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/checkpoints/{id}/restore` — restore checkpoint
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/policies/resources` — set CPU/mem limits
- `POST /v1/sprites/{name}/policies/network` — set egress allowlist

### Nice-to-have (P2)
- `GET/POST /v1/sprites/{name}/fs/{path}` — read/write files
- `GET /v1/sprites/{name}/services` — list services

## Design

```rust
pub struct SpritesClient {
    client: reqwest::Client,
    base_url: String, // default "https://api.sprites.dev/v1"
}

impl SpritesClient {
    pub fn new(token: &str) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn with_base_url(token: &str, base_url: &str) -> Result<Self>; // for testing
    
    pub async fn create_sprite(&self, name: &str, opts: &CreateOpts) -> Result<Sprite>;
    pub async fn get_sprite(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Sprite>;
    pub async fn delete_sprite(&self, name: &str) -> Result<()>;
    pub async fn exec(&self, name: &str, cmd: &str) -> Result<ExecOutput>;
    pub async fn create_checkpoint(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Checkpoint>;
    pub async fn set_resource_policy(&self, name: &str, policy: &ResourcePolicy) -> Result<()>;
    pub async fn set_network_policy(&self, name: &str, domains: &[&str]) -> Result<()>;
}
```

Auth: Bearer token from SPRITES_TOKEN env var or config.

TDD:
1. Test client construction with/without token (error on missing)
2. Test URL building for each endpoint
3. Test request serialization for create/exec/checkpoint
4. Test response deserialization (mock JSON responses)
5. Test error handling (4xx, 5xx, network errors)
6. Integration test gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "sprites-integration")]` or env var

No dependency on ExecutionBackend trait — this is a pure API client. Can be built in parallel with the trait.

description:
Wire the ExecutionBackend into the reconciliation loop. This is the integration bead — connects the trait, backends, and config to the existing reconciler.

## Changes

title: Checkpoint lifecycle: snapshot on dispatch + on completion for sprites backend
description:
Integrate sprites checkpoints into the bead lifecycle for reproducibility and debugging.

## Checkpoint points

1. **Post-provision**: After sprite is provisioned and files injected, before agent runs. This is the "clean state" checkpoint — enables re-running from scratch.
2. **Post-completion**: After agent exits (pass or fail). This captures the agent's work for review, even if the sprite is destroyed.
3. **Pre-verify**: Before running test suite. If tests break the environment, restore this checkpoint and re-verify.

## Implementation

Add to SpritesBackend:
```rust
async fn provision(&self, opts: &ProvisionOpts) -> Result<ExecHandle> {
    // ... create sprite, set policies, inject files ...
    if self.checkpoint_on_complete {
        self.client.create_checkpoint(&sprite_name).await?; // "clean-state"
    }
    // ...
}
```

Add lifecycle hooks to ExecutionBackend trait:
```rust
/// Called after agent completes, before verification.
async fn on_agent_complete(&self, handle: &ExecHandle) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }

/// Called after verification passes/fails, before destroy.
async fn on_verify_complete(&self, handle: &ExecHandle, passed: bool) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }
```

SpritesBackend implements these to create named checkpoints:
- `{bead_id}-agent-done-{timestamp}`
- `{bead_id}-verified-{pass|fail}-{timestamp}`

## Checkpoint metadata stored in Dolt

Log checkpoint IDs as bead events:
```sql
INSERT INTO bead_events (bead_id, event_type, payload)
VALUES ('rsry-abc', 'checkpoint', '{"id": "cp-xyz", "phase": "agent-done", "sprite": "rsry-abc"}');
```

This enables `rsry restore <bead-id> --phase agent-done` for debugging.

TDD:
1. SpritesBackend creates checkpoint on provision (when enabled)
2. SpritesBackend creates checkpoint on agent complete
3. Checkpoint IDs logged to Dolt events
4. No checkpoints created when checkpoint_on_complete = false
5. Checkpoint failure is non-fatal (log warning, continue)

Depends on: SpritesBackend + SpritesClient beads

title: Worktree-scoped bead state: each worktree gets a Dolt branch fork of main
description: Currently worktrees cant access .beads/ (only main has it). The fix isnt to symlink — its to make each worktree a Dolt branch. Agent creates worktree → Dolt branches beads state → agent writes to branch → on merge, Dolt merges bead state too. The bead diff IS the work diff. Zero-copy from main (Dolt prolly tree shares unchanged rows). This is the same architecture as jj workspaces but for bead data. Enables: atomic code+bead commits (rsry-95a67e), O(diff) merges (rsry-95b291), per-agent state isolation.

title: Org-level beads: cross-repo architectural truths tracked in a shared namespace
description: Integration facts like 'mache uses ley-line C FFI' or 'rosary dispatches via ACP to agents with mache MCP' dont belong to any single repo. Need an org-level bead namespace (e.g. art-* prefix) stored in a shared Dolt DB (maybe ~/.rsry/org.db or the art monorepo .beads/). The PM agent creates and maintains these. They surface as threads linking repo-scoped beads. Linear projects per integration (not per repo) would visualize these. This is what the product-manager agent role tracks — the connective tissue between repos.

title: Mache as universal bead interface: Dolt ↔ SQLite ↔ filesystem ↔ MCP via schema engine
description: Mache schema engine is the adapter between storage and interface. Dolt stores beads (versioned, mergeable). Mache projects them as: (1) MCP tools (today — rsry serve), (2) mounted filesystem (tomorrow — mache-85t), (3) SQLite tables (via ley-line arena). Write path always converges to Dolt. The agent picks whichever interface fits: MCP for programmatic, filesystem for file-based agents, SQL for direct queries. The schema is the universal translator. AST merge via mache write-back pipeline handles all paths.

title: Interrupt protocol: bug found → bead → dispatch fix → wait or workaround → resume
description: When a tool breaks mid-workflow, the process: (1) auto-create P0 bead, (2) dispatch fix agent, (3) if blocking wait, (4) if not fall back to CLI. For self=true repos, the reconciler self-heals. For external repos, the detection differs — need a closure/callback pattern so each repo can define its own failure detection. The reconciler cant assume all repos behave like rosary.

title: Binary version tracking: detect stale MCP processes after install
description: After task install, stale rsry serve processes run old binary. Fix: embed build hash, signal running processes to restart on install (SIGHUP or UDS), include hash in MCP initialize response. Claude Code spawns multiple rsry serve processes — all must be same version.
